2ddadb22-c8c8-fea5-7824-e382d09fdbdd.story_is: Norður af túni er Kotás. Hann er sérstæður, nokkuð hár, og er suðurhlið hans snertispöl norður af Lambhúshól. Var Norður-Hólakot þar í brekkunni, og sjást þess enn merki. Það var einnig nefnt Efra-Hólakot og Upp-Hólakot. Þarna bjó síðast Gísli Guðmundsson árið 1805.

2ddf6692-af6c-905d-f04c-d2a469bebdd3.story_eng: Landdísarsteinn is a large boulder where huldufólk (hidden people) were believed to live. Children were not allowed to pick the geitnaskóf (rock tripe, a lichen growing on the stone) or anything else the hidden people used to adorn their home. Long ago the stone is said to have come tumbling down from the hillside. When people caught sight of it they were frightened, because it was heading straight for the farm. Had it rolled over just one more time, it would have landed on the farm.
2ddf6692-af6c-905d-f04c-d2a469bebdd3.story_is: Í þessum stóra steini bjó huldufólk og máttu börn ekki hirða þar geitnaskóf né annað sem huldufólkið hafði til híbýlaprýði. Steinn þessi kom endur fyrir löngu ofan úr hlíðinni og þegar sást til hans varð fólkið hrætt, því hann stefndi á bæinn, og ef hann hefði tekið eina veltu til hefði hann verið kominn á bæinn.

2dfa3bab-fc4f-1b10-4731-9e79d063f4ef.story_eng: Stórugrjót, 'the big rocks', lie directly above Stóristeinn, 'the big stone'. A great rockfall is believed to have come down from the part of the mountain called Öxlin during the earthquake of 1784, and Stóristeinn is thought to have fallen at the same time.
2dfa3bab-fc4f-1b10-4731-9e79d063f4ef.story_is: Beint upp af Stórasteini eru Stórugrjót. Talið er að í jarðskjálftanum 1784 hafi orðið mikið hrun úr fjallinu þar sem heitir Öxlin, og mun Stóristeinn þá hafa hrunið líka.

2dfa69f9-80d7-fc32-0fd8-252b49a60636.story_eng: Ræningjalág, "Robbers' Hollow", is a deep hollow that runs down from the scree below the peak to just in front of the farm's home field. It is said to be the hollow the robbers took up to the farm when Austmaður attacked Hringur, the farmer at Hringsdalur, who had only a few men with him. Austmaður settled old scores with Hringur by killing him. So the tale is told in Hringssaga.
2dfa69f9-80d7-fc32-0fd8-252b49a60636.story_is: Þetta er sögð lágin sem ræningjarnir fóru heim að bænum er Austmaður sótti að Hring bónda í Hringsdal og fámennum, enda gerði hann upp við Hring gamlar sakir með því að hann drap hann. Svo segir Hringssaga. Lágin er djúp og gengur úr urðardrögum, niður af núpnum og framan við túnið.

2e19e6cd-925a-ab55-4846-4b6db8eab16f.story_eng: Veislubali, roughly 'feast slope', got its name because men out on the autumn sheep round-ups were given refreshments here before setting off. One of them exclaimed, "Why, it's a real feast!", and that is how the person who wrote this description came up with the name.
2e19e6cd-925a-ab55-4846-4b6db8eab16f.story_is: Veislubali fékk nafn sitt af því að þarna fengu leitarmenn í haustleitum hressingu áður en lagt var upp. Einn leitarmanna sagði: „Það er bara veisla!“ og þannig datt þeim sem þetta ritar nafnið í hug.

2e50020f-0a70-ce1c-c800-9573882fdc2f.story_eng: A stable stood here, built in the 19th century and torn down in the first half of the 20th; it is now gone. Around 1990 a fence was taken down on Nautanes, and in it was an oak post with holes and broken wooden pegs that caught the eye of the man who removed it. A local man said the post had once been a support in this stable and had come from a French schooner that was wrecked in Skjálfandi bay in the 19th century. The oak was still sound, rotten only where the post had stood in the ground.
2e50020f-0a70-ce1c-c800-9573882fdc2f.story_is: Þarna stóð hesthús, byggt á 19. öld og rifið á fyrri hluta 20. aldar. Upp úr 1990 var rifin girðing á Nautanesi. Í henni var eikarstaur með götum og brotnum trétöppum sem þótti athyglisverður. Sagt var að þessi staur hefði verið stoð í hesthúsinu og kominn úr franskri skútu sem strandaði á Skjálfanda á 19. öld. Eikin var ófúin nema þar sem staurinn hafði staðið í jörð.

2e527593-367c-4914-a73a-ae55321b40a2.story_eng: Þvottadalur means "washing dale". This hollow now lies in a newly cultivated hayfield, but it was once a fairly deep dip that always stood full of water in winter. Laundry from the farm Skip was often washed there, at least in part.
2e527593-367c-4914-a73a-ae55321b40a2.story_is: Laut í nýræktuðu túni sem var áður alldjúpur dalur og stóð ævinlega fullur af vatni á vetrum. Þar var tíðum þveginn þvottur frá Skipum, að einhverju leyti.

2e6b7952-2260-82fd-83f8-47194c543f2f.story_eng: Árnahvammur is named after Árni Gíslason from Skörðum, who died of exposure here. A gerningahríð, a storm raised by sorcery, was sent against him, and the story can be found in the Icelandic folk tales (Þjóðsögur). The hollow lies where the road bends around the shoulder of the hill.
2e6b7952-2260-82fd-83f8-47194c543f2f.story_is: Þar sem vegurinn beygir fyrir öxlina tekur við hvammur sem heitir Árnahvammur. Þar varð úti Árni Gíslason frá Skörðum. Var gerð að honum gerningahríð, og má sjá frásögn af því í Þjóðsögum.

2e769162-dc38-b945-0f4e-efb4d34ba128.story_eng: Svartagil, the Black Ravine, is marked by the black conglomerate cliffs that line it. Stories tell that a battle was once fought here and that the dead were buried at Leiðaflöt. A spearhead is said to have been found in Svartagil as proof of this.
2e769162-dc38-b945-0f4e-efb4d34ba128.story_is: Svartagil einkennist af svörtum þursabergsklettum meðfram gilinu. Sögur herma að þar hafi verið barist og líkin verið grafin á Leiðaflöt. Átti að hafa fundist spjótsoddur í Svartagili því til sönnunar.

2e7b6681-138f-8d1f-2b8d-b56b1b8ed6fa.story_eng: Bænhúshóll means chapel hill, and it is believed that a small chapel, a bænhús, stood here in olden times. The hill lies at the eastern end of the home field known as Framtún.
2e7b6681-138f-8d1f-2b8d-b56b1b8ed6fa.story_is: Talið er að á Bænhúshóli hafi verið bænhús til forna. Hóllinn er austast í Framtúni.

2e7e470f-7a30-0e89-f8ee-9fef42d9ed13.story_eng: Kjölshaus is the southernmost end of the ridge called Kjölur, west of the Rangártjarnir ponds, and a built cairn stands on its top. On the grassy slope to the south of the ponds lies Mallandsel, a sel (a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked). West of Kjölshaus lies the near end of the lake Aravatn. A short way down along the lake stood Aravatnsskáli, a hut where people are said to have stayed while out gathering Iceland moss (grastekja). Only faint traces of its ruins can still be seen.
2e7e470f-7a30-0e89-f8ee-9fef42d9ed13.story_is: Kjölshaus er suðurendinn á Kjölnum, vestan við Rangártjarnir, en sunnanhallt við þær er Mallandsel í grösugum halla. Á hausnum er hlaðin varða. Vestur af Kjölshaus er fremri endi Aravatns. Stutt frá honum, niður með vatninu, var Aravatnsskáli. Sagt er að þar hafi fólk legið við við grasatekju. Aðeins sér fyrir rústunum.

2e849b27-ce79-c24f-1211-238def91a5d2.story_eng: Gráblesi is a small water-filled hollow just north of the home field, right beside the old mountain path Fjallsgata and at the north-east corner of the high lava ridge north of the field. The name, which means a grey horse with a white blaze, is believed to come from a horse that met with an accident there.
2e849b27-ce79-c24f-1211-238def91a5d2.story_is: Gráblesi er vatnsstampur norðan túns, rétt við Fjallsgötu og við norðausturhorn háa hraunkambsins sem er norðan við túnið. Talið er að nafnið stafi frá hesti sem hafi slysast þar.

2e94f475-3a4d-a09a-b73d-047541e847a1.story_eng: Krossvöllur was once a stretch of rough, hummocky grassland, mown every year, and yet the grass always grew thick and lush. This puzzled many people, because nothing was ever spread on the field to fertilise it. Strips of heathland ran across the grassland in the shape of a cross, cutting it apart, and the field probably took its name from that (kross means cross). It is now a hayfield.
2e94f475-3a4d-a09a-b73d-047541e847a1.story_is: Krossvöllurinn er í Háholtsvelli, áður kargþýft valllendi og slegið árlega en samt alltaf síbreiðugras. Furðaði marga á þessu þar sem aldrei var neitt borið á völlinn. Inni í þessu valllendisstykki voru móar sem krossskáru teiginn í sundur og hefur völlurinn líklega dregið nafn sitt af því. Þar er nú tún.

2e950998-5d82-5eea-9ff0-e5b78aa87f70.story_eng: Sandar, also called Sandakvísl, is an old riverbed of Héraðsvötn, very wide in places, running southwest and west of Borgarey. Today it usually holds very little water and is nearly dry when the river is at its lowest. In great floods, however, it becomes deep enough that horses must swim, and its great width makes it daunting to cross. Sandar was long notorious for quicksand, even in dry sand, probably because old pools there had later filled with sand. One man is known to have died there: Björn Ólafsson, a farmer at Eyhildarholt, originally from Auðólfsstaðir in Langidalur and brother of the Reverend Arnljótur Ólafsson at Bægisá. On 5 May 1853, at the far end of Sandar just south of the farm Syðri-Húsabakki, he and his horse vanished in shallow water, and neither was ever seen again. A later writer noted that the other branches of the river were carrying less water while Sandar was growing, and thought that within a few decades much of Héraðsvötn might flow west through Sandar again, as it is believed to have done for centuries.
2e950998-5d82-5eea-9ff0-e5b78aa87f70.story_is: Sandar eru gamall farvegur Héraðsvatna, mjög breiður á köflum, suðvestan og vestan við Borgarey. Í Söndum er nú að jafnaði mjög lítið vatn, og má kalla að þurrir séu þegar lægst er í Vötnunum. Í stórflóðum eru þeir hins vegar sundvatn og þá ekki árennilegir, vegna þess hve breiðir þeir eru. Sandar voru lengi illræmdir fyrir sandkviku, jafnvel í þurrum sandi. Munu þar áður hafa verið gamlir hyljir sem sand hefur síðan borið í. Vitað er um einn mann sem fórst þar, Björn Ólafsson, bónda í Eyhildarholti, frá Auðólfsstöðum í Langadal og bróður séra Arnljóts Ólafssonar á Bægisá. Hann fórst 5. maí 1853 yst í Söndum, rétt sunnan við bæinn á Syðri-Húsabakka. Hvarf þar maður og hestur á grunnu vatni og sást hvorugur síðan. Vatnsmagn í Austurkvíslinni og Stokkunum hefur farið minnkandi hin síðari ár. Suðurkvíslin virðist halda nokkuð í horfinu, en Sandarnir vaxa. Ekki þykir fráleitt að ætla, ef fram heldur sem horfir, að eftir nokkra áratugi muni verulegur hluti Vatnanna renna vestur Sandana, eins og talið er að verið hafi um aldir.

2ec478a9-949a-40e1-68d6-78e7f1926715.story_eng: The name Þvottá means "washing river". It is said that wool was once washed in this stream, which is how it got its name.
2ec478a9-949a-40e1-68d6-78e7f1926715.story_is: Lækurinn heitir svo þar sem sagt er að ull hafi verið þvegin í honum.

2ed0ba8e-3651-4340-8d44-fc2bfb610b15.story_eng: Gamla-Stífla means "the old dam." The dam was cast in concrete in 1966. Before that, the river was dammed with a large driftwood log laid across it and sealed with turf. That dam had to be taken out before the spring thaw so it would not be washed away.
2ed0ba8e-3651-4340-8d44-fc2bfb610b15.story_is: Stíflan var steypt 1966. Fyrir þann tíma var stíflað með stóru rekaviðartré sem lagt var þvert í ána og þétt að með torfi. Þá stíflu varð að taka fyrir vorleysingar svo hún skolaðist ekki í burtu.

2edc3302-7d6e-4125-a460-90795d2d82e2.story_eng: Lónveita was a stretch of wet land below the waterfalls known as Fossarnir, where the river Bleiksá once flowed, with Álatorfa lying south of the river. Here the sheep gathered from the mountains were watched through the night before the fjallrétt, the autumn round-up where the flocks were sorted. All of this land has since been taken by the river Þverá and is described as little more than black sand; Lónveita no longer exists.
2edc3302-7d6e-4125-a460-90795d2d82e2.story_is: Niður af Fossunum var Lónveita, þar sem Bleiksá rann áður, en Álatorfa sunnan við ána. Þar var fjallsafnið vaktað nóttina fyrir fjallrétt. Land þetta allt er nú komið í Þverá og má teljast svartur sandur.

2ee6c009-4c69-1d11-e7a3-112060e63d6b.story_eng: Brunnhellishólmi lies in the river Laxá just below the farm Hóll. Facing it on the island of Geldingey is Brunnhellishró with the cave Brunnhellir. The name means roughly 'well-cave islet', but an old boundary register calls the islet Brumhelluhólmi. This may have been its original name, later turned into Brunnhellishólmi through folk explanation. Yet a closer look at Brunnhellir shows the faint outline of a ditch running from the cave down to Laxá, and water still seeps out along it. It is said there was a spring here where sheep kept in the cave were watered, so no one had to fetch water for them from the river. Springs like this were often called brunnar, wells.
2ee6c009-4c69-1d11-e7a3-112060e63d6b.story_is: Rétt neðan við Hól er Brunnhellishólmi og á móti honum í Geldingey Brunnhellishró með Brunnhelli. Í landamerkjaskrá er þessi hólmi kallaður Brumhelluhólmi. Mætti því gera því skóna að það hafi verið nafn hólmans í upphafi en seinna orðið að Brunnhellishólma við alþýðuskýringu. En þegar grannt eru skoðaðar aðstæður við Brunnhelli sést móta fyrir skurði frá hellinum og fram í Laxá og vætlar vatn undan hróinu eftir honum. Sagt er að þarna hafi verið uppspretta sem sauðfé í hellinum var brynnt við svo ekki þyrfti að sækja handa því vatn út í ána. Svona uppsprettur voru oft kallaðar brunnar.

2ef49257-d588-7a51-7a7d-74d2ef28d3f7.story_eng: Syðra-Stekkjargil and its twin, Stekkjargil ytra, are two gullies running down towards the river Héraðsvötn, just south of the boundary between the farms Steinsstaðir and Reykir. They are said to have been formed by water draining east out of the Steinsstaðaflói marsh. A stream flowing north-east from the marsh splits at the end of a gravel ridge and runs down both gullies. Their names point to a stekkur, a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes during the milking season, somewhere in this area. One local man remembered seeing some stonework in one of the gullies that may have been the remains of such a fold.
2ef49257-d588-7a51-7a7d-74d2ef28d3f7.story_is: Stekkjargil ytra og Stekkjargil syðra eru austur undir Héraðsvötnum, skammt sunnan við landamerki Steinsstaða og Reykja. Sagt er að þau gil muni hafa orðið til vegna vatnsrennslis austur úr Steinsstaðaflóa. Lækur sem fer norðaustur úr flóanum klofnar við enda melhryggs og rennur niður bæði Stekkjargilin. Nöfn giljanna benda til að stekkur hafi verið á þessum slóðum, og heimildarmaður man eftir að hafa séð einhverja hleðslu í öðru gilinu sem hugsanlega hafi verið leifar af stekk.

2f006a07-21bd-4795-93e8-a2ac97ff05b8.story_eng: Hot springs once flowed straight out of the rock in the hillside a little north of Varmahlíð and somewhat higher up. Below the springs lay a scree of boulders, and the warm water seeped down through it, leaving the stones white with silica. The place was therefore called Hvítaberg, "white rock", and the springs Hvítabergslaugar. The springs have since been harnessed to heat the houses of the Húsmæðraskólinn (the housekeeping school) and Varmahlíð. When that happened, the white colour disappeared from the stones, and the name Hvítaberg is no longer heard.
2f006a07-21bd-4795-93e8-a2ac97ff05b8.story_is: Í hlíðinni, rétt norðan við Varmahlíð og nokkru ofar, spretta fram heitar laugar út úr bergi. Niður frá laugauppsprettunum var grjóturð og seytlaði laugavatnið um urðina, og voru steinarnir þarna hvítir af kísil úr laugavatninu. Þarna var nefnt Hvítaberg og laugarnar Hvítabergslaugar. Þær eru nú notaðar til upphitunar húsa í Húsmæðraskólanum og í Varmahlíð. Hvíti liturinn á steinunum hvarf þegar laugarnar voru beislaðar, og Hvítaberg heyrist ekki nefnt lengur.

2f446c61-0d01-cece-5281-e7f568e9d6a4.story_eng: Selbrekka, meaning 'shieling slope', is a high slope. At its foot lies Sel, an old sel (a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked), where the faint outlines of old ruins can still be made out. The site lies midway between Skyggnir and Selhóll, a large scoria hill with a crater bowl in its top.
2f446c61-0d01-cece-5281-e7f568e9d6a4.story_is: Mitt á milli Skyggnis og Selhóls er Sel. Þar sér móta fyrir gömlum tóttum neðan undir hárri brekku, Selbrekku. Selhóll er stór gjallhóll með gígskál í kolli.

2f492275-9d93-5b7b-185a-a5afa25065b3.story_eng: Riddari (the Knight) is a rock pillar on the south-eastern side of the mountain. It was once used as a sjómið, a landmark fishermen lined up with another landmark to find their fishing grounds at sea. Its partner was another rock of the same name above Straumsvík, which has sadly been destroyed. From Riddari there is a walkable route down the mountain that passes through a large stone arch. At the very top of the mountain stands a cairn, which is really a rock dyke with stones piled around it.
2f492275-9d93-5b7b-185a-a5afa25065b3.story_is: Í suðaustri er klettadrangur í fjallinu sem heitir Riddari. Fyrrum var Riddarinn sjómið af öðrum samnefndum ofan Straumsvíkur sem því miður hefur verið fargað. Þaðan er fær gönguleið niður af fjallinu og liggur hún í gegnum stóran steinboga. Efst uppi á fjallinu er varða sem er í raun berggangur sem grjóti hefur verið hlaðið í kringum.

2f52c700-69d1-b508-8807-c7c584a0d55e.story_eng: Hálsgróf, also called Grófin or Draugagróf (Ghost Hollow), is a deep dip cutting across the upper part of the ridge, and the road from Hjaltadalur over to Kolbeinsdalur runs through it. A sheep-sorting fold once stood here, where sheep from the round-up were sorted to their owners. Two shepherds, one from each valley, from the farms Fjall and Víðines, fought here and both were killed. They were buried in cairns on the edges of the ridge. After this, such strong hauntings arose around the fold that it was moved down to Heljardalseyrar, where it still stands. It is said that even now the clash of weapons can be heard in Draugagróf by anyone passing through after nightfall.
2f52c700-69d1-b508-8807-c7c584a0d55e.story_is: Vegurinn úr Hjaltadal yfir í Kolbeinsdal liggur um Hálsgróf. Grófin er djúp laut þvert í gegnum Ásinn ofarlega. Hún er líka nefnd Draugagróf. Þar var eitt sinn skilarétt. Þar börðust tveir smalar, sinn úr hvorum dal, frá Fjalli og Víðinesi, og féllu báðir. Þeir voru dysjaðir á hálsbrúnunum. Eftir þennan atburð gerðist svo magnaður draugagangur umhverfis réttina að hún var færð fram á Heljardalseyrarnar, þar sem hún stendur enn. Ekki er laust við að enn þyki mega heyra vopnaglamur í Draugagróf sé farið þar um eftir dagsetur.

2f63c8c2-71ad-f665-4dc3-ca5be0ad39a2.story_eng: Hólkotsflói is a calm, slow-flowing stretch of the river, running south from the Hólkotsfoss waterfall to the rapids below Langhólmafoss. It was an old ferry crossing used from the farm Brettingsstaðir. The quiet water also claimed lives: Jóhann Guðnason drowned here in 1891, and Stefán Sigurðsson and Guðjón Sigurgeirsson in 1901.
2f63c8c2-71ad-f665-4dc3-ca5be0ad39a2.story_is: Hólkotsflói er lygnan frá Hólkotsfossi suður að strengjunum neðan við Langhólmafoss. Þar var ferjustaður, gamall ferjustaður frá Brettingsstöðum. Þar drukknaði Jóhann Guðnason árið 1891, og Stefán Sigurðsson og Guðjón Sigurgeirsson árið 1901.

2f700133-e465-4dc8-936e-393a3cdb2846.story_eng: On the eastern rim of the Strjúgsgil ravine, where the slope begins to rise more steeply, stands a rock shaped like a human figure. It is called Kelling, and the name is never pronounced Kerling, with an R. Kerling is the usual Icelandic word for an old woman.
2f700133-e465-4dc8-936e-393a3cdb2846.story_is: Á austurbrún Strjúgsgils, þar sem Strjúgsgilsfláin byrjar að rísa brattar, er klettur með mannsmynd sem kallaður er Kelling. Nafnið er aldrei borið fram Kerling, með r-i.

2f7fc0ff-25a7-4e53-8753-90af3ffbef43.story_eng: Miðaftanshóll is a large gravel hill a short way out from the farm Bjarnastaðir, running up and down the slope, with the old path passing along its foot. The name refers to miðaftann, an old time of day in the early evening. No stone cairn can be seen there now, but one must once have stood on the hill, built as an eyktarstaður from Bjarnastaðir. This was a time marker: when the sun stood above it as seen from the farm, people knew what time of day it was.
2f7fc0ff-25a7-4e53-8753-90af3ffbef43.story_is: Miðaftanshóll heitir stór melhóll skammt utan við Bjarnastaði. Liggur hann upp og ofan og er gatan neðst í hólnum. Engin grjótvarða sést þar nú, en varðan hlýtur að hafa verið þar, hlaðin í eyktarstað frá Bjarnastöðum.

2f9394ed-5648-9121-4605-79767782d75d.story_eng: Takaklettur is a rock above Tjónsvík that links the upper cliffs with the sea cliffs. A narrow passage runs through it and shares its name. In this area it is the only passable route around Blakkur. A gate stands in the passage to control the movement of sheep.
2f9394ed-5648-9121-4605-79767782d75d.story_is: Klettur yfir Tjónsvík sem tengir saman efri kletta og sjávarkletta. Í klettinum er mjór gangur sem ber sama nafn og er hann eina leiðin sem fær er fyrir Blakk á þessum slóðum. Hlið er í ganginum til að stýra umgangi sauðfjár.

2fa650a7-ab1c-47a4-b8e1-18085513cefc.story_eng: Hraungarður, whose name means 'lava wall', is a ridge that runs out along the old hayfields of the farm Gröf. The very first hayfields at Gröf were said to have been on the north side of this ridge. For a time the farmhouse itself stood just east of the ridge, along with a stable on Hesthústún, the 'stable field'.
2fa650a7-ab1c-47a4-b8e1-18085513cefc.story_is: Hraungarður liggur út með gömlu túnunum í Gröf og voru fyrstu túnin sögð norðan í hryggnum. Austan við hrygginn var um tíma bærinn og Hesthús á Hesthústúni.

2fbaa994-0d5e-cad5-3854-667fdf6bfa2a.story_eng: Ölæðisbanki, also called Ölæðið, is a fishing ground within Rósagarðurinn. The story goes that a skipper was on his way home from a voyage to Germany when, in a drunken state (ölæði means drunkenness), he cast his net here and made a good catch. Ever since, the fishing spot has been called Ölæðið.
2fbaa994-0d5e-cad5-3854-667fdf6bfa2a.story_is: Í Rósagarðinum er Ölæðið. Sagan segir að skipstjóri einn hafi verið að koma úr siglingu frá Þýskalandi. Hann kastaði þarna í ölæði á heimleiðinni og fékk góðan afla. Eftir það heitir veiðistaðurinn Ölæðið.

2fc99612-e309-7202-3e92-b7ee945ef59f.story_eng: Urðarhóll stands roughly in the middle of the head of Myrkárdalur valley. Behind it a great rock juts out of the glacier, called Snyrta. A troll woman of that name is said to have been caught there by daylight, which in Icelandic folklore turns trolls to stone. When the glacier was larger than it is now, the scene, seen from far out in the valley, looked rather like a huge woman sitting there, with the top of Urðarhóll as her lap. The likeness has faded since the glacier shrank.
2fc99612-e309-7202-3e92-b7ee945ef59f.story_is: Nokkurn veginn fyrir miðjum botni Myrkárdals er Urðarhóll. Bak við hann stendur klettur einn mikill út úr jöklinum og kallast hann Snyrta. Tröllkonu með því nafni á að hafa dagað þarna uppi. Meðan jökullinn var meiri en nú er hann, var ekki ólíkt því til að sjá langt utan úr dalnum að þarna sæti stórvaxin kona, en þá var Urðarhólskollurinn kelta kerlingar. Líkingin við þetta hefur minnkað síðan jökullinn rýrnaði.

301d6b69-b231-495e-98ca-b5ea60fcbadc.story_eng: Clear ruins once stood here of a small cottage farm where men lived alone in the 19th century. One of them was Benóný Guðlaugsson, who was known by the name of Glettinganes. The ruin is believed to have been levelled in 1958, and nothing of it remains. The name Tótt is the Icelandic word for a ruin.
301d6b69-b231-495e-98ca-b5ea60fcbadc.story_is: Þarna var glögg tótt eftir kotbýli einsetumanna á 19. öld. Þarna bjó til dæmis Benóný Guðlaugsson, kenndur við Glettinganes. Tóttin mun hafa verið sléttuð árið 1958.

3021d5f5-0c2c-6ab2-c065-9fa8bde2877c.story_eng: Sultastígur is an old riding track across the heath. Before a road for cars was cleared over Reykjaheiði, the people of Víkingavatn often crossed the heath to Húsavík in summer, sometimes riding without loads and sometimes with pack-horse trains. They took the shortest way west from Víkingavatn, running along the ridges known as Veggir, past Sultir and south of Sjónarhóll, then southwest until they reached the main road near the farm Fjöll. The two routes met at Fjallabeitarhús, a sheep house (beitarhús) out in the grazing land. The track has been completely abandoned since cars could cross Reykjaheiði.
3021d5f5-0c2c-6ab2-c065-9fa8bde2877c.story_is: Áður en bílvegur var ruddur yfir Reykjaheiði fóru Vatnsbæingar oft á sumrum yfir Reykjaheiði til Húsavíkur, bæði lausríðandi og í lestaferðum. Var þá jafnan farin stysta leið vestur frá Víkingavatni, vestur með veggjunum, fram hjá Sultum, meðfram vestari Veggjum, sunnan Sjónarhóls og suðvestur þaðan, þangað til komið var vestur að Fjöllum og á aðalveginn sem lá og liggur enn suður frá bænum Fjöllum. Komu þessir vegir saman hjá Fjallabeitarhúsum. Reiðgata þessi heitir Sultastígur og er nú aflögð með öllu, síðan bílfært varð yfir Reykjaheiði.

30301163-0410-dc03-e872-dfa2df2a07b2.story_eng: Arnarsæti is a smooth, newly cultivated hayfield just southeast of Hálsasker, joined to it. It was once rough heath outside the home field, covered in small, closely packed tussocks. The farmers of Svínafell gave the field its name, roughly "Örn's seat", because of an event shortly before 1940. One autumn a small plane landed on the home field at Hálsasker to fetch a patient, Katrín Jónsdóttir, wife of Runólfur Jónsson, the district administrator (hreppstjóri) at Sandfell. The pilot was Agnar Koefod Hansen. The following spring Örn Johnson, later a captain with the airline Flugfélag Íslands, flew Katrín back home. He was expected to land in the same spot as Agnar, but for some reason he did not like the look of it and set down instead on the tussocky heath outside the field, which the locals thought a daunting place to land. Both the landing and the take-off went well, and this was thought a fortunate outcome given the conditions.
30301163-0410-dc03-e872-dfa2df2a07b2.story_is: Arnarsæti heitir slétt nýræktartún suðaustur af Hálsaskeri og áfast við það. Þar var áður þýfður mói utan túns með fremur smáu og þéttu þýfi. Svínafellsbændur gáfu nýræktartúninu þetta örnefni af því tilefni sem hér greinir: Laust fyrir 1940 lenti að hausti til lítil flugvél á túninu í Hálsaskeri til að sækja sjúkling, Katrínu Jónsdóttur, konu Runólfs Jónssonar hreppstjóra í Sandfelli. Flugmaðurinn var Agnar Koefod Hansen. Vorið eftir flaug Örn Johnson, síðar flugstjóri hjá Flugfélagi Íslands, með Katrínu til baka. Ætlast var til að hann lenti á túninu á sama stað og Agnar. Af einhverjum ástæðum leist Erni ekki á þennan lendingarstað og lenti á þúfnamóanum utan túns. Þótti heimamönnum þar óárennilegur lendingarstaður. Lendingin heppnaðist þó vel og flugtakið einnig. Þótti það gæfulega takast miðað við aðstæður.

3035346f-b23a-5267-9fe0-628946fdf6dd.story_eng: Skógarhjalli is a ledge by the gorge Knararárgil. From here it was possible to walk up onto Bjargið (the Cliff), though the route was thought to be hard going for horses. Beyond Skógarhjalli, Bjargið becomes very high and impossible to climb all the way to the ravine Auðunargjá, opposite the old Selfljót bridge. According to oral tradition, a man named Auðun is said to have skied down that ravine and stayed on his feet all the way to the flat ground below, which was considered a great feat.
3035346f-b23a-5267-9fe0-628946fdf6dd.story_is: Skógarhjalli er við Knararárgil. Þar er gengt upp á Bjargið, en þótti torleiði fyrir hesta. Inn af Skógarhjalla er Bjargið mjög hátt og ókleift allt inn undir Auðunargjá, sem er á móts við gömlu Selfljótsbrú. Munnmæli herma að Auðun nokkur hefði rennt sér niður gjána á skíðum og staðið brekkuna allt niður á jafnsléttu. Þótti þetta mikið afrek.

30636cc6-ff4e-c888-2a08-a75f6edb164d.story_eng: Prestapyttur, the Priests' Pool, is a pool in the farm brook Bæjarlækur in Ormsstaðadalur. It owes its name to a dispute over meadow boundaries between 1931 and 1939. On one side was séra Gísli, the assistant priest at Eiðar, who then lived at Ormsstaðir; on the other was Bjarni, the farmer at Ásgeirsstaðir. Once, when the two came to blows, Bjarni put the priest into the pool. It is not known exactly which pool it was, but local informants believe the one marked on the map is the most likely, since it lies closest to the boundary.
30636cc6-ff4e-c888-2a08-a75f6edb164d.story_is: Prestapyttur er í Bæjarlæknum inni í Dal (Ormsstaðadal). Tilefni nafnsins er að á árunum 1931–1939 deildu um engjamörk séra Gísli, aðstoðarprestur á Eiðum, sem þá bjó á Ormsstöðum, og Bjarni bóndi á Ásgeirsstöðum. Eitt sinn er þeir flugust á færði Bjarni prestinn í pyttinn. Ekki er nákvæmlega vitað hvaða pytt um ræðir, en heimildarmenn telja að sá sem merktur er sé líklegastur, enda næst landamerkjum.

306c9c25-ee16-3df3-09f2-a49771c5fad1.story_eng: On the slope north of the farmhouse a mare named Sóta gave birth to a foal. The foal was very skittish, and Árni Sigurðsson, the last farmer at Heiðarsel, had trouble getting close enough to see whether it was a colt or a filly. It fluttered about and kept darting behind its mother. In the end Árni saw that it was a filly, and she was named Fluga, which means fly. Fluga later became Árni's main riding horse, and when her life came to an end she was put down on the slope north of the farm and buried there with all her riding gear. The name Flugugröf means Fluga's grave.
306c9c25-ee16-3df3-09f2-a49771c5fad1.story_is: Í brekkunni norðan við íbúðarhúsið kastaði meri sem hét Sóta. Folaldið var mjög styggt og átti Árni Sigurðsson, síðasti ábúandi á Heiðarseli, í erfiðleikum með að komast að því til að sjá kynið. Folaldið flögraði um og flaug alltaf á bak við merina. Á endanum sá Árni þó kynið og að það var meri. Hún fékk nafnið Fluga. Fluga varð síðar helsti reiðhestur Árna og þegar ævi hennar lauk var hún felld í brekkunni norðan við bæinn og grafin þar með öllum reiðtygjum.

30832e1c-4289-58d9-3bd2-cd793f0417a8.story_eng: Gerðisvíkur are two small coves on the lake, cut into the eastern side of Þórðarhöfði. At some point in the distant past there was a farm here, and the ruins of its buildings can still be seen, along with a túngarður, the old wall that once enclosed the farm's home field.
30832e1c-4289-58d9-3bd2-cd793f0417a8.story_is: Í austanverðan Þórðarhöfða eru tvær smávíkur við vatnið og heita þær Gerðisvíkur. Þar hefur einhvern tímann í fyrndinni verið býli og eru þar húsarústir og túngarður.

30a1b979-718d-3f0e-27a4-95ced6d2de3c.story_eng: Hvammar is an area of grassy hollows west of the river Rangá. At its southern end lie Stekkjarlág and Stekkjarmór, where there is a stekkur, a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes in spring. In Stekkjarlág is Sundpollur, a pool where Marteinn Sigurðsson taught swimming for several springs after 1910.
30a1b979-718d-3f0e-27a4-95ced6d2de3c.story_is: Hvammar heitir svæði vestan Rangár. Syðst í þeim eru Stekkjarlág og Stekkjarmór og þar er stekkur. Í Stekkjarlág er Sundpollur þar sem Marteinn Sigurðsson kenndi sund nokkur vor eftir 1910.

30d41e50-1304-ba6e-49c8-ddbf84b396a0.story_eng: Nónhóll is a high lava hill with an ancient cairn on top, standing where the lava rises highest, southwest of the farm Eyjólfsstaðir. For years its true name was lost. People at the farm Syðra-Fjall called it Sjónarhóll, and it went by that name at Eyjólfsstaðir too during the writer's father's first years there. Later Benedikt Jakobsson came to the farm, old and blind, and talked with the father about the place names on the land. He revealed that the hill had been an eyktamark for Eyjólfsstaðir, a landmark that told the time of day by the sun's position, and that its name was Nónhóll, after nón, mid-afternoon. The name had fallen out of use after 1870.
30d41e50-1304-ba6e-49c8-ddbf84b396a0.story_is: Hár hraunhóll með fornri vörðu, þar sem hraunið er hæst suðvestur af Eyjólfsstöðum. Hér var glatað nafn. Frá Syðra-Fjalli var hóllinn nefndur Sjónarhóll, og svo var hann einnig nefndur hér fyrstu ár föður skrásetjara. En þegar Benedikt Jakobsson kom hingað gamall og blindur og faðir skrásetjara ræddi við hann um örnefni jarðarinnar, kom fram að þetta var eyktamark frá Eyjólfsstöðum og hét Nónhóll. Nafnið hafði fallið niður eftir 1870.

30db752c-a7a7-4519-5fb5-6b47108260cd.story_eng: This hollow or rock shelter lies in the band of cliffs east of Háahnúkur. The outlaw Arnes Pálsson, who lived in hiding in the wilderness, is believed to have stayed here, helped by the farmer.
30db752c-a7a7-4519-5fb5-6b47108260cd.story_is: Í klettabeltinu austan við Háahnúk er skál eða skúti. Talið er að Arnes Pálsson útilegumaður hafi haldið þar til og notið aðstoðar bóndans.

30dc2e35-5be9-9472-1bd9-02b8cf76a768.story_eng: When the farmhouse at Ófeigsfjörður burned down on Whit Sunday 1914, the household moved into Stóra-hlaða, the Big Barn. They lived there until they could move into a newly built house, known as "Gamla húsið" (the Old House), before Christmas the same year.
30dc2e35-5be9-9472-1bd9-02b8cf76a768.story_is: Þegar bærinn í Ófeigsfirði brann á hvítasunnudag 1914 kom heimilisfólkið sér fyrir í Stóru-hlöðunni og var þar þar til flutt var í nýbyggt hús, „Gamla húsið“, fyrir jól sama ár.

30e03d51-2207-4cb1-b5f6-b15676db17a8.story_eng: Tíðagata, whose name can be read as 'the path to church services', was an old path running through Kirkjuskarð (Church Pass), the gap between the Hellishólar hills. It is said to have continued on up into Ölfus. The path led east across the Sléttahraun lava field and on eastwards along Hjallafjall.
30e03d51-2207-4cb1-b5f6-b15676db17a8.story_is: Milli Hellishóla er Kirkjuskarð. Um það liggur Tíðagata og áfram upp í Ölfus, eins og sagt var. Tíðagata lá austur yfir Sléttahraun og austur með Hjallafjalli.

30ecfb00-ab06-47ac-b604-b8737e074cb9.story_eng: Prestaskarð means "priests' pass". The story goes that the priests of Kirkjubær and Hjaltastaður had fallen out, met here and made their peace, and the name is probably drawn from that. The pass lies in front of Krókavatn lake on Litla-Skarðsás, and people and flocks of sheep being driven usually went this way.
30ecfb00-ab06-47ac-b604-b8737e074cb9.story_is: Sú saga er sögð að prestar á Kirkjubæ og Hjaltastað hafi verið ósáttir, hist þarna og sæst, og líklega er nafnið af því dregið. Prestaskarð er framanvert við Krókavatn á Litla-Skarðsás. Alla jafna fóru fólk og fjárrekstrar um skarð þetta.

311f27e1-d1b1-5c76-fedb-02691b04695d.story_eng: Rigningarrimi means roughly "rain ridge", a name that comes from how the strip of grassland was used. In rainy spells, when the low hollows filled with water, haymaking was moved up here. The ridge stretches across the boundary into the land of Brúnavallakot.
311f27e1-d1b1-5c76-fedb-02691b04695d.story_is: Riminn dregur nafn sitt af því að þangað var flúið með heyskap þegar dælarnar fóru í vatn í rigningartíð. Hann nær yfir mörkin og í land Brúnavallakots.

313af124-8c81-b002-6b04-eb2bbef6e8ca.story_eng: Baðstofugrund is one of several place names here that begin with baðstofa. Together they suggest that at some point there was a baðstofa of the ancient kind on this spot, a bathhouse where people took steam baths heated by fire. Fuel would never have been a problem, as there is plenty of driftwood along this shore.
313af124-8c81-b002-6b04-eb2bbef6e8ca.story_is: Öll baðstofunöfnin hér benda til þess að einhvern tíma hafi verið þarna baðstofa í fornum stíl. Ekki hefur skort eldsmatinn því nóg er þar af rekaviði.

3145a731-7487-a7ef-79da-4cccaf21c165.story_eng: Ræningjahellir, the Robbers' Cave, is a small cave with a pool in the middle, hard to spot unless you know where it is. The islanders are believed to have hidden in this cave in 1627, when the Turks went raiding and plundering along the East Fjords.
3145a731-7487-a7ef-79da-4cccaf21c165.story_is: Lítill hellir með tjörn í miðjunni, lítt sýnilegur nema kunnugum. Talið er að eyjabúar hafi falið sig í þessum helli er Tyrkir fóru um Austfirði rænandi og ruplandi árið 1627.

314915e3-2a12-6e56-3cda-54ea5fef7fa9.story_eng: Neðri-Tjörn, also called Sykurtjörn (Sugar Pond), is the outermost of three ponds here. The others are Bæjartjörn, furthest west, and Miðtjörn. Sykurtjörn takes its name from an accident in 1914, when a man dropped sugar into the pond. The sugar had been meant for more useful purposes, though not for brewing, as some believed. The road runs between this pond and Bæjartjörn.
314915e3-2a12-6e56-3cda-54ea5fef7fa9.story_is: Tjarnirnar eru þrjár. Bæjartjörn er vestust, svo er Miðtjörn og utast er Sykurtjörn. Hún dregur nafn af slysi sem þar varð árið 1914, þegar maður missti í hana sykur sem átti að fara til þarfari hluta, þó ekki í brugg eins og sumir töldu. Vegurinn liggur milli Bæjartjarnar og Sykurtjarnar.

3152bbcc-1d53-4615-54c9-d2aa32d8b2f9.story_eng: Rauðakelda is the source of a stream, rising in the slope north of the gully Norðurgil. The water carries a great deal of mýrarrauði, the reddish bog iron ore found in Icelandic wetlands, which fits the name: rauð means red and kelda a spring or boggy pool.
3152bbcc-1d53-4615-54c9-d2aa32d8b2f9.story_is: Norðan við Norðurgil í brekkunni er lækjaruppspretta sem heitir Rauðakelda. Í henni er mikill mýrarrauði.

3182c1ba-5bc9-fb86-b3b9-4144bad2bde2.story_eng: Fálkhóll was the highest rise directly above the farm. Its name means falcon hill, and a falcon was often seen there. The hill is gone now: soldiers tore it completely apart.
3182c1ba-5bc9-fb86-b3b9-4144bad2bde2.story_is: Beint upp af bænum var Fálkhóll. Það var hæsta hæðin upp af bænum. Fálki sást oft þar á ferð. Hermenn rifu hólinn allan í sundur.

318f4d66-e182-47a6-815c-e707f7067bf1.story_eng: A cottager named Hjörleifur once built a small sheep house here. On the very first night he housed his sheep in it, one of the ewes died, and the next night the same thing happened. After that he gave up, and the house was torn down. The spot lies below Gvendarhóll, a hillock where the first settler of the farm is said to be buried.
318f4d66-e182-47a6-815c-e707f7067bf1.story_is: Þar byggði húsmaður að nafni Hjörleifur eitt sinn fjárhúskofa, en fyrstu nóttina sem hann hýsti í húsinu drapst ein ærin og næstu nótt fór á sömu leið. Þá gafst hann upp og svo var húsið rifið. Hjörleifstættur er niður af Gvendarhóli, þar sem frumbyggi jarðarinnar á að vera grafinn.

31946ae4-aa71-cf6b-2614-6d22dbd08bae.story_eng: The name, roughly 'Torment Rock', comes from how hard it was to make the way across it passable for horses. In 1967 the narrow path where people clambered over the rock with their horses could still be clearly seen, just north of the vehicle track. From Kvalaklöpp a very narrow spine of bare rock runs all the way down to the river. It is easy to see when looking out over the land from the slopes above.
31946ae4-aa71-cf6b-2614-6d22dbd08bae.story_is: Klöppin heitir svo vegna þess hve illt var að gera þar greiðfært fyrir hesta. Árið 1967 mátti vel sjá mjóan stíginn þar sem prílað var yfir með hestana, rétt fyrir norðan bílaslóðina. Frá Kvalaklöppinni gengur örmjór klapparrani allt niður að á, og sést hann vel þegar horft er yfir landið úr brekkunum fyrir ofan.

31a9e590-e44b-2e96-17c7-f80a3e77247a.story_eng: Strákhæðir are two lava hills. The hills seemed to grow larger the farther one went from them, and from a distance they looked like two men. The name fits: strákur means boy or lad, and hæðir means hills. Cairns once stood on the hills, and the road to Þorlákshöfn ran between them.
31a9e590-e44b-2e96-17c7-f80a3e77247a.story_is: Strákhæðir eru tvær hraunhæðir. Hæðirnar stækkuðu eftir því sem fjær dró frá þeim og voru eins og tveir menn að sjá. Vörður voru á hæðunum. Vegurinn til Þorlákshafnar lá á milli Strákhæðanna.

31af56d0-b743-4dec-98d5-414aa9eef3fc.story_eng: Stallar, south of Fögruhlíð, had an older name, Skeiðar, used especially for the upper part. The terraces served as a weather sign. If the evening fog settled on Skeiðar before it reached Hnjúkurinn, the peak on Kinnarfell, dry weather was likely the next morning. If the fog came to Hnjúkurinn first, rain was certain.
31af56d0-b743-4dec-98d5-414aa9eef3fc.story_is: Suður af Fögruhlíð heita Stallar, fornt nafn á þeim er Skeiðar, einkum efri hlutanum. Þeir voru veðurviti. Ef kvöldþoku lagði fyrr á Skeiðarnar en á Hnjúkinn á Kinnarfelli, þá voru líkur fyrir þurrki að morgni, en úrkoma var vís kæmi þokan fyrr á Hnjúkinn.

31affdb5-102f-ee88-198c-5a837f5b7905.story_eng: Up on the edge of the ravine are low hills known as Hró, overgrown with willow. There used to be a great deal of grey willow here, in bushes so large that people played hide-and-seek among them. The grey willow is now gone, and tea-leaved willow (rauðvíðir) has taken its place.
31affdb5-102f-ee88-198c-5a837f5b7905.story_is: Upp á gilbarminum eru holt sem nefnd eru Hró, víði vaxin. Þar var áður mikill grávíðir, stórir runnar, svo farið var þar í feluleiki. Grávíðirinn er nú horfinn, en rauðvíðir kominn í staðinn.

31b41f72-8072-4ac3-1c92-68b7f7079d73.story_eng: Bæjarhóll is the old farmstead site of Kollsvík. It is a tall, large mound up beneath the mountain Núpur, and it has probably built up entirely from many centuries of settlement. There were often two households farming in Kollsvík. The farm stood on the most sheltered spot in the cove, with a wide view, and water was fetched from Brunnhús (well house) a short way below the mound. In 1857 a deadly disaster struck the farm, which is now believed to have been an avalanche from Núpur. Many of the farmers of Kollsvík were leading men in their district. One of the best known from earlier times is Einar Jónsson, the forefather of the Kollsvík family line, Kollsvíkurætt.
31b41f72-8072-4ac3-1c92-68b7f7079d73.story_is: Gamla bæjarstæðið í Kollsvík. Hár og mikill hóll uppi undir Núpnum, sem sennilega hefur eingöngu hlaðist upp af margra alda byggð. Í Kollsvík var oft tvíbýli. Bærinn var á skjólsælasta staðnum í Víkinni og víðsýni mikið. Vatn var sótt í Brunnhús skammt neðan hólsins. Árið 1857 dundi mannskætt áfall yfir bæinn, sem nú er álitið að hafi verið snjóflóð úr Núpnum. Kollsvíkurbændur voru margir höfðingjar í sinni sveit. Einn þekktasti þeirra frá fyrri tíð er Einar Jónsson, ættfaðir Kollsvíkurættarinnar.

31b5a79b-9b1e-a981-74d6-fb3ff78f378b.story_eng: Mannabeinahóll, 'hill of human bones', lies right beside the hayfield of the farm Smjörhóll. Around the turn of the century the soil of a bank on the hill blew away, and human bones came to light. Bridge builders working not far away took the skull and kept it with them for a while, then returned it to the hill. Later the doctor Arnbjörn Ólafsson from Ferjubakki took the skull.
31b5a79b-9b1e-a981-74d6-fb3ff78f378b.story_is: Mannabeinahóll er alveg við túnið á Smjörhóli. Þar blés upp barð um aldamót og komu í ljós bein úr manni. Brúarsmiðir sem voru þar ekki fjarri fengu hauskúpuna og höfðu hjá sér og skiluðu henni síðan aftur í hólinn. Arnbjörn Ólafsson læknir frá Ferjubakka fékk síðan hauskúpuna.

31b6296a-bc04-9a1f-8ce8-90e3805eef68.story_eng: Ólafsvallasel was an ancient sel, a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked, belonging to the farm and church estate of Ólafsvellir. It lay in a green oasis in the lava field Merkurhraun, on a grassy lava ridge called Selhóll. Accounts differ on who used it last. It is said that the last to keep livestock there was the Rev. Guðni Guðmundsson, priest at Ólafsvellir from 1835 to 1843, while another account names his successor, the Rev. Pétur Stephensen, priest there from 1843 to 1859. The shieling no longer exists.
31b6296a-bc04-9a1f-8ce8-90e3805eef68.story_is: Ólafsvallasel er gróðurvin í Merkurhrauni, fornt sel frá Ólafsvöllum. Selið stendur á grónum hraunrima sem kallaður er Selhóll. Sagt er að sr. Guðni Guðmundsson, prestur á Ólafsvöllum 1835–1843, hafi síðastur haft þar í seli, en aðrir segja að það hafi verið sr. Pétur Stephensen, prestur á Ólafsvöllum 1843–1859.

31c9b058-8453-470d-9d0d-8dd7d810ae89.story_eng: Hvammkot was an old hjáleiga, a small tenant croft belonging to a larger farm. It stood on the slope south of the farm driveway and was enclosed by a wall. Below it lies a nameless hollow, and further south is another dry hollow with Vinnukonueyri (the servant woman's bank), a green riverbank stretching west to the river.
31c9b058-8453-470d-9d0d-8dd7d810ae89.story_is: Gömul hjáleiga, Hvammkot, var í brekkunni sunnan við heimreiðina, og var kotið umlukt garði. Neðan við Hvammkot er nafnlaus hvammur, en þar suður af er annar þurrlendur hvammur og þar heitir Vinnukonueyri, græn eyri vestur að ánni.

31ebf135-77c3-3d2f-70c6-672c9fca6141.story_eng: By old custom, the women owned all the driftage that washed up on Balinn. It is a gravel beach beneath fairly high banks, running from inside the headland of Garðsendavík almost all the way to Vogar. Driftage, mostly driftwood, was a valuable resource on Iceland's treeless coasts.
31ebf135-77c3-3d2f-70c6-672c9fca6141.story_is: Að fornum sið áttu konur allan reka á Balanum. Þar er malarfjara undir allháum bökkum og nær hann frá Garðsendavíkurnefinu heim undir Voga.

31f88f9a-4673-4b8f-dd31-b4d0bf911420.story_eng: Seta, meaning 'seat', is a large boulder at the western end of Langarimi. It is believed to have been carried here in an ice floe by a river flood. Around the turn of the last century it stood about two feet out of the ground, flat on top, and was thought to make an excellent seat. It has since sunk below the turf, though it can still be felt when the grass is mown.
31f88f9a-4673-4b8f-dd31-b4d0bf911420.story_is: Seta er steinn vestast í Langarima, nokkuð sunnan við Hólinn. Er það bjarg mikið sem mun hafa komið í jaka með árflóði. Um aldamótin síðustu stóð hann um tvö fet úr jörðu, sléttur að ofan, og þótti ágætt sæti. Nú er hann horfinn niður fyrir grassvörð en verður þó vart þegar slegið er.

31facd39-2627-4209-8de1-d0c8980e3c54.story_eng: A foal is said to have drowned in this creek, and that is how it got its name, which means 'foal creek'. A nearby rock is said to have been named after the same event. The creek carries water from the Ásamýrar marshes out into the river Jórvíkurá.
31facd39-2627-4209-8de1-d0c8980e3c54.story_is: Folald kvað hafa drukknað þar og fékk þá kíllinn nafn og kletturinn líka. Folaldakíll er afrennsli Ásamýranna út í Jórvíkurá.

31fc869e-82a8-f656-7740-db0ef9bf8d92.story_eng: Flassabakki takes its name from Jónas flassi, who lived at Fosssel and was allowed to mow the hay here. The bank lies just below the pond Pöddutjörn.
31fc869e-82a8-f656-7740-db0ef9bf8d92.story_is: Framan undir Pöddutjörn er Flassabakki. Þar fékk Jónas flassi, sem bjó í Fossseli, að slá. Af því er nafnið.

31ff9340-ae35-7d88-2196-fd9ca596171c.story_eng: Jónssker (Jón's skerry) is named after Jón Þór Þorbergsson, known as Nonni. A humorous verse is told about him: "Gloom is quick to come over me / when work must be done in a hurry. / But Nonni moved Fjörusker / and other notable places."
31ff9340-ae35-7d88-2196-fd9ca596171c.story_is: Skerið er nefnt eftir Jóni Þór Þorbergssyni (Nonna). Um hann var kveðið: Vill mjög sækja víl að mér / ef vinna á með hraði. / En Nonni færði Fjörusker / og fleiri merka staði.

32043860-3fde-2614-7160-98043dd18a0f.story_eng: Old fragments of ruins on the eastern side of Fjallstún, a short way above the road, mark the site of the farm Fjall. A large farmstead in the old style once stood here, and a metalsmith is said to have lived there. Fjallstún itself, the farm's former home field, is a hill that has been covered by landslides; only remnants of the field remain.
32043860-3fde-2614-7160-98043dd18a0f.story_is: Gömul tóftarbrot austanvert í Fjallstúni, skammt fyrir ofan veginn. Þar hefur verið mikill bær í fornum stíl og búið málmsmiður. Fjallstún er skriðurunnin hæð og þar eru leifar af túni bæjarins Fjalls.

320b1753-3c33-b28a-239d-dcae5f68293a.story_eng: There were fairly high sand banks and eroded turf edges here, and they were said to have played some part in local stories as a place for lovers' meetings at the time of the réttir, the autumn sheep round-ups. The banks have since been levelled, and the spot is now a hayfield.
320b1753-3c33-b28a-239d-dcae5f68293a.story_is: Þar voru allháir sandbakkar og rofabörð sem þóttu koma nokkuð við sögu sem staður til ástafunda um réttir. Bakkarnir hafa verið jafnaðir út og er þar nú tún.

3227c952-9a5c-a62d-71f9-4a3a8816f39d.story_eng: Seltorfa, west of the river Selá, was the site of a sel (a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked) belonging to the farm Raufarfell, in use from the Age of Settlement until around 1500 or 1600. It is a fairly large patch of grassland that had begun to erode, and much of the eroded ground has since been sown with grass. In the eroded ground on its western side, the remains of a building's walls can still be seen.
3227c952-9a5c-a62d-71f9-4a3a8816f39d.story_is: Seltorfa er vestan Selár. Þarna hefur verið sel frá Raufarfelli frá landnámsöld og fram til 1500 eða 1600. Þetta er nokkuð stór grastorfa sem var að blása upp, og hefur verið sáð í rofið að töluverðum hluta. Í rofinu að vestan má sjá leifar af húshleðslu.

322cd7c6-8c77-4875-b0fa-6e2e1f093884.story_eng: Arnbjörn is a hillock a little south and slightly east of another hillock called Þorkell. Two ancient men were said to be buried in these mounds: Arnbjörn was supposed to have a chest of gold, while Þorkell was said to lie buried in a ship. According to oral tradition, people once tried to dig into the mounds, but each time it seemed to them that the farmhouse was ablaze. Some years ago Þorkell was dug away completely and used for the road leading up to the farm. Nothing remarkable happened, and nothing was found.
322cd7c6-8c77-4875-b0fa-6e2e1f093884.story_is: Sunnar og aðeins austar en Þorkell er annar hóll, nefndur Arnbjörn. Sagt var að í hólum þessum væru heygðir tveir fornmenn. Átti Arnbjörn að hafa gullkistu, en Þorkell vera heygður í skipi. Munnmæli eru um að grafa hafi átt í þessa hóla, en mönnum sýnst bærinn standa í björtu báli. Fyrir nokkrum árum var Þorkell alveg mokaður upp og notaður í veginn heim að bænum. Ekkert markvert gerðist og ekkert fannst.

32381daa-7d93-8acd-c8fe-8520d0646f2a.story_eng: Borgarmýri is a marsh lying on the south side of the ridge Borgarás. Very old ruins stand in the marsh.
32381daa-7d93-8acd-c8fe-8520d0646f2a.story_is: Sunnan undir Borgarási er Borgarmýri og þar eru mjög gamlar rústir.

32463aaf-7c7d-446b-835f-8fd10c003d39.story_eng: Kofaholt, roughly "hut hill", is said to have been the site of an old shooting hut, a small shelter used for hunting, and some traces of it can still be seen. Old charcoal pits, where charcoal was once made, also lie nearby. The hill is just south of Kálfadalur, a little west of the line towards the farm.
32463aaf-7c7d-446b-835f-8fd10c003d39.story_is: Sagt er að á Kofaholti hafi verið gamall skotkofi og sjá má nokkur merki um hann. Þarna í nánd eru einnig gamlar kolagrafir. Holtið er rétt sunnan við Kálfadalinn, litlu vestar en í stefnu á bæinn.

325ce8b2-5af5-853a-6091-04842838b10a.story_eng: Krosshólmi is a small, 300-metre-long islet in the middle of the river, its northern end lying opposite the southern tip of Þingey. The ford here, Krosshólmavað, is believed to have been blessed by Guðmundur góði (Guðmundur the Good, a 13th-century bishop said to have blessed many springs and wells). It is not known whether the name, which contains the word kross (cross), comes from that. No livestock graze the islet at any time of year, so its plants are left undisturbed. On the gravel banks to the south and north grow river beauty, alpine meadow-grass and a plant locally called sandkoppablóm. Up on the islet, which stands fairly high, there are dwarf birch, woolly willow and juniper, with the odd tuft of tufted hair-grass, mat-grass in the hollows, alpine meadow-rue, moonwort and hawkweed. On the face of the bank grow sweet vernal grass and large lady's mantle.
325ce8b2-5af5-853a-6091-04842838b10a.story_is: Talið er að Guðmundur góði hafi vígt vaðið hér, Krosshólmavað, en ekki er vitað hvort nafnið er dregið af því. Krosshólmi, 300 m langur, er smásker í fljótinu miðju. Ysti endi hans nær á móts við syðsta enda Þingeyjar. Í Krosshólma er engin skepna allan ársins hring og gróður því verndaður. Á eyri sunnan og norðan á eru eyrarrósir, sandkoppablóm og fjallasveifgras. Uppi á hólmanum, sem er nokkuð hár, er hrís, loðvíðir og einir, einstaka snarrót, finnungur í lautum, brjóstgras, tungljurt og undafífill. Framan í bakkanum er ilmreyr og stórvaxinn maríustakkur.

326529a8-79d3-938c-b975-2b43b4e5f265.story_eng: Drangatindur is a high peak. According to legend, the keys to a chest of gold hidden beneath a certain waterfall are kept up on the peak. But whoever wishes to take them must know nothing of God.
326529a8-79d3-938c-b975-2b43b4e5f265.story_is: Hár tindur. Þar segir sagan að lyklar séu geymdir að gullkistu undir fossi nokkrum, en sá sem vill ná þeim má ekki vita neitt um Guð.

32654622-9fec-492f-ad89-101e984e2081.story_eng: This hill is also called Álaskyggnir, and that is probably the more correct name. Álfaskyggnir would suggest elves (álfar), but on both sides of the hill grassy channels (álar) run down into the slopes of Lyngdalsbrekkur. Shepherds probably climbed the hill to look out for sheep in these channels. A concrete pillar stands on the hill.
32654622-9fec-492f-ad89-101e984e2081.story_is: Hóllinn er einnig nefndur Álaskyggnir og líklega er það réttara nafn, því beggja vegna hans eru grasálar niður í Lyngdalsbrekkur. Smalar hafa líklega farið þar upp að skyggnast eftir fé í álunum. Steyptur stöpull er á Álaskyggni.

3297025e-01aa-82ef-0c8a-a013262413d0.story_eng: An elf woman lives in this hill, according to a tale in the folk-tale collection of Jón Árnason. In everyday speech the hill is usually called Hvasshóll.
3297025e-01aa-82ef-0c8a-a013262413d0.story_is: Álfkona býr í þessum hól, samanber frásögn í Þjóðsögum Jóns Árnasonar. Í daglegu tali er hóllinn jafnan nefndur Hvasshóll.

32a69a6b-48ad-18aa-884d-af6abb2b988f.name_eng: Heimarafstöð, remains of a home power station
32a69a6b-48ad-18aa-884d-af6abb2b988f.story_eng: This small home power station could produce electricity all year round, because the pond above it never froze. A channel carried the water down from the pond into the station. Árni Jónsson regularly went up to clear the strainer, mostly during spells of changeable weather, when plant matter or ice clogged it.
32a69a6b-48ad-18aa-884d-af6abb2b988f.story_is: Heimarafstöðin gat framleitt rafmagn allt árið vegna þess að ofar var lón sem aldrei fraus. Frá lóninu kom renna niður í rafstöðina sem vatnið rann um. Árni Jónsson fór reglulega þar upp og hreinsaði frá síunni. Það var aðallega við umhleypingar í veðri, þegar gróður eða klaki stíflaði sigtið.

32c1d6fd-96f1-3ad6-876d-420a8f1b52ec.story_eng: Neðri-Brattabrekka is the lower of two slopes called Brattabrekka, the upper and the lower, a name that means "steep slope" and was given because of how steep it is. Below Brattabrekka was a usual resting place for travellers. Those coming down from the mountain rested there to let their horses graze and to adjust the riding gear, and those about to set out over the mountain prepared themselves for the hardships that lay ahead.
32c1d6fd-96f1-3ad6-876d-420a8f1b52ec.story_is: Brattabrekka efri og neðri kallast svo vegna þess hve brött hún er. Undir Bröttubrekku var venjulegur hvíldarstaður ferðamanna. Þeir sem komu af fjalli hvíldu þar til þess að lofa hestum „að grípa niður“ og laga á þeim reiðfærin, og þeir sem voru að leggja í fjallið bjuggu sig undir erfiðleikana sem voru fram undan.

32ce9654-db42-21fa-74a7-f0653555d70e.story_eng: Borgarhólar are three small hillocks at the western edge of the bog, and the easternmost holds the remains of a fjárborg, a round stone-walled shelter for sheep. After Ófeigur Vigfússon of Fjall bought Framnes in the fourth decade of the 19th century, he kept between 20 and 30 wethers (castrated rams) there. The grazing could be excellent, but in frosty weather ice could form over the bog.
32ce9654-db42-21fa-74a7-f0653555d70e.story_is: Þrír smáhólar vestast í mýrinni og eru leifar af fjárborg í þeim austasta. Eftir að Ófeigur Vigfússon í Fjalli keypti Framnesið á fjórða tug nítjándu aldar hafði hann þar milli 20 og 30 sauði. Þarna gat verið hin ágætasta beit en í frostum gat lagst ís yfir mýrina.

32deaf01-48a5-e6af-0bbc-4159280fff75.story_eng: The story goes that during the years of the First World War, the islanders (Eyjamenn) were allowed to cut wood on the slope here and paid for it with fish, or tros (small, low-value fish), which was landed in this cove. The stream Hrökkálslækur flows into Trosvík.
32deaf01-48a5-e6af-0bbc-4159280fff75.story_is: Sagan segir að á fyrri stríðsárum hafi Eyjamenn fengið skógarhögg þarna í hlíðinni eða brekkunni og borgað með fiski eða trosi, sem hafi verið skipað þarna upp. Hrökkálslækur fellur í Trosvík.

32ee80fd-1f35-72c6-84a5-e0d1a259ef76.story_eng: The ruin of Langikofi, the "long hut", lies in the home field, east of the stream that runs east of the farm mound. The only body ever to have washed ashore here was laid out in this hut. A note added in 2016 says that a stable now stands on the spot.
32ee80fd-1f35-72c6-84a5-e0d1a259ef76.story_is: Í túninu er Langakofatóft, austan við lækinn austur af Bæjarhólnum. Í þessum kofa stóð uppi eina líkið sem rekið hefur. Nú er hér hesthús, árið 2016.

32f00650-c752-d8e9-5b2e-a3156dfc5308.story_eng: This bridge over the kíll, a narrow, slow-flowing channel west of the farm, was built around 1906 and has always been kept in repair. It was never called anything other than Brú, simply 'bridge'. Time and again there were near-accidents on it and beside it, though no one ever lost their life.
32f00650-c752-d8e9-5b2e-a3156dfc5308.story_is: Brúin á kílnum vestur af bæ var aldrei nefnd öðruvísi en Brú. Hún var gerð um 1906 og henni hefur ávallt verið haldið við. Af henni og við hana hefur hvað eftir annað legið við slysum, þó að ekki hafi orðið mannskaðar.

32f5370c-bf09-1b4d-5672-dddd81368c5c.story_eng: What the sisters from Hegrabjarg were told was the ancient farm Hegrastaðir is a rather small mound of ruins rising out of the moorland, a short way east of the main road. Just over 40 m to the north, the outline of another ruin can be made out. The settlement-era farm Hegrastaðir, dating from the time Iceland was first settled, is thus said to lie in two different places, and the old description makes no attempt to explain why.
32f5370c-bf09-1b4d-5672-dddd81368c5c.story_is: Það sem Hegrabjargssystrum var sagt að væri fornbýlið Hegrastaðir er fremur lítill rústahóll upp úr móum, spöl austan þjóðvegarins. Rúmum 40 m norðar mótar fyrir annarri tóft. Landnámsbýlið Hegrastaðir er þannig á tveimur stöðum, en ekki hefur verið reynt að ráða í hvernig á því stendur.

330978f7-1927-4a46-b298-97c8ebd56d2f.story_eng: Lestavað, whose name means 'pack-train ford', is a ford across the river Laxá, straight out from Horn. It was a common crossing for travellers from the inland districts heading to Blönduós by way of Húnsstaðasandur, and people spoke of 'going at Hornið'. From the ford the route followed the river up on its north side, to about where a road was later built. There it turned north and passed above the marsh, roughly where the old national road ran.
330978f7-1927-4a46-b298-97c8ebd56d2f.story_is: Vað í Laxá beint út frá Horni, algeng leið til Blönduóss fyrir ferðamenn úr framsveitum sem fóru um Húnsstaðasand. Var talað um að fara á Horninu. Leiðin lá svo upp með ánni að norðan, upp undir þar sem vegur kom síðar, og þar var beygt til norðurs og farið ofan við flóann, u.þ.b. þar sem gamli þjóðvegurinn lá.

331002cd-2074-e8af-d0bf-34c4d6c3bb6c.story_eng: Sellækir are the small streams that run on either side of the place known as Sel, where the farm Brú had its beitarhús (a sheep house out in the grazing land). It is said that the gravel banks along the river here were once all grassy land, and that the area may have been called Fagranes, a name that lives on in nearby names such as Fagrimelur and Fagramelslækur.
331002cd-2074-e8af-d0bf-34c4d6c3bb6c.story_is: Sitt hvoru megin við Selið eru smálækir sem nefnast Sellækir. Almennt er talað um Sel, en þar voru beitarhús frá Brú. Sagt er að eyrarnar hér með ánni hafi allar verið gróið land og ef til vill hafi þar heitið Fagranes, sem lifir í nöfnum, en utar með ánni eru Fagramelslækur og Fagrimelur, melhorn niður við ána.

33546cab-163c-ee97-e655-6c713785cd5f.story_eng: Djöflakamrar, a name beginning with the word for devils, was once a continuous stretch of rushes lying between two strips of sedge, Sultarlangsflaga and Lambatangaflaga. The ground beneath was bad, a sticky clay mire, and the area was hard to work. That is probably why it was given its name. The rushes have since disappeared entirely, and the sedge has spread in from both sides, so that in some places the two strips now meet.
33546cab-163c-ee97-e655-6c713785cd5f.story_is: Á milli Sultarlangsflögu og Lambatangaflögu er alllangt bil, og var allt þetta bil áður samfelld sefflaga. Var þar vondur botn (leirkesja) og erfitt að vinna, og mun sú vera ástæða til þess að sefflaga þessi var nefnd Djöflakamrar. Nú er allt sefið horfið, en störin hefur teygt sig fram frá báðum hliðum, svo að nú nær hún saman sums staðar.

335a5be8-4308-c0ee-0516-92b4b493b138.story_eng: Byrgi was the hut of the ferrymen who carried travellers across Vesturós, where the western branch of the Héraðsvötn river meets the sea. A cable ferry crossed here, about 50 metres north of the rock that the bridge now rests on, from 1892 until the bridge was finished in 1925. The ferrymen called their shelter Byrgi, and sometimes Byrgishvammur. The place was thought to be haunted while the ferrymen were there. Lights were often seen in the cliffs above Byrgi, mostly by people coming from the west. In those cliffs was a small ledge called Meyjarsæti (the maiden's seat), with room for perhaps two people. It probably disappeared when the rock above the hut was blasted away and the stone used for the wings of the bridge. The last ferryman was Hróbjartur Jónasson, who worked the ferry from 1922 to 1925 and built his shelter in 1923 a few metres north of the rock, where earlier ferrymen's huts had stood. His hut was rebuilt in the autumn of 1996.
335a5be8-4308-c0ee-0516-92b4b493b138.story_is: Ferjumenn sem fluttu fólk yfir Vesturós, þar sem vestari kvísl Héraðsvatna fellur til sjávar, höfðu hér kofa sem þeir nefndu Byrgi og kölluðu stundum Byrgishvamm. Um 50 metrum norður frá Ósakletti, sem brúin yfir Ósinn liggur af, var svifferja á Ósnum um 30 ára bil, frá 1892 þar til brúarsmíði lauk árið 1925 og dragferjan var aflögð. Reimt þótti við Ósinn þegar ferjumennirnir voru þar. Það sáust oft ljós í klettunum fyrir ofan Byrgið og sáu það einkum menn sem komu vestan frá. Í klettunum ofan við kofann var smástallur sem kallaður var Meyjarsæti. Þar var líklega sæti fyrir tvo, varla meira pláss. Hann mun hafa horfið við sprengingar þegar kletturinn ofan við Byrgið var sprengdur niður og grjótið notað í brúarvængina. Hróbjartur Jónasson var síðasti ferjumaður við Vesturós, á árunum 1922–1925, og byggði sér skýli árið 1923 nokkrum metrum norðan við Ósklett þar sem fyrri ferjumannsskýli höfðu staðið. Haustið 1996 var kofi Hróbjartar byggður upp.

3364d235-d0ad-ba0b-7546-92ffffea77f7.story_eng: Hulduklettur, the hidden people's rock, stands at the lower end of the Selmýri bog. Huldufólk (hidden people) are said to have lived here well into recent times. They helped their neighbours with the keeping of the sheep, in return for the kindness shown to them. Once, for example, while they had no milk, they were allowed to milk Forystugrána, a grey lead ewe. It was always the housewife who milked her. One time, while the farm's housewife was away, she had forbidden anyone to milk Grána. The girl who milked the ewes in the fold disobeyed and milked her anyway. The next day, as she was heating the milk, she spilled it on herself and was badly burned. Another autumn, when sheep were buried in snow far and wide, not a single animal from the farm Þverá was lost in the drifts. Many more such examples could be told.
3364d235-d0ad-ba0b-7546-92ffffea77f7.story_is: Neðst við Selmýrina er svonefndur Hulduklettur. Þar hefur huldufólk búið allt fram á okkar daga. Veitti það nágrönnum sínum ýmsa þjónustu við fjárgeymslu, sem var endurgjald fyrir hjálpsemi því til handa. Eitt sinn fékk það til dæmis að mjólka Forystugránu meðan það var mjólkurlaust. Það var ávallt húsfreyja sem mjólkaði hana. Eitt sinn var það í fjarveru húsmóður, sem hafði bannað að Grána yrði mjólkuð, að stúlka sú sem mjólkaði kvíaærnar brást því boði og mjólkaði Gránu. En daginn eftir, þegar hún flóaði mjólkina, hellti hún á sig og skaðbrenndist. Eitt haust, þegar fé fennti víða, fennti enga skepnu frá Þverá, og svo mætti lengi telja.

33767a09-5043-cd56-16f6-cc12fe19209b.story_eng: This marsh takes its name from the coast guard vessel Óðinn (the small one). Its crew were allowed to gather Arctic tern eggs here, and they combed through the nesting ground so thoroughly that a tern has never been seen in the marsh since.
33767a09-5043-cd56-16f6-cc12fe19209b.story_is: Skipverjar á varðskipinu Óðni (litla) fengu að tína kríuegg í mýrinni og fínkembdu varpið svo að þar hefur aldrei sést kría síðan.

337ca94c-51f0-23ea-d53b-2eff5a5585ec.story_eng: In the valley of Mjóidalur, a little south of the river Grjótá, lie the ruins of the farm Mjóidalur. It was a hjáleiga, a small dependent farm, belonging to Mýri, and it was abandoned in 1894. When the farm was built, it was raised on older ruins, where a place called Mjóadalskot is mentioned in 1712. The valley itself, through which the river Mjóadalsá flows, is the westernmost and northernmost part of the common highland pasture.
337ca94c-51f0-23ea-d53b-2eff5a5585ec.story_is: Í Mjóadal, aðeins sunnan Grjótár, eru rústir eftir býlið Mjóadal, sem var hjáleiga frá Mýri. Mjóidalur fór í eyði 1894. Þegar þetta býli var byggt var það byggt á tóftum þar sem 1712 er nefnt Mjóadalskot. Mjóidalur er vestasti og nyrsti hluti afréttarinnar og eftir honum rennur Mjóadalsá.

338638ca-52ab-69d9-0c2f-9c7749fc3b7a.story_eng: Rjúkandahylur is a pool in the river beside Undirlendi, a strip of grassland down by the riverbank. It was said that the river froze over quickly here. The name means 'steaming pool'.
338638ca-52ab-69d9-0c2f-9c7749fc3b7a.story_is: Í ánni við Undirlendi, gróðurræmu niður við ána, er Rjúkandahylur. Þar var sagt að ána legði fljótt.

33910404-ff9b-ba04-054a-a0ceec770fce.story_eng: Skarðsgötur, also called Þegjandadalsgötur, is a footpath that runs beside Þorgerðarfjallshorn and on south onto Hryggir. It is part of the Prestgötur, the 'priests' paths', which run from Grenjaðarstaður to Þverá.
33910404-ff9b-ba04-054a-a0ceec770fce.story_is: Með Þorgerðarfjallshorni liggja Þegjandadalsgötur eða Skarðsgötur, um Stekkjargrund og suður á Hryggi. Þær eru hluti Prestsgatna sem ná frá Grenjaðarstað í Þverá.

33b820cc-5905-0140-9651-8ec0f4bec0d6.story_eng: Bárðarfall is a smooth, level patch of grassland just north of Þröngagata. The farmer of Ytra-Skeið, who had fallen, is said to have been buried in a cairn here. The name means "Bárður's Fall".
33b820cc-5905-0140-9651-8ec0f4bec0d6.story_is: Norðan við Þröngagötu er sléttur flötur sem heitir Bárðarfall. Þar á að hafa verið dysjaður bóndinn á Ytra-Skeiði sem hafði fallið.

33bab2c0-aa91-7e35-9ff7-2165d1bdd2ce.story_eng: Hjallhólar are rocky hills with sand lying between them. According to the grandmother of the person who described the place, huldufólk (hidden people) lived here.
33bab2c0-aa91-7e35-9ff7-2165d1bdd2ce.story_is: Hjallhólar eru klettahólar og sandur á milli. Þar bjó huldufólk, að sögn ömmu heimildarmanns.

33cb6d85-4c88-d3de-df0c-3de43d4a15d6.story_eng: According to Landnáma, the medieval Book of Settlements, a son of Grímur Grímólfsson of Agðir is said to have spent his first winter here, at the time he settled Tjörnes between the rivers Tunguá and Ós. The remains of this abandoned farm lie just southeast of Efri-Reiðdalur, right beside the main road on its east side. The site was protected in 1930.
33cb6d85-4c88-d3de-df0c-3de43d4a15d6.story_is: Samkvæmt Landnámu á son Gríms Grímólfssonar af Ögðum, landnámsmaður, að hafa dvalið á Böðólfsstöðum sinn fyrsta vetur, er hann nam Tjörnes milli Tunguár og Óss. Eyðibýlið er örskammt suðaustur af Efri-Reiðdal, fast við þjóðveginn að austan. Böðólfsstaðir voru friðlýstir árið 1930.

33d53b8f-2752-6891-1e7f-b83574fac08f.story_eng: Þrengsli, meaning "the narrows", is a grassy hollow or small grassy valley in the lava, worn with deep track ruts. In former times this was in effect the main road from Kílhraun south out of the lava field. There was no other way out of the lava, but this route made a reasonable road for horses. The track ran south from the old milking pen (stöðull) north of Ærhúsflóð.
33d53b8f-2752-6891-1e7f-b83574fac08f.story_is: Þrengslin eru graslaut eða grasdalur með götuskorningum í hrauninu sem farið var eftir og voru eiginlega þjóðvegurinn frá Kílhrauni og suður úr hrauninu áður fyrr. Ekki var hægt að komast út úr hrauninu annars staðar, en þetta var sæmilegur vegur fyrir hesta. Gatan lá frá gamla stöðlinum norðan við Ærhúsflóðið og suður úr.

33e4f825-7f65-4960-aabf-8cba1428686b.story_eng: Merkiklöpp is the outermost part of Rauðuklappir, the rocks from which the landslide Merkiskriða fell. A merlin often nested here, and sometimes a raven. The outcrop lies at the foot of a slope on the boundary with the farm Hafralækur, and the name means "boundary rock".
33e4f825-7f65-4960-aabf-8cba1428686b.story_is: Yst í Rauðuklöppum, sem Merkiskriða féll fram af, er Merkiklöpp. Þar átti smyrill oft hreiður, en hrafn stundum. Klöppin er neðst í brekku á merkjum móti Hafralæk.

33efb4de-4aba-9020-c57b-c329e02f1bcd.story_eng: Nýhús, meaning 'New House', stood in the south-west corner of the land. It began as a small hut built before the time of the farmer known in the record as Kr.J. He enlarged it to hold 25 to 30 lambs, and that is probably when it got its name. Later Ásm.Kr. enlarged the buildings again. At the time of the description it was a house for about 70 to 80 sheep, with two feeding troughs and a manger along the eastern gable. Beside it was a hay barn holding about 60 horse-loads of hay. The house no longer stands.
33efb4de-4aba-9020-c57b-c329e02f1bcd.story_is: Nýhús var nefnt í suðvesturhorninu og var byggt fyrir daga Kr.J. Þar var kofi, en Kr.J. stækkaði hann svo að hann tók 25–30 lömb, og þá mun nafnið hafa komist á. Síðar stækkaði Ásm.Kr. húsin, og var það þá orðið um 70–80 kinda hús með tveimur görðum og jötu fyrir austurstafni. Við það var hlaða sem tók um 60 hesta. Húsið er nú horfið.

340e9813-ed71-1468-9ccf-202b2787c899.story_eng: Þorleifshóll was a fairly large mound, named after a man said to have been buried there in a burial mound. The mound has since been dug away, and only a low rise remains in the hayfield.
340e9813-ed71-1468-9ccf-202b2787c899.story_is: Hóllinn ber nafn sitt af manni sem þar er sagður heygður. Hann var allstór og var norður af Tóttum en var mokaður út og er nú bali í túninu.

3410e907-b38b-7e1f-fddf-428ff476d8c5.story_eng: Göngudalur is a small, narrow valley cutting up through Fellin, with steep gravel slopes on both sides. The old road to Siglufjörður once ran up through the valley itself; today the Siglufjörður road climbs onto Fellin at the valley mouth, usually called Göngudalskjaftur. The valley is still walked in winter, and that is where its name comes from: Göngudalur means roughly "walking valley".
3410e907-b38b-7e1f-fddf-428ff476d8c5.story_is: Upp í gegnum Fellin skerst lítill og mjór dalur sem heitir Göngudalur og eru brattir melar beggja vegna að honum. Mynni dalsins kallast venjulega Göngudalskjaftur og þar liggur Siglufjarðarvegurinn upp á Fellin, en áður lá hann upp Göngudalinn. Enn er dalurinn genginn á vetrum og hefur hann nafn af því.

341a95d4-bc57-664d-ec87-ccdc2cf7dee4.story_eng: Neðrahraun, the lower lava field, stretches from Kaupstaðavegur, the road to the trading place, down to Kleif. In its southern part is a ridge called Háikambur. North of it lies Byrgi, a shelter where trout were kept in storage in the old days. Northeast of Byrgi, west of the ford Sauðavað, are Sauðavaðsborgir, and close by are a cave, Sauðavaðsborgarhellir, and a fox den, Sauðavaðsborgargreni.
341a95d4-bc57-664d-ec87-ccdc2cf7dee4.story_is: Neðrahraun kallast hraunið frá Kaupstaðavegi og niður að Kleif. Syðst í því er kambur sem kallast Háikambur. Norðan hans er Byrgi þar sem silungur var hafður í geymslu í gamla daga. Norðaustur af Byrginu og vestur af Sauðavaði eru Sauðavaðsborgir og þar hjá eru Sauðavaðsborgarhellir og Sauðavaðsborgargreni.

34338080-c10a-ae6a-098f-964cac69d718.story_eng: This small stone-built turf hut, about 7 m² in floor area, is the oldest farm building in Iceland. Hesthúsið á Hólum, the stable at Hólar, has stood with its roof on and in use since 1650. For most of that time it served as a cowshed in summer and a stable for horses in winter, and later it became a smokehouse.
34338080-c10a-ae6a-098f-964cac69d718.story_is: Hesthúsið á Hólum er elsta hús á Íslandi til búskaparnota. Það er steinhlaðinn torfkofi, um 7 m² að gólffleti, og hefur staðið með þaki og í notkun síðan 1650. Lengst af var það sumarfjós en hesthús að vetrum, en síðar reykkofi.

3442eb1e-3213-7314-5416-50fcfc2257ff.story_eng: Námustallur, 'the mine ledge', was blasted into the rock face at Tungunáman, a mine above the middle of the cove. During the First World War the national treasury (landssjóður) ran a large coal-mining operation here. From the ledge, the mine tunnels, Námugöngin, led into the bank. A little south of it and somewhat lower is Smiðjutótt, the ruin of the mine's ironsmithy. The mining produced a great deal of waste, which was carted out on rail wagons and piled up out into the sea. The heap caught fire and burned for two to three years. It is called Námuhaugur and is being worn away by the sea.
3442eb1e-3213-7314-5416-50fcfc2257ff.story_is: Upp úr miðri víkinni var Tungunáman. Þar var mikil kolavinnsla á vegum landssjóðs á heimsstyrjaldarárunum fyrri. Þar var sprengdur stallur í bergið, Námustallur. Af honum lágu Námugöngin inn í bakkann. Sunnan hans en nokkuð lægra er Smiðjutótt. Þar stóð járnsmiðja námunnar. Mikill úrgangur losnaði við kolavinnsluna og var honum ekið út á sporvögnum, og hlóðst hann upp fram í sjó. Í honum kviknaði og var eldur þar uppi í 2–3 ár. Hann er nú nefndur Námuhaugur og eyðist óðum af sjógangi.

344df3b3-dfa7-1bc6-e291-b989589ecde6.story_eng: Innrihæð and its neighbour Ytri-hæð are the two highest points on the ridge Selásinn, lying some distance apart around the middle of the ridge. Kristbjörg recalled that when the sheep were being rounded up, she and the other children were made to stand on these heights to block the animals' way.
344df3b3-dfa7-1bc6-e291-b989589ecde6.story_is: Tveir hæstu punktarnir á Selásnum heita Ytri-hæð og Innri-hæð. Þær eru um miðjan ásinn með nokkru millibili. Kristbjörg segir að þau krakkarnir hafi verið látin standa fyrir á þessum hæðum þegar verið var að smala.

34612b60-ee73-4c23-9812-1aa3096babf4.story_eng: Grásteinn, whose name means 'grey stone', is said to be a dwelling place of huldufólk, the hidden people of Icelandic folk belief who are thought to live unseen in rocks and hills.

34624c94-0ad5-63ff-8817-6df69ad9f85a.story_eng: Gullhóll means "toy hill", from gull, an old word for a child's toy. The historian Bogi Th. Melsteð told the collector that the hillock was given this name in his father's time at Klausturhólar, because his father's children played there with their toys. It lies near the farmyard, on the boundary between Klausturhólar and Hólakot.
34624c94-0ad5-63ff-8817-6df69ad9f85a.story_is: Bogi Th. Melsteð sagnfræðingur sagði að hólnum hefði verið gefið þetta nafn í tíð föður hans í Klausturhólum, af því að börn hans léku sér þar með gullin sín. Gullhóll er skammt frá hlaðinu, austan og ofan við Hundakrók, og er í mörkum milli Klausturhóla og Hólakots.

34638f88-69f6-c9e6-ec4f-cea8665acac2.story_eng: Sturlulág is a grassy hollow on the southern part of Hólmaberg, where the boundary between the farms Kárastaðir and Hróarsdalur runs across. It is said to take its name from a man called Sturla, one of the thieves who lived in Grendalir. He is said to have been chased from there and either ran off the cliff here or was killed. In the stony scree in the hollow there is said to have been an old fox den (tófugren), though little can be seen of it now.
34638f88-69f6-c9e6-ec4f-cea8665acac2.story_is: Á Hólmabergi sunnanverðu er graslægð sem merki Kárastaða og Hróarsdals liggja yfir og heitir Sturlulág. Hún á að draga nafn af manni sem Sturla hét. Var hann einn af þjófum þeim sem héldu til í Grendölum og átti að hafa verið eltur þaðan utan að og hlaupið þarna fram af berginu eða verið drepinn. Í Sturlulág átti að vera gamalt tófugren í grjóturð sem þar er, en sést lítið fyrir nú.

348c4ee2-a21a-b4d5-4b93-b46daac75f23.story_eng: Lákatangi is a spit of land on the shore of Botnsvatn, below the Stórurð scree. Together with nearby Lákaeyri, it is named after Þorlákur Guðnason, who lived for many years at Braut in Húsavík and later emigrated to North America.
348c4ee2-a21a-b4d5-4b93-b46daac75f23.story_is: Lákatangi er við Botnsvatn niður undan Stórurð. Hann og Lákaeyri eru kennd við Þorlák Guðnason, er lengi bjó í Braut á Húsavík, en flutti síðar til Vesturheims.

349276f1-a36e-e8fe-1597-5e5a9ad7007d.story_eng: Millstones once turned here, driven by water from the river Núpsá, and the channel that carried the water to the mill can still be seen. The mill itself is gone. The person who recorded the description vaguely remembered remains of stone walling where the mill probably stood, likely from before 1970.
349276f1-a36e-e8fe-1597-5e5a9ad7007d.story_is: Hér hafa verið myllusteinar knúnir með vatni úr Núpsá og sést enn skurðurinn sem vatnið var leitt eftir. Myllan er horfin, en skrásetjari man óljóst eftir leifum af hleðslu þar sem hún stóð líklega, sennilega fyrir 1970.

34960a8c-214a-20af-9d6f-33443ac4755f.story_eng: Here stood the wool-working house (tóvinnuhús) of Magnús Þórarinsson, a two-storey timber building. It was the first of its kind in Iceland since Innréttingar, the 18th-century workshops founded by Skúli Magnússon. Wool was carded and processed here from 1882–1883 until the house burned down in 1923. The machinery was driven by an overshot water wheel in the stream Fjóslækur. Wool from the district and from further afield was worked here. The building no longer exists.
34960a8c-214a-20af-9d6f-33443ac4755f.story_is: Þarna stóð tóvinnuhús Magnúsar Þórarinssonar, tvílyft timburhús, það fyrsta á landinu eftir Innréttingar Skúla Magnússonar. Ull var kembd og unnin þar frá 1882–1883, þar til húsið brann árið 1923. Yfirfallshjól í Fjóslæk knúði vélar verksmiðjunnar. Ull úr héraði og víðar að var unnin í Tóvinnuhúsinu.

34b0ba45-fcd7-4040-5e27-6b05976de916.story_eng: Kvíabrún is a terrace just above the home field of Hallbjarnarstaðir, below the higher slope of Neðstabrún. A kví was a pen where ewes were gathered to be milked. Tryggvi, who gave the account, did not know the name Kvíabrún himself, but such pens stood at nearby Kvíaból, where old ruins of buildings could still be seen. At that time Hallbjarnarstaðir was still a single farm, before it was later divided. Tryggvi remembered the pens at Kvíaból from when he was a small child; after that the ewes were milked in the sheep houses.
