It has a particularly good seat where the elves sit. Its door faces east, where there is a deep cleft in the rock. According to the place-name record, the hill no longer exists.
3c3d00ec-bf16-f33e-7ef0-26b6f9876cb2.story_is: Strokkhóll er huldufólkshóll í miðjum Vellinum við vegamótin. Í honum á að hafa heyrst strokkhljóð. Í laginu er hann ekki ósvipaður kirkju með tveimur turnum og er sá eystri hærri. Þar er einkar gott sæti, þar sem álfarnir sitja. Dyrnar snúa mót austri og er þar djúp klettaglufa. Hóllinn er nú horfinn.

3c463f80-b0a0-b049-ed74-5296cfa5a100.story_eng: Sóleyjarfletir is a stretch of smooth, flat grassy patches, a piece of meadowland where the ground has been cleared. The name means roughly "buttercup flats". There is warmth in the ground here, and later a borehole was drilled for hot water with good results. A pump house was built over the borehole, and a road and a pipeline were laid from here east to the school at Hafralækjarskóli.
3c463f80-b0a0-b049-ed74-5296cfa5a100.story_is: Sóleyjarfletir eru sléttir balar milli Stóramós og Skriðunnar, þar sem hefur hreinsað úr. Þar er ylur í jörð og var síðar borað eftir heitu vatni með góðum árangri. Byggt var dæluhús yfir holuna og vegur og leiðsla lögð þaðan austur í Hafralækjarskóla.

3c4b6f61-065d-47f2-8198-95660d6f08b8.story_eng: Krummasteinn, whose name means 'raven stone' (krummi is a common Icelandic word for raven), no longer exists. Around 1980 the slope where it lay was bulldozed to make it workable by machine, and the stone was buried in the process.
3c4b6f61-065d-47f2-8198-95660d6f08b8.story_is: Þegar brekkunni var ýtt fram um 1980 til að gera hana véltæka, þá var Krummasteinn dysjaður.

3c4ed738-f1a8-4c46-a8e2-de519992b1ca.story_eng: In the upper of the Tröllaskarð passes, Skít-Oddur killed the troll-woman Birna, who lived in Birnufell. The name means "trolls' pass", and people always speak of the passes in the plural.
3c4ed738-f1a8-4c46-a8e2-de519992b1ca.story_is: Í efra Tröllaskarðinu drap Skít-Oddur skessuna Birnu sem bjó í Birnufelli. Alltaf er talað um skörðin í fleirtölu.

3c6b7873-8daf-b368-dcc1-625147a1d7af.story_eng: Rekstraralda was a gravel ridge that once ran from southwest to northeast. Sheep were driven along it to graze on the gravel flats, and that is where the name comes from: rekstur means the driving of livestock. The ridge is now gone. According to the description, it had disappeared some 40 years before the description was written.
3c6b7873-8daf-b368-dcc1-625147a1d7af.story_is: Rekstraralda var melalda sem lá áður norður frá suðvestri til norðausturs, en hún er nú horfin; hún hvarf fyrir 40 árum. Eftir henni var fé rekið til beitar í melinn og er nafnið af því dregið.

3c7ac6d4-1514-0b10-95c4-12becb2b28a4.story_eng: Neðri-Jónskrókur is the lower of two grassy but uneven nooks known together as Jónskrókar, lying south and southeast of Stekkjargrund. They are named after Guðjón Jónsson, who had them for mowing hay when he lived here in húsmennska, as a lodger on the farm without land of his own.
3c7ac6d4-1514-0b10-95c4-12becb2b28a4.story_is: Sunnan og suðaustan við Stekkjargrundina eru Jónskrókar, Efri- og Neðri-, grasgefnir og ósléttir. Jónskrókar eru kenndir við Guðjón Jónsson sem hafði þá til slægna þegar hann var í húsmennsku hér.

3c96e4ff-b0bf-732a-e7eb-79fd8e06d17c.story_eng: Hólmi is a fairly large area rising above Engidal and the river Hólmaá, reaching up to Kvísl and Lagsá. Kvísl is a channel that runs from the river Laxá over into Hólmsá and sometimes floods into it when the water is high. Because of this, people spoke of having to ride across the river twice there, since it was otherwise impassable if it had to be crossed in one go.
3c96e4ff-b0bf-732a-e7eb-79fd8e06d17c.story_is: Hólmi er upp af Engidal og Hólmaá, allstórt svæði sem nær upp að Kvísl og Lagsá. Kvísl er læna sem liggur úr Laxá yfir í Hólmsá og hleypur stundum í hana í vatnavöxtum. Þess vegna var talað um að þurfa að ríða ána þar tvívegis, því að hún var annars ófær ef fara þurfti hana í einu lagi.

3cac1874-e8e6-567e-84b1-b840321d7eb1.story_eng: Kofi ("hut") is the name of a ruin on the boundary with the farm Hlíðskógar. The remains are believed to be those of a goat shed, and the piece of land around it is called Geitakofastykki, the goat-shed plot. It is said that the goats here lay in the open, and that whoever tended the sheep at the beitarhús (a sheep house out in the grazing land) at Hlíðskógar would stop by here on the same round.
3cac1874-e8e6-567e-84b1-b840321d7eb1.story_is: Kofi heita rústir á merkjum móti Hlíðskógum, og eru merkin sunnan við hann. Er talið að þar séu leifar eftir geitakofa. Stykkið í kringum hann heitir Geitakofastykki. Sagt er að geiturnar þarna hafi legið fyrir opnu en að sá sem sinnti fé á beitarhúsunum í Hlíðskógum hafi komið við þarna um leið.

3ccc5796-a4d1-4708-ee12-8c0c42102c60.story_eng: Gepilsfit is a grassy patch beside the brook Gepilslækur, next to Gepilsmór. All the Gepils- names are said to come from an old woman who lost a spoon in the brook and complained loudly about her lost "gepill".
3ccc5796-a4d1-4708-ee12-8c0c42102c60.story_is: Gepilsfit er við Gepilslæk og þar hjá er Gepilsmór. Gepilsnöfnin eru þannig til komin að kerling ein týndi spæni í lækinn og fáraðist mikið yfir geplinum sínum.

3ceb72c9-472c-f55c-e8d5-c43b7c4a1daa.story_eng: Hidden people (huldufólk) are said to live on the slopes of Búðarbrekkur, on the south and east side of Þórðarhöfði. According to the story, the farmer from Þrastarstaðir came here when he was on his way to Hofsós, and a hidden-folk merchant gave him an exceptionally beautiful silk scarf as a bonus with his purchase.
3ceb72c9-472c-f55c-e8d5-c43b7c4a1daa.story_is: Sunnan og austan á Þórðarhöfða eru Búðarbrekkur. Þar á að búa huldufólk. Þangað kom, segir sagan, bóndinn frá Þrastarstöðum, sem ætlaði í Hofsós, og fékk að kaupbæti forkunnarfallegan silkiklút hjá huldukaupmanni.

3d0e71f9-9374-03b9-8820-26bba0930863.story_eng: Klauf is a narrow inlet between flat coastal rocks in the middle of Kollsvíkurver, a fishing station, and it can only be seen at low tide. At high tide boats could land straight onto the sand, but at low tide or when the sea was low the ground under the keel was not always as soft, except here in this narrow cove between the rocks, Klaufin.
3d0e71f9-9374-03b9-8820-26bba0930863.story_is: Vik milli hleina í miðju Kollsvíkurveri, sem er ekki sýnilegt nema um fjöru. Um flóð var lent upp í sand, en um fjöru, eða þegar lágsjávað var, var stundum ekki eins mjúkt undir kili, nema í þessu þrönga viki milli hleina, Klaufinni.

3d1f7898-2f4f-d0c6-1d90-40851ba8c178.story_eng: The name Huldukonuklettur means "hidden woman's rock", a huldukona being a woman of the huldufólk (hidden people). Between the rock and the stream lay a grassy álagablettur, a spot under a spell or taboo, and it was always left unmown.
3d1f7898-2f4f-d0c6-1d90-40851ba8c178.story_is: Milli klettsins og lækjarins var grasgefinn álagablettur sem látinn var ósleginn.

3d3d27a8-cb2d-4266-a8e2-c6837943b575.story_eng: The name means Mill Brook. A boundary agreement signed in 1915 between the farms Kirkjuból and Lönd included a special clause: Kristján Þorsteinsson was allowed to leave his hut, and the water mill standing close by it, untouched for as long as he lived, entirely free of charge. That mill was presumably in this brook. In earlier times the boundary between Kirkjuból and Lönd was reckoned by Myllulækur.
3d3d27a8-cb2d-4266-a8e2-c6837943b575.story_is: Í undirrituðum landamerkjasamningi á milli Kirkjubóls og Landa árið 1915 fylgir þessi klausa: „Þá er og Kristjáni (Þorsteinssyni) heimilað að láta kofann og vatnsmyllu er stendur þar rétt hjá, standa óhreyft, á meðan hann lifir, allt endurgjaldslaust.“ Væntanlega er þar átt við vatnsmyllu í Myllulæknum. Áður voru landamerki á milli Kirkjubóls og Landa miðuð við Myllulækinn.

3d7332d9-4db1-4265-8d77-8bd0fba7420e.story_eng: Fossvegur runs from the Stórafoss reservoir, along the foot of the hill Kollhóll, down to the Gamla Stífla (the Old Dam). The penstock of the power plant, the pipe that carries water down to the turbines, is buried in the road. Its route passes the settlements of huldufólk (hidden people) in Brattakinn, which lies on the other side of the river Skarðsá.
3d7332d9-4db1-4265-8d77-8bd0fba7420e.story_is: Frá Stórafosslóninu liggur Fossvegur neðst í Kollhólnum niður að Gömlu stíflunni. Fallpípa virkjunarinnar er grafin niður í Fossveginn. Leið fallpípunnar liggur fram hjá byggðum huldufólks í Bröttukinn sem er handan Skarðsár.

3d845321-f5d2-bf30-c91e-6372d6352269.story_eng: Krókáll is a pool in the river, southwest of the skerry Sandsker, and an old salmon-netting spot. A seine net was drawn here to catch salmon, and it took two boats to haul it.
3d845321-f5d2-bf30-c91e-6372d6352269.story_is: Suðvestur af Sandskeri er í ánni Krókáll, gamall laxadráttur. Hann var dreginn með tveimur bátum.

3dba850e-4776-49af-a3d1-819eb0c51418.story_eng: Grásteinn, the 'grey stone', is a dwelling place of huldufólk (hidden people), the unseen beings of Icelandic folk belief.

3dc6a6f3-55bd-4779-945b-5789ae0fd7bc.story_eng: Beitarhúsalækur, also called Ytri-Grófarlækur, takes its name from the beitarhús (a sheep house out in the grazing land) that it flows past. These sheep houses were abandoned in 1936. Shortly before 1900, about 90 sheep were buried by snow in the streambed just below Víðihjalli, and all of them died.
3dc6a6f3-55bd-4779-945b-5789ae0fd7bc.story_is: Lækurinn dregur nafn sitt af beitarhúsum sem hann rennur fram hjá. Þessi beitarhús voru aflögð 1936. Skömmu fyrir aldamótin 1900 fennti um 90 kindur í lækjarfarveginum rétt neðan við Víðihjalla og drápust þær allar.

3dd4a13e-0054-47f8-04bd-5a376a6767b1.story_eng: According to the story, the bishop always took water for himself from this spring. Gvendarbrunnur rises in the home field a short way out from and below the church at Hólar. Its name means Gvendur's Well; Gvendur is a familiar form of Guðmundur, a name linked to Guðmundur góði (Guðmundur the Good, a 13th-century bishop said to have blessed many springs and wells).
3dd4a13e-0054-47f8-04bd-5a376a6767b1.story_is: Heima í túni, skammt fyrir utan og neðan Hólakirkju, er uppsprettulind sem heitir Gvendarbrunnur. Sagan segir að þar hafi biskup ætíð tekið vatn handa sjálfum sér.

3de17d8d-4c1b-c9fc-2bbf-1e39b9d7e385.story_eng: Saxa is a sea spout, a narrow cleft and pool in the rocks that acts like a grinder. Seawater mixed with chopped-up seaweed is forced through the narrow passage and a round hole in the rocks, shooting high into the air and up onto land, especially in a strong north-easterly wind. The name means "the chopper", from the common verb saxa, to chop.
3de17d8d-4c1b-c9fc-2bbf-1e39b9d7e385.story_is: Sjávarhver, kvörn eða hylur í klettunum. Þar spýtist sjór blandaður þarakurli hátt í loft og á land upp um þrengsli og kringlótt gat upp úr klettunum, einkum í strangri norðaustanátt.

3dee6f91-87d5-7b43-4c1c-be14e69a8408.story_eng: Efri-Sýrlækur is described as the oldest farm here, and it had to move more than once to escape the river Þjórsá. According to the land register of Árni Magnússon and Páll Vídalín from 1708, the farms of Sýrlækur first stood in Sýrlækjarbót. Within living memory at that time, they were moved up onto some islets that by then lay between the mainland and an island, and traces of buildings from both farms could still be seen. Then Þjórsá broke through the land, and the branch of the river that had to be crossed to reach the island came to flow there. The farms were moved once more, away from the river, and Efri-Sýrlækur went to the place where it stood in 1708. Judging by that text, the move probably took place in the 16th or 17th century. Bót is an islet in Þjórsá shared by Efri-Sýrlækur and Syðri-Sýrlækur. Reaching it by boat used to be difficult because of the river and the islet's steep banks, but in recent years the river channel has shifted, and in spring it is now possible to get to Sýrlækjarbót mostly with dry feet. Rams grazed there until the 20th century, but there has been no grazing for several decades.
3dee6f91-87d5-7b43-4c1c-be14e69a8408.story_is: Elsti bærinn. Í Jarðabók Árna Magnússonar og Páls Vídalíns frá 1708 segir að jörðin Sýrlækur eða Sýrlækir hafi fyrst staðið í Sýrlækjarbót og þaðan verið færð í manna minni upp í nokkra hólma sem þá voru milli lands og eyjar, og sæjust enn byggingarmerki til hvorra tveggja bæjanna. Síðan braust Þjórsá í gegnum landið og rennur þar nú sá hluti árinnar sem yfir er að sækja til eyjarinnar. Þaðan voru bæirnir aftur færðir undan ánni, Efri-Sýrlækur þangað sem hann stóð þá. Ef marka má þennan texta var bærinn líklega færður á 16. eða 17. öld. Bót er hólmi í Þjórsá, sameign Efri- og Syðri-Sýrlækjar. Áður var erfitt að komast þangað á bát sökum árinnar og hversu brattir bakkar hólmans eru, en á síðustu árum hefur farvegur Þjórsár færst til og því hægt að komast í Sýrlækjarbót þurrum fótum að mestu að vori til. Þar var hrútabeit fram á 20. öld en engin beit hefur verið þar í nokkra áratugi.

3df66cfb-03a8-81fc-dde6-e6857d7319f4.story_eng: Prestahraunsgata, the priest's lava path, takes its name from the early days of church services at Saxhóll and Ingjaldshóll, when one priest served both churches. This was the path he travelled between them to carry out his duties. The track begins in Djúpudalir, on the boundary between the old Breiðuvíkurhreppur and Neshreppur ytri districts, where it continues on from Efstivegur.
3df66cfb-03a8-81fc-dde6-e6857d7319f4.story_is: Prestahraunsgata dregur nafn af því að í upphafi kirkjuhalds á Saxhóli og á Ingjaldshóli þjónaði sami prestur þessum kirkjum báðum og þetta er sú gata sem hann fór á milli til embættisverka. Gatan tekur við af Efstavegi í Djúpudölum á hreppamörkum Breiðuvíkurhrepps og Neshrepps ytri.

3df7c1be-e17a-176c-1915-8116cb052186.story_eng: Grænutóftir ("the green ruins") is the shared name for three hummocky enclosures lying in a row, each with fragments of old ruins on it. They lie a short way beyond the wall that marked where livestock were driven up to summer pasture, above the farm Leiti. The ruins are probably the remains of sheep houses rather than of dwellings.
3df7c1be-e17a-176c-1915-8116cb052186.story_is: Skammt utan við upprekstrargarðinn ofan Leitis eru þrjú þúfnagerði í röð og á þeim öllum forn tóftabrot. Þetta heitir einu nafni Grænutóftir og eru sennilega fremur fjárhúsminjar en rústir mannabústaða.

3e12a011-6dc4-338b-1cea-3f4699cc6abd.story_eng: Tungutorfur, which local people also call Torfur, are grassy stretches on the bank north of Skeifárbás, where the slope is grown over from the edge of the bank right down to the shore. The grass here was good enough for cows, and in earlier years the slopes were mown every year. One part, Bröttubrekkur (the name means steep slopes), was so steep that it had to be mown wearing crampons. The dried hay was usually carried up on horses, and in winter sometimes on men's backs, along a zigzag path called Langisneiðingur that ran across the southern part of the slopes and up into the gorge Skeifárgil. The slopes are dangerous for animals, and not without reason: avalanches come down here every winter, and four or five head of livestock have fallen to their deaths here since the last turn of the century.
3e12a011-6dc4-338b-1cea-3f4699cc6abd.story_is: Norðan Skeifárbáss er bakkinn gróinn upp til miðs og algróinn frá brún í fjöru á alllöngum kafla er norðar dregur. Þarna eru Tungutorfur, eða Torfur eins og heimamenn nefna þær. Í þeim er kúgæft gras og voru þær slegnar árlega fyrr á árum. Hluta þeirra, Bröttubrekkur, varð að slá á mannbroddum. Þurrt heyið var oftast flutt upp á hestum, en stundum borið upp af mönnum á veturna, eftir Langasneiðingi sem lá út Torfur sunnan til og upp í Skeifárgil. Torfurnar eru hættulegar skepnum og ekki að ástæðulausu. Snjóflóð falla þar hvern vetur og fjórir til fimm gripir hafa hrapað þar til dauðs frá síðustu aldamótum.

3e1aebb1-a9e5-1990-f6ba-694f40ebc8c5.story_eng: Pyttakíll is a channel in the wet meadowland of Grímsfláin where fergin (water horsetail) grows. In it lies a large, grassless pool called Grákollupyttur. Sigurður Ólafsson recorded that he once cut a horsetail stalk out of this pool that was about five ells long (an ell being an old measure of length) and had nearly 70 joints. Two spits of sedge meadow, Bæjarnes and Bæjartangi, reach east into the channel, and the old meadow bridge, Engjabrúin, runs across Bæjartangi.
3e1aebb1-a9e5-1990-f6ba-694f40ebc8c5.story_is: Vestur í Grímsflánni er Pyttakíll, ferginskíll, og í honum er stór graslaus pyttur sem nefndur er Grákollupyttur. Sigurður Ólafsson skar eitt sinn upp úr honum ferginsstrá um fimm álnir á lengd, og voru nær 70 liðir á því. Tvö nes, Bæjarnes, sem er stararengi, og Bæjartangi, ganga austur í kílinn, og liggur Engjabrúin á Bæjartanga.

3e27557a-1680-2bac-7bb3-d67ed8d91b55.story_eng: Hesthús, meaning horse house, stood south of the farmhouse, and in summer the cows were usually milked there. A short way off, some 70–80 metres from the farm, was Kvíaból, where the ewes were milked until fráfærur, the old practice of separating lambs from their mothers so the ewes could be milked, came to an end in 1932. These outbuildings disappeared long ago, and no trace of Kvíaból can be seen.
3e27557a-1680-2bac-7bb3-d67ed8d91b55.story_is: Sunnan bæjar var Hesthús. Kýr voru venjulega mjólkaðar þar á sumrum. Skammt þaðan, um 70–80 metra frá bænum, var Kvíaból en þar voru ær mjólkaðar uns fráfærum var hætt árið 1932. Þessi útihús eru fyrir löngu horfin og Kvíabólsins sjást engin merki.

3e2dbc60-08c5-64a4-d01f-8b9f4f521578.story_eng: Hrútey was usually mown for hay every other year, but the top of the island was never to be cut. A strong spell or warning was said to lie on it. The writer never heard what was supposed to happen if the rule was broken, and knew of no one who had broken it. Everyone considered it their plain duty to spare the flowers growing on the island's top. Each year a pair of oystercatchers and a pair of great northern divers nested on Hrútey, along with a few ducks.
3e2dbc60-08c5-64a4-d01f-8b9f4f521578.story_is: Hrútey var oftast slegin annað hvert ár en eyjartoppinn mátti ekki slá. Lágu þar á sterk ummæli. Ekki heyrði ég hvað átti helst að koma fyrir ef út af var brugðið og vissi heldur ekki til að það væri gert. Það töldu allir sjálfsagða skyldu sína að hlífa blómaskrautinu á eyjartoppnum. Í Hrútey verptu árlega ein tjaldhjón og ein himbrimahjón og fáeinar endur.

3e349b33-5cbc-bb37-92d5-f132ba643086.story_eng: Oral tradition tells that 18 men once set out together from Steingrímsfjörður to cross south over Heiðarbæjarheiði, the moorland route that ends near Gróustaðir in Gilsfjörður. All of them died of exposure on the way except one.
3e349b33-5cbc-bb37-92d5-f132ba643086.story_is: Munnmæli herma að 18 menn hafi eitt sinn farið saman úr Steingrímsfirði suður yfir Heiðarbæjarheiði, sem endar nálægt Gróustöðum í Gilsfirði. Urðu þeir allir úti nema einn.

3e356829-bda9-0644-19b6-435421536eed.story_eng: Þverflóð was a very long but narrow, miry marsh overgrown with bottle sedge, stretching up towards Rofhól. Ewes often died in the marsh in spring when they went after the fresh growth. The marsh has since dried up with drainage.
3e356829-bda9-0644-19b6-435421536eed.story_is: Geysilangt en mjótt forarflóð sem náði fram undir Rofhól, vaxið blástör. Í flóðinu drápust oft ær á vorin þegar þær sóttu í gróðurinn. Flóðið hefur nú þornað með framræslunni.

3e439297-fca5-4408-8a9c-ebec1a0bc43a.story_eng: Gálgahæð, meaning "gallows hill", is a high gravel hill east of the farm Langhúsum. It lies just west of a spot by the river called Gálgi ("gallows"), where criminals are believed to have been executed in earlier centuries. A stone bridge now crosses the river at Gálgi.
3e439297-fca5-4408-8a9c-ebec1a0bc43a.story_is: Austur af bænum Langhúsum við ána er Gálgi, þar er talið að sakamenn hafi verið teknir af fyrr á öldum. Þar er nú steinbrú yfir ána. Vestur af henni er há melhæð sem heitir Gálgahæð.

3e48dd82-d926-9f9c-0bef-d0b328e9ca04.story_eng: Útigönguhnaus is said to lie on Langahlíð, a name that refers to livestock left to fend for themselves outdoors. Of it the old description says: "Sheep have survived there, and men have died of exposure." The hillside is said to continue on from the western edge of Stóra-Svalbarð and stretches a long way north, and its northernmost end is called Heiðarendi.
3e48dd82-d926-9f9c-0bef-d0b328e9ca04.story_is: Útigönguhnaus er sagður vera á Langahlíð. Þar hafa kindur lifað af og menn orðið úti. Langahlíð er sögð framhald út af vesturbrún Stóra-Svalbarðs og nær hún langt til norðurs, út á móts við Skollagrenisás, og heitir nyrsti endi hennar Heiðarendi.

3e4ed141-b0c6-1fe3-47ca-39cedd044aca.story_eng: Fagrakinn, meaning roughly "fair slope", is a grassy slope that faces south towards the sun. It is described as a fairly large hollow, grown over with grass, where there is probably shelter from most wind directions. It lies on the old land boundary, south of the cairn Dómsvarða. The boundary line between the farms Ás and Kárastaðir runs across the hollow, and it marked the north-western corner of the land. Southwest of it is a cave called Imbuhellir. The Imba it refers to later moved away from the district and became the mother of the dance teacher Heiðar Ástvaldsson.
3e4ed141-b0c6-1fe3-47ca-39cedd044aca.story_is: Fagrakinn er grasbrekka sem liggur móti suðri og sól. Hún er allstór, algróinn bolli vestur á landamerkjum og þar er líklega skjól fyrir flestum vindáttum. Hún er suður undan Dómsvörðu og liggur landamerkjalínan milli Áss og Kárastaða yfir lautina, en þar er útnorðurhornmerki landsins. Imbuhellir er suðvestan við Fögrukinn. Sú Imba flutti síðar burt úr sveitinni og varð móðir Heiðars Ástvaldssonar danskennara.

3e5874ff-281a-4b9f-ac8b-f869c6798827.story_eng: On a green knoll stand the remains of a ruin, and another ruin lies on a second knoll just above it. The place is called Stekkur (a stekkur was a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes), and in the second quarter of the 20th century it was known as Laufskálastekkur. This was clearly once an ancient farm. Several very old-looking ruins can be seen here, surrounded by a home-field wall that can be traced almost unbroken all the way round. There are no stories about a farm on this spot, and its name has been lost. The nearby place names Ytra- and Syðra-Laufskálaholt are thought without doubt to preserve it: the farm was built on a wooded hillside and was given the name Laufskáli, made of the words for leaf and hall.
3e5874ff-281a-4b9f-ac8b-f869c6798827.story_is: Á grænum hól er tóttarbrot og þar heitir Stekkur. Önnur tótt er á öðrum hól þar rétt ofar. Heimild er fyrir því að á öðrum fjórðungi 20. aldar var þetta kallað Laufskálastekkur. Þar var fyrrum fornbýli og þar eru greinilega nokkur mjög fornleg tóftarbrot, kringd túngarði sem rekja má nánast óslitið allt umhverfis. Engar sagnir eru um bæ á þessum stað og nafn hans er týnt. Örnefnin Ytra- og Syðra-Laufskálaholt geyma þó vafalítið nafn bæjarins. Hann hefur verið byggður í skógi vaxinni hlíð og fengið nafnið Laufskáli.

3e64e3fd-1727-22f9-1719-7dcf6d5a02a0.story_eng: Strákamýri lies by the sea, northeast of the farm Nes. Several stone pillars stand here, each about the height of a man. Folk belief holds that they are troll boys turned to stone: they were out travelling here when the sun rose, and at that moment they became rock.
3e64e3fd-1727-22f9-1719-7dcf6d5a02a0.story_is: Strákamýri er í norðaustur frá Nesi við sjóinn. Þar eru nokkrir steinstrókar um mannhæðar háir, og hermir svo þjóðtrúin að það séu steinrunnir tröllastrákar. Þeir voru þarna á ferðalagi þegar sólin kom upp og urðu þá samstundis að steini.

3e82e45b-4093-25bf-7687-36cec28f1741.story_eng: Þríhyrningur (the name means 'triangle') lies to the east of the farm Vatnsdalur, and it served as a way of telling the time. It is believed that it is mid-morning in Vatnsdalur when the sun strikes the north-west corner of Þríhyrningur.
3e82e45b-4093-25bf-7687-36cec28f1741.story_is: Þríhyrningur er í austur frá bænum, því talið er að miður morgunn sé í Vatnsdal þegar sól ber í norðvesturhorn Þríhyrnings.

3e89ef42-3c1f-717b-dfb6-3f2d3c1360f9.story_eng: Mávakambar, meaning 'gull crests', is a large expanse in the upper cliffs of Blakknes. Fulmars once nested here in great numbers, and their eggs were collected. To reach the nests, men first lowered themselves on ropes onto Höfðinn, the headland, or got onto it by way of Sveltisgangurinn. Long clefts run down from Höfðinn, and men and eggs were often hauled back up by rope.
3e89ef42-3c1f-717b-dfb6-3f2d3c1360f9.story_is: Mikið flæmi í efri klettum í Blakknesi, frá Sighvatsstóði suður að Strengbergsgjá. Þar hefur verið mikið fýlavarp og eggjataka. Er þá fyrst sigið á Höfðann eða farið á hann um Sveltisganginn. Langir lásar eru niður af Höfðanum og voru menn og egg oft tekin upp á vaðdrætti.

3e8aa8ac-7424-7561-19c9-357fcbd9027e.story_eng: Einarsbeð, also called Syðribeð, is a plot of land south of Sauðhúsvöllur. At its lower end is Einarshús, a house usually known as Fríkirkjan (the Free Church). When it was built in 1917, the bones of people and horses were found in its foundations, along with a spear.
3e8aa8ac-7424-7561-19c9-357fcbd9027e.story_is: Einarsbeð, eða Syðribeð, er sunnan við Sauðhúsvöll. Neðst í því er Einarshús, venjulega nefnt Fríkirkjan. Það hús var byggt 1917 og fundust í grunninum bein manna og hesta, sömuleiðis spjót.

3e93e637-b797-e364-5474-7303d596abae.story_eng: In the eastern part of Stekkjardalur, a small valley southwest of the old home field of the Kárastaðasel shieling, are the remains of fráfærnastekkir. These were folds used at weaning time, when the lambs were separated from the ewes so that the ewes could be milked. The valley, whose name means 'fold valley', takes its name from them.
3e93e637-b797-e364-5474-7303d596abae.story_is: Í Stekkjardalnum austanverðum, suðvestur frá Seltúninu við Kárastaðasel, er brot af fráfærnastekkjum, og dregur dalurinn nafn af því.

3e9592cc-2231-440b-9a50-af68b0dff908.story_eng: Merkihnúta is one of the Hnútur, three small hillocks standing in a triangle in the middle of the wet meadowland of Grunnuslýjur. Merki means boundary or marker, and the name is taken to point to an old division of the hay meadows here. This is where the meadows were split between the brothers Jón and Ásm.
3e9592cc-2231-440b-9a50-af68b0dff908.story_is: Hnútur eru þrjár smáhæðir í þríhyrningi í miðjum Grunnuslýjum og er ein þeirra nefnd Merkihnúta. Bendir það nafn til fornra engjaskipta á þeim, og þar urðu skipti milli bræðranna Jóns og Ásm.

3e9c81bb-9724-1d0f-2fc4-75808145e820.story_eng: According to an old source, this is where the farm originally stood. Later there were sheep houses here out in the home field, with a well beside them, but these have now disappeared completely. A single small hole remains, perhaps where the well once was. Just south of where the sheep house stood, a fairly large stream gully begins and grows shallower towards the west.
3e9c81bb-9724-1d0f-2fc4-75808145e820.story_is: Fjárhúsin úti á túni eru nú alveg horfin. Þar var brunnur við húsin og á þessum stað var hið forna bæjarstæði samkvæmt heimild. Þarna er ein hola, lítil ummáls, ef til vill þar sem brunnurinn var. Sunnan við stæði fjárhússins er austurendi á allmiklu lækjargili sem grynnist til vesturs.

3eab13d0-ab2a-fe21-63c8-1e0ed0478661.story_eng: These grass-covered ruins are what remains of the farm buildings of Móeiðarhvols-Norðurhjáleiga, a hjáleiga (a small tenant farm dependent on a larger farm, here Móeiðarhvoll). The farm was abandoned in the 1890s. The layout of the buildings can still be clearly made out on top of the knoll, as can the wall of the kitchen garden that surrounded them.
3eab13d0-ab2a-fe21-63c8-1e0ed0478661.story_is: Hér eru grasi grónar rústir bæjarhúsanna í Móeiðarhvols-Norðurhjáleigu, en sú jörð fór í eyði á tíunda tug 19. aldar. Enn sést greinilega móta fyrir húsaskipan uppi á hólnum, svo og kálgarðsveggnum í kring.

3eac930d-d7ee-4064-b139-093cf96a4e24.story_eng: Klauf is a slanting path that climbs up and over the cliff called Klifið, or Ásklif, roughly halfway between two other paths, Stampagata and Nóngata. The shepherd from Ássel used to go up this way when he tended the sheep at Ássel, a sel (a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked).
3eac930d-d7ee-4064-b139-093cf96a4e24.story_is: Klauf heitir sniðgata upp og yfir Klifið (Ásklif). Er hún svo sem miðja vegu milli Stampagötu og Nóngötu. Upp Klauf þessa gekk Ásselssmali þegar hann gætti fjár á Ásseli.

3ec05a96-601b-9bd3-4711-fe576e396947.story_eng: The name Þjófhellir means "thief cave", in the singular. Two thieves are believed to have settled in the cave for a time, yet it is never called Þjófahellir, "cave of the thieves".
3ec05a96-601b-9bd3-4711-fe576e396947.story_is: Hellirinn er aldrei nefndur Þjófahellir þó að þjófarnir hafi verið tveir sem talið er að hafi sest þar að um tíma.

3eda6f5f-afb5-4517-9576-dc5e79ca907f.story_eng: A small hut called Magnúsarkofi once stood here. It took its name from Magnús Ívarsson, a farmer at Hjarðarhaga in Jökuldalur, who drowned in Lagarfljót shortly after 1920. His body washed ashore below the home field at Skógargerði, and it was laid out in this hut before burial, which gave the hut its name.
3eda6f5f-afb5-4517-9576-dc5e79ca907f.story_is: Þarna stóð kofi nefndur Magnúsarkofi. Hann dregur nafn af því að þar stóð uppi lík Magnúsar Ívarssonar, bónda í Hjarðarhaga á Jökuldal, sem drukknaði í Lagarfljóti skömmu eftir 1920. Lík hans rak neðan við túnið í Skógargerði.

3efbfbdd-db80-14a8-ecb5-60f9acc66e7b.story_eng: Karl ("the old man") and his partner Kerling ("the old woman") are rock figures in the cliffs above Hrútastígur. The cliff face curves inward here, leaving a point on either side of the hollow, and in these points the shapes of an old man and an old woman can be seen. The old man's eye is formed by a small cleft where a raven sometimes nests. It is called Karlsauga, "the old man's eye".
3efbfbdd-db80-14a8-ecb5-60f9acc66e7b.story_is: Upp af Hrútastíg eru Karl og Kerling. Þar hvelfist nokkuð inn í klettana, þannig að oddar myndast sitt hvorum megin við hvelfinguna. Í oddunum koma fram myndir af karli og kerlingu. Augað á karlinum myndast af gjögri sem hrafninn verpir stundum í. Það heitir Karlsauga.

3eff08a2-df04-ebb8-08f3-285d2d471e4f.story_eng: Rolluskútar are two small rock overhangs on the seaward side of the Syðriklettar cliffs, south of the fishing station Kollsvíkurver. The name combines rolla, a ewe, and skúti, a rock shelter. They are not large, but sheep could stand in them out of the weather. The sand shifts a great deal here, and the shelters are often buried in it. The fishermen staying at the station used Rolluskútar as their toilet. A special 'sýslumaður' (district magistrate) was appointed to see that the place was kept clean. The men wrestled in glíma, traditional Icelandic wrestling, for this office, and it went to the one who lost every bout.
3eff08a2-df04-ebb8-08f3-285d2d471e4f.story_is: Í Rolluskútum gengu vermenn örna sinna. Sérstakur sýslumaður sá um að þar væri þrifalega um gengið. Var glímt um embættið og sá hlaut sem öllum glímum tapaði. Skútarnir eru tveir, sjávarmegin í Syðriklettum sunnan Kollsvíkurvers. Þeir eru ekki stórir, en fé gat staðið þar í skjóli. Mikil hreyfing er þarna á sandinum og oft eru skútarnir á kafi í sandi.

3f005746-3445-4bcf-acb9-b3cc32a055ed.story_eng: This hill takes its name from a childhood episode. Some time before 1900, the brothers Kristján and Jónas Jónsson, then little boys at Hrifla, were sent to drive the sheep southeast to graze by the river. By the time they reached this spot, Jónas, the younger of the two, was very tired. Kristján left him at this hill to be looked after while he drove the flock further on, and the name stuck: geyma means to keep or look after. The hill lies just south of Hádegishóll, the tallest of the hills in this area.
3f005746-3445-4bcf-acb9-b3cc32a055ed.story_is: Nafnið er þannig til komið að þegar Kristján og Jónas Jónssynir voru litlir drengir í Hriflu nokkru fyrir 1900 voru þeir látnir reka fé til beitar suðaustur að fljóti. Þegar þarna var komið var Jónas orðinn mjög lúinn, enda var hann yngri. Geymdi Kristján hann hjá þessum hól meðan hann rak féð lengra, og festist þá nafnið við hólinn. Geymsluhóll er suður af Hádegishóli, sem hæst ber af hólunum þar.

3f127e44-fd4e-3e5d-3641-363d5870f389.story_eng: Brjóst means "breasts", and these are the breasts of Kerling, a great troll woman in the rock. They are a large rock ledge facing east, fairly high above Smásetur, and it is mainly this ledge that gives the giant troll woman her feminine shape. They are said to be about six metres wide and nine metres long. Above Brjóst, Kerling grows narrower.
3f127e44-fd4e-3e5d-3641-363d5870f389.story_is: Brjóst Kerlingar vísa mót austri allhátt fyrir ofan Smásetur. Eru þau stór klettastallur sem einkum ljær hinni miklu tröllkonu kvenlega mynd. Þau munu vera nálægt sex metrum á breidd og níu á lengd. Ofan Brjósta mjókkar Kerling.

3f28dd4d-0b12-f358-d672-eb4f979e6051.story_eng: Pálsrétt is a gap in the bank beside the ditch, just south of the old lambfold. It is named after Páll Sigurðsson, who for a time was the hotel manager at Varmahlíð. He ran a horse-training station and had his facilities at this spot.
3f28dd4d-0b12-f358-d672-eb4f979e6051.story_is: Örstuttu sunnar en Stekkurinn er skarð í brúnina við síkið og heitir það Pálsrétt. Hún er kennd við Pál Sigurðsson, sem um skeið var hótelstjóri í Varmahlíð. Hann var með tamningastöð fyrir hesta og hafði aðstöðu á þessum stað.

3f375a76-9036-c268-2842-3bbfc45f6fd0.story_eng: This hayfield is named after two bulldozer operators, Gísli Óskarsson and Óttar Skjóldal, who spent a long time one autumn around 1965 harrowing and levelling the land to make it into a hayfield. It runs south from Einbúi to the boundary between Þorsteinsstaðir (now Stórhóll) and Brúnastaðir.
3f375a76-9036-c268-2842-3bbfc45f6fd0.story_is: Túnið er nefnt eftir tveimur ýtumönnum, þeim Gísla Óskarssyni og Óttari Skjóldal, sem unnu lengi við að herfa og jafna land undir tún haust eitt í kringum 1965. Það liggur suður frá Einbúa að landamerkjum milli Þorsteinsstaða (nú Stórhóls) og Brúnastaða.

3f41367b-8966-6546-e807-08f2040ce906.story_eng: A story has long been attached to the name of this skerry: it is said that Örn, the mate of the settler Kollur, wrecked their ship here, as Landnáma (the Book of Settlements) relates. This is thought to be the first shipwreck in Iceland on record, and with it the first rescue of people from a shipwreck. Arnarboði lies in the sea about 100 metres from land, off Grundatún. It is covered at high tide but shows at every low tide. It is really part of the point Grundatangi, though the tide never falls far enough for it to join the land.
3f41367b-8966-6546-e807-08f2040ce906.story_is: Sú saga hefur fylgt nafni Arnarboða að þar hafi Örn, stýrimaður Kolls landnámsmanns, brotið skip þeirra líkt og Landnáma greinir frá. Það mun vera fyrsta skipsstrand við Ísland sem sögur fara af, og um leið fyrsta björgun manna frá skipsstrandi. Boðinn er í sjó undan Grundatúni, um 100 metra frá landi, og fer á kaf um flóð en er uppi um hverja fjöru. Arnarboði er eiginlega hluti Grundatanga, þó aldrei falli svo mikið út að hann verði landfastur.

3f45e68c-4b97-476b-94bc-f268519f67f4.story_eng: Nónás is a ridge connected with tales of the huldufólk (hidden people), which can be found in the folk-tale collection of Sigfús Sigfússon. The ridge lies north of Nónengi and ends at Hrútahraun, a heavily fissured, rocky mound.
3f45e68c-4b97-476b-94bc-f268519f67f4.story_is: Í þjóðsögum Sigfúsar Sigfússonar má finna huldufólkssögur er tengjast Nónási. Ásinn er norðan við Nónengi og endar við Hrútahraun, sem er mjög sundursprunginn klettahraukur.

3f4f5397-a4fe-a0ad-27e2-cac6bc431ac3.story_eng: Gullkistuvík means 'gold chest cove'. Just east of the cove is where the Laxfoss ran aground.

3f533f9c-429f-bb96-461a-2a149dabe005.story_eng: The farm Jökulfell in Morsárdalur is believed to have stood near the woodland of the same name, at the spot later known as Bæjarstaður. It had a hálfkirkja, a minor church or chapel, served by the priest from the parsonage at Rauðilækur. There is some likelihood that Jökulfell, along with the settlement in Morsárdalur and on the eastern part of Skeiðarársandur, was destroyed in a great glacial flood from Grímsvötn in 1350. The farm no longer exists.
3f533f9c-429f-bb96-461a-2a149dabe005.story_is: Talið er að bærinn Jökulfell í Morsárdal, þar sem síðar var kallað í Bæjarstað, hafi staðið í grennd samnefnds skógar. Þar var hálfkirkja sem þjónað var frá prestsetrinu Rauðalæk. Nokkrar líkur eru til að bærinn í Jökulfelli og byggð í Morsárdal og á austanverðum Skeiðarársandi hafi eyðst í miklu hlaupi úr Grímsvötnum árið 1350.

3f5a9d55-2c5d-3cb3-f137-f8195241095c.story_eng: Össurskvörn was a grain mill that once stood in the river here. It is thought to have been the last grain mill in Rauðasandshreppur, and was probably one of the so-called kóngskvarnir, the "king's mills" that the king sent to Iceland. The mill was destroyed when a dam was built for a power station, and no trace of the mill house can be seen today.
3f5a9d55-2c5d-3cb3-f137-f8195241095c.story_is: Össurskvörn var kornkvörn sem áður var í Ánni. Þetta mun hafa verið síðasta kornkvörnin í Rauðasandshreppi, og var hún líklega ein af kóngskvörnunum svonefndu, sem konungur sendi til Íslands. Össurskvörn var eyðilögð þegar byggð var stífla fyrir rafstöð og sést ekki fyrir kvarnarhúsinu nú.

3f705d57-18eb-4f06-9f22-0f61fe0124ae.story_eng: Háski is a small cove enclosed by cliffs, lying about halfway between two stretches of shore. Sheep sometimes jump down into it, and they can perish there if the surf rises. The name itself is a plain Icelandic word meaning danger or peril.
3f705d57-18eb-4f06-9f22-0f61fe0124ae.story_is: Um miðja vegu milli Heimustufjöru og Miðfjöru er smábás, klettum girtur, sem Háski heitir. Fé stekkur stundum niður í hann og getur farist ef brim gerir.

3f774622-d7cd-f268-bb61-ae18e0d38996.story_eng: This hollow once held the ruins of a stekkur, a small fold where lambs were penned apart from the ewes in spring, but the ruins are now gone. Below the fold was a stretch of moorland known as Félagsgarður, the 'co-operative garden', where several farmers grew potatoes together between 1910 and 1912. The land is now a hayfield.
3f774622-d7cd-f268-bb61-ae18e0d38996.story_is: Í Stekkahvammi, út af Berjaholti, voru rústir af stekk, nú horfnar. Neðan við stekkinn var mólendi og þar var svokallaður Félagsgarður, þar sem nokkrir bændur stunduðu kartöflurækt í félagi á árunum 1910–1912. Þar er nú tún.

3fa81332-64db-180a-b916-bca1544b20a8.story_eng: Þúfukollur is a tall, cone-shaped lava ridge. Just east of it stands the newly built house Þúfa. At the southern end of the ridge, just west of the house, is a prominent stone that looks like the face of a troll, and this troll has also been given the name Þúfukollur. These are new place names, given by Ólafur Þröstur Stefánsson after he built Þúfa in 2020. He also named the clearing south of the ridge Þúfukollsrjóður, and the high lava ridge east of that clearing Þúfukollskambur.
3fa81332-64db-180a-b916-bca1544b20a8.story_is: Þúfukollur er hár, keilulaga hraunkambur. Rétt austan við hann stendur nýbyggt hús, Þúfa. Syðst í Þúfukolli, rétt vestan við húsið, er áberandi steinn sem líkist andliti á trölli. Þetta tröll hefur hlotið nafnið Þúfukollur. Sunnan við kambinn er Þúfukollsrjóður og austan við rjóðrið er hár hraunkambur, Þúfukollskambur. Þessi nýju örnefni gaf Ólafur Þröstur Stefánsson eftir að hann byggði húsið Þúfu árið 2020.

3fd2e2ea-6a59-03ee-793d-286ae9aa676d.story_eng: Flói was a marsh lying directly below the farm, stretching out along the hollow west of the lava field known as Hraunið and down into the gorge of Jökulsá. It is recorded as no longer existing. A stream flowed from the marsh down into the gorge, and just beyond it, opposite the northern tip of the lava called Hraunhali, lies the ruin of a stekkur, a small fold where lambs were penned apart from the ewes. This was Gamli-Stekkur (the Old Fold), at a spot called Klauf.
3fd2e2ea-6a59-03ee-793d-286ae9aa676d.story_is: Flóinn er niður undan bænum og nær út eftir draginu vestan við Hraunið og út og niður í Jökulsárgil. Úr Flóanum fellur lækur niður í gilið og utan við lækinn, á móti Hraunhalanum, er stekkjarrúst. Þar var Gamli-Stekkur, við svonefnda Klauf. Hraunhali heitir norðurendinn á Hrauninu, sem er austan við Flóann og meðfram Héraðsvatnagilinu.

3fe453e0-cd91-fb49-8c24-3477467b2b11.story_eng: Uppgönguauga is a spring-fed hole in the water east of Bæjarvík that always stays open and barely freezes. In summer it is a cold spring, and it is a lifeline for the trout. A dog belonging to Þórólfur Jónasson, who was then farming at Sílalækur, drowned here. Since then the spot has often been called Garmsgat, from garmur, an old word for a dog.
3fe453e0-cd91-fb49-8c24-3477467b2b11.story_is: Austan Bæjarvíkur er Uppgönguauga. Það er alltaf opið, frýs illa, er kaldavermsl á sumrum og lífæð fyrir silunginn. Þarna drukknaði hundur sem Þórólfur Jónasson átti, þá búandi á Sílalæk, og síðan er staðurinn oft kallaður Garmsgat.

3feacbfd-5a8c-4030-a605-485458c251e7.story_eng: Helgufell (Helga's fell) is said to take its name from a milkmaid from the farm Kirkjuból who died of exposure here. She was caught in a northerly blizzard on her way from the cowshed to the farmhouse, and the storm drove her off the right path.
3feacbfd-5a8c-4030-a605-485458c251e7.story_is: Mælt er að fellið dragi nafn sitt af mjaltakonu frá Kirkjubóli sem hafi orðið þar úti í norðanbyl, er hrakti hana af réttri leið frá fjósinu til bæjar.

400bf065-429a-450e-906c-92f64a636151.story_eng: Fundarholt, meaning 'meeting hill', was at one time the meeting place of the people of the district. The meetings were held here sometime before the turn of the century.
400bf065-429a-450e-906c-92f64a636151.story_is: Í Fundarholti var fundarstaður sveitarbúa einhvern tíma fyrir aldamót.

400e7681-71df-86b7-3180-4a082652b1e6.story_eng: Djöflapunktur means "Devil's Point". This spot in the sea earned the nickname on a fishing crew's sea chart after it tore their fishing line apart and would not give it back. Some devil is down there holding on to it, they said. At least the fish get to swim there in peace.
400e7681-71df-86b7-3180-4a082652b1e6.story_is: Þetta svæði í sjónum fékk viðurnefnið Djöflapunktur í sjókortinu okkar eftir að hafa rifið í sundur línuna okkar og ekki viljað skila henni til baka. Einhver djöfull er þarna niðri að halda í hana. Þarna fær fiskurinn allavega að synda í friði.

4042790e-fd69-0dd6-055f-3c50e98e5011.story_eng: On the south side of the hill Byrgisholt are the stone walls of an old structure called Byrgi, which gave the hill its name. An old tradition says there was a shelter (byrgi) here where weaned lambs were kept. In the old farming year, lambs were taken from the ewes in early summer so the ewes could be milked. These lambs were watched over by a herder while they grazed in the nearby marsh Gerðismýri.
4042790e-fd69-0dd6-055f-3c50e98e5011.story_is: Sunnan undir Byrgisholti eru hleðslur gamals mannvirkis sem heitir Byrgi og er nafngjafi holtsins. Gömul sögn er að þar hafi verið byrgi sem fráfærnalömb voru hýst í, en þau voru setin í Gerðismýri.

405920bb-0687-53fa-a52e-0c5d7bbfec07.story_eng: During the mining years of 1914–18, a hut built entirely of earth, roof and walls alike, stood down by the river, just north of the end of the bridge. It was put up by Húsavíkurhreppur, the local district, which kept men here mining coal for the district. Once, during a heavy downpour, the hut collapsed, and that is how it got its name: Hruni, meaning "collapse".
405920bb-0687-53fa-a52e-0c5d7bbfec07.story_is: Suður við ána, norður af brúarsporðinum, var á námuárunum 1914–18 byggður moldarkofi, þak sem veggir, á vegum Húsavíkurhrepps sem hafði þar menn við kolanám fyrir hreppinn. Einhverju sinni hrundi hann saman í stórrigningu og hlaut af því nafnið Hruni.

40645d69-e47e-b251-4eca-dd9a8d8b6d19.story_eng: This grassy hollow lies above Grjótnes, a gravel spit that reaches a little way west into Vötnin, a short distance south of the bridge. It has two names. Grjótneshvammur is the old one; the other, Trúlofunarhvammur (Engagement Hollow), is a newer name, though not one given "with official approval". The hollow is lovely in summer and draws many young and lively people, and even old ones too, as a drivable road runs right beside it. It is said that the hollow serves most people well who have grown tired of living alone and have not managed to escape it any other way. It is even said to have worked for old bachelors and spinsters, and the collector thought it likely that it lived up to its name. It has also been called Áningarlaut, the resting hollow, since it was a favoured place to stop and rest.
40645d69-e47e-b251-4eca-dd9a8d8b6d19.story_is: Grjótnes er malarnes sem gengur lítið eitt vestur í Vötnin skammt fyrir sunnan Vatnabrúna. Upp af nesinu er hvammur sem heitir tveimur nöfnum. Annað er Grjótneshvammur og er það gamalt, en hitt er Trúlofunarhvammur og er það nýnefni, þó ekki „með stjórnarleyfi“. Hvammur þessi er sumarfagur og dregur mjög að sér ungt og fjörugt fólk og jafnvel gamalt líka, enda liggur bílfær vegur rétt hjá hvamminum. Sagt er að hvammurinn gefist flestum vel sem þreyttir eru orðnir á einlífi og ekki hafa haft lag á að losna við það með öðru móti. Hvammurinn kvað jafnvel hafa dugað gömlum piparkörlum og kerlingum, og er líklegt að hann kafni ekki undir nafni. Hvammurinn hefur einnig verið nefndur Áningarlaut, enda hefur hann verið kjörinn áningarstaður.

40682b5b-e0b3-43e3-b145-2ba06cabe783.story_eng: Skúrarnef, meaning 'shed point', lies on the inner side of Breiðavíkurnef. A shed once stood below it, and while boats still went out after Greenland shark, shark liver oil was rendered there, the last time shortly before 1920.
40682b5b-e0b3-43e3-b145-2ba06cabe783.story_is: Skúrarnef er innanvert á Breiðavíkurnefi. Þar undir var í eina tíð skúr, og á meðan enn var gert út á hákarl var þar brætt lýsi, síðast skömmu fyrir 1920.

407e0593-347a-98de-ba09-da0ad5afdfef.story_eng: According to old oral tradition, a woman died of exposure on this slope while travelling from Seyðisfjörður. The slope lies just beyond the river Innri-Stangará.
407e0593-347a-98de-ba09-da0ad5afdfef.story_is: Innan við Innri-Stangará er Gunnubrekka. Þar varð úti kona á leið frá Seyðisfirði samkvæmt gömlum munnmælum.

408e5f52-75b7-b6b9-60b2-09653cb1f90b.story_eng: Víkin is a broad cove with a shingle beach, though at times shell sand has been washed up onto it for a while. Here, and on other shingle beaches in this area, wandering stones (flökkusteinar) of Greenlandic rock can sometimes be seen.
408e5f52-75b7-b6b9-60b2-09653cb1f90b.story_is: Í Víkinni, breiðum vogi neðan Smáhryggja, er malarfjara, en stundum hefur þó ruðst þar upp skeljasandur um tíma. Þarna, og víðar í malarfjörum á þessum slóðum, má stundum sjá flökkusteina úr grænlensku bergi.

40b02e41-5f91-e52c-8ed5-ed1b0436c261.story_eng: This fissure takes its name from a young ram. Roughly twenty years before the description was written, a ram lamb was found in a crack on the northwest side of Grenishnúta. People began to speak of the fissure where the 'hrússi', a familiar word for a ram, had been found, and before long it was being called Hrússagjá.
40b02e41-5f91-e52c-8ed5-ed1b0436c261.story_is: Fyrir á að giska tuttugu árum fannst lambhrútur í sprungu norðvestan í Grenishnútunni. Upp úr því var farið að tala um gjána þar sem hrússi fannst og áður en langt leið var farið að tala um Hrússagjá.

40b6f84e-a8e9-c589-9717-66d97273a97a.story_eng: Brunngilshöfði is the northern edge of the gully Brunngil, down on the bank above the sea. Across the gully, near the edge of the bank, lie the ruins of the abandoned farm Smárabakki. It was built by Guðmundur Snorrason, a man from the south of Iceland who worked as a blacksmith at the Tungunáma mine, and he lived there for some years with his family. Out on the bank, southwest of the ruins, is a small grassy patch called Smárabakkatorfa.
40b6f84e-a8e9-c589-9717-66d97273a97a.story_is: Norðurjaðar Brunngils, niður á sjávarbakkanum, nefnist Brunngilshöfði. Hinum megin gilsins, fram undir bakkabrúninni, er eyðibýlið Smárabakki. Það byggði Guðmundur Snorrason, sunnlenskur maður og járnsmiður við Tungunámuna, og bjó þar nokkur ár með fjölskyldu sinni. Fram á bakkanum, suðvestur af rústunum, er dálítil grastorfa sem heitir Smárabakkatorfa.

40dceb74-bed0-1153-9f2d-de6f35f58b30.story_eng: Beitarhúsatún is believed to be the name of the hayfield beside the old Beitarhús, out on the flat land to the east. A beitarhús was a sheep house out in the grazing land. The sheep houses stood where a timber shed stands now. They are gone, though some remains of them are said to still be visible.
40dceb74-bed0-1153-9f2d-de6f35f58b30.story_is: Austur á flatlendinu, þar sem nú stendur timburskúr, voru Beitarhús sem nú eru horfin. Þó eiga að sjást þar einhverjar leifar af húsunum. Túnið þar hjá mun heita Beitarhúsatún.

40f0491d-db8c-499a-bca9-25834d4413e6.story_eng: Ingileifarbær was a small farmhouse that stood on the eastern part of a large, fully grassed mound at the southern end of the home field. The mound runs east to west and is covered in extensive ruins. Ingileif Símonardóttir and Einar Guðmundsson lived here, and the house took its name from Ingileif. The house is no longer standing.
40f0491d-db8c-499a-bca9-25834d4413e6.story_is: Syðst í túninu er stór hóll sem snýr endum í austur og vestur, algróinn, með miklum rústum. Þar stóð Ingileifarbær austan til á hólnum. Þar bjuggu Ingileif Símonardóttir og Einar Guðmundsson.

410c840e-fee0-cce8-b9b3-c50ced604264.story_eng: This smithy belonged to Helgi Jónsson, who farmed at Merkigarður with Ingigerður Halldórsdóttir from 1923. Helgi was a well-known blacksmith who worked a great deal at his craft, and the smithy was his workplace. It is said that once, when coal was scarce, he sent for (or fetched) lignite from Vesturdalur and used it in the forge instead. Helgi died in 1954, having given up farming some time before. The smithy still stands on a small rise some way out from and above the farmhouse. It is a handsome building with a corrugated-iron roof, and it was probably repaired after Helgi's time. Its last use was as a smokehouse. A plot around it has recently been fenced and planted with young trees, and a few years earlier five birch saplings were planted on its south side.
410c840e-fee0-cce8-b9b3-c50ced604264.story_is: Smiðja Helga Jónssonar stendur enn. Helgi Jónsson og Ingigerður Halldórsdóttir bjuggu í Merkigarði frá 1923. Helgi var mikill og kunnur járnsmiður og stundaði þá iðn mikið. Smiðjan var hans vinnustaður. Sagt er að eitt sinn þegar hörgull var á kolum hafi Helgi sent eftir (eða sótt) surtarbrand fram í Vesturdal og notað í smiðjunni í stað kola. Helgi lést 1954 en var hættur búskap nokkru áður. Smiðjan er nokkurn spöl utan og ofan við íbúðarhúsið og stendur á smáhæð. Hún er hið myndarlegasta hús, með bárujárnsþaki. Líklega hefur verið hresst upp á hana eftir daga Helga, enda þarf hún viðhald eins og önnur hús. Smiðjan hefur síðast þjónað hlutverki reykhúss. Nýlega hefur verið girtur blettur umhverfis hana og gróðursettar þar trjáplöntur, en nokkrum árum fyrr voru gróðursettar fimm birkiplöntur sunnan við smiðjuna.

4125d134-46cd-38b3-aa49-80f397b21b0e.story_eng: Tungunáma was a coal mine above the middle of the cove, where extensive coal mining was carried out by the national treasury (landssjóður) during the First World War. A ledge, Námustallur, was blasted into the rock, and from it the mine tunnels, Námugöngin, ran into the bank. South of the ledge and somewhat lower is Smiðjutótt, the ruin where the mine's ironsmithy stood. The mining produced a great deal of waste, which was carted out on rail wagons and piled up out into the sea. The heap caught fire and burned for two to three years. It is called Námuhaugur and is being worn away by the sea.
4125d134-46cd-38b3-aa49-80f397b21b0e.story_is: Upp úr miðri víkinni var Tungunáman. Þar var mikil kolavinnsla á vegum landssjóðs á heimsstyrjaldarárunum fyrri. Þar var sprengdur stallur í bergið, Námustallur. Af honum lágu Námugöngin inn í bakkann. Sunnan hans en nokkuð lægra er Smiðjutótt. Þar stóð járnsmiðja námunnar. Mikill úrgangur losnaði við kolavinnsluna, sem var ekið út á sporvögnum og hlóðst upp fram í sjó. Í honum kviknaði og var þar eldur í tvö til þrjú ár. Hann er nefndur Námuhaugur og eyðist af sjógangi.

4126d23f-7fab-1aae-2611-296f2999a698.story_eng: Leynitjörn lies at the south-western corner of the island, where the banks called Kirkjubakkar come to an end. The pond is not large, but it is deep. Because of the higher ground surrounding it, it cannot be seen until one has reached its edge, and that is where its name comes from: Leynitjörn means 'hidden pond'.
4126d23f-7fab-1aae-2611-296f2999a698.story_is: Kirkjubakkarnir enda við Leynitjörn á suðvesturhorni eyjarinnar. Tjörnin er ekki stór um sig en djúp og sést ekki fyrr en að henni er komið vegna hávaða umhverfis hana, og ber hún nafn af því.

4131caf7-e294-48f9-898f-e82329c17548.story_eng: In the cliffs on the east side of the river Þverá, some way in, there is a rock shelter. This was where the mountain men (fjallmenn, the farmers who rounded up sheep from the highland pastures each autumn) spent the night on every round-up. The shelter and the land around it were, and still are, called Hellrar, also written Hellar.
4131caf7-e294-48f9-898f-e82329c17548.story_is: Hamrar eru austanmegin við Þverá og nokkuð innarlega í þessum hömrum er hellisskúti. Þar var náttstaður fjallmanna í öllum leitum. Þessi skúti og landið þar umhverfis var og er kallað Hellrar eða Hellar.

41348109-4004-c427-27f1-98851c65af8e.story_eng: Félagar, meaning "comrades" or "companions", is a scoria crater with the river Tungnaá flowing right through it. It was formerly known as Rist and Táberg. These earlier names referred to two hydrologists, Sigurjón Rist and Eberg Elefsen, who worked for Orkustofnun, the National Energy Authority.
41348109-4004-c427-27f1-98851c65af8e.story_is: Félagar eru gjallgígur sem Tungnaá rennur í gegnum. Félagar nefndust áður Rist og Táberg. Nöfnin vísuðu í vatnamælingamennina Sigurjón Rist og Eberg Elefsen sem unnu hjá Orkustofnun.

413592d4-efd4-63d7-f6ad-7e7d44a852ab.story_eng: This rock shelter on the west side of Sigurðarhæð is also called Sigurðarhellir. A large stone wall has been built up at the shelter, and a man named Sigurður is said to have lived there in the old days. It was quite common for wandering vagrants to take shelter in caves like these.
413592d4-efd4-63d7-f6ad-7e7d44a852ab.story_is: Vestan í Sigurðarhæð er hellisskúti sem einnig heitir Sigurðarhellir. Mikil hleðsla er við skútann og á einhver Sigurður að hafa haldið þar til í gamla daga, enda var alvanalegt að flökkukarlar hefðust við í þessum hellum.

41451778-5484-423d-f0b9-ce9abea0ffaf.story_eng: Vörðumelur (the name means cairn gravel hill), also called Vörðumelar, is a group of gravel hills at the southern, eastern end of Móar. They enclose a small boggy hollow called Sótabæli, and on the northeast side of Vörðumelur lies a second hollow, Ytra-Sótabæli. A story is told about Sótabæli, and it is said that both of those it concerns are buried there. Water collected in both hollows, which usually held ponds. Vörðumelur has since been destroyed by gravel extraction.
41451778-5484-423d-f0b9-ce9abea0ffaf.story_is: Syðst í Móunum að austan er lítill mýrarbolli inniluktur af melum og heitir hann Sótabæli, en melarnir heita einu nafni Vörðumelar. Norðaustan í Vörðumel gengur annar mýrarbolli sem heitir Ytra-Sótabæli. Sögn er til um Sótabæli og eiga báðir að vera heygðir þar. Í báðum Sótabælum safnaðist vatn og voru þar venjulega tjarnir. Nú er búið að eyðileggja Vörðumel með malartöku.

415906c7-b28f-462b-a89d-543fd08b3bfc.story_eng: Around 1750, fishing boats put out to sea from Sverriseyri. The place is a small knoll of bare rock at the southern end of a gravel flat made up of gravel banks and spits.
415906c7-b28f-462b-a89d-543fd08b3bfc.story_is: Frá Sverriseyri var útræði um 1750. Þetta er dálítill klapparhnúður sunnan til á malarfláka með eyrum og töngum.

4163c557-1e8d-f585-6196-76b139118107.story_eng: There was a farm at Selsvellir in ancient times, and its ruins can still be seen here. The ruins themselves are still known by the name. The plains around them are flat and in places overgrown with brushwood. They lie just south of the hill Nýjabæjarhóll. A short verse was made about the place: "About Selsvöllur I have set in order such a run of verse: things go well for men, spring is good in Sperðill."
4163c557-1e8d-f585-6196-76b139118107.story_is: Á Selsvöllum var býli til forna, og sjást þar bæjarrústir sem enn kallast nafninu. Vellirnir sjálfir umhverfis rústirnar eru sléttir og sums staðar hrísi vaxnir. Þeir eru sunnan við Nýjabæjarhólinn. Um Selsvelli er þessi vísa: Um Selsvöll hef ég sett í lag svoddan kvæðaferli: Virðum gengur vel í hag, vorgott er í Sperðli.

416db819-466f-5e71-c2a8-cd0bf63704a2.story_eng: These grassy mounds, also called Kot, are said to be where the farm Hraungerði first stood. The old land register of Árni Magnússon and Páll Vídalín records the common belief that the farm burned to the ground here, and that charcoal and burnt, rusted iron could still be found in the soil, before the farm was moved to its present site. A report from 1821 instead says the farm was abandoned because of hauntings. Plates of iron, copper and brass were often found in the ruins, and a local farmer, Ólafur Þorkelsson, once found a brass spoon. It was also said that anyone passing the mounds at dusk would lose their way. Other stories tell that goods saved when the church at Skálholt burned were brought to Hraungerði, which then burned too, or that a storehouse there called Skálholt, used for goods on the way from Eyrarbakki to Skálholt, burned, and the farm was moved here for a time. No buildings have been visible since about 1930. When an attempt was made around 1950 to level the mounds, ash and building stones soon came up and the work was stopped. Faint traces of a sunken stone field wall remain.
416db819-466f-5e71-c2a8-cd0bf63704a2.story_is: Í Hraungerðislandi sjást fornar girðingar og byggðarleifar sem kallaðar eru Kot, og stærsti hóllinn Gamla-Hraungerði. Í Jarðabók Árna Magnússonar og Páls Vídalín segir að almenningsrómur sé að bærinn Hraungerði hafi áður staðið þar en brunnið af voðaeldi til kaldra kola. Fundust þar þá enn í jörðu bæði kol og brunnið, ryðétið járn, sem þessari sögu báru líkindavitni. Eftir brunann hafi bærinn verið fluttur þangað sem hann nú stendur. Í fornleifaskýrslu frá 1821 segir að bærinn hafi lagst af fyrir reimleika sakir. Oft hafi fundist í tóftabrotunum plötur af járni, eir og látúni, og bóndi nokkur, Ólafur Þorkelsson, fann þar eitt sinn skeið af látúni. Einnig var sagt að enginn færi um Kotin þegar húma tekur án þess að villast. Sögur herma líka að þegar kirkjan í Skálholti brann hafi það góss sem bjargað varð verið flutt í Hraungerði, þar hafi líka orðið bruni og bærinn því fluttur tímabundið í Gamla-Hraungerði. Önnur saga er sú að í Hraungerði hafi verið skemma sem nefndist Skálholt, þar sem vörur voru geymdar á leið frá Eyrarbakka til Skálholts, og hún hafi brunnið. Mannvirki hafa ekki sést í hólunum síðan um 1930. Þegar reynt var að slétta þá um 1950 kom fljótlega upp aska og hleðslugrjót og var verkinu þá hætt. Enn sést móta fyrir sokkinni steinaröð úr túngarði.

41826526-f454-4e3c-4650-f1eddd10333d.story_eng: Heyflói, whose name means hay marsh, lies above the ridge Bæjarás. Old haystack sites can still be found here, and on the knoll Engjarhóll. Hay was sometimes stored on them into the winter and then brought down to the farm on sledges, pulled by horses or by men.
41826526-f454-4e3c-4650-f1eddd10333d.story_is: Heyflói er fyrir ofan Bæjarás og nær upp að Skollahólum. Þar eru gömul heystæði stutt fyrir utan Litluárlæki og uppi á Engjarhóli, sem er skammt niður af Skollahólum. Stundum var hey geymt á þeim fram á vetur og síðan flutt niður á bæ á sleðum sem voru dregnir af hestum eða mönnum.

41e56a86-4be0-9534-3f0e-017c5c92eb22.story_eng: This cave goes by two names. One is Útilegumannahellirinn, the outlaws' cave, after the outlaws Eyvindur and Margrét, who were captured here. The other is Hallberuhellir, after Hallbera Jónsdóttir, who set up a farm at an old sel site in Lækjarbotnar. A sel was a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked.
41e56a86-4be0-9534-3f0e-017c5c92eb22.story_is: Hellirinn er ýmist kallaður Útilegumannahellirinn, eftir útilegumönnunum Eyvindi og Margréti sem handsömuð voru þar, eða Hallberuhellir, eftir Hallberu Jónsdóttur sem reisti bú í gamalli selstöðu í Lækjarbotnum.

41e9997b-a1bb-4fcb-8ec8-ae18b50bfee6.story_eng: Two different stories are told about how these rocks got their name. According to the place-name description for Hrafnabjörg, a woman died of exposure at Inguklettar in the first half of the 18th century. She was found the following spring with a grasapoki on her back, a bag used for gathering Iceland moss. She is said to have been called Ingibjörg, because Imbuhlíð, a slope in the land of Hallgeirsstaðir, is named after the same woman (Imba is a short form of Ingibjörg). The description for Hallgeirsstaðir tells it differently: Imbuhlíð is named after a young girl from Surtsstaðir who went out to look for the cows and was found dead at the front of the slope, by Imbuklettur in the land of Hrafnabjörg. The rocks stand directly above Kúluhvammar, with a survey cairn above them.
41e9997b-a1bb-4fcb-8ec8-ae18b50bfee6.story_is: Tvennum sögum fer af nafni klettanna. Í örnefnalýsingu Hrafnabjarga segir að við Ingukletta hafi kona orðið úti á fyrri hluta 18. aldar og fundist vorið eftir með grasapoka á bakinu. Hún mun hafa heitið Ingibjörg, því að Imbuhlíð í Hallgeirsstaðalandi er kennd við sömu konu. Í örnefnalýsingu Hallgeirsstaða segir hins vegar að Imbuhlíð sé kennd við stúlkubarn frá Surtsstöðum sem fór að leita að kúm en fannst örend fremst á hlíðinni við Imbuklett í Hrafnabjargalandi. Inguklettar eru beint upp af Kúluhvömmum og þar upp af er Landmælingavarða.

41ecda3e-5b03-8ba8-f81d-3f65c9d2fce0.story_eng: Traces of old irrigation ditches can still be seen out on the Grundin meadow. They were called Sörensskurðir, after a man named Sören Jónsson from Arndísarstaðir, who was foreman of a work crew of the old Ljósavatnshreppur farmers' association from 1883 to 1890. Around 1955, when the cows still roamed freely outdoors, part of the meadow was known as Kálfagirðing, the calf enclosure.
41ecda3e-5b03-8ba8-f81d-3f65c9d2fce0.story_is: Enn sjást úti á Grundinni merki um áveituskurði sem kallaðir voru Sörensskurðir. Þeir heita eftir Sören nokkrum Jónssyni frá Arndísarstöðum, verkstjóra í vinnuflokki Búnaðarfélags Ljósavatnshrepps hins forna 1883–1890. Um 1955, þegar kýr gengu frjálsar úti, var kölluð Kálfagirðing þar úti á Grundinni.

42134fb1-77f6-74dd-af76-d326481cc029.story_eng: Kráka, also called Krákuá, takes its name from an old woman, Kráka, who lived with her two sons at Krákutún in Veiðileysa, beside the river. Her sons fished hard, but once they ran out of bait. A pauper woman was boarded at Kráka's home, and the sons cut a piece from her thigh to use as bait. They went to sea, and nothing is told of their catch, but a violent storm blew up and they drowned at the landing place. Kráka is then said to have laid a curse that no fish would ever again be caught in the fjord, and also that no one would drown there at the landing. The sons are said to be buried in a cairn up on Melurinn, and a stone was always thrown onto it by anyone walking past. When all this was over, Kráka ran along the river and threw herself into its waterfall, which has since been called Krákufoss, a short way above Krákutún. Her husband is said to have lived on the north side of the fjord at Hrauntún, and the two could see each other straight across the water.
42134fb1-77f6-74dd-af76-d326481cc029.story_is: Kráka hét kerling sem bjó með tveimur sonum sínum í Krákutúni í Veiðileysu sem er við Krákuá. Synir hennar sóttu sjó af kappi en urðu eitt sinn uppiskroppa með beitu. Hjá Kráku var kerling ein niðursetningur. Þeir skáru stykki úr lærinu á kerlingunni til að nota í beitu. Þar með fóru þeir á sjó og segir ekki af afla þeirra. Það gerði á þá vitlaust veður og drukknuðu þeir í lendingunni. Kráka á þá að hafa lagt það á að aldrei skyldi fiskast bein úr sjó á firðinum framar og enn fremur að enginn myndi drukkna þar í lendingu. Synirnir eiga að vera heygðir uppi á Melnum í dys sem þar er og var ávallt kastað steini í hana þegar gengið var fram hjá henni. Þegar þetta var afstaðið hljóp Kráka fram með ánni og steypti sér í fossinn í henni sem síðan heitir Krákufoss og er skammt ofan við Krákutún. Bóndi Kráku á að hafa búið norðan fjarðarins í Hrauntúni og gátu þau séð hvort til annars þvert yfir fjörðinn.

421becd2-817d-6fd9-4986-3209610da868.story_eng: Mannabeinabollar, meaning 'human-bone hollows', are low dips in the lava below the road, near two large rocks called Mannabeinaklettar ('human-bone rocks'). According to the description, bones still lie there. The only exception is the skull, which was once there but was taken to Gagnfræðaskóli Akureyrar, the secondary school in Akureyri.
421becd2-817d-6fd9-4986-3209610da868.story_is: Út með brautinni er hraun, þar til kemur að svonefndum Mannabeinaklettum. Það eru tveir stórir klettar utan og austan við Hólmavaðshlið. Þar eru lágar í hrauninu, Mannabeinabollar, fyrir neðan veginn. Þar eru enn bein, nema hauskúpan, sem var þar, en er farin inn í Gagnfræðaskóla Akureyrar.

4221ff05-b48e-fbd8-4ddf-11bf86481a1b.story_eng: Oral tradition says that a man died of exposure at Stóristeinn. The name means "the big stone", and it fits: on a gravel hillock a short way southeast of the Næfurstaðarétt sheep fold, with a hollow between them, there is an enormous stone, well over a man's height and broad to match. This is believed to be Stóristeinn. Around it, the bare gravel was being revegetated by spreading hay and other material.
4221ff05-b48e-fbd8-4ddf-11bf86481a1b.story_is: Munnmæli segja að við Stórastein, sem er ekki langt frá Næfurstaðarétt, í landi Áss, hafi maður orðið úti. Á melhól skammt suðaustan við Næfurstaðarétt, drag á milli, er gríðarlega stór steinn, vel mannhæðar hár og eftir því digur. Þetta mun vera Stóristeinn. Þar hjá er verið að græða upp melinn með heyi og fleiru.

42413d9a-9838-8a44-b6dd-3c36b6919ca9.story_eng: Bakkahorn is the riverbank north of the road. At its northern end is a rocky knoll called Klöppin, and just beyond it lies Gamli ferjustaðurinn, the old ferry landing, where there is a small gap in the riverbank.
42413d9a-9838-8a44-b6dd-3c36b6919ca9.story_is: Árbakkinn norðan vegarins heitir Bakkahorn. Nyrst á honum er klapparhóll sem nefndur er Klöppin. Fyrir innan Klöppina er Gamli ferjustaðurinn og er þar dálítið skarð í árbakkann.

42486456-2175-5725-e8ce-1284c6ca95e2.story_eng: Biskupagarður means 'the Bishops' Garden'. In the beginning, the trees in this grove are said to have been as many as the bishops of Hólar, and each tree bore the name of one of them. That is why it came to be called Biskupagarður. For a time it was also known as Frúargarður, 'the Lady's Garden', because the headmaster's wife, perhaps more than one over the years, looked after the garden and its upkeep. It is also called Skrúðgarðurinn, the ornamental garden.
42486456-2175-5725-e8ce-1284c6ca95e2.story_is: Í upphafi munu trén í garðinum hafa verið jafnmörg Hólabiskupum og borið nöfn þeirra. Þess vegna hefur garðurinn verið nefndur Biskupagarður. Hann var að minnsta kosti á tímabili kallaður Frúargarður. Nafnið var tilkomið af því að skólastjórafrúin, ef til vill fleiri en ein, sá um garðinn, viðhald hans og fleira. Garðurinn er einnig nefndur Skrúðgarðurinn.

4292256f-fc6a-1af3-45b7-3b5e16bc13af.story_eng: Gerði is the southern part of a small, tussocky home field, where the ruins of a hut can still be seen. Bjarni Gunnarsson of Auðbjargarstaðir remembered that the farmer at Bangastaðir kept goats there.
4292256f-fc6a-1af3-45b7-3b5e16bc13af.story_is: Túnið er lítið og þýft. Sunnan til í því er svo nefnt Gerði og þar eru kofarústir. Bjarni Gunnarsson á Auðbjargarstöðum mundi eftir að Bangastaðabóndi hafði geitur þar.

4297a846-cbab-31bc-ff64-2be4ae97870a.name_eng: Stórhús, ruins of a sheep house
4297a846-cbab-31bc-ff64-2be4ae97870a.story_eng: Stórhús was one of two sheep houses that stood side by side in the middle of Tunga, the home-field strip north of the stream, northwest of the old farmhouse. The strip was named Tunga ("tongue") after its shape. Stórhús was the eastern of the two, with a hay barn, Stórhúshlaða, attached to its northern end. The western sheep house was called Gunnarshús, after Gunnar Benediktsson, who tended his livestock there around the turn of the 20th century.
4297a846-cbab-31bc-ff64-2be4ae97870a.story_is: Túnspildan norðan lækjar nefndist Tunga eftir lögun hennar. Á henni miðri, norðvestur frá gamla bæ, voru tvö samliggjandi fjárhús. Hið austara hét Stórhús og áföst við norðurenda þess Stórhúshlaða. Vestara fjárhúsið hét Gunnarshús eftir manni sem hirti fénað sinn um síðustu aldamót, Gunnari Benediktssyni.

429ec6a3-6b5a-b37a-2a34-543e9212aefc.story_eng: Koluvað is a ford on the river Kaldá, a short way west of where the Þingvellir road crosses the river. The ford had no name until it is said to have been named after a ewe called Kola, who kept crossing north over it in search of grassier land.
429ec6a3-6b5a-b37a-2a34-543e9212aefc.story_is: Skammt fyrir vestan Þingvallaveginn, þar sem hann liggur yfir Kaldá, er Koluvað á ánni. Það mun vera kennt við kind sem sótti mikið norður yfir vaðið á grösugra land. Áður var vaðið nafnlaust.

42a14474-dff4-493f-e0c4-daaa215bf761.story_eng: The timber house known as Áshúsið no longer stands here. It now stands at Glaumbær. It stood a little to the southwest and had a cellar under the whole house. It was a half-timbered house, built in 1883–1886 at Ás in Hegranes by the master builders Einar B. Guðmundsson of Hraun, Þorsteinn Sigurðsson of Sauðárkrókur and Ólafur Sigurðsson, the farmer at Ás. The Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Byggðasafn Skagfirðinga) has owned it since 1988. It was moved to Glaumbær in 1991 and rebuilt there in 1992–1995. Four generations of the same family lived in the house from 1886 to 1977. The couple who built it, Sigurlaug Gunnarsdóttir (1828–1905) and Ólafur Sigurðsson (1822–1908), were great champions of progress who worked hard for the cultivation of both land and people. For many years they held courses for boys and girls in their home, and various advances in the district between 1870 and 1910 can be traced directly to the Ás household.
42a14474-dff4-493f-e0c4-daaa215bf761.story_is: Nýrra timburhúsið, Áshúsið, sem nú stendur í Glaumbæ, var aðeins suðvestar og kjallari undir því öllu. Þetta var bindingsverkshús, reist 1883–1886 í Ási í Hegranesi. Forsmiðir voru Einar B. Guðmundsson á Hraunum, Þorsteinn Sigurðsson á Sauðárkróki og Ólafur Sigurðsson bóndi í Ási. Húsið hefur verið eign Byggðasafns Skagfirðinga frá 1988, var flutt að Glaumbæ 1991 og endurgert þar 1992–1995. Fjórar kynslóðir sömu fjölskyldu bjuggu í húsinu frá 1886 til 1977. Hjónin sem byggðu húsið, Sigurlaug Gunnarsdóttir (1828–1905) og Ólafur Sigurðsson (1822–1908), voru miklir framfarasinnar og beittu sér mjög fyrir ræktun lands og lýðs. Þau stóðu fyrir námskeiðahaldi bæði fyrir drengi og stúlkur um árabil á heimili sínu, og ýmsar framfarir í héraðinu á tímabilinu 1870–1910 má rekja beint til Ásheimilisins.

42a192cd-e7a8-3f98-41a4-2050d29044b0.story_eng: Oral tradition said that a farm called Grænabrekka once stood here, though the name is known only from word of mouth. It is probably the same place that the land register of 1713 calls Háistekkur, an old stekkur site belonging to the home farm (a stekkur was a fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes). The register noted visible enclosures and the remains of ruins, adding that no one knew of anyone ever having lived here. Later accounts describe what was probably a small homefield, the remains of several buildings and traces of a field wall running most of the way around. Ruins lie in four places, all on small hillocks, and the largest, measuring 6 by 9 metres, sits on the highest one. A little further south, at the eastern edge of the likely homefield, part of the wall can still be seen. The site lies below the gravel ridges, a short way south of the stream Grófarlækur.
42a192cd-e7a8-3f98-41a4-2050d29044b0.story_is: Munnmæli sögðu að þarna hefði verið bær sem hét Grænabrekka, en fyrir nafninu er aðeins munnleg heimild. Grænabrekka er líklega sama og Háistekkur, sem Jarðabókin frá 1713 nefnir: „Háistekkur, gamalt stekkjarstæði frá heimajörðinni, þar sést til girðinga og tóftaleifa. Ekki hefur hér byggð verið það menn vita.“ Þar er líklega dálítið tún og leifar af nokkrum húsum, og þar vottar fyrir túngarði langleiðina í kring. Tóftaleifar eru á fjórum stöðum og allar eru þær á smáhólum. Stærsta tóftin er á hæsta hólnum, 6x9 m. Litlu sunnar, austast í líklegu túni, sést túngarðsleif. Grænabrekka er neðan við melana norðast og skammt sunnan við Grófarlækinn.

42a9d472-d38e-4195-22f2-b672ef95f12c.story_eng: Miðstekkur is the name of grassed-over fragments of old turf walls on a small hill, at the southern and highest edge of the hayfield, right on the boundary between Laufskálar and Víðines. A stekkur was a fold where lambs were penned apart from the ewes. There are ancient ruins here, and Fjóla Gunnlaugsdóttir guessed that this may have been the site of the farm Grafarkot, whose location no one now knows for certain. Others consider this idea far-fetched, as tends to happen.
42a9d472-d38e-4195-22f2-b672ef95f12c.story_is: Miðstekkur heita gróin tóttarbrot á hólkorni syðst og efst í túninu, á landamerkjum Laufskála og Víðiness. Á Miðstekk eru fornar rústir og getur Fjóla Gunnlaugsdóttir sér þess til að þar hafi býlið Grafarkot verið, en enginn veit nú gjörla hvar það hefur verið. Aðrir telja þessa tilgátu fráleita, eins og gengur.

42b38442-e7a5-4252-8726-498bfbead7a4.story_eng: In the days when the school was at Bessastaðir, new pupils were made to roll down the steep northern slope of this hill, and it was done rather roughly. The hill stands close to the buildings, north of the lawn between the house and the church, where a flagpole now stands.
42b38442-e7a5-4252-8726-498bfbead7a4.story_is: Á dögum skólans voru nýsveinar látnir velta sér heldur ómjúklega niður snarbratta brekkuna norður af Bessastaðahól. Hóllinn er heima við bæjarhúsin, norður af flötinni milli húss og kirkju, þar sem fánastöng stendur nú.

42c995ac-6ab4-b832-8871-e383aabcfa3b.story_eng: Gvendarbrunnur is a spring just north of the old track that runs north along the mountain, and it is the first named place along that way. Its water is clean and clear, but the spring runs dry in long spells of drought. Whether it is named after Guðmundur góði (Guðmundur the Good, the bishop of Hólar, a 13th-century bishop said to have blessed many springs and wells) or after some other Gvendur who is now forgotten is hard to say.
42c995ac-6ab4-b832-8871-e383aabcfa3b.story_is: Fari maður gamla veginn norður með fjallinu er Gvendarbrunnur fyrsta örnefnið á þeirri leið. Það er uppsprettulind rétt norðan við götuna. Vatnið í henni er hreint og tært, en hún þrýtur í mikilli þurrkatíð. Hvort lind þessi er kennd við Guðmund góða Hólabiskup eða einhvern annan Gvend, sem nú er gleymdur, er ekki gott að vita.

42e0354e-b3c6-64bf-e9e1-786705561f4a.story_eng: Stekkjartún, close to the river Dalsá, once had a sheep house that held 40 sheep, with a round hay barn beside it. The house was used until the fjárskipti of 1951, when the sheep stock was culled and replaced, and perhaps for longer. A short distance to the east are the ruins of a farm, mostly worn away by wind erosion, which are believed to date from the 10th or 11th century.
42e0354e-b3c6-64bf-e9e1-786705561f4a.story_is: Á Stekkatúninu, skammt frá Dalsá, var fjárhús sem tók 40 kindur og hringlaga hlaða við. Húsið var notað fram að fjárskiptum 1951 og ef til vill lengur. Skammt austan við Stekkatúnið eru bæjarrústir, að mestu uppblásnar, taldar vera frá 10. eða 11. öld.

42e20d13-b44b-770e-3e4f-3093c07c0789.story_eng: Hrútakofi, meaning ram hut, was also called Syðstahús, the southernmost house. It stood in the south-eastern corner of the home field at Hellnasel, with a ridge of bare rock to its north. The hut lay in ruins for some years but was rebuilt in 1927 and could hold about 20 lambs.
42e20d13-b44b-770e-3e4f-3093c07c0789.story_is: Hrútakofi, einnig kallaður Syðstahús, er suðaustur í túnhorninu á Hellnaseli. Þar er klapparhryggur að norðan. Kofinn lá niðri um nokkur ár en var endurbyggður 1927 og tekur um 20 lömb.

42fe34d1-1cc3-d7c5-619e-90de70010da3.story_eng: A folk tale explains the name of this large boulder, which is split in two. Once there was a farmer in Haukadalur named Páll who was given to stealing. He went into hiding as an outlaw in a cave not far from the farm, but when people discovered where he was, he fled to this stone and stayed in the cleft of the rock. He was found again and chased from here by men both on horseback and on foot. It is said that he collapsed and died of exhaustion on Geitasandur below Reyðarvatn. The stone marks the meeting point of the lands of Kot, Dagverðarnes and the common highland pasture, and it can be seen from Austurtún, the eastern home field of Kot.
42fe34d1-1cc3-d7c5-619e-90de70010da3.story_is: Til er þjóðsaga um uppruna nafns Pálssteins: Einu sinni var bóndi í Haukadal er Páll hét. Hann var þjófgefinn og lagðist út í helli sem er þar skammt frá bænum. En menn urðu varir við hvar hann var og flúði hann þá til Pálssteins og hélt þar til í klettaskorunni. En hans varð vart á ný og var hann þá eltur þaðan, bæði ríðandi og gangandi. Mælt er að hann hafi sprungið á Geitasandi fyrir neðan Reyðarvatn. Steinninn er allstór og klofinn í tvennt og sést af Austurtúni. Í honum mætast lönd Kots og Dagverðarness og Kots og afréttarins.

430b4698-5f35-b233-dce4-cb32ffe23ae3.story_eng: Króaklettar are rocks just outside the farm's home field, above the shore called Króaklettsfjara. Against the side of the rocks stands an old wall built of stone, known simply as Grjótgarður, meaning 'stone wall'.
430b4698-5f35-b233-dce4-cb32ffe23ae3.story_is: Króaklettur er utan við túnið, upp af Króaklettsfjöru. Utan í Króaklettum er gamall garður úr grjóti og er hann nefndur Grjótgarður.

430f4d33-e06c-9755-6b2e-e6d85544c758.story_eng: The name Tjaldhóll means 'tent hill', and it suggests that people once pitched tents by the hill. There are reliable accounts that travellers were allowed to graze their horses on the land of Laugarnes, and perhaps also Bústaðir, while they went about their business in Reykjavík. The hill once marked the boundary of Kópavogur at Fossvogur. It lay on the bank above Hangandi, a short way from Hafnarfjarðarvegur and north of the Nesti petrol station in Fossvogur.
