It proved to be one of the most remarkable pagan graves from the Settlement Age ever found in Iceland. A rich chieftain had been buried here with his horse, his weapons and his jewellery. A porridge bowl found among the grave goods attracted a great deal of attention. The grave, with its original features, is now at the National Museum of Iceland, and few traces remain on the gravel knoll where it was found. The knoll rises fairly high, and it has been suggested that the departed chieftain could look out far and wide from his resting place.
5c5efae9-7a15-451e-baf3-7e20637f169e.story_is: Árið 1995 fannst fornmannsgröf rétt sunnan Þórisár í Skriðdal, spölkorn ofan við þjóðveginn. Þetta reyndist eitt merkasta kuml frá landnámsöld sem fundist hefur hér á landi. Ríkur höfðingi hefur verið heygður þar ásamt hesti sínum, vopnum og skartgripum. Grautarskál, sem fannst meðal munanna, vakti mikla athygli. Kumlið er með upphaflegum ummerkjum á Þjóðminjasafni Íslands, en á melkollinum þar sem það fannst eru fá ummerki. Melurinn rís nokkuð hátt í landi og tilgátan er sú að hinn gengni höfðingi hafi séð vel yfir frá legstað sínum.

5c7325b6-7c60-f541-0b60-42e1ae4c84c9.story_eng: Tungnavað is a ford across the river Skjálfandafljót, where the water breaks over a shallow stretch, a little north of the pool Hylur. It was crossed on horseback just above the tip of the gravel bank Tungnavaðseyri. The ford takes its name from the road that ran between the two farms called Tungur, Litlatunga and Stóratunga. Its bed is made of columnar basalt, which makes it firm underfoot but hard to cross for anyone who does not know it.
5c7325b6-7c60-f541-0b60-42e1ae4c84c9.story_is: Nokkru norðan við Hyl er brot á Skjálfandafljóti sem heitir Tungnavað, og er riðið rétt ofan við oddann á Tungnavaðseyri. Nafnið er dregið af því að vegurinn lá milli Tungnanna, Litlutungu og Stórutungu. Botninn í vaðinu er stuðlaberg og því traustur en vandfarinn nema kunnugum.

5c84c9c9-4acd-874f-0e10-0349267a2816.story_eng: Nýrækt, meaning 'new cultivation', is the oldest newly cultivated field belonging to the farm Grímshús, dating from 1927. It was broken with a tractor, the first one to come to this area. The machine was owned by Karl and Bjarni of Fótaskinn and Sigurður of Fagranes.
5c84c9c9-4acd-874f-0e10-0349267a2816.story_is: Elsta nýræktin frá Grímshúsum, frá árinu 1927. Hún var unnin með dráttarvél, þeirri fyrstu sem kom á þetta svæði. Karl og Bjarni í Fótaskinni og Sigurður í Fagranesi áttu vélina.

5c961d6c-8ead-8319-ffa2-d90bc1880f9c.story_eng: This cliff rises above the stretch of shore called Gripdeild, which runs from the stream Selvogsneslækur to Grasdalsvarp. Its name comes from a story about the shore below. The farmer of Ós and the farmer of Njarðvík are said to have quarrelled there over the driftage, the right to driftwood and anything else washed up on the beach. They settled it with their fists, and the Njarðvík farmer won. Since then the driftage there has belonged to Njarðvík. Gripdeild is an Icelandic word for seizing or grabbing something by force.
5c961d6c-8ead-8319-ffa2-d90bc1880f9c.story_is: Ofan við Gripdeild við sjóinn heitir Gripdeildarflug, en Gripdeild nær frá Selvogsneslæk að Grasdalsvarpi. Um Gripdeild er sú saga að Ósbóndi og Njarðvíkurbóndi deildu þar um reka og létu hendur skipta, og hafði Njarðvíkurbóndi betur. Síðan hefur reki þar tilheyrt Njarðvík.

5c9651ea-a2c4-4542-6fbe-f7d9aded4135.story_eng: Bótarfjall is a mountain east of the Skarðslækur stream, somewhat lower than its neighbour Reykjafjall. Its name comes from an old arrangement between two farms. The farmer at Heiðarbót was allowed to graze his livestock on this land in return for Þverárteigur, a piece of Heiðarbót's own land where the farmer at Þverá cut hay.
5c9651ea-a2c4-4542-6fbe-f7d9aded4135.story_is: Austan við Skarðslækinn er fjall, heldur lægra en Reykjafjall, sem heitir Bótarfjall. Nafnið er dregið af því að þetta land mátti Heiðarbótarbóndinn nota til beitar í stað Þverárteigs í Heiðarbótarlandi, sem Þverárbóndi hafði til slægna hjá honum.

5c9ff7b8-75f5-8adf-a077-b2d2efd3c472.story_eng: Klaufarbrekka is a slope below the grassy strip called Klaufargeiri. The grazing here is rich, and early in the summer the milking ewes from the farm Ásgeirsbrekka were herded and watched over here. It was a very long way to bring them, yet the milkmaids claimed they could tell from the milk pail when the ewes had not grazed here that day.
5c9ff7b8-75f5-8adf-a077-b2d2efd3c472.story_is: Niður af Klaufinni er grasivaxinn geiri nefndur Klaufargeiri og neðar Klaufarbrekka. Þarna er kjarngott beitiland og þarna voru kvíaær frá Ásgeirsbrekku setnar framan af sumri. Þetta er afar löng leið, en þó þóttust mjaltakonurnar finna það á fötunni ef ærnar höfðu ekki verið þarna þann daginn.

5ca6f5aa-3aaa-10ed-ec28-7c0c1843d1a3.name_eng: Loftstóft, ruins of a sheep house
5ca6f5aa-3aaa-10ed-ec28-7c0c1843d1a3.story_eng: The ruins of a sheep house west of Ópugil were once the sauðahús of Loftur of Vatnsnes, a house for his sauðir, or wethers (castrated rams kept for wool and meat). The name means Loftur's ruin. Loftur was last recorded as farming there in 1913. Before that he had lived for a long time at Vatnsnes, and he was the last to keep wethers.
5ca6f5aa-3aaa-10ed-ec28-7c0c1843d1a3.story_is: Fjárhústættur vestan við Ópugil voru sauðahús Lofts í Vatnsnesi. Hann var þar síðast búandi árið 1913, en bjó áður lengi í Vatnsnesi og hafði síðastur sauði.

5cac480f-e81c-431a-82da-df0b668f43bc.story_eng: Sortudý was a wet mire hole low in the marsh called Sortumýri, just south of the farm's old home-field wall. Animal skins were once laid in the mire to rot, and this was called að bereyða. The land has since been drained, and the exact spot of the mire has been lost.
5cac480f-e81c-431a-82da-df0b668f43bc.story_is: Neðarlega í Sortumýri, sunnan við túngarð, var Sortudý. Í dýið voru látin skinn til rotnunar og var það kallað að bereyða. Mýrin hefur verið ræst fram og staðsetning dýsins er týnd.

5cb743ff-d262-37d5-6ee5-7d3faaead877.story_eng: Skógarselsgötur were old riding paths that led from Hólar to Skógarsel, at the southern end of Seljadalur. A sel was a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked. Just outside and above the farm Bollastaði, these paths crossed Götur, which was the main route along the west side of Reykjadalur before a road was built and in places ran quite high on the hillside. In the land of Kárhóll, near the boundary, Skógarselsgötur run southwest through a pass called Götuskarð.
5cb743ff-d262-37d5-6ee5-7d3faaead877.story_is: Skógarselsgötur voru reiðgötur frá Hólum í Skógarsel syðst í Seljadal. Rétt fyrir utan og ofan Bollastaði skerast þær og Götur, sem voru alfaraleið um Reykjadal að vestan áður en vegur var lagður og lágu sums staðar allhátt í hlíðinni. Í Kárhólslandi, næst merkjum, er Götuskarð, og um það liggja Skógarselsgötur til suðvesturs.

5cbe955e-ef32-1b5a-59d8-af3a4ff343bf.story_eng: Ancient riding tracks and an old main route once crossed the grassy flats of Stóriflötur and Gatnaflötur, south of Hestamó. The route led to a ford on the river Arnarvatnsá and passed right through the farmyard of the farm.
5cbe955e-ef32-1b5a-59d8-af3a4ff343bf.story_is: Um Austurfleti, þar á meðal Stóraflöt og Gatnaflöt sunnan við Hestamó, lágu fornar reiðgötur og þjóðleið að vaði á Arnarvatnsá og um hlaðið á bænum.

5cc5a4ad-e311-f093-f35b-9f59b35fa64a.story_eng: Seen from the farm Skápadal, the sun stands over this ravine at dagmál, the old Icelandic name for mid-morning, so it served as a day-mark for telling the time. The farm is said to have once stood here, before a landslide destroyed it. The ravine lies just beyond the farm, on the side away from the sea, as one comes into the valley.
5cc5a4ad-e311-f093-f35b-9f59b35fa64a.story_is: Frá Skápadal eru dagmál í Dagmálagili. Þar var bærinn áður en skriða eyðilagði hann. Gilið er framan við bæinn, fjær sjó, þegar komið er inn í dalinn.

5cd1f054-0682-48d9-a2cc-bdaf6227e87e.name_eng: Bugar, ruins of an abandoned farm
5cd1f054-0682-48d9-a2cc-bdaf6227e87e.story_eng: These are the ruins of an abandoned farm that was once a hjáleiga, a small tenant croft belonging to the farm Ásgautsstaðir. People settled here long before 1700, but the croft often stood empty for decades at a time. It was finally abandoned in 1906, and only ruins remain.
5cd1f054-0682-48d9-a2cc-bdaf6227e87e.story_is: Hér eru rústir eyðibýlis sem var hjáleiga frá Ásgautsstöðum. Hófst þar byggð löngu fyrir 1700 en var oft í eyði áratugum saman og fór endanlega úr byggð árið 1906.

5ce2328a-34b6-c92a-c183-d29fe51fb9b0.story_eng: Litlaparadís, meaning Little Paradise, is a grassy patch in the meadow called Paradísarengi (Paradise Meadow) by Ljóskugróf. It has a companion named Stóraparadís, Great Paradise. According to local tradition, these names come from womanising.
5ce2328a-34b6-c92a-c183-d29fe51fb9b0.story_is: Í Paradísarengi við Ljóskugróf eru Litlaparadís og Stóraparadís. Þessi nöfn eru kennd við kvennafar að sögn.

5cedc817-5aab-2bd7-085f-b1329697ead0.story_eng: Leyningur is a hollow running to the northeast with hills on both sides, east of the church and some way from the stream. Just north of it stood a sheep house with two feeding rows, known as Kerhús (also Karhús), where a concrete tub (baðkar) had been cast. High up in the hollow was Hannesarkofi, a small hut named after Hannes Pétursson, a maker of hagldir (the wooden or horn rings used on pack-horse ropes). The hut is now completely gone; it was removed when the home fields were levelled.
5cedc817-5aab-2bd7-085f-b1329697ead0.story_is: Leyningur er austur undan kirkjunni og nokkuð frá læknum. Hann liggur til norðausturs og hólar eru beggja megin við hann. Rétt norðan við Leyning voru fjárhús, tveggja garða, sem voru nefnd Kerhús (Karhús), en þar var steypt baðkar. Ofarlega í Leyningi var Hannesarkofi, sem kenndur var við Hannes Pétursson hagldasmið. Hannesarkofi er alveg horfinn, hann vék vegna túnasléttunar.

5cf9cb4d-3b39-9945-db93-346a1c9fad46.story_eng: Folaldamór, the foals' moor, is a very tussocky, grassy moor lying between gravel ridges, with Miðaftanshólar to the north and the long east–west ridge of Langimelur to the south. During the years Björn Þorkelsson farmed here, it was a fixed rule that the hay cut from this moor was given to the foals.
5cf9cb4d-3b39-9945-db93-346a1c9fad46.story_is: Sunnan við Miðaftanshóla var lækur og sunnan við hann Langimelur, sem er aflangur austur-vestur. Á milli þessara mela er mjög þýfður grasmór sem heitir Folaldamór. Á búskaparárum Björns Þorkelssonar var það föst regla að gefa folöldunum heyið úr þessum mó.

5d0ba196-df8e-da1c-dfcc-6caba440fc7f.story_eng: Breiðamýri is believed by most to be the same marsh that in ancient times was called Skálamýri, which marked the southern boundary of the land claim of Kráku-Hreiðar, one of the early settlers. Eiríkur, the settler at Goðdalir, gave him "the whole Tunga down from Skálamýri." By that account, Hreiðar's land reached from Hafgrímsstaðir in the south out to the end of Reykjatunga, where the land of Vindheimar is now. The old name fits: from many angles the marsh does look rather like a bowl (skál). It is a flat, fully overgrown marsh, roughly round but slightly elongated from northeast to southwest. It was once hard to cross in places because it was so wet, but it has now been drained. The boundary between the farms Litlidalur and Brúnastaðir runs across the gravel banks at its upper, northern end, and the marsh drains southwest into the brook.
5d0ba196-df8e-da1c-dfcc-6caba440fc7f.story_is: Flest rök mæla með því að Breiðamýri sé hin sama og til forna var nefnd Skálamýri og afmarkaði landnám Kráku-Hreiðars að sunnan. Eiríkur landnámsmaður í Goðdölum gaf honum „Tunguna alla niður frá Skálamýri.“ Samkvæmt því hefur landnám Hreiðars náð sunnan frá Hafgrímsstöðum út á enda Reykjatungunnar þar sem nú er land Vindheima. Mýrin sýnist óneitanlega býsna skálarlaga frá ýmsum sjónarhornum. Þetta er flöt mýri, algróin, áður illfær á köflum vegna bleytu en nú uppþurrkuð. Hún er nokkurn veginn hringlaga, þó aðeins aflöng frá norðaustri til suðvesturs. Efst í henni, á melum norðantil, eru landamerkin milli Litladals og Brúnastaða. Afrennsli er til suðvesturs í Lækinn.

5d55560a-7953-cf2e-5505-2b3362f575f6.story_eng: Vallargarður is the turf wall that once enclosed the home field of Hvammkot, an abandoned farm on the east side of the road, opposite Kárastaðir. The home field measured about four dagsláttur (an old measure of hayfield area) and was walled all the way around with turf. The wall can still be made out in most places, though it has slumped flat and in some stretches has disappeared. The farm ruins lie only on Klapparhól, the knoll above the marsh along which the road runs. There is a very long ruin, much the highest in the middle, a fairly long one to the south, and a much smaller one to the north, with what looks like a wall in front. Between 1870 and 1880 there were horse stables at the deserted farm, and when Gísli Gunnarsson lived here a few goats were kept there and milked in summer.
5d55560a-7953-cf2e-5505-2b3362f575f6.story_is: Hvammkot var eyðibýli austan við veginn, á móti Kárastöðum, fyrir ofan mýrarflóann. Túnstærð var um 4 dagsláttur og hefur túnið verið algirt með torfgarði. Vallargarður er umhverfis og hann er víðast glöggur, en þó útflattur og sumstaðar horfinn. Rústir sjást ekki annars staðar en á sjálfum bæjarhólnum, Klapparhól. Þar er mjög löng rúst, miklu hæst í miðjunni. Sunnan við er alllöng rúst, óskipt að sjá, og norðan við miklu minni rúst, og framan við er eins og verið hafi garður. Neðan undir bæjarhólnum er mýri og vegurinn liggur eftir henni. Milli 1870 og 1880 voru hesthús á eyðibýlinu, og er Gísli Gunnarsson bjó hér voru hafðar þarna nokkrar geitur og þær nytjaðar á sumrin.

5d8d7d60-1463-f9a3-7100-2d1ea121e2f5.story_eng: Kálfatjörn means calves' pond, and it is said that two calves perished here. According to local oral tradition, a nykur, the water horse of Icelandic folklore, was supposed to have had an underground passage between Kálfatjörn and the lake Stapavatn. The pond has never dried up, even though drainage ditches run just south of it, since the wetland to the north remains untouched. It lies at the foot of the ridge Hálsinn, at the northern end of the wetland called Flóinn.
5d8d7d60-1463-f9a3-7100-2d1ea121e2f5.story_is: Sagt er að í Kálfatjörn hafi farist tveir kálfar. Munnmæli herma að nykur hafi átt að hafa jarðgöng á milli Kálfatjarnar og Stapavatns. Kálfatjörn hefur ekki þornað þótt skurðir séu rétt sunnan við hana, enda er Flóinn norðan við óspilltur. Tjörnin er austan undir Hálsinum, við norðurenda Flóans.

5dcb4635-4ccb-40de-5a33-b3b15874e344.story_eng: Gíslamór was the southernmost part of the home field Niðurtún. It was named after Gísli Finnsson, who farmed at Hamar in Stífla from 1836 to 1860. Gísli is believed to have used this patch of moor for a while to cut hay, because the home field at Hamar was very small. Gíslamór is among the places in Stífla that have since disappeared under water.
5dcb4635-4ccb-40de-5a33-b3b15874e344.story_is: Syðsti hluti Niðurtúns hét Gíslamór, kenndur við Gísla Finnsson, bónda á Hamri í Stíflu frá 1836 til 1860. Er talið að Gísli hafi um skeið haft móinn til slægna en tún var mjög lítið á Hamri. Gíslamór er meðal þeirra örnefna sem hurfu undir vatn.

5df6d1df-dee7-5745-0688-a6638036ddd1.story_eng: The farm of Dagverðarnes stood high on the southern side of a ridge, with a wide view in all directions. The land was once wooded: a tradition still survives that tents of woodcutters stood at Dagverðarnes, much like the tents of haymakers at Safamýri during the mowing season. The farm was abandoned in 1912, when its buildings collapsed in earthquakes and rebuilding them was not thought feasible.
5df6d1df-dee7-5745-0688-a6638036ddd1.story_is: Dagverðarnes stóð hátt sunnan í brún og er mikið víðsýni þaðan. Landareignin hefur áður verið skógivaxin, því sögn er enn til um það að í Dagverðarnesi hafi verið tjöld skógarhöggsmanna, líkt og heyskaparmanna við Safamýri um sláttinn. Bærinn fór í eyði árið 1912. Hús féllu þá í jarðskjálftum og ekki þótti fært að byggja þau upp aftur.

5e18f8dc-3636-294b-f023-44a48ae2c89a.story_eng: Legend has it that a hairy paw came out of this cliff holding a skálm, a knife, and cut the rope of a man who had been lowered down the cliff face, so that he fell to his death. The name Skálmabjörg, also known as Skálmar, is said to come from this story.
5e18f8dc-3636-294b-f023-44a48ae2c89a.story_is: Sagan segir að loðin loppa hafi komið út úr bjarginu með skálm (hníf) sem skar á festi sigmanns svo að hann hrapaði til bana. Af þessari frásögn kemur nafnið Skálmabjörg.

5e1d98b8-898d-5404-b40b-8ee28cad7973.story_eng: Hamramýri was an álagablettur, an enchanted spot under a spell, and it was not to be mown. If anyone cut the hay here, it was supposed to cost the life of a large farm animal, such as a cow or a horse.
5e1d98b8-898d-5404-b40b-8ee28cad7973.story_is: Hamramýri er álagablettur. Hana mátti ekki slá. Ef hún var slegin átti það að kosta stórgrip.

5e376858-d4ce-4d40-9a1a-838157023837.story_eng: Grettisstillur, 'Grettir's stepping stones', are large stones lying in the river. Oral tradition says that Grettir (Grettir the Strong, the outlaw hero of the sagas) put them in the river so that he could cross with dry feet. The writer of the description did not accept this. He wrote that the stones were already lying on the gravel flats when the river shifted its course there. He allowed that Grettir may once have used them to cross, since a nimble, vigorous man could well run over the river on them when the water is low. But the stones are far too big for any one man to lift or move.
5e376858-d4ce-4d40-9a1a-838157023837.story_is: Eru það stórir steinar sem eru í ánni. Ekki heita þeir svo vegna þess að Grettir hafi sett steina þessa í ána til þess að ganga þar þurrum fótum yfir eins og munnmælin herma, heldur hafa þessir steinar verið á melunum þegar áin breytti farvegi sínum þangað. Má vera að Grettir hafi einhvern tímann notað þá til þess, því það er ekki loku fyrir það skotið að vaskleikamaður geti hlaupið á þeim yfir ána þegar hún er eilítil, en þeir eru ærið of stórir til þess að einn maður megi hefja þá eða hreyfa.

5e45a8b2-0e80-a572-aeec-c0ab25105c17.story_eng: Háfsvatnsdæld, also called Háfsvatnadæld, is a deep hollow west of Háfsvatn holding two small lakes, Háfsvatn and Leirvatnslón. The area was once rich in birdlife, ducks among them, and there are stories that birds were caught on the lakes with a háfur, a hand net.
5e45a8b2-0e80-a572-aeec-c0ab25105c17.story_is: Háfsvatnsdæld eða Háfsvatnadæld er djúp dæld vestan Háfsvatns eða Háfsvatnaöldu með tveimur vötnum, Háfsvatni og Leirvatnslóni. Á þessu svæði var mikið fuglalíf, til dæmis önd, og sagnir eru um að fugl hafi verið veiddur með háf á vötnunum.

5e54258d-7978-7ecb-8336-2e46321cf627.story_eng: Vetrarleið, the 'winter route', was the way earlier generations crossed west over the Héraðsvötn river. It lay near the boundary between Helluland and Utanverðunes and led down and west onto Borgarsandur. This was one of the first places where the ice on the river became strong enough to bear a horse. It was also the site of the northern of the two Helluland fords. The other ford ran from the meadow around the northern end of Kríuhólmi and up onto Skógar, where a cutting had been made in the bank that can probably still be seen. The ford no longer exists.
5e54258d-7978-7ecb-8336-2e46321cf627.story_is: Leið forfeðranna vestur yfir Héraðsvötnin, kölluð Vetrarleið, var út undir landamerkjum Hellulands og Utanverðuness. Lá hún þar niður og vestur á Borgarsand. Þar kom einna fyrst hestfær ís á Vötnin og þar var norðara Hellulandsvaðið. Hellulandsvöðin voru tvö. Annað þeirra var þar sem Vetrarleiðin var, en hitt af enginu, um norðurenda Kríuhólma, og upp á Skóga þar sem gert hafði verið vik, sem líklega sést ennþá.

5e57e53f-5e42-36c3-2e2b-0e0d0cfe094d.story_eng: The outlines of three haystacks (desjar) can still be clearly made out at Heygarður. Hay from the episcopal seat of Skálholt is said to have been stacked here. Beside the hay yard lies a round, ball-shaped basalt stone. According to legend, the men of Skálholt did not consider anyone fit for haymaking at Útverk unless he could lift this stone to his shoulder with one hand, equally well with either hand. It surely took a man of at least average strength.
5e57e53f-5e42-36c3-2e2b-0e0d0cfe094d.story_is: Mótar vel fyrir þremur desjum í Heygarði. Á þar að hafa verið borið saman hey frá Skálholtsstað. Við Heygarðinn er kúlulaga blágrýtissteinn. Honum fylgir sú sögn að Skálholtsmenn hafi eigi talið þann mann færan til heyskapar í Útverkum sem ekki gat jafnhent stein þann annarri hendi og jafnt hvorri sem var. Víst þurfti meðalmann til.

5e6d6d2d-a8c8-f222-39b6-0a9340e2bfe1.story_eng: Hæringshlaup, meaning Hæringur's leap, is the southernmost part of the Drangey cliffs. Hæringur is said to have climbed the island where no one had ever gone before, meaning to come at the brothers from behind. When Illugi turned to face him, Hæringur went over the edge here.
5e6d6d2d-a8c8-f222-39b6-0a9340e2bfe1.story_is: Syðsti hluti Drangeyjarbjargs. Sagt er að Hæringur hafi farið fram af því þegar Illugi sneri móti honum, en Hæringur hugðist koma aftan að þeim bræðrum eftir að hafa klifið eyna þar sem enginn hafði áður farið.

5e77f909-9392-2915-da94-5196de836137.story_eng: Grænhóll was a small, grassy hillock where the children of Blesastaðir used to play, keeping their own little pretend farm there. In 1954 Hermann built a sheep house and a hay barn on the spot, and the hillock gave way to the barn, so it no longer exists. A candle factory has since operated there.
5e77f909-9392-2915-da94-5196de836137.story_is: Þetta var lítill og gróinn hóll og var áður leiksvæði barnanna á Blesastöðum, sem höfðu þar bú. Hermann byggði þar fjárhús og hlöðu árið 1954 og vék þá hóllinn fyrir hlöðunni. Þar hefur verið kertaverksmiðja.

5e9931f4-a465-1489-9ee0-ba1b45940b13.story_eng: On Belgholt stands a stone shaped like a smiðjubelgur, the bellows of a smithy, and its surface is wrinkled all over. North of the hill runs a stream called Bugalækur.
5e9931f4-a465-1489-9ee0-ba1b45940b13.story_is: Á Belgholti er steinn sem líkist smiðjubelg í laginu og er allur hrukkóttur. Norðan við Belgholt er lækur sem heitir Bugalækur.

5e9cebd8-ca2f-8483-b796-3db99b9b892a.story_eng: Bæjarpollur is a fishing spot on the river along Mjóubakkar, the narrow banks south of Syðri-Laugahvammur, and there is said to be a story behind the name. Road workers once pitched their tents very close by. One of them, Stefán Tómasson from Brettingsstaðir in Laxárdalur, was a keen fisherman, and he often slipped away to this spot with his rod. The road workers felt that their food always took a turn for the better after these fishing trips.
5e9cebd8-ca2f-8483-b796-3db99b9b892a.story_is: Meðfram ánni sunnan Syðri-Laugahvamms heita Mjóubakkar og veiðistaður þar nefnist Bæjarpollur. Er saga til nafnsins. Vegavinnumenn höfðu eitt sinn tjöld sín þar örskammt frá, og einn úr þeirra hópi, mikil veiðisál, Stefán Tómasson frá Brettingsstöðum í Laxárdal, skrapp oft á þennan stað með stöng sína. Þótti vegavinnumönnum jafnan bregða til hins betra um viðurværi sitt eftir þær veiðiferðir.

5eb14c77-3e08-493d-1165-5a7949215911.story_eng: Hátún is an ancient abandoned farm, probably dating back to the Settlement Age. An old oral tradition among the people of Fram-Vellir says that the farm once had 18 doors hung on hinges. The mountain Höttur was in old times called Hátúnahöttur, after this farm. Settlement here is believed to have ended during the Black Death. Later, the main farm of the Hátún lands (Hátúnatorfa) was built at Tunguhagi.
5eb14c77-3e08-493d-1165-5a7949215911.story_is: Hér er fornt eyðibýli, sennilega síðan á landnámsöld. Forn munnmælasaga meðal Fram-Vellinga segir að þar hafi verið 18 hurðir á hjörum. Fjallið Höttur hét að fornu Hátúnahöttur. Talið er að byggð hafi lagst af í Svartadauða. Seinna var aðalbýli Hátúnatorfunnar reist í Tunguhaga.

5eb69ba6-a592-b683-3168-1da79e33224a.story_eng: Þorsteinsþúfa is a fairly large mound in the hayfield just below the farmhouse at Þorsteinsstaðir, about 50 metres from the dwelling, and it has never been disturbed. It is built in the shape of a cross, and for that reason it has also been called Krossþúfa (Cross Mound). It once stood among tussocks below the farmyard, but the ground around it has since been mostly levelled. An old tradition, backed, it is said, by experience, holds that the mound must not be touched, and that anyone who disturbs it will suffer harm; hence its other name, Álagaþúfa (Spell Mound). Some say that the man the farm was named after, Þorsteinn, lies buried beneath it, while others say he lies in a gravel hillock down in the marshes called Þorsteinshóll.
5eb69ba6-a592-b683-3168-1da79e33224a.story_is: Þorsteinsþúfa er í túninu skammt neðan við bæinn á Þorsteinsstöðum, eða um 50 metra frá íbúðarhúsinu, og er óhreyfð. Það er gömul sögn (og reynsla) að ekki megi hrófla við þúfunni, en ef það sé gert verði menn fyrir tjóni. Þúfan er allstór og byggð í kross, og hefur hún einnig verið kölluð Krossþúfa. Var hún áður í þýfi fyrir neðan hlaðið, en nú er sléttað að mestu umhverfis hana. Sumir segja að maður sá, er bærinn fékk nafn af, liggi undir henni, en aðrir, að hann liggi í melhóli niðri í mýrum, er heitir Þorsteinshóll.

5ecf5f19-85f4-1b8b-f7e3-9b3362da7644.story_eng: Íshústjörn, the "ice-house pond", was a hollow east of the church that was flooded with water from the stream Kaupstaðalækur when the frosts set in. Ice was carried from it to the ice house, where bait was kept. When the pond was frozen, it was also used for skating. The place no longer exists.
5ecf5f19-85f4-1b8b-f7e3-9b3362da7644.story_is: Lægð austan við kirkjuna sem vatni var veitt í úr Kaupstaðalæknum þegar frysta tók. Var ís fluttur þaðan í íshúsið þar sem beita var geymd. Tjörnin var og notuð til skautaiðkana þegar ís var á henni. Tjörnin er ekki lengur til.

5ed7e34a-94b5-8d8c-106c-815f17aa2d46.story_eng: In 1927 old bones were found deep down in a lava hole on this mound of lava, just west of the lava cave Víðgelmir. It is considered quite likely that the bones belong to Skeggi, the first man Grettir killed, and the place fits strikingly well with Grettis saga, the saga of the outlaw Grettir. The mound was given its name, Skeggjabunga (Skeggi's mound), when the bones were found.
5ed7e34a-94b5-8d8c-106c-815f17aa2d46.story_is: Rétt vestan við Víðgelmi er hraunbunga sem nefnd er Skeggjabunga. Þar fundust gömul bein niðri í djúpri hraunholu árið 1927. Eru taldar miklar líkur á að bein þessi séu úr Skeggja þeim er Grettir vó fyrstan manna, enda kemur staðurinn einkennilega vel heim við Grettlu. Fékk hraunbungan nafn sitt þegar beinin fundust.

5ed87297-7c1c-462b-985d-e12cb0eb98af.story_eng: Dómhæð means 'judgement hill'. It was said that court judgements were once held here. It lies to the west of a mound called Taðhóll.
5ed87297-7c1c-462b-985d-e12cb0eb98af.story_is: Sagt var að á Dómhæð hefðu farið fram dómar. Hún er vestur af Taðhól.

5ee8d0e7-adb6-35ea-10c4-f7eccf1afc4d.story_eng: Skriðlaut, roughly "crawling hollow", gets its name from a mishap during haymaking. One day, while Jón Eymd was making hay here, someone sent him fresh salmon from the farm Útverk. He ate it so heartily that he got stomach pains so severe he thought he would barely survive. He dragged himself around the hollow, crawling and rolling about, and that is how the place got its name.
5ee8d0e7-adb6-35ea-10c4-f7eccf1afc4d.story_is: Þegar Jón Eymd var þarna að heyja gerðist það dag einn að honum var sendur nýr lax frá Útverkum að borða. Tók hann svo hraustlega til matarins að hann fékk af því svo mikla magaverki að hann hugði sér naumast líf. Dróst hann þá um lautina, skreið þar um og velti sér. Er nafnið þar af komið.

5eea5ab8-4eda-400c-ba86-2cb97c2701d1.story_eng: Beinaverksmiðjan, 'the bone factory', stands east of the road, a short distance from the hill Stöðlakotshæð. It was built in 1953 by the people of Eyrarbakki and Stokkseyri, who ground their fish waste there.
5eea5ab8-4eda-400c-ba86-2cb97c2701d1.story_is: Austan vegarins, örskammt frá Stöðlakotshæðinni, er Beinaverksmiðjan. Hún var byggð 1953 af Eyrbekkingum og Stokkseyringum. Þar mala þeir fiskiúrganginn sinn.

5eeb9e83-fb8c-5321-aa3d-95e819fd0c97.story_eng: The name means roughly 'old farm patch'. This tongue of land has now gone under water, and only a single ruin still rises above the surface. The farm of Á stood here before 'the Fire' (Eldur), as the description calls it. Soon after the Fire the farm was moved east to Gamla-Á, and not long after that it was moved again.
5eeb9e83-fb8c-5321-aa3d-95e819fd0c97.story_is: Torfan er komin í vatn og aðeins ein tóft stendur upp úr. Bærinn að Á stóð þar fyrir Eld. Hann var fluttur austur að Gömlu-Á fyrst eftir Eld en var fluttur þaðan skömmu seinna.

5f094a78-3cfd-d5ca-7149-f066eb67ce63.story_eng: Húsandarvik is a small cove on the river Laxá, opposite Helluvað and just below the spot where a cable ferry (kláfur) once crossed the river from 1912 until after 1940. Only the wires of the ferry remain, but its name, Kláfurinn, has stayed alive among local people. The name Húsandarvik, which refers to the húsönd (Barrow's goldeneye, a duck), is not an old place name.
5f094a78-3cfd-d5ca-7149-f066eb67ce63.story_is: Gegnt Helluvaði, neðan við Kláfinn, er Húsandarvik, ekki gamalt örnefni. Skammt ofan við Helluvaðsfót var kláfur á Laxá frá 1912 fram yfir 1940. Þar eru nú einungis vírarnir eftir en örnefnið hefur hlotið sess í vitund heimamanna.

5f13f119-f1ca-47ab-91fa-03f283cc46cd.story_eng: There were old stories of a bænhús, a small prayer house or chapel, at the farm Syðriskál (Syðri-Leikskálaá), but the place where it had stood was believed to be completely lost. That changed when digging began for a braggi, an arched hut-style building, out from and below the farmhouse. Human bones appeared in the bank. It was then decided to close the bank up again, preserve the site undisturbed and move the building a few metres. A resident of Syðriskál who worked on the job was a butcher, and he realised at once that these were not the bones of farm animals. The prayer house itself no longer exists.
5f13f119-f1ca-47ab-91fa-03f283cc46cd.story_is: Sagnir voru um bænhús á Syðriskál (Syðri-Leikskálaá) og talið að staðurinn þar sem það stóð hefði með öllu glatast, þar til farið var að grafa fyrir braggabyggingu út og niður af bænum. Í bakkanum komu í ljós mannabein og var þá ákveðið að ganga frá, loka bakkanum, varðveita staðinn óraskaðan og færa bygginguna um nokkra metra. Þess má geta að íbúi á Syðriskál sem vann við verkið er kjötiðnaðarmaður og áttaði sig strax á að þarna var ekki um bein úr húsdýrum að ræða.

5f20bd58-f704-457a-047c-4b280bb60e0b.story_eng: Vilhjálmsvör is a fairly large landing cove where the cliffs give way to low banks. It is named after a certain Vilhjálmur who had rowed out to fish from here, and the name is thought to be old. It was never a good landing, as the shore is stony and there was little shelter from onshore seas, except mainly from a westerly swell. One fine, calm evening in the spring of 1899, a French schooner named Telephone sailed into Vilhjálmsvör, or was carried there largely by the southward tidal current. The ship was said to have sprung a leak, but people found something suspicious about it. The catch was apparently small, and it was believed the crew had wanted to get away from the fishing. Most of the ship and its contents were salvaged and a large auction was held.
5f20bd58-f704-457a-047c-4b280bb60e0b.story_is: Þegar berginu sleppir eru lágir bakkar. Þar er vör allstór sem kennd er við Vilhjálm nokkurn er hafði róið þaðan og mun það nafn gamalt. Ekki er hægt að segja að landtaka sé þar góð því að fjaran er grýtt og lítið var í hafátt nema þó helst fyrir vestansjó. Vorið 1899 sigldi frönsk skonnorta, Telephone að nafni, kvöld eitt í blíðskaparveðri upp í Vilhjálmsvör, eða barst þangað að miklu leyti með suðurfallinu. Átti að hafa komist leki að skipinu en eitthvað þótti það grunsamlegt. Afli þótti víst lítill og ætluðu menn að skipshöfnin hefði viljað losna frá veiðunum. Mestöllu úr skipinu var bjargað og haldið mikið uppboð.

5f2629b8-5a52-f5bd-354d-570a5ddbb6d1.story_eng: Brytaskálafjara takes its name from the ruins that stand on its banks. These are said to be the remains of old fishing huts, and the beach is said to have been used back then as a landing place where boats were drawn up. Other place names nearby are also named after the huts. Fairly long stretches of flat rock lead here from Páskahellir. Here a strip of low-lying land begins and grows wider further in.
5f2629b8-5a52-f5bd-354d-570a5ddbb6d1.story_is: Fjaran dregur nafn af tóftum sem standa á bökkum hennar. Þær eru sagðar vera gamlar fiskiskálatættur og fjaran þá notuð fyrir uppsátur, enda eru þarna örnefni sem draga nöfn af skálunum. Frá Páskahelli eru nokkuð langar klappir að fjörunni. Þarna fer að koma dálítið undirlendi sem heldur áfram að breikka eftir því sem innar dregur.

5f40f215-fc29-7d18-184f-9b97aa998a49.story_eng: This ledge, also simply called Hjalli, lies beside the river Teigará, where the river falls down from the hillside above Sveppahlíð. Its name is made of plain words meaning roughly 'house-ruin ledge'. Below it once stood old beitarhús (sheep houses out in the grazing land) belonging to the farm Skeggjastaðir.
5f40f215-fc29-7d18-184f-9b97aa998a49.story_is: Ofan við Sveppahlíð rennur Teigará og þar sem hún fellur ofan af hlíðinni heitir framan við hana Hjalli eða Húsatóttahjalli. Niður undan honum voru gömul beitarhús frá Skeggjastöðum.

5f53f0a6-a9bf-0762-fe03-8a93910abdf4.story_eng: Háls is an abandoned farm north of the Eiríksstaðadysjar cairns. It is now called Hálstóftir, 'the Háls ruins'. The ruins have lent their name to the ground around them. The scree beyond them is called Hálstóftaurð. A flat rocky stretch to the north, once simply called Fles, is now known as Hálstóftafles.
5f53f0a6-a9bf-0762-fe03-8a93910abdf4.story_is: Eyðibýlið Háls er norðan við Eiríksstaðadysjarnar og er nú nefnt Hálstóftir. Út af tóftunum er kölluð Hálstóftaurð. Norðan við tætturnar heitir Fles og er það nú nefnt Hálstóftafles.

5f54d704-b7b9-45ea-3693-9fdeb27d5242.story_eng: Grænakelda (the green bog) on Handanbæjarmýrar was known as a deadly bog, a quagmire where animals could drown. It dried out a good deal when a ditch was dug to drain it, but it remained just as dangerous to sheep as before. A strip of wet, boggy channels ran from Grænakelda down to Ala.
5f54d704-b7b9-45ea-3693-9fdeb27d5242.story_is: Grænakelda var drápsdý á Handanbæjarmýrum. Hún þornaði mikið þegar skurður var grafinn úr henni, en var hættuleg fé eftir sem áður. Seilarsvæði lá úr Grænukeldu niður í Ala.

5f5b44b8-eed0-41b1-106d-c69778bd13c5.story_eng: Strompgljúfrafoss drops down into the gorge of Strompgljúfur, and the waterfall was sometimes simply called Strompur (chimney). It also goes by Úðafoss (spray falls). A woman who lived at Dynjandi said that Böðvar Bjarnason of Hrafnseyri had changed the names of the waterfalls here, and that the name Úðafoss for this one most likely came from him.
5f5b44b8-eed0-41b1-106d-c69778bd13c5.story_is: Niður í Strompgljúfur fellur Strompgljúfrafoss eða Strompur, eins og fossinn var stundum nefndur. Kona sem bjó á Dynjanda sagði að Böðvar Bjarnason á Hrafnseyri hefði breytt nöfnum fossanna. Hún sagði að frá honum muni vera komið nafnið Úðafoss á Strompgljúfrafossi.

5f5d0f1c-a35b-42cb-9a59-de7054cea408.story_eng: Sveltishilluklettur is the rock face directly above Sveltishilla, a ledge in the Grenjaklettar cliffs near the boundary of Háls. Sheep often made their way out onto this ledge and starved to death there, and the ledge's name, roughly 'starvation ledge', is presumably taken from this. The land boundary runs through the ledge itself.
5f5d0f1c-a35b-42cb-9a59-de7054cea408.story_is: Í Grenjaklettum, næst mörkum á Hálsi, er Sveltishilla og í henni landamörkin. Í hillu þessa fara oft kindur og svelta til bana og mun nafnið af því dregið. Ofan við Sveltishillu er Sveltishilluklettur.

5f6eb1c5-7ab7-802d-b938-c52c2c4de27b.story_eng: From 1912 until some time after 1940, a kláfur crossed the river Laxá here, a little above Helluvaðsfótur. A kláfur is a cable car, a small carriage hung on wires and pulled across a river. Today only the wires remain, but the name has kept its place in the minds of local people. According to Arnljótur at Arnarvatn, bold young men from the farms Arnarvatn and Helluvað would amuse themselves by crawling along the cables across the river to fetch the car whenever it was on the far side.
5f6eb1c5-7ab7-802d-b938-c52c2c4de27b.story_is: Skammt ofan við Helluvaðsfót var kláfur á Laxá frá 1912 fram yfir 1940. Þar eru nú einungis vírarnir eftir en örnefnið hefur hlotið sess í vitund heimamanna. Hugdjarfir ungir menn á Arnarvatni og Helluvaði léku sér að því að skríða á strengjunum yfir ána til að sækja kláfinn ef hann var hinum megin árinnar þegar að var komið, sagði Arnljótur á Arnarvatni.

5f8665b2-4d95-4265-bfdf-dca714669140.story_eng: At the northern end of this hill there is a rocky cleft. A man known as Kleifa-Jón died of exposure there, and he became a most ferocious ghost who walked again after his death.
5f8665b2-4d95-4265-bfdf-dca714669140.story_is: Á norðurenda holtsins er klettaskora. Þar varð úti maður sá sem kallaður var Kleifa-Jón og gerðist hin hatrammasta afturganga.

5fa884f7-6d56-4b9f-a2a9-318d80f0ff4e.story_eng: The Vogar (coves) lie at the outermost tip of Krossnes, the headland on which the Krossnes farm stands. Where the shore called Balinn ends and the coves begin, a small notch cuts into the bank. It has a gravel beach on its outer side and bare rock on its inner side, and it is called Bás. Small things often drift ashore there. Next comes a fairly long but narrow inlet that is extremely deep. It has three names: Hundavogur (dog cove), Kattarvogur (cat cove) and the crude Kuntuvogur. Dogs and cats were drowned in this inlet until at least the middle of the 20th century. The animals were put in a sack, with a stone tied to them to keep them company on the last stretch. Further in is a somewhat wider cove called Byrðingavogur, and on its homeward side is the outermost rocky point of Krossnes. Inside that point lies Sigurðarvogur, bounded by the point and by skerries off the bay beyond. That bay is Bæjarvík, usually just called Víkin, and the farm stands above it.
5fa884f7-6d56-4b9f-a2a9-318d80f0ff4e.story_is: Nesið sem bærinn stendur á heitir Krossnes. Yst á því eru Vogarnir. Þar sem Balinn endar en Vogarnir taka við er smá skora upp í bakkann. Utan við hana er malarfjara en klappir innan við. Skoran nefnist Bás og þar rekur oft eitthvað smálegt. Næst kemur nokkuð langur en þröngur bás og er hann hyldjúpur. Á honum eru þrjú nöfn, Hundavogur, Kattarvogur og hið dónalega nafn Kuntuvogur. Í þessum vog var hundum og köttum drekkt fram yfir miðja 20. öld að minnsta kosti. Kvikindin voru sett í poka og steinn bundinn við þau til fylgdar síðasta spölinn. Innar er enn annar vogur nokkru breiðari og nefnist Byrðingavogur. Heiman til við hann er ysta klettanesið á Krossnesi. Innan við það er Sigurðarvogur sem markast af nesinu og flúrum utanvert við víkina þar fyrir innan. Sú vík heitir Bæjarvík en oftast í daglegu tali Víkin. Bærinn á Krossnesi stendur uppi af Bæjarvíkinni.

5fa95f21-51e8-2585-a9af-b15397e0d46e.story_eng: Litli banki (the Little Bank) is one of three fishing banks on the Djúpslóð grounds. Its name, along with that of its neighbour Pínulitli banki (the Tiny Little Bank), comes from Axel Schiöth. The third bank, Læsti banki (the Locked Bank), is believed to have got its name after Guðmundur Kjalar, skipper of the Málmey SK, fished southwest of a spot called Fylkishóll and the size of his catch was kept rather quiet.
5fa95f21-51e8-2585-a9af-b15397e0d46e.story_is: Á Djúpslóð eru þrír bankar sem nefnast Litli banki, Pínulitli banki og Læsti banki. Nöfnin á Litla banka og Pínulitla banka eru komin frá Axel Schiöth. Talið er að Læsti banki hafi orðið til þegar Guðmundur Kjalar, skipstjóri á Málmey SK, hafði verið á veiðum suðvestan við svonefndan Fylkishól. Það fór eitthvað hljótt um aflabrögðin og slóðin fékk þetta nafn vegna þess.

5fd7d837-47c7-b73e-52c3-64e07f51ec86.story_eng: This spring is said to have been blessed by Guðmundur góði (Guðmundur the Good, a 13th-century bishop said to have blessed many springs and wells). Its water is said to taste good and be refreshing.
5fd7d837-47c7-b73e-52c3-64e07f51ec86.story_is: Lindin var vígð af Guðmundi góða og er vatnið sagt bragðgott og hressandi.

5fe7c344-daef-a897-a6d6-6153897144ab.story_eng: Long ago, the people of Viðfjörður and the people of Sandvík once fought a battle here. The marsh lies below the end of Mjósundamelur, a gravel ridge running across the slope.
5fe7c344-daef-a897-a6d6-6153897144ab.story_is: Í Vatnsmýri börðust Viðfirðingar og Sandvíkingar eitt sinn til forna. Mýrin er undir enda Mjósundamels, þvermels sem liggur neðan við Mjósund.

5fec5153-8d40-789c-fca4-8925b947f865.story_eng: This path is named after a woman known as Imba holgóma (holgóma means cleft-palated), whose name was Ingibjörg. She lived much of the time at the farm Breiðumýri. She took this route so that she would not have to pass by the farm Hraunkot, because she was afraid the children there would make fun of her.
5fec5153-8d40-789c-fca4-8925b947f865.story_is: Stígurinn er kenndur við konu sem nefnd var Imba holgóma, en hún hét Ingibjörg og var mikið til heimilis á Breiðumýri. Hún fór þessa leið til að koma ekki við á Hraunkoti, þar sem hún var hrædd um að börn gerðu gys að sér.

603c93ba-43e7-3c07-f4cd-e134b32fdd46.story_eng: The name means peat stack, and locals simply spoke of going "up to Svörður" (peat). The main peat-cutting ground lay at the north-eastern end of the Fellsmýri bog, by the southern mouth of Torfdalur. The dried peat was kept here in a stack and fetched as needed, often with a horse and sled over hard, crusted snow. A ruin of the stack site remains.
603c93ba-43e7-3c07-f4cd-e134b32fdd46.story_is: Talað var um að fara upp í Svörð. Aðalmótekjan er norðaustast í Fellsmýri, við suðurkjaftinn á Torfdal. Þar er rúst eða tóft. Svörðurinn var hafður þarna í hlaða og sótt í hann, oft með hest og sleða í harðfenni.

60534348-1bad-4402-ad18-3e9ac07f9fa7.story_eng: Hraungarðsendi is the far end of Hraungarður. Beyond the hayfield, in a hollow off this end, lie peat pits (mógrafir, where peat was dug), with the knoll Mógrafarholt beyond them and the gravel hill Svarðarholt to the south. Further out and higher up is Pálsskógur, a wood named after Páll Guttormsson from Hallormsstaður, who sowed birch there from Bæjarstaðaskógur.
60534348-1bad-4402-ad18-3e9ac07f9fa7.story_is: Hraungarðsendi er út af Hraungarði. Utan við tún, í dæld út af Hraungarðsenda, eru mógrafir og utan við þær Mógrafarholt, en sunnan við þær melhóll, Svarðarholt. Utan og ofan við það er Pálsskógur, nefndur eftir Páli Guttormssyni frá Hallormsstað sem þar sáði birki úr Bæjarstaðaskógi.

6091b1c5-e142-0a79-8457-6cc58032a7e7.story_eng: According to legend, two girls died of exposure in this shallow valley, and the name Meyjadalur means "valley of the maidens". It lies north of the lake Leirvatn and west of Rúnasteinn, and the stream Lónakíll flows out of it.
6091b1c5-e142-0a79-8457-6cc58032a7e7.story_is: Sögn er að í þessu daldragi hafi tvær stúlkur orðið úti. Það er norðan við Leirvatn og vestur af Rúnasteini, og úr því kemur Lónakíll.

6099c07f-0202-f94b-f0aa-855c4fafa4be.story_eng: Bótólfsnes is the place where a man named Bótólfur was put to death, and the headland bears his name. It lies just beyond the river Vaðalsá.
6099c07f-0202-f94b-f0aa-855c4fafa4be.story_is: Rétt fyrir utan Vaðalsá er Bótólfsnes. Þar var Bótólfur tekinn af lífi.

60a0d498-4657-4aa7-b25e-b8f0004dff5c.story_eng: A skilarétt, a fold where sheep brought down from the summer pastures were sorted by owner, once stood at Hólkot. Its outline can still be seen, with two large pens and eight smaller ones around them. Hólkot was a farm on the ridge running southeast from Kárhóll. It was lived in for a long time before it was abandoned in 1712. Traces of a wall around Hólkot and Kárhóll can still be seen.
60a0d498-4657-4aa7-b25e-b8f0004dff5c.story_is: Á Hólkoti hefur verið skilarétt og sér enn fyrir tveimur stórum hólfum og átta minni í kring. Hólkot stóð á hrygg suðaustur af Kárhóli og var lengi í byggð en fór í eyði 1712. Enn sér fyrir garði í kringum Hólkot og Kárhól.

60a937a8-1583-3abc-7f76-a020118ee0e1.story_eng: A church and churchyard once stood on the southeast side of the old farm mound at Ásgarður. The last burial in Ásgarðskirkjugarður took place in the spring of 1882, and the church was torn down around 1883. The churchyard was levelled over in or after about 1930, and nothing of it remains to be seen today.
60a937a8-1583-3abc-7f76-a020118ee0e1.story_is: Kirkja og kirkjugarður stóðu suðaustan á gamla bæjarhólnum. Síðast var jarðað í Ásgarðskirkjugarði vorið 1882 og kirkjan var rifin um 1883. Sléttað var yfir kirkjugarðinn um eða eftir 1930.

60d01430-386e-0fd9-4fd5-dbf50d27c907.story_eng: Around 1900 the roof of Einhyrningshellir collapsed. The cave had served as a shelter for gangnamenn, the men who gathered sheep from the highlands in the autumn round-up, and after the collapse it could no longer be used. A hut was then built on the flat ground below the cave. It stood for only one year. It is believed to have been brought down by snow the winter after it was built, and it is no longer there. After that, the round-up men's shelter for the area inside Jökulkvísl was moved to Hólmárfoss, where it still was in 2025.
60d01430-386e-0fd9-4fd5-dbf50d27c907.story_is: Í kringum aldamótin 1900 féll hellisþakið á Einhyrningshelli, sem var afdrep gangnamanna, niður og ónýttist þá afdrepið í hellinum. Þá var byggður kofi á flötinni fyrir neðan hellinn. Hann stóð í eitt ár og er talið að hann hafi farið niður undan snjó veturinn eftir að hann var byggður. Í framhaldi af því var gangnamannaaðstaða innan Jökulkvíslar flutt að Hólmárfossi þar sem hún er enn þann dag í dag.

6102924a-7034-d12c-4592-0430864fb276.story_eng: Stífla, meaning dam, is a spot in the stream a little beyond Stiklur, where the stream makes a sharp bend towards the slope and then turns straight back again. Old dam walls still stand here, and there was once a floodgate, probably from the days of the Hafralækjarstífla irrigation scheme, which began in 1914. From here the stream flows north-east out of the land of Hafralækur.
6102924a-7034-d12c-4592-0430864fb276.story_is: Stífla heitir í læknum nokkru utan við Stiklur, þar sem skarpur krókur er á honum í átt til brekkunnar en strax aftur frá. Þar eru gamlir stíflugarðar og hefur verið flóðgátt, sennilega frá dögum áveitu Hafralækjarstíflu sem hófst 1914. Lækurinn rennur síðan til norðausturs út úr Hafralækjarlandi.

610920f9-71de-6f0c-cf70-2fb5d5a2ef1f.story_eng: This rock is named after Theódór Gunnlaugsson from Hafursstaðir, later of Austaraland in Öxarfjörður, author of the book "Á refaslóðum" (On the Trail of Foxes). Harp seals were once hunted from Buðlungahöfn, and Theódór is believed to have hunted seals in the harbour, though probably not harp seals, since by his time they had mostly stopped coming along the coast in large herds. The rock was given its name by Þorgrímur Þorsteinsson from Daðastaðir.
610920f9-71de-6f0c-cf70-2fb5d5a2ef1f.story_is: Steinninn er kenndur við Theódór Gunnlaugsson frá Hafursstöðum og síðar á Austaralandi í Öxarfirði, höfund bókarinnar „Á refaslóðum“. Fyrr á tíð var veiddur vöðuselur frá Buðlungahöfn. Theódór mun hafa verið við selveiðar í höfninni, þó tæpast veiðar á vöðusel, því vöðuselurinn var á tíð Theódórs að mestu hættur að ganga í torfum (kjórum) með landinu. Þorgrímur Þorsteinsson frá Daðastöðum nefndi steininn Theódór.

61157387-0bd7-a652-4cb1-0b9b17dcd5d0.story_eng: On a rise some 200–300 m southwest of the farm stood ruins known as Tættur. Some time before 1800, Eiríkur Vigfússon moved the Reykir farmhouse here to escape drifting sand. About 60 years later his son, also named Eiríkur, moved the farm back to its old site. The farm mound has since been levelled and is now a hayfield, and the ruins are no longer there.
61157387-0bd7-a652-4cb1-0b9b17dcd5d0.story_is: Tættur voru á hæð suðvestur frá bænum, 200–300 m. Þangað flutti Eiríkur Vigfússon Reykjabæinn undan sandfoki nokkru fyrir aldamótin 1800. Eiríkur sonur hans flutti svo bæinn aftur á sinn gamla stað um 60 árum síðar. Bæjarhóllinn hefur verið sléttaður og er nú tún.

611851a4-5e9e-9e65-7f3c-9908c483af10.story_eng: Eyði is a skerry off Eyðisfjara beach. It is dome-shaped, though the dome is flattened, fairly large and rather flat on top. At high tide it is so low that the sea washes over it if there is any swell. At low tide a sandbar leads out to it, and, unlikely as it may seem, the sandbar is also called Eyði. Otherwise a channel about two metres wide, which always holds water, separates the skerry from the shore. Sheep were sometimes cut off by the tide out on Eyði, but they came to no harm.
611851a4-5e9e-9e65-7f3c-9908c483af10.story_is: Úti fyrir Eyðisfjöru er eyðisker sem Eyði heitir. Það er kúpulaga en kúpan þó útflött. Skerið er allstórt um sig og nokkuð flatt að ofan. Um flæði er það ekki hærra en svo að yfir það gengur sjór ef nokkur kvika er, en um háfjöru er þar grandi út í Eyðið og heitir hann líka Eyði, þó ótrúlegt sé. Annars er um tveggja metra breið læna milli skersins og fjörunnar sem alltaf er sjór í. Fyrir kom að fé flæddi uppi í Eyðinu en það kom ekki að skaða.

61227fe0-a463-c3e4-2fc6-ba0256f92f17.story_eng: Kringlumýri was a flat bog used for haymaking, its main part covered in brok, a coarse bog grass. It has since been drained and dried and turned into a hayfield, so the bog itself is gone. It stretched south to the stream Baululækur. The bog took its name from Kringla, a very ancient-looking enclosure on the south side of a large hill above and to the south of it. Kringla is surrounded by a wall and is only about 100 metres across.
61227fe0-a463-c3e4-2fc6-ba0256f92f17.story_is: Ofan Votahvamms er eða var flöt mýri, Kringlumýri, heyskaparland. Hún er nú framræst og þurrkuð og orðin að túni. Aðalmýrin var með brokgresi. Mýrin náði suður að Baululæk og dregur nafn af Kringlu, sem er mjög fornlegt gerði sunnan í stóru holti suður og upp af Kringlumýrinni. Garðlag er umhverfis gerðið, sem er ekki nema svo sem 100 metrar í þvermál.

615dfd40-bb66-a0ca-52c0-0ad245200e75.story_eng: Bæli is a rounded, dome-shaped hillock lying between the ravines. The farmer Kollur is said to be buried here in a burial mound. His story is linked to the nearby Hildarhaugur.
615dfd40-bb66-a0ca-52c0-0ad245200e75.story_is: Bungumyndaður hóll milli giljanna. Þar á Kollur bóndi að vera heygður, en sjá einnig Hildarhaug.

615e2adf-1567-b20b-6f5e-41ab7fdcc464.story_eng: Hæðir was once a rough, uncultivated stretch of heath, thick with large tussocks, and the ancient main route of travel ran across it. Deep tracks of sand and soil had been worn into the ground there, smooth as could be, and people still living when this was recorded remembered them. The heath was later levelled, and Hæðir has now become part of the hayfield.
615e2adf-1567-b20b-6f5e-41ab7fdcc464.story_is: Á Hæðunum var áður stórþýfður óræktarmói og um þær lá áður þjóðleiðin hin forna. Voru þar djúpar sand- og moldargötur, rennisléttar, og muna núlifandi menn eftir þeim. Móinn var svo sléttaður og eru Hæðirnar nú orðnar að túni.

6161f31d-e7f8-6548-1b58-b89efd220995.story_eng: Kvernalækur, roughly 'quern stream', was the name used in earlier centuries for the stream that runs west of Íragerði and Kyndluhóll. The old name is said to appear in the Icelandic annals. The writer of the description remembered from childhood a small mill house that stood by the stream a short way below Kyndluhóll, where the millstones were driven by water power. In those days the stream was sometimes called Myllulækur, 'mill stream'.
6161f31d-e7f8-6548-1b58-b89efd220995.story_is: Svo nefndist fyrr á öldum lækurinn sem rennur vestan við Íragerði og Kyndluhól niður í pollinn. Heitið er sagt koma fyrir í íslenskum annálum. Mér er það í barnsminni að lítið mylluhús stóð við lækinn skammt neðan við Kyndluhól. Voru kvarnirnar knúðar vatnsafli. Lækurinn var þá stundum kallaður Myllulækur.

616330c9-65d6-4455-91b1-e9fe150a7fbc.story_eng: Dimmihellir means "the dark cave". Of the caves on the western side, it is the only one with a name. It lies west of the lighthouse and is the fourth or fifth sea cave from Nef. Sigtryggur of Steindalur said he had gone into the cave in a small open motorboat, so far in that he could not see his own hands, and he believed the cave to be fairly long.
616330c9-65d6-4455-91b1-e9fe150a7fbc.story_is: Af hellunum að vestanverðu hefur aðeins einn nafn. Hann er vestur af vitanum og heitir Dimmihellir. Dimmihellir er fjórði eða fimmti skúti frá Nefi. Sigtryggur í Steindal segist hafa farið inn í hellinn á smátrillu, þar sem hann sá ekki handa skil, og telur að hann sé þó nokkuð langur.

61672880-8ff9-1117-a802-64d392946938.story_eng: Svínahraun is a fairly large patch of rough lava standing up out of the surrounding Mekurhraun lava. It is sparsely vegetated, but the grassy land around it is good grazing. The lava has stayed above the floods, and snow seldom settles there. The name means "pig lava", and it might suggest that pigs once roamed free here in olden times.
61672880-8ff9-1117-a802-64d392946938.story_is: Svínahraun er allstór hraunkargi sem stendur upp úr Mekurhrauninu, lítt gróinn en valllendi í kring og gott beitiland. Svínahraunið hefur staðið upp úr flóðum og þar festir sjaldan snjó. Gæti nafnið bent til þess að þar hafi svín gengið úti forðum.

616732aa-82f1-75b4-4d03-f597f1f0f738.story_eng: Setur is a rise beside the river Laxá, south of Ásgeirsstaðir, reaching right down to the water. It is practically a lava island, flat on top and much higher than the rough, jagged lava around it. Somewhere in the rough lava nearby there is said to be a hidden treasure: five bottles of landi, Icelandic home-distilled spirits, left behind when the good brewer who made them died. Those who have searched for them have not found them.
616732aa-82f1-75b4-4d03-f597f1f0f738.story_is: Setur gengur fast að Laxá, sunnan við Ásgeirsstaði. Það er nánast sagt hraunhólmi, sléttur að ofan og mun hærri en úfið hraunið í kring. Þar í nánd, í úfnu hrauni, kvað vera falinn fjársjóður: fimm flöskur af landa sem bruggarinn góði dó frá. Leitendur hafa ekki fundið þær.

61764dd5-65db-12c2-559c-fd518d0dba21.story_eng: The name means "the French grave". It is the grave of a French lieutenant who died in an accidental shooting in Hjáleiguland in 1864, when officers from a warship came ashore to hunt golden plover.
61764dd5-65db-12c2-559c-fd518d0dba21.story_is: Leiði fransks lautinants sem lést af voðaskoti í Hjáleigulandi árið 1864, þegar foringjar af herskipi gengu á land til lóuveiða.

61966131-1769-4cc3-bd81-5e23944907cc.story_eng: This waterfall takes its name from the river Lagsá, a name most often written Laxá, 'salmon river'. That spelling is probably a misunderstanding, since salmon have surely never made their way into this river. The river lies on the boundary between two long-established farms that own it jointly, and the name comes from lag, meaning partnership or fellowship.
61966131-1769-4cc3-bd81-5e23944907cc.story_is: Örnefnið er oftast ritað Laxá, líklega fyrir misskilning því að lax hefur örugglega aldrei komist í þessa á. Hins vegar er áin á mörkum tveggja gamalgróinna jarða sem eiga hana í félagi, en lag merkir félag.

61a0c0a4-0a71-3976-afd0-fcf4bd53817e.story_eng: Helluvað, at the southern end of Nesið, was once the best ford on the river. Here the water ran over a slab of sandstone (hella means slab, vað means ford). At one time a dam was built across the river to raise the water onto the hay meadows. But as the river was narrowed, its current grew stronger, and it broke up the whole slab along with the dam. Where the slab and the ford used to be, there is now a good salmon pool.
61a0c0a4-0a71-3976-afd0-fcf4bd53817e.story_is: Helluvað var á ánni syðst við Nesið. Rann áin þar á sandsteinshellu og var þar hið besta vað. Eitt sinn var gerð þar stífla í ána og skyldi ná henni upp á engin. En er að ánni þrengdist jókst strengur í henni og braut upp alla helluna og stíflugerðina, svo nú er góður laxahylur þar sem áður var hellan og vaðið.

61bdd79a-fde9-44c6-b674-6e05b8e028f5.story_eng: A dog named Spakur was drowned in this pond, and it is from him that Spaktjörn takes its name.
61bdd79a-fde9-44c6-b674-6e05b8e028f5.story_is: Þar var drekkt hundi sem hét Spakur.

61ca9d7c-0751-4777-931f-52a2a91933bb.story_eng: In thaws the Skarðsá can become a raging torrent, and it was often a serious obstacle to travel until it was bridged in 1884. Kristbjörg Jónsdóttir was born at Botn in Þorgeirsfjörður in 1836, a year before her father and four other men drowned there while tending shark lines. Around or after 1860, poor, unmarried and pregnant, she sought shelter with her sister and mother at the poor croft of Miðgerði, hoping to give birth there. When word spread that a pauper was expected, the district officer Einar Ásmundsson, a member of parliament and wealthy farmer at Nes, sent word that she must leave before the birth, so the child would not become a charge on the parish of Grýtubakkahreppur. Kristbjörg set out on foot in driving rain up Dalsmynni, the shortest way into another parish. Crossing the swollen Skarðsá, which even the strongest men could not wade, she lost her footing and fell into the icy current. She struggled to the farm Skarð, where her child was stillborn. She lived to a great age but was never again with a man. According to a relative, whenever Einar of Nes was mentioned she said only: "ohhh... the blessed noble soul."
61ca9d7c-0751-4777-931f-52a2a91933bb.story_is: Skarðsáin getur í leysingum breyst í foráttufljót og var hún oft mikill farartálmi áður en hún var brúuð 1884. Kristbjörg Jónsdóttir var fædd á Botni í Þorgeirsfirði 1836, ári áður en faðir hennar drukknaði í Þorgeirsfirði ásamt fjórum mönnum þegar þeir vitjuðu hákarlavaðs. Kristbjörg var á sinni tíð víða í vinnumennsku. Eins og títt var um fátækar vinnukonur á Íslandi virðist hún hafa verið varnarlaus gegn ágengum og ófyrirleitnum karlmönnum. Um eða eftir 1860 leitaði hún til Sigurlaugar systur sinnar sem þá bjó í Miðgerði, þar sem María móðir þeirra bjó líka. Það var illa komið fyrir henni, hún var ógift og ófrísk, og í hinu fátæka koti vonaðist hún eftir skjóli til að fæða barnið. Þegar það fréttist um sveitina að von væri á sveitarómaga í Miðgerði fór hreppsnefndin að ókyrrast. Hreppstjórinn, Einar Ásmundsson, þingmaður og stórbóndi í Nesi, kom þeim skilaboðum skýrt í Miðgerði að þaðan skyldi Kristbjörg fara, með góðu eða illu, áður en barnið fæddist, svo það yrði ekki sveitfast og á framfæri Grýtubakkahrepps. Kristbjörg hélt af stað gangandi í slagviðri upp Dalsmynni, stystu leið í annan hrepp. Mögulega ætlaði hún að leita skjóls hjá frænku sinni á Ytra-Hóli í Fnjóskadal. Skarðsáin í vexti er ekki væð hraustustu mönnum, hvað þá vanfærri konu. Á leiðinni yfir ána varð henni fótaskortur og hún féll í ískalda, straumþunga ána. Við illan leik komst hún heim í Skarð og fæddi þar barnið andvana. Kristbjörg varð fjörgömul en aldrei aftur við karlmann kennd. Þegar minnst var á Einar í Nesi í hennar viðurvist átti hún aðeins eina setningu: „ohhh... blessaður öðlingurinn.“

61cb5183-97ca-4e5e-53bd-293aea0e9054.story_eng: Hetta is known as a dwelling place of elves (álfar), a home of the unseen folk of Icelandic belief. Its exact location is not precisely recorded.
61cb5183-97ca-4e5e-53bd-293aea0e9054.story_is: Í Hettu er álfabyggð. Staðsetningin er þó ónákvæm.

61dc2ebc-1fd5-b1db-0c29-69c5a4f6b2f3.story_eng: Langhellir is a rocky ridge, and its name means 'long cave'. According to old tales, a cave lies beneath it, and all sorts of ancient lore are tied to it, though no sign of the cave can be seen. It is said that a cat once went down into the ground here and came back up at Herjólfsstaðagarðar, and that when the cat got home, its tail had been singed. Neither the hill nor the cave may be touched. Once, when someone began disturbing the ground here, 60 ewes died.
61dc2ebc-1fd5-b1db-0c29-69c5a4f6b2f3.story_is: Grjótháls. Sagnir eru um að hellir sé hér undir og er ýmis forneskja kennd við hann en engin merki sjást þess. Sagt er t.d. að eitt sinn hafi köttur farið hér niður og komið upp á yfirborðið aftur í Herjólfsstaðagörðum. Sagt er að þegar kötturinn kom heim hafi rófan á honum verið sviðin. Ekki má snerta hólinn eða hellinn. Eitt sinn var eitthvert jarðrask hafið hér og þá fórust 60 ær.

61fba3c9-b85f-c0fc-eb10-f28c7f6f7c7a.story_eng: A small hillock on Haukamelsbörð holds the remains of an old sheep house that belonged to the farm Sogn. Around 1830, Magnús, the farmer at Sogn, is said to have kept his wethers (castrated rams) here, '16 and 20 in number', as it was phrased. The writer of the Sogn place-name record remembered the ruin clearly and found it unlikely that the house could ever have held 36 sheep. According to an old account, the land boundary ran at Sauðaklöpp, and the ruin lies within those bounds.
61fba3c9-b85f-c0fc-eb10-f28c7f6f7c7a.story_is: Á Haukamelsbörðum er smáhóll með leifum af fjárhúsi, og var það fjárhús frá Sogni. Þar hafði Magnús bóndi á Sogni (um 1830) sauði sína, 16 og 20 að tölu, eins og það var orðað. Sá sem skráði örnefnalýsingu Sogns mundi rústina greinilega og fannst honum ólíklegt að húsið hefði rúmað 36 sauði. Sögn er um að mörkin hafi verið í Sauðaklöpp, og er rústin innan þeirra marka.

61fceace-aca2-4450-b650-28688f8efdfe.story_eng: Borg, also called Óttarsstaðaborg or Kristrúnarborg, is an old fjárborg, a round dry-stone enclosure built to shelter sheep. A woman named Kristrún, who lived at the farm Óttarsstaðir, built it together with her farmhand, which is why it also bears her name. It dates from before the turn of the 20th century and is said to have been built around 1870. The shelter is still clearly visible and has been described as beautiful and well preserved.
61fceace-aca2-4450-b650-28688f8efdfe.story_is: Borg er gömul fjárborg og glögg, frá því fyrir aldamót. Hún er einnig kölluð Óttarsstaðaborg eða Kristrúnarborg. Kona, er Kristrún hét og bjó á Óttarsstöðum, hlóð hana ásamt vinnumanni sínum. Þetta er falleg og heilleg fjárborg frá Óttarsstöðum, sem sögð er hlaðin um 1870.

622e4c50-ac0b-f421-6d2e-2b5705fe90d9.story_eng: Vargakjaftur is a stretch of grassy, hummocky moorland where the remains of several old ruins can still be clearly seen. Long ago there was a farm here by the same name, probably one with no hayfield or grazing rights of its own. The name is made of plain words meaning "wolf's jaw" or "fox's jaw".
622e4c50-ac0b-f421-6d2e-2b5705fe90d9.story_is: Austur af Borgarkrók er gróið móaþýfi og sést þar vel fyrir nokkrum tóftarbrotum. Þarna heitir Vargakjaftur. Þar hafði áður fyrir löngu verið býli með þessu nafni, líklega grasnytjalaust.

6239b070-afae-48f2-9435-04bc43f573bf.name_eng: Ingveldarstaðir, ruins of an abandoned farm
6239b070-afae-48f2-9435-04bc43f573bf.story_eng: Ingveldarstaðir is an ancient abandoned farm. It is said that there was once a church here, and that an old burial ground was laid bare by wind erosion, though the bones were badly decayed.
6239b070-afae-48f2-9435-04bc43f573bf.story_is: Ingveldarstaðir er fornt eyðibýli. Sagt er að þar hafi verið kirkjustaður og að forn grafreitur hafi blásið upp, en beinin hafi verið mjög fúin.

626f0604-76e4-64fc-4038-b1155dd7b3ea.story_eng: A fairly tall waterfall stands where the river's gorge comes to an end, south of the home field of Eyri. The story goes that a man named Þorleifur meant to jump across the river here and fell into the falls, which have carried his name ever since.
626f0604-76e4-64fc-4038-b1155dd7b3ea.story_is: Þar sem gljúfrin með ánni enda, suður af Eyrartúni, er nokkuð hár foss í henni sem heitir Þorleifsfoss. Segir sagan að maður með þessu nafni hafi ætlað að stökkva yfir ána þarna og farið í fossinn.

6283b972-b1a3-5519-6fcd-7d999f9bf530.story_eng: Erfingi is a burial cairn where the shepherd from the farm Dragháls was buried. The cairn is a protected site and is listed on the register of ancient monuments.
6283b972-b1a3-5519-6fcd-7d999f9bf530.story_is: Í dysinni Erfingja var smalinn á Draghálsi dysjaður. Dysin er friðlýst og á minjaskrá.

62a470ed-90fb-0958-9223-d02007718aa8.story_eng: Flesjur lies down and to the north of the farm. It was once used as hayfield meadow. The ground was very wet but has since been drained. Near the middle of the marsh were quagmires called Inbudý, named after a servant woman who fell into them but was rescued. They have now disappeared because of the drainage ditches. At the northern end of Flesjur was a pool called Stararpollur. The stream Vallmóslækur flowed out of it, and while it runs through Flesjur it is called Flesjulækur.
62a470ed-90fb-0958-9223-d02007718aa8.story_is: Niður og norður af bæ heita Flesjur. Flesjur voru engi. Þær voru mjög blautar en hafa nú verið ræstar fram. Nærri því í miðri mýrinni voru dý sem hétu Inbudý, kennd við vinnukonu sem fór í þau en bjargaðist. Nú eru þau horfin vegna skurða. Nyrst í Flesjum var Stararpollur. Úr honum kom Vallmóslækurinn og er hann kallaður Flesjulækur meðan hann fer í gegnum Flesjur.

62a6f06b-18c9-343c-e34b-538c7e27aa95.story_eng: Stekkjarbrot (the name means roughly "fold ruin", from stekkur, a small pen where lambs were kept apart from the ewes) lies at the southern end of the land of Hvarf, just above Stekkjargrund. Around it are many grass-covered ruins of buildings, with an overgrown wall enclosing them. There was undoubtedly a farm here in ancient times. The stream Stekkjarlækur runs down the mountainside just south of the ruin.
62a6f06b-18c9-343c-e34b-538c7e27aa95.story_is: Í kringum Stekkjarbrotið eru mörg gróin húsabrot og gróinn garður í kring. Þarna hefur vafalaust verið býli til forna. Stekkjarbrot er syðst í Hvarfslandi, rétt ofan við Stekkjargrund, og Stekkjarlækur fellur ofan fjallið sunnan við það.

62ae3e7c-b951-cd66-8361-1dd4d32a7b74.story_eng: Ófeigur Vigfússon built a large protective wall running from up on the mountain down to the floodlands, strong enough to hold back cattle and horses. It was meant to keep the large livestock out of the home field and the hay meadows, and it worked well. The wall had two gates, one in Víðaskarð and the other just below Hofin. After Ófeigur's time the wall was not kept up as it should have been.
62ae3e7c-b951-cd66-8361-1dd4d32a7b74.story_is: Ófeigur Vigfússon byggði mikinn vörslugarð ofan úr fjalli og niður að flóðum og hélt þessi garður stórgripum. Garðurinn var til varnar því að stórgripir færu í tún og engjar og gaf góða raun. Tvö hlið voru á garðinum, annað í Víðaskarði en hitt neðan undir Hofunum. Eftir daga Ófeigs var garðinum ekki haldið við sem skyldi.

62bb365e-c154-466e-800b-313ceea1d4c4.story_eng: Svörður, meaning peat, is a name used for the peat diggings in Svarðarmýri, a fairly large bog northeast of Tíðaklettur. The bog itself is named after the peat pits in it, which are probably not very old. Locals would say "ég ætla út á Svörðinn", meaning "I'm going out to the Svörður."
62bb365e-c154-466e-800b-313ceea1d4c4.story_is: Svarðarmýri heitir allstór mýri norðaustur við Tíðaklett, kennd við svarðargrafir í henni, líklega ekki mjög gamlar. Þar er líka kallaður Svörður: „Ég ætla út á Svörðinn.“

62c1ae92-86bf-4010-bf99-07b83cde93ad.story_eng: Kumlhóll is a headland down by the sea at the western edge of the home field of the farm Dvergasteinn. Its name contains kuml, an old word for a pagan burial mound. Out in front of it lies a skerry called Kollusker. East of the hill is a small cove with a sandy beach. Above the cove, at its eastern end, there once stood a small dwelling house called Björgvin, which is believed to have been built shortly before the turn of the century before last. The house was later floated across the fjord and set up again on Ströndin, part of the settlement known as Búðareyrarbyggð, so it no longer stands here.
62c1ae92-86bf-4010-bf99-07b83cde93ad.story_is: Kumlhóll er höfði niður við sjó vestast í túni Dvergasteins. Þar framan við er sker, nefnt Kollusker. Smávík með sendna fjöru er austan við hólinn og ofan við hana austast var lítið íbúðarhús, nefnt Björgvin, sem mun hafa verið reist skömmu fyrir þarsíðustu aldamót. Því var síðar fleytt yfir fjörðinn og það sett upp á Ströndinni, sem er hluti af því sem heitir Búðareyrarbyggð.

62dc1be9-5c69-465a-a3b6-501c50d1eea9.story_eng: Innsta-Rot was the innermost of a row of lagoons known as Rot, which ran down from the many kílar (narrow creeks) on Nesið. The first creek was Vitlausikíll, then Þröngikíll and then Vaðalskíll, and below them lay Ysta-Rot, Mið-Rot and Innsta-Rot, the outer, middle and inner Rot. These lagoons were known to be dangerous places.
62dc1be9-5c69-465a-a3b6-501c50d1eea9.story_is: Í Nesinu eru margir kílar. Fyrstur var Vitlausikíll, þá Þröngikíll og þá Vaðalskíll. Niður úr kílunum gengu lón sem kölluð voru Rot, Ysta-, Mið- og Innsta-Rot. Þar voru hættur.

62de17c8-dd6c-f4fc-8c0c-f2659b9a1f76.story_eng: Galandi was a beitarhús, a sheep house out in the grazing land, and the forerunner of the later sheep houses west of Eggjar. It stood just east of the high ridges of Eggjar, south of Gloppugil, and considerable ruins can still be seen. The sheep houses here were large. In 1995 part of one wall was still standing to its full height, along with parts of other walls, stone courses built up to about the height of a sheep, and little had changed by January 2002. Little can be seen of the hay stack site, but a fairly large patch of hayfield had been levelled south of the houses, and around it the base of a fence wall can be seen. A short way northeast of the houses there was a well, but it was dangerous for lambs and was therefore filled in. The land here is grassy almost up to the highest ridges, and the hill to the west, Stórhöfði, is the highest point on the western edge of Eggjar.
62de17c8-dd6c-f4fc-8c0c-f2659b9a1f76.story_is: Forveri beitarhúsanna vestan við Eggjarnar voru beitarhús rétt austan við háar Eggjarnar, sunnan Gloppugils, og hétu þau Galandi. Þar sjást talsverðar húsaleifar. Að Galanda hafa verið stór fjárhús og árið 1995 stóð veggpartur alveg uppi og hluti af öðrum veggjum, þ.e. grjóthleðslur upp í kindarhæð. Heystæði sést lítið, en sléttaður hefur verið allstór túnblettur suður frá húsunum og í kringum hann sést undirhleðsla girðingar. Þetta var nánast óbreytt í janúar 2002. Brunnur var skammt norðaustur af húsunum. Hann var hættulegur lömbum og þess vegna fylltur upp. Á þessum slóðum er land gróið nánast upp á efstu eggjar. Hæðin vestan við húsin heitir Stórhöfði og ber hann hæst þar á vesturbrún Eggja.

62e665ad-b1de-44e4-b36b-55fb1bc60806.story_eng: Gvendarbrunnur is a spring that was blessed by Guðmundur góði, Bishop of Hólar (Guðmundur the Good, a 13th-century bishop said to have blessed many springs and wells). The name means Gvendur's well, Gvendur being a familiar form of Guðmundur.
62e665ad-b1de-44e4-b36b-55fb1bc60806.story_is: Uppspretta sem vígð er af Guðmundi góða Hólabiskupi.

6312d54a-d4af-5d45-54e4-cd7f3adb0e7c.story_eng: Konusteinn, meaning 'woman's stone', is a large stone on the southern slope of Svalbarðsháls, a very prominent hill north of Víðidalur. A woman died of exposure there, and the stone is named after her.
6312d54a-d4af-5d45-54e4-cd7f3adb0e7c.story_is: Konusteinn er stór steinn sunnan í Svalbarðshálsi, en þar varð úti kona. Svalbarðsháls er mjög áberandi hæð norðan við Víðidal.

6317dc54-a23d-52c6-439f-6ce27b4ca9d0.story_eng: Hulduhólar are rocky hills up on the island of Bjarnarey. The only known story about them comes from Sveinn Jónsson, a farmer at Fagradalur. He told of a woman, a hidden woman (one of the huldufólk, or hidden people), who appeared to him in a dream on Bjarnarey, probably twice. The dream woman foretold events in the life of Sveinn and his family that later came to pass.
6317dc54-a23d-52c6-439f-6ce27b4ca9d0.story_is: Uppi á eyjunni eru klettahólar sem nefnast Hulduhólar. Eina sögnin sem kunn er um Hulduhóla er sú sem Sveinn Jónsson, bóndi í Fagradal, sagði um konu, huldukonu, sem birtist honum í draumi í Bjarnarey, líklega tvívegis. Sagði draumkonan fyrir um atvik sem síðar komu fram í lífi Sveins og hans fólks.

632d0af3-7c5f-8ab6-1299-5333176e5d38.story_eng: Naustavík was long a landing place for boats rather than a home. In old times it served as the landing for the farm Utanverðunes, and around 1713 two or three boats from Hegranes went out fishing from here in spring and autumn. A description from 1840 mentions a beitarhús (a sheep house out in the grazing land), a fishing hut, drying sheds and a landing still in use, as well as seal nets set both summer and winter. No one lived here, apart from the shelter of the fishing hut. After 1900, Jósteinn Jónasson was given leave to settle here by Magnús Gunnarsson, the farmer at Utanverðunes. Jósteinn built himself a þurrabúð shelter, a cottage for someone without a farm of their own, and had grazing and hay from the land of Utanverðunes. He lived here from 1915 to 1935 with his housekeeper, Guðmunda Sigurðardóttir, and they then moved to Svanavatn. When he gave up, no one settled at Naustavík again, and the land was used by the farmer at Utanverðunes.
632d0af3-7c5f-8ab6-1299-5333176e5d38.story_is: Til forna var Naustavík heimræði frá Utanverðunesi og um 1713 gengu þaðan 2–3 skip til sjósóknar vor og haust úr Hegranesi. Árið 1840 voru í Naustavík beitarhús, sjóbúð, hjallar og útræði, þá enn notað, og eins selalagnir sumar og vetur. Engin byggð var þar sett nema sjóbúðarskýli. Eftir aldamótin 1900 fékk Jósteinn Jónasson byggðarleyfi hjá Magnúsi Gunnarssyni bónda á Utanverðunesi. Reisti Jósteinn sér þurrabúðarskýli og hafði beit og grasnytjar úr landi Utanverðuness. Ábúendur 1915–1935 voru Jósteinn Jónasson og bústýra hans, Guðmunda Sigurðardóttir, og fóru þau þaðan að Svanavatni. Þegar Jósteinn brá búi byggðist býlið ekki aftur, en var nytjað af ábúanda heimajarðarinnar.

6338960d-220f-3f8b-35b4-d54534c36460.story_eng: Selhús, also called Fremstahús, are the ruins of a beitarhús, a sheep house out in the grazing land, belonging to the farm Gilsárteigur. They stand right beside the river Gilsá, somewhat farther up than the farm's other sheep houses. A brook called Sellækur runs close by the ruins on its way into Gilsá.
6338960d-220f-3f8b-35b4-d54534c36460.story_is: Fast við Gilsá, nokkru ofar en önnur beitarhús Gilsárteigs, eru beitarhúsatættur sem kallast Selhús eða Fremstahús. Fast við tætturnar rennur lækur í Gilsá sem heitir Sellækur.

6343abd2-7872-4deb-8a72-cb2a1ede6dee.story_eng: Draugaból, whose name means roughly 'ghosts' lair', is a cave at the bottom of the ravine. Opposite it, on the north side of the ravine, are several small caves known as Drápuskútar.
6343abd2-7872-4deb-8a72-cb2a1ede6dee.story_is: Í botni gilsins heitir Draugaból. Þar á móti, norðan megin í gilinu, eru nokkrir smáhellar sem kallast Drápuskútar.

63447ca4-a9fe-14af-f3a9-144666738642.story_eng: A raven has nested on Hrafnabrík (raven crag) for many decades. It is one of a row of crags known as Bríkurnar, south of Stekkjarhvammur. Further south along the row come Hallið, Huldufólkskirkjan (the Hidden People's Church; huldufólk are the hidden people of Icelandic folk belief) and finally Syðstabrík, where the crags end.
63447ca4-a9fe-14af-f3a9-144666738642.story_is: Á Hrafnabrík hefur hrafn verpt í marga áratugi. Hún er suður af Stekkjarhvammi og er ein af Bríkunum. Sunnan við hana kemur Hallið, svo Huldufólkskirkjan og Syðstabrík, og þá eru Bríkurnar búnar.

634a0654-3454-2503-56db-c7c28a9c4f64.story_eng: Sjómannavað means "the fishermen's ford". In earlier times, people from the inland districts are believed to have done some fishing from the shores of Skjálfandi bay. It is thought likely that people from Skriðuhverfi, for example, rode across this ford when they went to sea or went to fetch fish. The ford lies a little above the mouth of the river channel Ytri-Kvísl.
634a0654-3454-2503-56db-c7c28a9c4f64.story_is: Á fyrri tíð mun útræði hafa verið stundað eitthvað af innsveitamönnum við Skjálfanda. Er líklegt að t.d. Skriðhverfungar hafi riðið vað þetta þá er þeir fóru til sjós eða að sækja fisk. Vaðið er nokkru fyrir ofan Ytri-Kvíslarkjaft.

636a49b5-77f0-3f93-45b5-dc61e5754f01.story_eng: Hundalækur means "dog stream". It is said that a stray dog was once seen from the farm Þverá and was later found dead in the stream. The stream rises high on Mylluholt hill and flows northeast down into the river Þverá.
636a49b5-77f0-3f93-45b5-dc61e5754f01.story_is: Flækingshundur átti að hafa sést frá Þverá og fundist síðan dauður í læknum. Hundalækur sprettur upp ofarlega í Mylluholti og rennur norðaustur af því, niður í Þverána.

63d4d6cd-3a87-44d3-821f-16e09f62d5c0.story_eng: Brenna, a name meaning 'burning', is a stretch of heath below the brushwood that lies under the cliffs of Hnjúkur. Charcoal used to turn up in every patch of bare, eroded ground here, a sign that a great deal of charcoal was once made on this slope. In later years Brenna has become much more overgrown. Some people believe it reaches all the way from the cliffs down to Teigahall, just above the marshland that rises from the river.
63d4d6cd-3a87-44d3-821f-16e09f62d5c0.story_is: Neðan við klettana í Hnjúknum er kjarrlendi, en þar niður af heitir Brenna, niður á Hallið milli giljanna. Í Brennu var áður viðarkol að finna í hverju flagi, sem sýnir að hér hefur mikið verið gert til kola. Brenna hefur gróið mikið upp hin seinni ár. Sumir telja að Brenna nái alla leið frá klettum niður á Teigahall, sem er rétt fyrir ofan mýrlendið upp frá ánni.

63d80434-e528-5719-833b-d5f86e3dd3e6.story_eng: Faint traces of old ruins can still be made out here, beneath a high slope called Selbrekka. A sel was a summer shieling, where livestock were kept and milked. The site lies midway between Skyggnir and Selhóll, a large scoria hill with a crater bowl on its top.
63d80434-e528-5719-833b-d5f86e3dd3e6.story_is: Mitt á milli Skyggnis og Selhóls er Sel. Þar sér móta fyrir gömlum tóttum neðan undir hárri brekku, Selbrekku. Selhóll, norðvestur af Skyggni, er stór gjallhóll með gígskál í kolli.

63d8df2c-5a1e-0a6d-5dcc-2359e8b8d50a.story_eng: Valþjófur is a stony ledge set quite high up in Miðdalur, at the head of the valley Valþjófsdalur. Some have claimed that Valþjófur the settler lies buried in a burial mound up on this ledge, and, as the description puts it, no one can be faulted for believing that if they wish.
63d8df2c-5a1e-0a6d-5dcc-2359e8b8d50a.story_is: Í Miðdal fyrir botni Valþjófsdals er allhátt uppi grjóthjalli einn sem nefndur er Valþjófur. Einhverjir munu hafa haldið því fram að þarna uppi á grjóthjallanum sé Valþjófur landnámsmaður heygður, og engan getur víst sakað að þeir taki slíkt trúanlegt sem það vilja.

63ed558d-d166-c6b6-1ad3-b9d718b841ef.story_eng: A small hut called Hestarétt (horse fold) once stood on a low, round-topped knoll in the home field, and the knoll still carries the name today, though the hut is gone.
