96be3ffe-2598-3b8b-1bef-8d035d0933c5.story_eng: An ancient burial mound was laid bare here when the wind blew away the soil around it. The name fits: kuml is an old word for a grave from pagan times, and teigur means a strip of field.

96c7f78f-fada-9578-e3a8-d421e25ce417.story_eng: Below the main road, on its western side, lie heather-covered banks called Stekkjarbörð, meaning roughly "fold banks". They hold the ruins of a stekkur, a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes in early summer so the ewes could be milked. The banks also have many grassy hollows, but their names are not known.
96c7f78f-fada-9578-e3a8-d421e25ce417.story_is: Fyrir neðan þjóðveginn, vestan við hann, eru lyngivaxin börð sem heita Stekkjarbörð og í þeim eru stekkjarrústir. Í börðunum eru margar graslautir, en ekki er kunnugt um nöfn á þeim.

96dcd159-8e99-4ea6-bd95-aa7289f5d1fb.story_eng: At the northern end of the Flóagaflstún homefield there is a low grassy mound. This is where the farm Flóagafl stood for about 1000 years, from the 10th century to the 20th. The farm was abandoned in 1904, and its last farmer was named Guðmundur Ólafsson. The farmhouse is now gone.
96dcd159-8e99-4ea6-bd95-aa7289f5d1fb.story_is: Þegar komið er að Flóagaflstúni sést að nyrst er bali í túninu. Þar var bærinn Flóagafl í um 1000 ár, allt frá 10. öld til 20. aldar. Hann lagðist í eyði árið 1904. Síðasti ábúandinn hét Guðmundur Ólafsson.

97035e88-9b0a-f92e-8256-d52154ff369f.story_eng: Tracks run south along these banks beside the lakes, known locally as Vötnin. In the days when people travelled mostly on horseback, this was quite a busy route. Down by Rauðhamar no fewer than 26 to 30 tracks can be seen running almost side by side, showing how much traffic once passed along the lakes.
97035e88-9b0a-f92e-8256-d52154ff369f.story_is: Suður með Vötnunum eru götur eftir Vatnabörmum, en þar var allfjölfarin leið fyrrum, meðan mest var ferðast á hestum. Þarna niður við Rauðhamarinn sjást ekki færri en 26–30 götur sem næst samsíða, sem sýna að allfjölfarin leið hefur verið meðfram Vötnunum.

9703fdd7-8eb0-9a30-21ae-fe55b685f31b.story_eng: The name means "Cave of the Hundred Men." A hundred people are said to have hidden here from the Turks, which gave the cave its name, though this is not recorded anywhere. The cave lies in the middle of the lava field. It is low and about 80 feet long, with two chambers, the longer of which faces southwest.
9703fdd7-8eb0-9a30-21ae-fe55b685f31b.story_is: Í þessum helli eiga hundrað manns að hafa falist fyrir Tyrkjum og þaðan er nafnið komið, en þess sést hvergi getið. Hellirinn er lágur, í miðju hrauni, 80 fet á lengd með tveimur körmum, og snýr sá lengri til útsuðurs.

97128c34-7520-11df-7f6b-aeba8afd3415.story_eng: Stöðull is a low hill south of the farm, inside the home-field fence and just south of a ditch that runs there now. It is believed that there were once ewe pens (kvíar) here, where the sheep were gathered for milking. A horse corral stood here and still does, with another small pen or shelter just east of it.
97128c34-7520-11df-7f6b-aeba8afd3415.story_is: Stöðull er holt suður af bæ, sunnan við skurð sem þar er nú, innan túngirðingar. Þar er talið að kvíar muni hafa verið, og þar var og er hestarétt og önnur lítil rétt eða byrgi austan við hestaréttina.

971b35c8-4b07-2946-4916-003851c3d9e1.story_eng: The old farmhouse stood on this mound. It was one of three timber houses on Tjörnes built from the wood of the mine hall (Námuskálinn), at Hallbjarnarstaðir, Hringver and Ytri-Tunga. The house at Ytri-Tunga was taken down in 1966–67.
971b35c8-4b07-2946-4916-003851c3d9e1.story_is: Þarna stóð gamli bærinn, eitt af þremur timburhúsum sem reist voru á Tjörnesi úr viðum Námuskálans, á Hallbjarnarstöðum, Hringveri og Ytri-Tungu. Ytri-Tunguhúsið var tekið niður 1966–67.

9736f4b3-1eb0-11a0-62ec-e69008466947.story_eng: This tongue of land, said to be tussocky, lies between Silungakelda and the river Höfðaá. It takes its name from Sigfús Sigfússon, the collector of Icelandic folktales, who was allowed to make hay here. Around 1910 he lived at the farm Höfði as a lodger, someone who kept a household on another person's farm without land of his own.
9736f4b3-1eb0-11a0-62ec-e69008466947.story_is: Sigfús Sigfússon þjóðsagnaritari fékk að heyja hér, en hann var í húsmennsku á Höfða um 1910. Tanginn er sagður þýfður og liggur á milli Silungakeldu og Höfðaár.

9738180b-bd5e-506c-08be-d373fa9d395c.story_eng: Álfakista, meaning "elf chest" or "elf coffin", is a great stone, or rather a boulder, jutting out into the gorge of the river Grjótá just below the waterfall Lambamelsfoss. A king's grave is said to lie there, though presumably not the grave of a king of this world.
9738180b-bd5e-506c-08be-d373fa9d395c.story_is: Álfakista er mikill steinn eða öllu heldur bjarg sem skagar fram í árgil Grjótár rétt neðan við Lambamelsfoss. Þar mun vera konungsgröf en væntanlega ekki þessa heims veru.

974c030f-3cee-e5ee-5c25-7e0874872650.story_eng: This bank rises above Semingsbás, a cove south of Skálavík. From the bank, a path called Semingsbásarstígur runs slantwise northward down into the cove across the scree slopes of Semingsbásarskriður. Kristján Þorsteinsson from Naustavík fell to his death there. He was considered fearless on cliffs. There is also a story that long ago a man named Semingur fell there and was killed. Another path leads down into the cove along Röðull, a knife-edged ridge that separates Skálavík from Semingsbás.
974c030f-3cee-e5ee-5c25-7e0874872650.story_is: Upp úr Semingsbás er Semingsbásarbarð og af því liggur Semingsbásarstígur skáhallt norður í básinn um Semingsbásarskriður. Þar hrapaði til bana Kristján Þorsteinsson frá Naustavík. Hann var talinn fullhugi í klettum. Sögn er til um það að þarna hafi fyrir löngu síðan hrapað maður að nafni Semingur og beðið bana. Sunnan við Skálavík er Röðull, eggþunnur hryggur sem skilur að Skálavík og Semingsbás, og eftir honum liggur stígur niður í básinn.

9759ef43-6e23-451d-b1c1-06101d5ecc8c.story_eng: Finnbogafoss is where the stream Finnbogalækur reaches the coast, and the waterfall drops straight into the sea. According to tradition, a man named Finnbogi once fished well in the waters just off the falls.
9759ef43-6e23-451d-b1c1-06101d5ecc8c.story_is: Finnbogafoss er þar sem Finnbogalækur fer til sjávar og fellur fossinn í sjó fram. Sögn er að Finnbogi nokkur hafi fiskað vel framan við hann.

97671080-e2c7-9b57-f56e-e3ba8882d842.story_eng: Stekkjarskriða takes its name from the ruins of an old stekkur, a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes so the ewes could be milked. The ruins lie at the southern end of the scree. The scree lies at the foot of the hillside along the river Dalsá and is fairly well grown over with vegetation.
97671080-e2c7-9b57-f56e-e3ba8882d842.story_is: Syðst í Stekkjarskriðu eru stekkjarrústir, og er skriðan kennd við þær. Hún er í hlíðarrótum með Dalsá, frá Klöpp suður að horni, og er allvel gróin.

97719d02-c346-6831-402a-ff50c37b4396.story_eng: Ruins stand here a short way in front of Flosahryggur, just below the mountainside. There was an elongated knoll running along the slope, and the lower part of the slope was a scree of large boulders. Several ruined walls stood at Stekkur because people lived here for a few years after 1850. The only farmer known to have lived here was Ólafur, son of Þorgrímur Sigurðsson, a farmer at Breiðavík. Ólafur was married to Þóra Þórðardóttir. In 1851 this small farm was called Urðarhvammur, meaning 'scree hollow', and in 1854 it was called Stekkur. A stekkur is a lambfold, a small pen where lambs were kept apart from the ewes so the ewes could be milked. The name Stekkur is without doubt much older than the farm, and the place had probably stopped being used as a lambfold by the time people settled here.
97719d02-c346-6831-402a-ff50c37b4396.story_is: Á Stekknum voru tóttir nokkrar, enda var búið þar nokkur ár eftir 1850. Rústirnar eru spölkorn fyrir framan Flosahrygg, rétt undir fjallshlíðinni. Þar var aflangur hóll meðfram hlíðinni, en neðri hluti hennar var stórgrýtisurð. Eini búandinn sem vitað er um þar var Ólafur, sonur Þorgríms Sigurðssonar bónda í Breiðavík, kvæntur Þóru Þórðardóttur. Árið 1851 er þetta býli nefnt Urðarhvammur, en 1854 er það nefnt Stekkur. Vafalaust er þó Stekksnafnið miklu eldra en þetta, og líklegt að staðurinn hafi verið lagður niður sem stekkur þegar hér var komið sögu.

9776b017-8ea9-0086-db41-855369fae3b1.story_eng: A woman travelling between the farms Skálpagerði and Garðsá in foul weather sought shelter beneath the rocks of this hill and died there of exposure. The name Kerlingarhóll means the old woman's hill.
9776b017-8ea9-0086-db41-855369fae3b1.story_is: Kona á leið milli Skálpagerðis og Garðsár í vonskuveðri leitaði skjóls undir klettunum og varð úti.

977be79e-e8a6-98f3-bc0d-981b05ec0bea.story_eng: Ytri-Nátthagi (the outer night pasture) lies below a narrow ledge called Einstigi and is almost entirely enclosed by cliffs. A boulder-strewn scree, Ytri-Stekkurð, at the foot of a high crag separates it from its neighbour, Fremri-Nátthagi. In the scree there is a cave, and in front of the cave a stekkur, Ytristekkur, was built of stone. A stekkur was a small fold used in spring when lambs were separated from the ewes.
977be79e-e8a6-98f3-bc0d-981b05ec0bea.story_is: Ytri-Nátthagi er undir mjóum stalli sem nefnist Einstigi. Nátthaginn er að mestu hömrum girtur, en stórgrýtt urð, Ytri-Stekkurð, undir háum kletti skilur hann frá Fremri-Nátthaga. Í urðinni er hellir, og stekkur, Ytristekkur, var hlaðinn úr grjóti þar framan við hellinn.

977cb247-c70c-42bc-9ce5-2913275c7324.story_eng: Þóreyjarborg is named after a woman who died of exposure there. It is a tall rocky crag just west of the home field of Hendilkot, standing on the boundary between the farms Hamar and Keldudalur. On its north side is the corner marker where the boundaries of Hamar and Ríp meet.
977cb247-c70c-42bc-9ce5-2913275c7324.story_is: Þóreyjarborg er nefnd eftir konu sem þar varð úti. Þetta er há klettaborg á landamerkjum Hamars og Keldudals, vestan við Hendilkotstún. Á henni norðanverðri er hornmerki Hamars- og Rípurlandamerkja.

978949b0-34f1-ebbd-55c8-6801cede7d4f.story_eng: Melbreiðarstekkur is one of the places that have disappeared under water. Low down in the bog Melbreiðarflói stood the ruins of this stekkur, a small fold where lambs were penned apart from the ewes. The site was considered rather unusual for a fold, so far down in the bog, but no other fold has been found on the land of Melbreið. Beside it were two more ruins, probably old sites where haystacks once stood.
978949b0-34f1-ebbd-55c8-6801cede7d4f.story_is: Neðarlega í Melbreiðarflóa voru rústir af Melbreiðarstekk, en staðurinn er nú horfinn undir vatn. Þetta þótti heldur óvenjulegt stekkjarstæði lengst niðri í flóa, en annað fyrirfinnst ekki í Melbreiðarlandi. Tvennar rústir voru þarna auk stekkjarins og er þar sennilega um að ræða forn heystakkastæði.

979dec0d-f2b3-409b-9f0b-a270a20f0322.story_eng: The name Smjörkistuteigar is made of plain Icelandic words and means roughly 'butter-chest meadows'. In summer, milking ewes were kept here, and it was no doubt a place where someone sat watching over them as they grazed, a job known as hjáseta. The milk here was plentiful and rich in summer.
979dec0d-f2b3-409b-9f0b-a270a20f0322.story_is: Á þessum stað hafa kvíær verið á sumrin og hefur þar eflaust verið hjásetustaður. Þar var mikil mjólk og kostug á sumrum.

97a486ed-a05c-0a88-bf3b-f3571f219640.story_eng: Ystabunga is where the fell reaches its highest point, and it has a good view. An old common saying held that three places lie at exactly the same height above the sea: the mountain Húsavíkurfjall, the farmyard at Reykjahlíð, and Ystabunga on Kinnarfell. The summit lies a little north of Miðbunga, on the high peak of Ytrihnjúkur.
97a486ed-a05c-0a88-bf3b-f3571f219640.story_is: Á Ystabungu er Fellið hæst og þaðan er gott útsýni. Gamalt almannamál er það að jafn hátt sé frá sjó, þetta þrennt: Húsavíkurfjall, hlaðið í Reykjahlíð og Ystabunga á Kinnarfelli. Ystabunga er lítið norðan við Miðbungu, utan í háhnjúk Ytrihnjúks, út af Dimmadal.

97a590a6-6453-4058-bf64-be7b41b5619f.story_eng: Kirkjugróf (church gully) is a deep stream gully east of the farm Skörð, running towards the southwest. It probably takes its name from a church or chapel (bænhús, a small private chapel on a farm) that stood at Skörð long ago. Just north of it is Hesthústunga, a tongue of land with a small ruin on it. The place no longer exists.
97a590a6-6453-4058-bf64-be7b41b5619f.story_is: Austan við bæinn í Skörðum, sunnan við Hesthústungu, er djúpt lækjardrag sem liggur til suðvesturs og heitir Kirkjugróf. Mun það draga nafn af kirkju eða bænhúsi sem var hér endur fyrir löngu í Skörðum. Á Hesthústungu er lítil tóft.

97bbb609-40b2-6e50-98ad-08fe940c4ee2.story_eng: Grímsleiði (Grímur's grave) is a small mound west of Goðhóllinn, out by the wall. Grímur, the man who fell at the hands of Hallkell, is said to lie buried here. Hallkell was the first to settle at Klausturhólar.
97bbb609-40b2-6e50-98ad-08fe940c4ee2.story_is: Vestan við Goðhólinn, vestur við garðinn, er þúfa sem nefnd er Grímsleiði. Þar á að vera heygður Grímur sá er féll fyrir Hallkeli, er byggði fyrstur Klausturhóla.

97c81ebe-3734-48e3-38f6-dea65756d37d.story_eng: At Pyttakelda a stream runs underground for a stretch of 40 to 50 metres, and small trout can be caught through little openings in the bog above it. The spot has always been a popular fishing place for the children and young people of the farm Fjall.
97c81ebe-3734-48e3-38f6-dea65756d37d.story_is: Í Pyttakeldu er hægt að veiða smásilung upp um smáop í mýrinni, en á 40–50 metra löngum kafla rennur lækur þar neðanjarðar. Pyttakelda hefur ávallt verið vinsæll veiðistaður fyrir börn og unglinga í Fjalli.

97e33f04-0356-bcfa-1639-e9a8575feaab.story_eng: Sigurðarhæð is a hill of bare rock. On its west side is a small rock shelter called Sigurðarhellir, with a large stone wall built at its mouth. A man named Sigurður is said to have stayed there in the old days, and it was quite common for wandering vagrants to take shelter in caves like these.
97e33f04-0356-bcfa-1639-e9a8575feaab.story_is: Sigurðarhæð er klapparhæð og vestan í henni er hellisskúti sem heitir Sigurðarhellir. Hleðsla mikil er við skútann og á einhver Sigurður að hafa haldið þar til í gamla daga, enda var alvanalegt að flökkukarlar hefðust við í þessum hellum.

97ee7469-f8e2-45d3-94c3-efe017466c28.story_eng: Hundavogur is a fairly long but narrow inlet in the rocks, and it is extremely deep. It has three names: Hundavogur (dog inlet), Kattarvogur (cat inlet) and a rude one, Kuntuvogur. Dogs and cats were drowned here until at least the middle of the 20th century. The animals were put in a sack, and a stone was tied to them for company on the last stretch. The inlet lies among the Vogarnir, the coves at the outer end of Krossnes, the headland on which the farm stands.
97ee7469-f8e2-45d3-94c3-efe017466c28.story_is: Yst á Krossnesi, nesinu sem bærinn stendur á, eru Vogarnir. Þar er nokkuð langur en þröngur bás og er hann hyldjúpur. Á honum eru þrjú nöfn, Hundavogur, Kattarvogur og hið dónalega nafn Kuntuvogur. Í þessum vog var hundum og köttum drekkt fram yfir miðja 20. öld að minnsta kosti. Kvikindin voru sett í poka og steini bundið við þau til fylgdar síðasta spölinn.

97feb8a8-e0cc-b5a0-dbb6-cab7420eaf87.story_eng: Ingibjargarpyttur is one of several pits in the wetland called Keldan. It is said to be named after Ingibjörg Jóhannsdóttir, the district's schoolteacher, who was travelling by sledge along the Sleðabrautin (the sledge track) with an escort. Things went badly here, and at least the horse fell into one of the pits, which has carried her name ever since. Just to the south, beside a small gravel mound, there seemed to be faint traces of an old structure. The bog hole no longer exists.
97feb8a8-e0cc-b5a0-dbb6-cab7420eaf87.story_is: Norðan við lítinn mel út við votlendi virtist votta fyrir mannvirkjaleif. Þar norðan við eru pyttir í Keldunni og heitir einn þeirra Ingibjargarpyttur. Tilefni nafnsins var sagt að það hafi verið að barnakennari sveitarinnar, Ingibjörg Jóhannsdóttir, var þarna á ferð á sleða eftir Sleðabrautinni ásamt fylgdarmanni. Þarna tókst svo illa til að að minnsta kosti hesturinn lenti ofan í einn pyttinn. Af því fékk pytturinn nafn.

981e7ef6-d82d-9680-3232-fff50f545b57.story_eng: These fairly high, prominent peaks rise above the farm. It is said that Kollur of Kollsstaðir climbed up onto the peaks and threw his staff from there, and that it came down by Kollslækur in Hálsasveit. The farm once stood where the beitarhús (sheep houses out in the grazing land) now are. At that time the peaks are thought to have been called Kollshamar, and the farm Kollshamar as well.
981e7ef6-d82d-9680-3232-fff50f545b57.story_is: Hnúkarnir eru upp af bænum, allháir og áberandi. Sagt er að Kollur á Kollsstöðum hafi farið upp á hnúkana og hent þaðan staf sínum og hann komið niður hjá Kollslæk í Hálsasveit. Bærinn var áður þar sem beitarhúsin eru. Hnúkarnir hafa þá heitið Kollshamar og bærinn Kollshamar.

982bf220-a46d-cf70-eca4-b94ff7398c10.story_eng: Bollamór lies in the hay meadow straight out from the farm of Jódísarstaðir. It gave good hay, though the ground was covered in small, hard tussocks, and it was called "unginn úr enginu", literally "the chick of the meadow". In the middle of Bollamór is a deep hollow, and this hollow gives the place its name (bolli means bowl).
982bf220-a46d-cf70-eca4-b94ff7398c10.story_is: Í enginu beint út af bænum á Jódísarstöðum er Bollamór, heygóður en smákargaþýfður – „unginn úr enginu“. Í Bollamó miðjum er djúp dokk sem gefur honum nafn.

9846cde7-8861-eece-12e6-1c7d22472f3f.story_eng: This tongue of land between the rivers Syðri-Höfðagilsá and Þvergilsá, just beyond Kamburinn, was once a resting place for travellers. Tradition holds that the chieftain Þorgeir Ljósvetningagoði stopped to rest here while carrying the body of his brother-in-law Ásbjörn to be buried at Ljósavatn.
9846cde7-8861-eece-12e6-1c7d22472f3f.story_is: Í tungunni á milli Syðri-Höfðagilsár og Þvergilsár, utan við Kambinn, var áningarstaður. Þar segir sagan að Þorgeir Ljósvetningagoði hafi áð er hann flutti lík Ásbjörns mágs síns til greftrunar á Ljósavatni.

984d1bdc-660f-a9f5-79ef-c262967e571e.story_eng: Guðrúnarstaðahóll is a high bank of sand. Somewhere near it there was probably once a farm called Guðrúnarstaðir, which gave the hill its name. Ruins of buildings came to light here when soil erosion stripped away the ground.
984d1bdc-660f-a9f5-79ef-c262967e571e.story_is: Guðrúnarstaðahóll er hátt sandbarð austur frá Bæjarnöf. Þar nálægt mun sennilega einhvern tíma áður hafa verið býlið Guðrúnarstaðir. Komu þar í ljós tóftir við uppblástur.

98543382-5b94-4c16-8584-2b57d6ce0b03.story_eng: Brönuskál, meaning Brana's bowl, is a bowl-shaped slab of rock east of Eyrarnar. It is named after the troll woman Brana, who was said to have lived in Bláhvammur.
98543382-5b94-4c16-8584-2b57d6ce0b03.story_is: Skálarmynduð hella austan við Eyrarnar. Hún er kennd við tröllskessuna Brönu sem sögð var hafa búið í Bláhvammi.

98603f71-d484-4436-8f2b-b01f00172a96.story_eng: Neðstahvilft, the 'lowest hollow', is the first part of Hringvershvilft, also called Hvilftin, a surprisingly large and varied grassy hollow that runs south from Bátatorfan. Beitarhús, sheep houses out in the grazing land, once stood at the western end of Neðstahvilft. The outermost of them, called Borgin, had last been used about 30 years before this account was written. South of Borgin are the ruins of an older sheep house and a barn that stood there until not long before. Some traces of old verbúðir, the huts where fishermen stayed during the fishing season, are also said to remain here.
98603f71-d484-4436-8f2b-b01f00172a96.story_is: Til suðurs frá Bátatorfunni liggur Hringvershvilft eða Hvilftin, furðu stór og margbreytilegur grashvammur, og er þar fyrst Neðstahvilft. Beitarhús voru áður vestast í Neðstuhvilft. Það ysta heitir Borgin og var síðast notað fyrir 30 árum, en sunnan við Borgina eru tóttir af eldra fjárhúsi og hlöðu sem þar voru ekki fyrir alls löngu, og suður af þeim er Húsahvammur. Einnig munu þarna vera nokkur merki um gamlar verbúðir.

98947dd4-5e38-7527-48c9-5bd9ba0e945e.story_eng: This pond lies in a narrow bog and was counted among the worst dangers in the land of Kirkjubær. Hardly a year is said to have passed without some livestock going into it, most often more than one animal. The sheep were wild for the sedge growing along its edges, which drew them to the brink. In later times the pond came to be called Drápstjörn, which means 'killing pond'.
98947dd4-5e38-7527-48c9-5bd9ba0e945e.story_is: Inn af Efritjörn liggur önnur mýri, mjórri. Í henni er ein versta hættan í Kirkjubæjarlandi. Mun ekki hafa liðið svo ár að ekki færi eitthvað af skepnum í þessa tjörn, oftast fleiri en ein skepna. Var féð vitlaust í störina við rendur hennar. Þessi tjörn er nú síðar nefnd Drápstjörn.

989c7b27-9f01-bef5-f265-ae931a478819.story_eng: Stekkamelur is the outermost named gravel hill in a row of them running inland along the river. In front of it lies a ravine, Stekkagil. Both the ravine and the hill take their names from sheep pens (stekkur) that once stood in the ravine.
989c7b27-9f01-bef5-f265-ae931a478819.story_is: Inn með ánni eru melar, og heitir sá ysti þeirra sem nafn hefur Stekkamelur. Framan við hann er Stekkagil. Dregur gilið og melurinn nafn af kvíum (stekk) sem voru í gilinu.

98a4f7ef-fe2b-8b24-5fca-99e2881d56be.story_eng: Where the rivers Ólafsfjarðardalsá and Holtsdalsá meet, they form a fairly large tongue of land. Old oral tradition holds that the settler Bárður Suðureyingur built his farm here. He is said to have named it Mjóvidalur, meaning 'narrow valley', and to have named the river Mjóvadalsá.
98a4f7ef-fe2b-8b24-5fca-99e2881d56be.story_is: Þar sem Ólafsfjarðardalsá og Holtsdalsá koma saman myndast allstór tunga og herma svo forn munnmæli að Bárður Suðureyingur landnámsmaður hafi reist þar bæ sinn og kallað hann Mjóvadal og ána Mjóvadalsá.

98b5cfd7-681b-43ba-7393-27bddb9fe75c.story_eng: Bardagalágar means "battle hollows". These are dips in the land above Gjögrin that cannot be seen from Gjögrin below. According to the story, the farmers of Tunga and Sellátranes once fought each other here, and the cause of the fight was Urðavellir.
98b5cfd7-681b-43ba-7393-27bddb9fe75c.story_is: Upp undan Gjögrunum eru lautir sem ekki sjást neðan frá Gjögrunum og heita þær Bardagalágar. Þar segir sagan að Tungubóndinn og Sellátranesbóndinn hafi eitt sinn barist og var bardagaefnið Urðavellirnir.

98d1ebdc-e179-ca13-e617-2f4343e3da10.name_eng: Eðvaldshús, ruins of a sheep house
98d1ebdc-e179-ca13-e617-2f4343e3da10.story_eng: A sheep house once stood on the ridge here, at the top edge of the old home field. It was called Eðvaldshús, or Lambhús (lamb house), and was named after Eðvald Eyjólfsson, a postman who lived for a time at Ormsstaðir. The house no longer stands.
98d1ebdc-e179-ca13-e617-2f4343e3da10.story_is: Á ásnum, efst við gamla túnið, stóð fjárhús nefnt Eðvaldshús eða Lambhús, kennt við Eðvald Eyjólfsson póst sem bjó um tíma á Ormsstöðum.

98d2106f-90c3-49a8-d154-c28681b44edc.story_eng: On 21 January 1841 an avalanche fell from Ytri-Hvammshnjúkur down between the Haukabrekkur slopes, and Sigurður Hallsson, an 18-year-old farmer's son and shepherd from Hvammur, was killed there. Syðri-Haukabrekkur is a fairly broad gravelly knoll in the hollow directly below Hvammsskál.
98d2106f-90c3-49a8-d154-c28681b44edc.story_is: Úr Ytri-Hvammshnjúk féll snjóflóð hinn 21. janúar 1841 niður á milli Haukabrekknanna og fórst þar 18 ára bóndasonur og sauðamaður frá Hvammi, Sigurður Hallsson. Syðri-Haukabrekkur kallast allbreiður melhaus í kverkinni beint niður undan Hvammsskálinni.

98e2ce10-52f5-2851-a536-ac37aade1438.story_eng: Gunnufuð is a cleft in the mouth of the Hvannárgil gorge. In later times a certain Magnús goði used the cleft as a fold to gather his sheep that grazed outdoors through the winter. Since then it has more often been called Mangafuð.
98e2ce10-52f5-2851-a536-ac37aade1438.story_is: Í gilskjaftinum á Hvannárgili er skoran Gunnufuð. Síðar réttaði Magnús nokkur goði útigangsfé sitt í skorunni og hefur hún verið fremur nefnd Mangafuð.

990c6fba-4959-d828-ddca-541f223d145d.story_eng: Helguþúfa is a cone-shaped hill with a rock face at the front, rising directly above Langatangi. No one knows where the name comes from. According to oral tradition, a tunnel is supposed to lead up into Helguþúfa from the shore. It is also said that three crosses are cracked into the grass on top, which is entirely grass-covered. Helguþúfa is described as a very strange place.
990c6fba-4959-d828-ddca-541f223d145d.story_is: Helguþúfa er strýtumynduð og klettur að framan, beint upp af Langatanga. Enginn veit af hverju nafnið er dregið. Munnmæli eru um að göng eigi að vera upp í Helguþúfu úr fjörunni. Sagt er að á henni eigi að vera þrír krossar sprungnir í grasið, en þúfan er algróin grasi að ofan. Helguþúfa er mjög einkennilegur staður.

997488b1-9116-4e62-bfa9-dd6d17499498.story_eng: Volgalaug is a warm spring, about 40°C, in the gully by the southwest corner of the largest greenhouse. All the drinking and household water for the farm Reykir was once fetched from here, until water was piped in from Kaldalind. The spring is now covered over, and its water is used for the swimming pool.
997488b1-9116-4e62-bfa9-dd6d17499498.story_is: Volgalaug er volg uppspretta, um 40° heit, í gilinu við suðvesturhorn stærsta gróðurhússins. Þangað var sótt allt neysluvatn frá Reykjum, þar til vatn var leitt úr Köldulind. Lindin er nú hulin og vatnið notað í sundlaugina.

997a8160-9150-c24c-824f-e26927ee3dbf.story_eng: Þyrill was a tall, round gravel hill of unusual shape at the lower end of Ytrimelar, the gravel flats where the main road runs. The name suggests a whirlwind, yet there was hardly anything special about the weather there, as the hill was not that high, and the local informant did not know where the name came from. The road authority had its eye on the hill as a source of gravel for road surfacing. It was saved, though only after some of it had been taken, and it was thought likely to be left in peace from then on. It is now recorded as no longer existing. Just west of the hill lies Þyrilskot, a very old abandoned farm. Traces of the farmhouse, the sheep houses and a circular home-field wall could still be seen there, and a stekkur (a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes) was later built down inside the ruins.
997a8160-9150-c24c-824f-e26927ee3dbf.story_is: Þar sem þjóðvegurinn liggur heita Ytrimelar. Neðst í þeim er hár, kringlóttur og sérkennilegur melhóll sem heitir Þyrill. Varla er neitt sérstakt um veður þar, hann er ekki það hár, og ekki er vitað hvernig á nafninu stendur. Fleiri há holt eru þarna. Vegagerðin hafði augastað á hólnum til ofaníburðar, en tekist hefur að bjarga honum og er líklega tryggt að hann verði látinn í friði hér eftir. Aðeins hefur hann þó verið skertur. Hóllinn er nú skráður horfinn. Rétt vestan við hólinn er gamalt eyðibýli nefnt Þyrilskot. Þar sér enn fyrir bæ, fjárhúsum og hringlaga túngirðingu, og er það mjög gamalt. Stekkur hefur verið byggður þar niðri í.

998d104a-d08b-0167-812d-4d0f1dd8a07e.story_eng: Hlíðarnámur, also called Reykjahlíðarnámur or Hverir, is a field of mud pots at the eastern foot of the mountain, with Hveraröndin lying to the east of it. In earlier times there were fairly large sulphur mines here, which is where the names come from: námur means mines.
998d104a-d08b-0167-812d-4d0f1dd8a07e.story_is: Hverir er leirhverasvæði austan undir fjallinu og austan þeirra er Hveraröndin. Svæði þetta er einnig nefnt Hlíðarnámur eða Reykjahlíðarnámur. Hér voru allmiklar brennisteinsnámur til forna.

9990c41b-cb1f-e524-dfa1-f3708735ecd2.story_eng: Fjóshólsbrekka is the slope on the southwest side of Fjóshóll (cowshed hill), a hill just west of the farm. Hidden people (huldufólk) are said to live in Fjóshóll, and nothing there may be disturbed.
9990c41b-cb1f-e524-dfa1-f3708735ecd2.story_is: Vestan við bæinn er Fjóshóll. Þar er huldufólksbyggð og má ekki hreyfa þar neitt. Suðvestan í hólnum er Fjóshólsbrekka.

9990d552-e639-459d-a22b-6b8b573e7a68.story_eng: Flekatá is a very grassy stretch of land. Towards its southern end lie the ruins of a farm of the same name, which was inhabited for a number of years in the late 19th century. The outermost part of the land is called Hvilftarbakki or Jaðar.
9990d552-e639-459d-a22b-6b8b573e7a68.story_is: Flekatá er mjög grösug og á henni sunnarlega eru rústir eftir samnefnt býli, sem þar var í byggð um nokkurt árabil seint á nítjándu öld. Flekatá liggur beint upp af Sandhvilftinni, milli Hvilftar og Rekárgils, og yst heitir Hvilftarbakki eða Jaðar.

999dda35-0e57-4610-8bc7-443408da39aa.story_eng: This marsh is named after a playful skyr fight. A woman named Kristín worked as a farmhand for Jason Steinþórsson. One day out on the hay meadows the two were joking around while eating skyr, a thick Icelandic dairy food. The fun got rougher, and in the end they were throwing skyr at each other to see who had the better aim.
999dda35-0e57-4610-8bc7-443408da39aa.story_is: Kristín nokkur var vinnukona hjá Jasoni Steinþórssyni. Þau voru eitthvað að gantast á engjunum og voru að borða skyr. En svo kárnaði gamanið og að lokum voru þau farin að kasta skyri hvort á annað og reyndu hæfni sína, hvort hitti betur.

99ad8d9d-3ac3-ac2d-d3a0-4378950c8db1.story_eng: Below the home field at Saxhóll are very old walls built of lava stone, the remains of night pens or walled enclosures. Sumartröð (roughly 'summer enclosure') is the lower of the two; the one nearer the home field is called Blesatröð. Inside Sumartröð is another stone structure, most likely a fold where ewes were milked. This was done after the lambs had been separated from their mothers, an old practice known as 'fráfærur', so that the ewes' milk could be used by the household.
99ad8d9d-3ac3-ac2d-d3a0-4378950c8db1.story_is: Neðan við tún á Saxhóli eru mjög fornar hleðslur úr hraungrjóti. Það eru nátthagar eða traðir. Sumartröð er sú neðri, en sú sem er nær túninu heitir Blesatröð. Innan Sumartraðar er hleðsla, líkast til kvíar þar sem sauðfé var mjólkað þegar fært var frá.

99b51766-7575-4df5-2010-b5bfc9e398bc.story_eng: Stekkjarnef is a promontory on the southwest side of the Hagahraun lava field. Its name refers to the old stekkur (a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes in spring) that lies below it on its east side. A very short distance away is the cave Hagahellir. The walls built up in front of the cave mouth show clearly that it was once used for keeping livestock.
99b51766-7575-4df5-2010-b5bfc9e398bc.story_is: Suðvestan á Hagahrauni heitir Stekkjarnef en austan undir því er gamall stekkur. Örskammt þaðan er Hagahellir. Greinilegt er á hleðslum fyrir hellismunnanum að hann hefur verið notaður til búfjárvörslu.

99bec6f8-7e71-288a-3aa9-3ac3011562e6.story_eng: High up in this gully stands a stone called Huldusteinn. The gully lies on the north side of the stream Gerðislækur.
99bec6f8-7e71-288a-3aa9-3ac3011562e6.story_is: Ofarlega í Syðragerðislækjargili er Huldusteinn. Gilið er norðan við Gerðislæk og Rinda.

99c70c6c-b8cc-4749-a487-a24b2f8a07ea.story_eng: According to local oral tradition, a priest drowned here in winter while making his house visits, the rounds a parish priest made to the homes of his parishioners. The name Prestspyttur means "the priest's pool".
99c70c6c-b8cc-4749-a487-a24b2f8a07ea.story_is: Munnmæli eru um að þarna hafi prestur drukknað að vetri til í húsvitjun.

99e4dd75-caa6-c6d5-62f6-7a128753a879.story_eng: By the lake stands a naust, a boat shed, called Stafnsnaust, also known as Víðanaust. A clear path, Stafnsgata, runs west from it to the farm Stafn, dating from the time when people from Stafn came here to fish.
99e4dd75-caa6-c6d5-62f6-7a128753a879.story_is: Við vatnið heldur norðar er naust sem nefnt er Stafnsnaust, líka nefnt Víðanaust. Þaðan liggur skýr gata, Stafnsgata, vestur í Stafn frá þeim tíma er hér var stunduð veiði frá Stafni.

99e6d72f-f0b5-4222-8bd2-c03a9e538204.story_eng: Einbúi (a word for someone who lives alone) is a solitary stony hillock rising out of the flat bog, high up on the marsh above the farm Hólkot. Héðinn, one of the original settlers, is said to be buried here. People once began digging into the mound, but mishaps stopped the work, and it is said that disturbing the burial mound brings misfortune. In shape it is not unlike the mounds Mánahaugur and Válahaugur. Close by runs Héraðsgarður, an old wall stretching from the river Máná to Mývatnssveit.
99e6d72f-f0b5-4222-8bd2-c03a9e538204.story_is: Ofarlega á mýrinni, upp af Hólkoti, er stakur hóll með grjóti í sem heitir Einbúi og stendur upp úr sléttri mýrinni. Þar á Héðinn landnámsmaður að vera heygður. Grafið hefur verið í hólinn, en óhöpp stöðvuðu verkið. Er sagt að það boði ógæfu að róta í haugnum. Þessi haugur er ekki ósvipaður í lögun og Mánahaugur og Válahaugur. Rétt hjá Einbúa er göngugarður sá sem liggur frá Máná til Mývatnssveitar og heitir Héraðsgarður.

99ec7c76-5095-f431-fea7-2d79ff957e5b.story_eng: Rolluberg is a rocky ridge running south from the southwest corner of the lake Vatnskotsvatn. On its northeastern part stands the sheep-sorting fold of the people of Rípurhreppur, built of stone. A natural rock wall runs along its west side, and the sheep are driven along this wall and into the fold. Þórarinn Jónasson of Hróarsdalur said that Rolluberg was a dwelling of huldufólk (hidden people). An old account tells of a rider passing the strange cliffs west of Vatnskot who saw farmhouse gables standing side by side. In some places people and horses stood in the yards, and elsewhere people stood in doorways, some dressed as common folk and others as gentry. He was so absorbed by the sight that he hardly heard what his companion Sigurður was saying, until his horse stumbled and nearly threw him. The account may refer to the nearby Vatnskotsberg, but it has been linked to Rolluberg because of its reputation as a home of hidden people.
99ec7c76-5095-f431-fea7-2d79ff957e5b.story_is: Rolluberg er klettarani sem liggur frá suðvesturhorni Vatnskotsvatns og suður undir Urriðaberg. Á Rollubergi norðaustanverðu stendur fjárskilarétt Rípurhreppsbúa, hlaðin úr grjóti. Klettaveggur gengur með henni að vestan og er féð rekið meðfram honum og inn í réttina. Þórarinn Jónasson í Hróarsdal sagði að Rollubergið væri bústaður huldufólks. Í gamalli frásögn segir: „En undarlegir voru þessir hamrar fyrir vestan Vatnskot, þar var hver bæjarburstin við aðra, sums staðar stóð fólk og hestar á hlaðinu, en annars staðar stóð fólk í dyrum. Sumir voru klæddir að sið alþýðumanna, en aðrir að höfðingjasið. Ég veit ekki hve miklu ég tók eftir af því sem Sigurður var að tala við mig, því ég var með hugann svo bundinn við það sem ég sá. Allt í einu hrökk ég upp úr hugleiðingum mínum við það að hesturinn hnaut, svo ég var nálega hrokkinn af baki.“ Frásögnin gæti átt við Vatnskotsbergið, en hún er tengd Rollubergi vegna þess að þar á huldufólk að búa.

9a4f5311-6383-25ee-1829-ac49789f33e7.story_eng: Pósthestahúsin means "the post-horse houses". Here the postmen stabled their horses on their mail journeys between Reykjavík and South Iceland. Today only old, grass-covered ruins remain, north of the driveway leading up to the farm.
9a4f5311-6383-25ee-1829-ac49789f33e7.story_is: Þar hýstu póstarnir hesta sína í póstferðum milli Reykjavíkur og Suðurlands. Nú eru þar gamlar, grasi grónar tóftir norðan við heimreiðina að bænum.

9a539a32-b539-894c-cbc7-442989a85082.story_eng: When dogs or cats had more young than were wanted, the puppies and kittens were put in small bags with a stone and sunk in this pool, which is how it got its name, Hundadý (dý means a boggy pool, hundur a dog). The pond was strictly off limits to children at play.
9a539a32-b539-894c-cbc7-442989a85082.story_is: Þegar fjölgun varð hjá hundum eða köttum og þurfti að fækka voru afkvæmin sett í litla poka og steinn með og þeim sökkt í Hundadýið, og þar af er nafnið. Þessi tjörn var bannsvæði til barnaleikja.

9a76d3ff-7b13-2448-9c66-5dfbbd58fae8.story_eng: Pétursborg is a low, stout rock, slightly hollow, at the north-eastern corner of the Pétursborgarbruni lava field. It stands on the western boundary of the farm Knútsstaðir. A man named Pétur, a farmhand of Björn the sýslumaður (district magistrate) at Knútsstaðir, died of exposure here while walking to the beitarhús (a sheep house out in the grazing land) at Austari-Hellur.
9a76d3ff-7b13-2448-9c66-5dfbbd58fae8.story_is: Pétursborg er lágur, digur, lítið holur klettur við norðausturhorn Pétursborgarbruna, klettaborg á merkjum Knútsstaða að vestan. Þar varð úti Pétur, vinnumaður Björns sýslumanns á Knútsstöðum, þegar hann gekk á beitarhús á Austari-Hellur.

9a93955f-dc86-e34b-5003-39197e971986.story_eng: Sveltugjá means roughly 'starvation fissure'. As far as is known, nearly 20 sheep have died of starvation after becoming trapped in it. Stones have been built up in this fissure and in many others in the lava so that sheep could climb out of them. This was first done at the initiative of J.J., the farmer at Sílalækur, who died in 1946.
9a93955f-dc86-e34b-5003-39197e971986.story_is: Í Sveltugjá hafa farist í sveltu, svo vitað sé, nær 20 fjár. Í þessa gjá og margar fleiri í hrauninu hefur verið hlaðið til þess að fé hefði sig upp úr þeim. Það var fyrst gert fyrir atbeina J.J., bónda á Sílalæk, sem lést árið 1946.

9a9a54f1-19f2-baef-22b8-99f10fd25d9c.story_eng: According to oral tradition, a troll named Tumás was buried here under a mound of stones, and the place carries his name.
9a9a54f1-19f2-baef-22b8-99f10fd25d9c.story_is: Munnmæli segja að þar hafi verið dysjaður tröllkarl að nafni Tumás.

9aae6c3d-b2bf-4ef3-b741-ef7b45174da5.story_eng: Gíslasteinn (Gísli's Rock) takes its name from a man called Gísli who drowned in the river Eyjafjarðará. His body washed up onto this rock.
9aae6c3d-b2bf-4ef3-b741-ef7b45174da5.story_is: Gísli drukknaði í Eyjafjarðará og lík hans rak upp á steininn.

9ae1a62c-64bc-5da1-52a2-c30a0766b4f0.story_eng: Syðriá, the "southern river", runs just south of the farm Skriða, through a ravine called Syðraárgil a short way south of Árgil. In old times the river was called Gerðisá. South of the river are the ruins of a farmstead that was called Árgerði.
9ae1a62c-64bc-5da1-52a2-c30a0766b4f0.story_is: Á er þar næst sunnan við Skriðu sem heitir Syðriá. Næst sunnan við Árgilið og stutt á milli heitir Syðraárgil og áin kallast Syðriá. Til forna hét hún Gerðisá. Sunnan við ána eru bæjarrústir. Hét bærinn Árgerði.

9af7bc42-795e-6cb0-dc86-501980d09f3e.story_eng: Skökuhóll is a small hill below the home field at Bjarnastaðir. It is believed to have been an old custom at Bjarnastaðir to churn the butter in summer when the sun stood over this hill, and the name, from skaka, to churn, recalls this.
9af7bc42-795e-6cb0-dc86-501980d09f3e.story_is: Neðan við túnið á Bjarnastöðum, nálægt Kringlugili, er lítill hóll sem heitir Skökuhóll. Talið er að forn venja hafi verið að skaka strokkinn á sumrin á Bjarnastöðum þegar sólin var yfir þessum hól.

9b010d3c-91a4-4a9a-8b7d-1a12b19b1619.story_eng: Ássel is an old sel, a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked, that belonged to the farm Neðra-Ás. It lies on a small headland along the river Kolbeinsdalsá, below the mountain Elliði. Only traces of ancient buildings can still be seen there.
9b010d3c-91a4-4a9a-8b7d-1a12b19b1619.story_is: Meðfram Kolbeinsdalsá undir Elliða er nes eitt, ekki stórt, sem heitir Ássel. Það er gamalt sel frá Neðra-Ási. Þar sjást aðeins merki fornra bygginga.

9b06f3b4-60cb-d017-f051-c7068e23fe8c.story_eng: Landsendi, meaning land's end, is the bank where the mountain Viðarfjall runs out into the sea. Just off it lies Altari, "the altar". An old postal route once crossed Landsendi, running from the home field down to the shore at Altari. Taking this way was called going "um Fjörurnar", along the shores.
9b06f3b4-60cb-d017-f051-c7068e23fe8c.story_is: Þar sem Viðarfjallið gengur fram í sjó heitir bakkinn Landsendi. Fram af honum er Altari. Gömul póstleið lá um Landsenda af túninu og niður í fjöru við Altari. Það hét að fara um Fjörurnar.

9b1e2f6e-0d09-4585-94e9-459f470ad158.story_eng: Pytturinn (the pit) was a patch of marshland with a stream running through it. In it was an old peat pit that was sometimes used to cool the milk. The pit is gone now: it was filled in because animals kept getting into danger there.
9b1e2f6e-0d09-4585-94e9-459f470ad158.story_is: Mýrarfláki með læk. Í honum var gömul mógröf sem var stundum notuð til að kæla mjólkina. Hún er horfin núna, því fyllt var upp í hana þar sem dýr voru að fara sér að voða.

9b2e4835-f777-a295-c8bc-52626c99ee9b.story_eng: Leiðaröxl, along with the nearby pass Skarð, was a route people often took when heading out into the district or into Staðardalur. It served as the church road from the farms Geirmundarstaðir and Gilsstaðir. Leiðaröxl is considerably higher than Skarð, but going over it was the shorter way. It was used less often, mainly in winter, when the going there was often better.
9b2e4835-f777-a295-c8bc-52626c99ee9b.story_is: Oft var farið um Leiðaröxl eða Skarð ef leið lá út í sveit eða fram í Staðardal. Var þetta kirkjuvegur frá Geirmundarstöðum og Gilsstöðum. Leiðaröxlin er talsvert hærri, en styttri leið var að fara hana. Hún var sjaldnar farin, nema helst að vetrarlagi, en þá var oft betra færi þar.

9b3c664a-2dba-15a9-7bc1-438de38b265e.story_eng: "Inn yfir fjall" ("in over the mountain") was the expression used at Stóruvellir for the route over the mountain. From the farm, a path known as Sneiðingur runs out and up the mountainside. A bridle path over the mountain was improved there, with stone culverts built over the worst streams, and these small bridges still stand. The route was used quite a lot. Once you come up onto the ridge, it is worth looking around if the weather is clear.
9b3c664a-2dba-15a9-7bc1-438de38b265e.story_is: „Inn yfir fjall“ var málvenja á Stóruvöllum. Frá Stóruvöllum liggur svokallaður Sneiðingur út og upp fjallið. Þar var lagfærður reiðvegur yfir fjallið og hlaðin ræsi yfir verstu lækina, og standa þær brýr enn. Þessi leið var töluvert farin. Þegar upp á ásinn kemur væri þess vert að líta í kringum sig ef bjart er veður.

9b4beb0a-b504-55c4-50b2-4467f27af523.story_eng: Ytriflös and its neighbour Syðriflös are skerries at the southern end of the shore once called Naustavíkurfjara. Somewhere up from these skerries, Baldvin Friðfinnsson from Kotamýrar is said to have climbed the cliff above them, which is called Vegghamrahorn.
9b4beb0a-b504-55c4-50b2-4467f27af523.story_is: Ytriflös og Syðriflös eru sunnan við Naustavíkurfjöru, en svo nefndist öll fjaran frá Króksbjargsfjöru að Ytriflös. Einhvers staðar upp frá Flösum kleif Baldvin Friðfinnsson frá Kotamýrum upp bjargið þar fyrir ofan, en það heitir Vegghamrahorn.

9b76eb4e-ccba-73dd-de61-42dbfd7c76bf.story_eng: Bankahúsloft was a fish-salting house that over the years served many other purposes, connected both to fishing and to cultural life. People danced in its loft, plays were performed there and Christmas parties were held. Large timber was also sawn in the building: one man stood down in the pit and another up in the upper loft, working a big two-handed saw two to three metres long between them. When fishing at Skálar had declined, the house was used, among other things, for baiting fishing lines. The children of Skálar did a good deal of the baiting, though there was always an adult with them. The building no longer stands.
9b76eb4e-ccba-73dd-de61-42dbfd7c76bf.story_is: Bankahúsloft var söltunarhús en hafði í gegnum tíðina ýmis önnur hlutverk, bæði tengd útgerð og menningu. Dansað var á Bankahúsloftinu, leikin leikrit og haldnar jólaskemmtanir. Einnig var þar sagaður stórviður. Við það verk stóð einn maður niðri í gryfjunni og annar uppi á efra loftinu. Á milli sín höfðu þeir stórviðarsög sem var tveggja til þriggja metra löng. Þegar minna var orðið um útgerð á Skálum var meðal annars beitt í húsinu. Krakkarnir á Skálum beittu talsvert, en alltaf var einhver fullorðinn með þeim við verkið.

9b9190a2-4aa0-471f-b282-463ce98c5a88.story_eng: Steinbogaklettur is named after a natural stone arch (steinbogi) that is believed to have once spanned the river Fögruhlíðará at a narrow rocky gorge on the boundary between the farms Hlíðarhús and Sleðbrjótssel. The arch collapsed long ago, and no one knows when. The gorge itself has been called both Steinbogi and Steinbogaklettur. According to one local account, however, the rock Steinbogaklettur stands towards the outer end of the ridge Selás, certainly some distance south of the gorge where the arch most likely stood.
9b9190a2-4aa0-471f-b282-463ce98c5a88.story_is: Á landamörkum Hlíðarhúsa og Sleðbrjótssels er klettaþröng sem nefnd er Steinbogi eða Steinbogaklettur. Þar er talið að hafi verið steinbogi yfir Fögruhlíðará, en hann er hruninn fyrir löngu og enginn veit hvenær. Samkvæmt munnlegri heimild er Steinbogaklettur þó utarlega á Selási, örugglega nokkru sunnar en þröngin þar sem Steinbogi hefur líklega verið.

9b9b2248-f81f-b251-3c62-d6693c33e0c2.story_eng: A man called Fúsi is said to have died of exposure here, caught out in the open, and the hill takes its name from him. It is also said to be haunted.
9b9b2248-f81f-b251-3c62-d6693c33e0c2.story_is: Hér á Fúsi nokkur að hafa orðið úti, og sagt er að þar sé reimt.

9ba30ad9-9472-e8ff-ca5e-f28ad6606068.story_eng: A story is told of this hollow. A man once lay down here to rest from mowing hay, and a boulder fell down on top of him. The boulder still lies in the hollow. It is called Auðunnarsteinn, and it has since split in two.
9ba30ad9-9472-e8ff-ca5e-f28ad6606068.story_is: Sagt er að eitt sinn hafi maður lagt sig þarna frá slætti, en þá hrapaði bjarg ofan á hann og er það allt í láginni enn. Steinninn er nefndur Auðunnarsteinn. Þessi steinn hefur klofnað í tvennt.

9bd22ec3-4562-9245-143b-ded311615406.story_eng: This mound is said to be the grave of Hrafnkell Freysgoði, the chieftain and priest of the god Freyr. It stands on a patch of hard, firm ground just beyond the stream Sjölindalækur. The mound was once dug into, and a few artefacts were found there.
9bd22ec3-4562-9245-143b-ded311615406.story_is: Hrafnkelshaugur er sagður grafhaugur Hrafnkels Freysgoða. Hann stendur á harðvellisgrund rétt utan við Sjölindalæk. Í hauginn var eitt sinn grafið og fundust þar nokkrar minjar.

9bd25176-e400-71b7-54e2-1b5f5e4c8ba6.story_eng: A farm once stood here, inhabited in 1896. It is thought to have been lived in for only a short time, and Eyjólfur Símonarson farmed here. Locals said "up to Kot" and "up in Kot". A hay barn also stood here, and traces of it could still be seen when the place names were recorded. The site of the farmhouse is still visible. A home-field map from 1920 shows an outbuilding in the same spot, so the ruins of the farm went on being used after people stopped living there.
9bd25176-e400-71b7-54e2-1b5f5e4c8ba6.story_is: Í Kot var bær, í byggð 1896. Mun hann hafa verið stutt í byggð og bjó þar Eyjólfur Símonarson. Sagt var upp í Kot og uppi í Kot. Þar stóð heyhlaða og sá enn fyrir henni þegar örnefnaskráin var skrifuð. Bæjarstæði Kots sést enn, og á túnakorti frá 1920 er útihús á sama stað. Tóftir bæjarins voru því notaðar áfram eftir að hann féll úr ábúð.

9be05482-5ac1-6af6-ae7d-ba33d06fb324.story_eng: In the old days this hollow above the farm Bakki held fishermen's huts (verbúðir), used when boats were rowed out from the fishing station of Láganúpsver. No trace of the huts can be seen in Búðalág today, as building materials were very much reused.
9be05482-5ac1-6af6-ae7d-ba33d06fb324.story_is: Í lautinni ofan Bakkabæjarins voru verbúðir í gamla daga, þegar útgerð var úr Láganúpsveri. Engar minjar þeirra sjást í Búðalág nú, enda var byggingarefni mjög endurnýtt.

9bef1cea-5d98-b51a-a516-43b37209fb1a.story_eng: Langahlíð, the 'long hillside', rises above Selbrún. In a shallow dip on the slope lie the ruins of a stekkur, a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes so the ewes could be milked. It was called Sveinsstekkur and is named after Sveinn Vigfússon. The fold probably belonged to Mjóanessel, the shieling of Mjóanes, a summer station where livestock were kept and milked.
9bef1cea-5d98-b51a-a516-43b37209fb1a.story_is: Langahlíð er upp af Selbrún. Í slakka í hlíðinni eru rústir af stekk sem hét Sveinsstekkur. Stekkur þessi tilheyrði líklega Mjóanesseli og er kenndur við Svein Vigfússon.

9bfae2a1-ab1f-45bc-9d69-1635d81f7c90.story_eng: Opposite the middle of Höfði, a slanting path (sneiðingur) climbs up through the rock face. It was often treacherous in winter, and its name, Illisneiðingur, means roughly 'the bad slanting path'. Above it, Höfði is at its lowest, at a point called Lághöfði.
9bfae2a1-ab1f-45bc-9d69-1635d81f7c90.story_is: Á móts við miðjan Höfða er sneiðingur í bergið, oft viðsjárverður að vetrarlagi, og kallast hann Illisneiðingur. Þar upp af er Höfðinn lægstur og heitir þar Lághöfði.

9c1024f6-ce5a-8898-542a-9261e580bca8.story_eng: Þjófapyttur (thieves' pool) is also called Drekkingarhylur (drowning pool) by some. Women who had been sentenced to death at the Þingskálaþing assembly were drowned here.
9c1024f6-ce5a-8898-542a-9261e580bca8.story_is: Þjófapyttur er einnig nefndur Drekkingarhylur af sumum. Þar var konum drekkt er dæmdar voru frá lífi á Þingskálaþingi.

9c3bb29e-a6d7-3ced-88a5-4fc8f6798738.story_eng: Efriblá is a large marshy area above Kiðastekkshöfði. A ridge called Langás runs into the marsh, and above its southern end lie the ruins of Grásteinssel, a set of beitarhús (sheep houses out in the grazing land). The easternmost part of the marsh is a bog called Langásdý.
9c3bb29e-a6d7-3ced-88a5-4fc8f6798738.story_is: Ofan við Kiðastekkshöfða er Efriblá, stórt mýrarsvæði. Inn í blána gengur Langás og upp af honum syðst eru rústir af beitarhúsunum Grásteinsseli. Austast í blánni er Langásdý.

9c46e0aa-e478-1ca9-597c-8116a52a47ec.story_eng: Fjósstígshellir is a fairly large cave in the lava, just east of the lava ridge and south of the track. Inside it there is an old garði, a low wall of the kind used to divide or feed sheep. In earlier times sheep were kept in the cave, and one local man's grandfather kept his yearling sheep there.
9c46e0aa-e478-1ca9-597c-8116a52a47ec.story_is: Beint austur af Fjósstíg, rétt austan við hraunkambinn, sunnan við vegslóðann, er Fjósstígshellir. Hellirinn er nokkuð stór og í honum er gamall garði. Í hellinum voru hafðar kindur áður fyrr og þar voru eitt sinn geymdir gemlingar.

9c6426ab-d826-8d22-d0c4-5e6ffe157b22.story_eng: Krosshóll is a large, grassy hill of stones, the biggest hill near the farm and easy to spot, with a tussock on its top. The name means "cross hill", and one theory holds that a cross was set up here in Christian times and the hill was then regarded as a holy place. A spell lay on it: it must never be mown. The people living on the farm took care that the hill was not disturbed, for example when a tractor was working the land around it long ago. One local recalled burning off dead grass near the hill on a day with a north wind, when the fire swept over it. The following year he met with two mishaps, and these were blamed on his not having respected the spell.
9c6426ab-d826-8d22-d0c4-5e6ffe157b22.story_is: Hóllinn er stór, gróinn grjóthóll, stærsti hóllinn í grennd við bæinn og því áberandi. Þúfa er efst á hólnum. Kenning er um að kross hafi verið settur á hólinn í kristinni tíð og þá litið á hólinn sem helgan stað, enda fylgdu krosshólnum þau álög að ekki mætti slá hann. Gættu ábúendur þess vel að ekki væri hróflað við hólnum, svo sem þegar jarðvinnslutraktor var að vinna landið í kring fyrir löngu síðan. „Einu sinni var ég að brenna sinu í grennd við hólinn, það var norðanátt og eldurinn flögraði yfir hann. Árið eftir varð ég fyrir tveimur óhöppum og var því kennt um að ég hefði ekki virt álögin.“

9c7ca8c2-c058-a598-f221-fc44fe130cb3.story_eng: Garðssandur is the name given to the flat shore along the sea, running east towards the eastern mouth of the Héraðsvötn river. Just west of it lies Litli-Garður, where remains of old assembly booths can be found, and from there a slope leads down to the flats of Garðssandur, with wetland further south. Work has been done here to restore vegetation and to stop the sand from drifting, using bales of hay. South of the road the farmers of Garður have already revegetated a fairly large area. To look at, it resembles a hayfield, but it is grazing land.
9c7ca8c2-c058-a598-f221-fc44fe130cb3.story_is: Garðssandur er fjaran kölluð með sjónum austur undir eystri Héraðsvatnaós. Austan við Litla-Garð, þar sem eru leifar þingbúða, er brekka niður að flatlendinu Garðssandi og votlendi sunnar. Nokkuð hefur verið unnið að uppgræðslu á Garðssandi, eða að því að hefta sandfok þar með heyrúllum. Sunnan vegarins hafa Garðsbændur þegar grætt upp allstórt svæði, sem til að sjá lítur út eins og tún, en er beitiland.

9c892229-7fa8-4d55-83ec-982a4f98d0e0.story_eng: Útvogsréttir, also called Þorkelsgerðisréttir, is a sheep fold beside the old home-field wall of the farm Torfabær. The fold was moved here after the great flood of 1925, and it is still in use.
9c892229-7fa8-4d55-83ec-982a4f98d0e0.story_is: Útvogsréttir eða Þorkelsgerðisréttir eru við túngarðinn í Torfabæ, milli Torfabæjar og Eimu. Réttin var flutt þangað eftir flóðið mikla 1925. Þessar réttir eru enn notaðar.

9ca01eb7-534a-9bae-0bcf-182a6a30437b.story_eng: Gauraslóð is a fishing ground off the east coast that is believed to have got its name in 1971–72. Cod and haddock are caught here, and in some places saithe as well. The seabed has several knolls, and it is considered a difficult area to fish. The northernmost knoll, about 10 miles west-southwest of Hvalbak, is called Stóri gaur, and it lies very shallow, only 20 fathoms down. Nearby are Sómastaðir and Hestasteinn. Fishing was often good around Hestasteinn, but Sómastaðir is said to be a poor name for its spot: "sómi" means honour, and the trawl often came up there in tatters that were no honour to anyone. Another knoll, the 19-mile gaur, lies between Breiðdalsvík and Djúpivogur, 19 miles from Streiti, and Gauraslóð is believed to have originally taken its name from it.
9ca01eb7-534a-9bae-0bcf-182a6a30437b.story_is: Talið er að Gauraslóð hafi fengið nafn 1971–72. Á henni fæst þorskur og ýsa og sums staðar veiðist ufsi. Þarna eru nokkrir hólar og þykir erfitt veiðisvæði. Nyrsti hóllinn er um það bil 10 mílur vestsuðvestur af Hvalbak og er hann kallaður Stóri gaur. Mjög grunnt er niður á hann, aðeins 20 faðmar. Skammt frá eru Sómastaðir og Hestasteinn. Oft gaf vel í kringum Hestasteininn, en að sögn eru Sómastaðir ekki réttnefni því að trollið kom oft upp í druslum sem enginn sómi var að. Nítján mílna gaurinn er á milli Breiðdalsvíkur og Djúpavogs, 19 mílur frá Streiti. Talið er að Gauraslóðin hafi upphaflega fengið nafn sitt af nítján mílna gaurnum.

9ca5709f-e0f1-b194-97bc-638c2d35a6f0.story_eng: Heygarðshólar is a cluster of pseudocraters (rootless craters) opposite the Nafarsker skerries of Geldingey. Among them is a fissure called Hrútagjá, 'Rams' Rift', named because rams were lost there long ago. Southeast of the craters stands a spire-shaped rock called Strokkur. It has a hole in its top where a Barrow's goldeneye (húsönd) usually nests.
9ca5709f-e0f1-b194-97bc-638c2d35a6f0.story_is: Heygarðshólar eru gervigígaþyrping gegnt Nafarskerjum í Geldingey. Í þeim er Hrútagjá, en þar týndust hrútar fyrir margt löngu. Suðaustur af Heygarðshólum er strýtumyndaður klettur sem heitir Strokkur. Hola er ofan í klettinn og verpir þar jafnan húsönd.

9cae6347-f0e0-74db-44e1-430947d8e457.story_eng: Einbúi, meaning "the hermit" or "the one who lives alone", is a small solitary rock standing on its own southwest of Ketilhóll. Elves and huldufólk (hidden people) are said to live there. Below the rock the land slopes to the south, and this area is called Einbúatún, "Einbúi's hayfield".
9cae6347-f0e0-74db-44e1-430947d8e457.story_is: Einbúi heitir stakur smáklettur suðvestan við Ketilhól. Þar er sagt að álfar og huldufólk búi. Fyrir neðan Einbúa og suðvestan við hann hallar landinu til suðurs og heitir þar Einbúatún.

9cc2eefd-3fac-8e30-f6e3-cc61fed3158e.story_eng: A wall once ran around this home field. The name, Stekkatún, suggests there was once a stekkur here, a small fold where lambs were penned apart from the ewes, but there are no records of one. A sheep house has stood in Stekkatún for a long time, and it is still there.
9cc2eefd-3fac-8e30-f6e3-cc61fed3158e.story_is: Garður var áður kringum túnið og nafnið bendir til þess að þar hafi verið stekkur, en engar heimildir eru um það. Lengi hefur verið fjárhús í Stekkatúninu og er það þar enn.

9ccef049-f89f-a00b-b742-75bbf9acd538.story_eng: Miðdegisás means 'midday ridge'. Together with its neighbour to the west, Nónmelsás (nón being the old name for mid-afternoon), it served as an eyktamark, a natural landmark used to tell the time of day by the position of the sun, as seen from Stöpulsel, a shieling (sel, a summer station where livestock were kept and milked). A hollow called Miðdegislág lies in the middle of the ridge, and a narrow, nameless gap separates it from Nónmelsás.
9ccef049-f89f-a00b-b742-75bbf9acd538.story_is: Miðdegisás er næstur Nónmelsási að austan og í hann miðjan er lægð, Miðdegislág. Á milli ásanna er mjótt sund, nafnlaust. Norðan Miðdegisáss er nokkur rakur móflati að Kamarlæk. Þessi nón- og miðdegisörnefni eru eyktamörk frá Stöpulseli.

9d114aa8-9907-c2ed-bab1-0dd9837c5f91.story_eng: A small trickle of a stream runs down a hollow called Miðaftanslaut at the edge of the slope. It takes its name from a building called Hornhús at the northernmost part of the homefield, and the stream ran down just north of that house. Some remains of buildings once lay just west of the newer sheep-house barn, which stands west of the sheep houses. They disappeared when soil was pushed aside to build the barn, and Hornhús probably stood there. The stream comes down from the slopes just north of that spot and runs on down to the end of Langimelur.
9d114aa8-9907-c2ed-bab1-0dd9837c5f91.story_is: Eftir Miðaftanslaut í brúninni rennur lækjarsytra sem kölluð er Hornhúslækur, kenndur við svonefnt Hornhús nyrst á túninu. Rennur lækurinn niður norðan við húsið. Rétt vestan við nýju fjárhúshlöðuna, sem er vestan við fjárhúsin, voru einhverjar húsaleifar en þær hurfu þegar jarðvegi var ýtt til vegna hlöðubyggingarinnar. Þar hafa líklega Hornhús staðið. Hornhúslækur kemur niður úr brekkunum rétt norðan við og rennur út og niður rétt sunnan við enda Langamels.

9d172e48-8b84-d9da-332a-acd67cf54254.story_eng: Gildruhóll means "trap hill". A fox trap once stood on this hill below the slope, and the outline of its stone walls can still be made out. The scree slopes around the hill are called Gildruhólsskriður after it.
9d172e48-8b84-d9da-332a-acd67cf54254.story_is: Á hólnum var tófugildra og sést enn móta fyrir hleðslum eftir hana. Hóllinn er fyrir neðan hlíð og í kringum hann eru Gildruhólsskriður.

9d18a721-c864-405f-6825-3fe818ea3e13.story_eng: Paradísarsandur is the beach closest to Standandanes, and driftwood and seaweed often wash up on it. No one knows for certain how it came to be called Paradísarsandur, "Paradise Sand". One theory is that those who came out through Bessagat on a mirror-calm sea found the view beautiful, with the cove rising up from the sand before them. Another is that the name comes from the great amount of driftwood that collected here, as driftwood was a valuable resource.
9d18a721-c864-405f-6825-3fe818ea3e13.story_is: Paradísarsandur er fjaran næst Standandanesi og er oft í henni reki og þari. Ekki er vitað með vissu af hverju Paradísarsandur dregur nafn. Ein tilgáta er sú að þeim sem komi út úr Bessagatinu í spegilsléttu þyki fagurt um að litast þar sem víkin blasir við upp úr Paradísarsandi. Önnur tilgáta er að nafnið sé dregið af mikilli rekasæld í sandinum.

9d2ba831-d57b-afdf-abda-2abffe29e5a3.story_eng: Bjargalág is a fairly large hollow a short way above Mígandisbjörg, on the outer side of the stream. It was believed to be an álagablettur, an enchanted spot that must not be disturbed. It was said that if a scythe were put to its grass, a spell of wet weather could be expected, leaving no dry days for the hay.
9d2ba831-d57b-afdf-abda-2abffe29e5a3.story_is: Skammt fyrir ofan Mígandisbjörg og utan við lækinn er allstór lægð sem heitir Bjargalág. Hún var talin vera álagablettur og sagt að búast mætti við óþurrkum ef þar væri borinn ljár í gras.

9d2fe98b-a7bf-4d17-8729-87163d5b6f94.story_eng: Arnoddur, a farmhand from the farm Stöð, is said to have been killed here. He was found in this scree, torn to pieces. The story is told in the folklore collection Gríma hin nýja.
9d2fe98b-a7bf-4d17-8729-87163d5b6f94.story_is: Hér á Arnoddur vinnumaður frá Stöð að hafa verið drepinn. Þar fannst hann tættur í sundur. Lesa má nánar um þetta í Grímu hinni nýju.

9d436ffe-eb0c-48c7-8421-f75be31334de.story_eng: Þorsteinsgat (Þorsteinn's Gap) is a narrow channel between two rocks near the farm Lönd. It is named after Þorsteinn from Hvalnes, who is said to have come to Lönd in a storm, probably around 1800, in a small boat and landed near the farm. People wondered where he could possibly have come ashore in such surf. When asked, he said he had landed in some kind of gap and showed them where. From then on the place was called Þorsteinsgat.
9d436ffe-eb0c-48c7-8421-f75be31334de.story_is: Þorsteinsgat er milli tveggja kletta. Þar lenti einu sinni Þorsteinn frá Hvalnesi. Þorsteinn á að hafa komið að Löndum í óveðri, trúlega um 1800. Var hann á bátkænu og lenti nálægt bænum. Menn undruðust hvar hann hefði getað lent í briminu sem var, en hann sagðist hafa lent í einhverju gati og sýndi fólki hvar. Var það því eftir þetta kallað Þorsteinsgat.

9d538a9a-b4b5-cd07-cc25-331a88dd2989.story_eng: A sheepfold was built of stacked stone on the west side of Eyjan in the summer of 1918. When the builders left after finishing it, the walls stood shoulder-high. The next time they came to the fold, after the Katla eruption in October 1918, it had vanished under ash. Today only the tops of the highest courses of stone can just be seen.
9d538a9a-b4b5-cd07-cc25-331a88dd2989.story_is: Vestan undir Eyjunni var hlaðin rétt sumarið 1918. Þegar réttarsmiðirnir fóru frá réttinni eftir að réttarsmíðinni var lokið voru réttarveggirnir axlarháir. Er þeir komu næst að réttinni eftir Kötlugosið 1918, í október, var réttin horfin undir ösku. Nú sést rétt ofan á efstu hleðslurnar.

9d671063-2eb0-86a2-bb17-2ff853bf03ea.story_eng: Hvammkot is an abandoned cottage farm above the marshy bog that stretches out from the home field of Kárastaðir. Already in 1840 it was described as a ruined, deserted croft. Its hayfield measured about four dagsláttur (an old measure, roughly the area one man could mow in a day) and was once completely enclosed by a turf wall. Between 1870 and 1880 there were horse stables on the deserted farm, and when Gísli Gunnarsson lived here a few goats were kept there and milked in the summers. The place is also recorded once under the name Háagerði, which is believed to be the same farm.
9d671063-2eb0-86a2-bb17-2ff853bf03ea.story_is: Hvammkot hefur heitið nú ónýtt eyðikot, ofan Kárastaðavöll, segir í sóknarlýsingu frá 1840. Það er eyðibýli fyrir ofan mýrarflóa þann er liggur frá heimatúninu. Túnstærð er um 4 dagsláttur og hefur túnið verið algirt með torfgarði. Milli 1870 og 1880 voru hesthús á eyðibýli þessu, og er Gísli Gunnarsson bjó hér voru hafðar þarna nokkrar geitur og þær nytjaðar á sumrum. Háagerði kemur fram á einni örnefnaskrá en ekki annars staðar, og hlýtur það að vera hið sama og Hvammkot.

9d6e1802-4b8a-4769-826f-502f9fbb8756.story_eng: Hlíðarendahellir, also simply called Hellir (the Cave), lies at the outer end beneath the cliff Hellisberg. It is a sea cave dating from the end of the Ice Age, and it made an excellent shelter for sheep. A wall about 40 metres long was built up along the overhanging rock. Below the cave is a hillock where there is a burial mound, an ancient grave.
9d6e1802-4b8a-4769-826f-502f9fbb8756.story_is: Yst undir Hellisbergi er Hellir, eða Hlíðarendahellir, ágætt fjárból. Hellirinn er sjávarhellir frá lokum ísaldar. Um 40 metra langur veggur hefur verið hlaðinn upp með slútandi berginu. Kumltótt er þar neðan við hellinn.

9d969633-5d1c-54e8-c1a6-02ad8c18f283.story_eng: Vitaðsgjafi was a fishing place that was said never to fail. The name means roughly "the sure giver". It was a salmon haul, where the net was drawn using a single boat. It lies between Horn and Ytri-Geithelliseyja.
9d969633-5d1c-54e8-c1a6-02ad8c18f283.story_is: Milli Horns og Ytri-Geithelliseyjar er veiðistaðurinn Vitaðsgjafi, sem þótti aldrei bregðast. Laxadrátturinn Vitaðsgjafi var dreginn á einum bát.

9da01ac2-50c6-0863-ba63-1a4ee65a294d.story_eng: Mylla (the Mill) was a water mill that stood south of Gvendarstaðir, beside the stream that marked the boundary between farms. The nearby hillock Myllubali and gully Myllugil take their names from it. The mill was looked after by Sigurlaug Þorkelsdóttir, who farmed at Brimnes from 1865 to 1896 and stayed on there afterwards. It was said that a man known as Myllu-Kobbi (Mill-Kobbi) built it. Anna Jónsdóttir remembered what was left of the mill: fragments of walls that the stream had partly broken down. The mill no longer exists.
9da01ac2-50c6-0863-ba63-1a4ee65a294d.story_is: Sunnan við Gvendarstaði var Mylla. Þar er Myllubali og Myllugil. Sigurlaug Þorkelsdóttir, sem bjó í Brimnesi 1865–1896 og dvaldi þar áfram, sá um mylluna, sem var vatnsmylla við landamerkjalækinn. Sagt var að það hafi verið Myllu-Kobbi sem setti mylluna upp. Anna Jónsdóttir man eftir leifum myllunnar, veggjabrotum sem lækurinn var búinn að brjóta niður að hluta.

9da41c00-5643-952f-3f1b-ba059d5f02f8.story_eng: Holur, meaning "holes", are undercut banks where trout often lie in the water beneath. Holes 20–25 cm across were cut down through the banks and covered with flat stones. Whenever fish was needed for the pot, people would "go to the Holes", and there was hardly ever a time when no fish was found underneath.
9da41c00-5643-952f-3f1b-ba059d5f02f8.story_is: Holbakkar þar sem svo hagar til að silungur liggur oft undir. Voru því stungnar holur gegnum bakkana, 20–25 cm í þvermál, og látnar hellur yfir. Ef nú vantaði í soðið var „farið í Holurnar“ og brást þá naumast að fiskur væri undir.

9dc2417d-ee38-4ba7-a786-e96ac34c96c2.story_eng: Refagildra means "fox trap". It is a built stone wall at the foot of a low rock outcrop, on its east side, in the north-east corner of Skriðumelur. The person who recorded it noted that it is not really a place name, but a structure worth remembering. The recorder's father thought it likely dated from the time of Árni Magnússon at the farm Skriða, who caught foxes (tófur) this way. The wall was damaged by thoughtless youngsters in 1945.
9dc2417d-ee38-4ba7-a786-e96ac34c96c2.story_is: Hleðsla austan undir lágri klöpp í norðausturhorni Skriðumels. Þetta er ekki eiginlegt örnefni heldur mannvirki sem gjarnan má muna. Faðir skrásetjara taldi líklegt að hún væri frá dögum Árna Magnússonar í Skriðu, sem veiddi tófur á þennan hátt. Hleðslunni var spillt af óvitaunglingum árið 1945.

9dc47955-1c58-00de-c7ba-e04637954bd4.story_eng: Sölvi, the son-in-law of Bjólfur, was buried here in a burial mound. The place still carries his name.
9dc47955-1c58-00de-c7ba-e04637954bd4.story_is: Sölvi, tengdasonur Bjólfs, var heygður í Sölvabotnum.

9dc625c6-1093-6700-1f4f-b916a9246f96.story_eng: Mófugladrangur, roughly 'moorland-bird pillar', is a round lava pillar standing on top of a small heap of stones. It lies just south of Dýjaveitur, close to an old cleared track that ran north through Nátthagi. For a long time, the frozen Laxá river also served as a road for horse-drawn sledges in winter, when people from the valleys travelled to the trading town of Húsavík.
9dc625c6-1093-6700-1f4f-b916a9246f96.story_is: Laxá var lengi notuð sem akvegur fyrir hestasleða á veturna þegar dalamenn fóru í kaupstað til Húsavíkur. Ruddur akvegur lá norður Nátthagann út að Dýjaveitum. Skammt sunnan við Dýjaveitur, rétt hjá þessum vegslóða, er lítið grjóthróf. Upp á því stendur hnöttóttur hraundrangur sem heitir Mófugladrangur.

9dd78474-655c-19ef-e4ac-855d2609ae61.story_eng: This heather-covered hollow is named after Ólöf Nikulásdóttir from the farm Arnkelsgerði. It is said that she kept her milking ewes here. Another story says that Ólöf and her sister Sigríður got on badly, and that Ólöf sometimes fled here to get away. A well-known tale tells how the two sisters competed to buy Arnkelsgerði, and Sigríður came out on top.
9dd78474-655c-19ef-e4ac-855d2609ae61.story_is: Botninn er lyngi gróinn og kenndur við Ólöfu Nikulásdóttur frá Arnkelsgerði. Sagt er að hún hafi haft þar kvíær sínar. Önnur saga segir að þeim systrum, Sigríði og henni, hafi samið illa og að hún hafi stundum flúið þangað. Fræg er sagan af því þegar þær kepptu um að kaupa Arnkelsgerði, og þar hafði Sigríður betur.

9dd89d43-0901-3449-118d-31e2c0826dcc.story_eng: Einarsstaðir is an ancient abandoned farm in the heath hollow called Einarsstaðakrókur, just north of Tvígarðar. It is said to be the only one of the old farms here that still keeps its name with certainty, as the names of the others have become confused over time. The ruins of a bænhús (a small private chapel) with a circular churchyard lie at Einarsstaðir. Paths run from Einarsstaðahólmi up to the farm; they are still fairly clear and are called Grasagötur.
9dd89d43-0901-3449-118d-31e2c0826dcc.story_is: Heiðarslakkinn rétt norðan við Tvígarða heitir Einarsstaðakrókur og þar er hið forna býli Einarsstaðir. Það er eina býlið sem enn heldur nafninu svo öruggt sé; nafnarugl hefur orðið á hinum. Bænhúsrúst með hringlaga kirkjugarði er á Einarsstöðum. Götur liggja frá Einarsstaðahólma og heim að Einarsstöðum. Eru þær allglöggar og nefnast Grasagötur.

9de6fe53-9d81-4af3-faf6-1b4debafc340.story_eng: Ullarnef, whose name means roughly 'wool nose', is a small point by the river. Wool was sometimes washed here and then rinsed in the river.
9de6fe53-9d81-4af3-faf6-1b4debafc340.story_is: Í Ullarnefi var stundum þvegin ull og þá skoluð í ánni.

9df195bd-89d2-11f9-7a5a-b587aea6a9c6.story_eng: Keldnatær is a set of grassy hollows beneath the edge of a lava field. The name comes from the farm Keldur, which is believed to have stood here in ancient times, and from "tær", here the plural of "tó" in the sense of a grassy hollow. The place is also known as Kjalnatær and Kelnatær.
9df195bd-89d2-11f9-7a5a-b587aea6a9c6.story_is: Graslautir undir hraunjaðri. Þær eru kenndar við bæinn Keldur, sem talið er að hafi staðið þarna til forna, og „tær“, sem hér er fleirtala af „tó“ í merkingunni graslaut.

9dfd7245-1e1d-22e9-334a-02ca082dc0c9.story_eng: Stórhóll, "big hill", is a large rocky hill on the outer part of Hnífar, above the cave Sandhellir. It was regarded as one of the greatest elf dwellings in the lands of Kollvík, and there was believed to be much coming and going between Sandhellir and Stórhóll through an underground passage. Children were strictly told not to make noise around Stórhóll, and this was respected. Some people in the 20th century believed they had seen huldufólk (hidden people) by the hill.
9dfd7245-1e1d-22e9-334a-02ca082dc0c9.story_is: Stór klettahóll utanvert á Hnífum, ofan Sandhellis. Þar er einn mesti álfabústaður í Kollvíkurlöndum, og mikill samgangur var talinn vera milli Sandhellis og Stórhóls gegnum undirgöng. Lagt var ríkt á við börn að vera ekki með hávaða í kringum Stórhól, og var það virt. Til var fólk á 20. öld sem taldi sig hafa séð huldufólk við hólinn.

9e3e0702-e22a-23b3-8b27-f0c985a66c99.story_eng: Háastrýta, roughly 'the high spire', is a conspicuous cone-shaped rock east of the southern corner of Selskógur. In front of it lies a stretch of rough, uneven ground. A hut was once built there against a rock overhang, and the spot is called Kofakargi, 'hut rough ground'.
9e3e0702-e22a-23b3-8b27-f0c985a66c99.story_is: Austur af suðurhorni Selskógs er áberandi strýtuklettur sem heitir Háastrýta. Fram af honum er ósléttur kargi. Þar var hlaðinn kofi við skúta og heitir þar Kofakargi.

9e40b414-bc4c-334c-b9b9-f4253a0e520b.story_eng: On the south side of the river Skíðadalsá, among a group of grassy hummocks on the lower ground, the ruins of old buildings can still be clearly made out. This place is called Nautasel, literally the cattle shieling. In earlier times the bishop's seat at Hólar kept its herd of cattle here during the summers, as Hólar owned all the land from Heljará innermost in the valley up to the mountains.
9e40b414-bc4c-334c-b9b9-f4253a0e520b.story_is: Sunnan við Skíðadalsá verða allmargir grasigrónir hólar hið neðra. Sést þar glögglega fyrir rústum eftir byggingar. Hér er nefnt Nautasel. Hafði Hólastaður áður fyrr hér nautahjörð sína á sumrin, enda átti staðurinn allt landið frá Heljará innst inn til fjalla.

9e4340ec-636a-820b-0762-300444852813.story_eng: Suðurormar is an area of hollows and rocky ledges with a little grass and moss, in barren land. The river Ósá partly has its source here. Beside Suðurormar runs a deep gully that has no name. There was a tale that a sheep thief once lived at Botni and had a hideout in these gorges. Traces of it were said to have been visible for a long time, but it has never been found despite searching. The thief was called Jón, and his wife is supposed to have once said: "Many things I remember, many things I remember. When my Jón had 18 carcasses up in the kitchen before he started cooking any of his own."
9e4340ec-636a-820b-0762-300444852813.story_is: Austur af Skersskógi eru lægðir og klettahjallar, vaxnir svolitlu grasi og mosa, og heita Suðurormar. Þarna er hrjóstrugt land og þarna á Ósáin upptök sín að nokkru. Með Suðurormum er djúpt gil sem ekki heitir neitt. Sögusögn var til um að eitt sinn hefði verið sauðaþjófur í Botni og hefði hann átt byrgi í þessum gljúfrum. Átti að sjást fyrir því lengi, en ekki hefur það þó fundist þrátt fyrir leit. Þjófurinn hét Jón og eitt sinn átti kona hans að hafa sagt: „Margt má ég mona, margt má ég mona. Þegar Jón minn átti 18 krof uppi í eldhúsi áður en hann fór að sjóða nokkuð af sínu.“

9e4cd567-48ee-3966-0432-345a1a2e5624.story_eng: Finnbogakambur is a fairly large, steep ridge with rounded sides. It takes its name from Finnbogi rammi (Finnbogi the Strong), hero of Finnboga saga. At its front end stands a pillar of rock about three metres high, narrow at the top and partly covered with vegetation on its summit. On this pillar Finnbogi is said to have defended himself against 15 men who attacked him, as told in the saga.
9e4cd567-48ee-3966-0432-345a1a2e5624.story_is: Finnbogakambur er allmikill brattur hryggur með ávalar hliðar. Dregur hann nafn af Finnboga ramma. Fremst á honum er um það bil þriggja metra stöpull, mjór að ofan og dálítið gróinn efst. Á honum á Finnbogi að hafa varist fimmtán mönnum er að honum sóttu, eins og segir í Finnbogasögu.

9e5631f2-e57f-00f5-43c7-7bc5e12f0c2b.story_eng: These low hills at the foot of the mountain are marked by eroded banks and gullies. Logs and remains of charcoal have been found here, in what the description also calls Kolviðarhólar (kol means charcoal, viður wood). This suggests that the slopes of Vörðufell were wooded in ancient times and that charcoal was made in the hills, as the name describes. Below and between the hills ran the pack-horse trails of the farmers at Iða and Helgastaðir. The farmers of Álfsstaðir also used these tracks to bring home hay when they went haymaking as far as the boundary of Helgastaðir, where the land was easy going, with horsetail and sedge meadow.
9e5631f2-e57f-00f5-43c7-7bc5e12f0c2b.story_is: Lágt holt eða hæð í fjallsrótunum með rofabörðum og skorningum. Þar í Kolviðarhólum hafa fundist lurkar og kolaleifar. Bendir það til þess að hlíðar Vörðufells hafi verið skógi klæddar til forna og gert til kola í hólunum eins og nafnið lýsir. Fyrir neðan hólana og milli þeirra lágu lestargötur bændanna á Iðu og Helgastöðum og heybandsgötur Álfsstaðabænda þegar þeir sóttu heyskap inn að mörkum Helgastaða, en þar var greiðfært land með elftingu og starengi.

9e5ab9cb-24d3-811c-5939-fb5ade223c55.story_eng: Around 1955 children built themselves a little play hut here, at the foot of Veituhóll, and called it Eddukofi (Edda's hut) after a kaupakona, a summer farmhand from Reykjavík, who helped them build it. The knoll above was where bait worms were set aside for ice fishing.
9e5ab9cb-24d3-811c-5939-fb5ade223c55.story_is: Undir Veituhólnum gerðu börn sér lítinn búkofa um 1955 og kölluðu Eddukofa eftir kaupakonu úr Reykjavík sem aðstoðaði við bygginguna. Á hólnum sjálfum var lagt til maðkveitu til dorgveiða.

9e5cb280-1ed1-0fab-2db9-eada0135dddf.story_eng: Hólhúsgerði is a hillock at the top of the home field, above the hillock called Hlöðuhóll. A small sheep house called Hólhús once stood here, and it was still in use for a while into the 20th century.
9e5cb280-1ed1-0fab-2db9-eada0135dddf.story_is: Upp af Hlöðuhólnum er annar hóll efst í túninu. Þar nefndist Hólhúsgerði, og voru þar fyrrum lítil fjárhús, Hólhús, sem voru notuð eitthvað fram á tuttugustu öld.

9e66eb85-2ae4-1bec-0b8e-12d4c82c4cfb.story_eng: Grenjaklettar is a band of cliffs near the boundary of the farm Háls. Its northern end, where the cliffs are considered to end and where they rise highest, is called Grenjaklettaöxl (öxl means shoulder). In the cliffs is a ledge called Sveltishilla, and the land boundary runs along it. Sheep often made their way onto this ledge and starved to death there, which is probably how it got its name, roughly 'Starvation Ledge'. The rock above it is called Sveltishilluklettur.
9e66eb85-2ae4-1bec-0b8e-12d4c82c4cfb.story_is: Í Grenjaklettum er Sveltishilla og í henni landamörkin. Í hillu þessa fara oft kindur og svelta til bana og mun nafnið af því dregið. Ofan við Sveltishillu er Sveltishilluklettur. Grenjaklettar eru næst mörkum á Hálsi, og nyrst, þar sem klettarnir teljast enda, er Grenjaklettaöxl og ber hún þar hæst.

9e81986b-4e03-4008-abb5-1dd81437560a.story_eng: Erlendshóll is a small hill that is believed to be named after Erlendur Þorvarðsson, a lawspeaker. It stands west of an old and fairly busy track that ran along the east and north sides of the home field, outside the old stone walls, and from there west over Hraunsheiði towards the Hlíð farms and beyond. The hill once lay outside the home field but is now inside it.
9e81986b-4e03-4008-abb5-1dd81437560a.story_is: Hóllinn heitir Erlendshóll og er talinn vera kenndur við Erlend lögmann Þorvarðsson. Austan og norðan við túnið, gömlu grjótgarðana, lá allfjölfarin gata, og frá norðvesturhorni túnsins lá hún vestur Hraunsheiði, upp á Hlíðarbæi og áfram út úr. Dálítill hóll var vestan við götu þessa, áður utan túnsins en nú innan þess.

9e8d272d-39ad-11da-7049-328e2de801ed.story_eng: Gránugjá is a fissure running northeast to southwest, narrowing towards its western end. It is said that a mare once fell into it and died. The name appears to come from Grána, a common name for a grey mare.
