Á þessari verstöð voru sagðar hvíla þær álögur að öll skip yrðu að vera farin burt úr víkinni fyrir hálfa tólftu viku sumars, annars myndi illa fara. Stundum kom það fyrir. Formenn hafa eflaust reynt að hitta á réttan tíma til að komast burt, en veður gat fljótt breyst svo ekki var hægt að komast burt og því varð að fara þegar betur viðraði. En þá urðu oft óhöpp.

cbec2fc8-b6f8-41e5-9be0-335dde5df04d.story_eng: Sundlág is a hollow holding a pool called Sundpollur, whose name means swimming pool. Here Marteinn Sigurðsson from Hrafnsstaðir, later a farmer at Háls, taught swimming in 1909 and 1910, which is believed to have been the first swimming instruction in the district. He taught swimming for several more springs, though then at Hrafnsstaðir, and there is said to be little doubt that three of his pupils were saved from drowning by what they learned from him.
cbec2fc8-b6f8-41e5-9be0-335dde5df04d.story_is: Neðan við Hjörleifstætt er Sundlág og í henni Sundpollur. Í þessum polli kenndi Marteinn Sigurðsson frá Hrafnsstöðum, síðar bóndi á Hálsi, sund árin 1909 og 1910 og mun það hafa verið fyrsta sundkennslan hér í sveit. Fleiri vor kenndi Marteinn sund en þá á Hrafnsstöðum og er lítill vafi á því að þrír af nemendum hans hafi bjargast frá drukknun fyrir það sem þeir lærðu hjá honum.

cc039193-b7e2-0955-1fad-d3d9220cb643.story_eng: Elínarhólmi lies straight out from the landing place. In old documents it is called Helenarey, and in Þórðar saga hreðu it appears as Elenuhólmur. It is a nesting islet that once belonged to the church at Miklibær in Óslandshlíð. The church gave it up in exchange for the right to cut twelve horse-loads of wood and brushwood in Viðvíkurskógur.
cc039193-b7e2-0955-1fad-d3d9220cb643.story_is: Beint fram undan lendingunni er Elínarhólmi, í fornum bréfum kallaður Helenarey og í Þórðar sögu hreðu Elenuhólmur. Þetta er varphólmi sem áður tilheyrði Miklabæjarkirkju í Óslandshlíð, sem lét hann í skiptum fyrir tólf hesta högg og rifhrís í Viðvíkurskógi.

cc0582d5-5014-fe61-e744-3c6089526ea0.name_eng: Þinghústóft, ruins of a meeting house
cc0582d5-5014-fe61-e744-3c6089526ea0.story_eng: These ruins mark the old assembly place of Suðurfjarðahreppur, where the district's meetings were held. The name means the ruin of the assembly house (þinghús).

cc0bb1e1-a9de-ee18-dd06-976657d96ef5.story_eng: The ruins here are called Sel, a word for a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked. They lie above the old riding paths a short way from the river Jökulsá, on the north side of a small stream called Sellækur, which runs into the river. The slopes rising above the ruins are called Selbrekkur.
cc0bb1e1-a9de-ee18-dd06-976657d96ef5.story_is: Norðan við Sellæk, ofan við reiðgötur skammt frá Jökulsá, eru tættur sem kallaðar eru Sel. Sellækur er lítill lækur sem rennur í ána spölkorn ofan við Sniðakinn. Selbrekkur heita upp af Seli.

cc1b4489-4122-d86c-c6d6-75d0b8428216.story_eng: Kaffiklettur means 'coffee rock'. The name seems to be fairly young, and the rock was probably once called Matarklettur, 'food rock'. It stands on a ridge almost in the middle of the Engi, the hay meadow, and the people working on the meadow are said to have often heated coffee here. No heather grew anywhere on the meadow to burn, so fuel had to be fetched from further away. The person who recorded the description remembered from childhood flakes of dried dung and fire marks on the stones. In his own time coffee was never heated here, but the sheltered hollow beside the rock was a place to rest and eat. The rock is about waist-high.
cc1b4489-4122-d86c-c6d6-75d0b8428216.story_is: Kaffiklettur er á hrygg upp af Vallavaðshringum. Nafnið ber með sér að vera ungt en líklegt er að hann hafi heitið Matarklettur. Hann er nánast á miðju Engi og er sagt að engjafólk hafi oft hitað þarna kaffi. Hvergi er lyngkló til á Enginu og hefur því orðið að afla eldiviðar lengra að. Skrásetjari mundi sem barn eftir taðflögum og eldslit á steinum. Aldrei var hitað þar svo hann myndi, en í skjólsælli laut við klettinn var hvíldar- og matarstaður. Kletturinn er um það bil mittishár.

cc3bf304-0666-65d2-66de-48fc07ad92b6.story_eng: Hrafnavík is a sheltered, grassy hollow rising from a cove of the same name on Lagarfljót, and a popular spot to visit on a walk. Above it towers Hrafnás, where ravens regularly nest. It is said that Grímur Droplaugarson rowed from here when he came from the killing of Helgi Ásbjarnarson, though another story says he waded or swam across the river at a place called Einhleypingur. There are ruins in Hrafnavík that have not been investigated.
cc3bf304-0666-65d2-66de-48fc07ad92b6.story_is: Hrafnavík heitir hvammur upp af samnefndri vík í Lagarfljóti. Þetta er skjólsæl og gróin „vík“, vinsæl til heimsókna í gönguferð. Ofan víkurinnar gnæfir Hrafnás, þar sem jafnan verpur hrafn. Sagt er að þaðan hafi Grímur Droplaugarson róið þegar hann kom frá vígi Helga Ásbjarnarsonar, en önnur saga segir að hann hafi vaðið eða synt yfir fljótið þar sem heitir Einhleypingur. Órannsakaðar tóftir eru í Hrafnavík.

cc5df05f-94c4-1262-0103-99fb13b86c8a.story_eng: Hundakofi means "dog hut". Only a faint ruin of it remains. Sigbjörn, the farmer at Múlastekkur, was the district's dog-cleanser, the man responsible for treating the community's dogs against worms. The hut is also said to have been used as a henhouse and as a smokehouse.
cc5df05f-94c4-1262-0103-99fb13b86c8a.story_is: Hér er ógreinileg tótt. Sigbjörn bóndi á Múlastekk var hundahreinsunarmaður sveitarinnar. Einnig er nefnt að kofinn hafi verið nýttur sem hænsnakofi og einnig sem reykhús.

cc63d265-faa5-7762-f441-bc5112b7ff40.story_eng: This dry-stone wall runs up along the scree slope and marks off the afrétt, the common highland pasture where sheep grazed through the summer. It was mostly built in just two weeks in March 1895, and a great many people took part in the work. In all, the wall was 420 fathoms long, roughly 750 metres. Small sheepfolds were built on either side of it, one on the outer side and the other to the south.
cc63d265-faa5-7762-f441-bc5112b7ff40.story_is: Upp eftir skriðunni er grjóthlaðinn afréttargarður. Garðurinn var að mestu byggður á tveimur vikum í mars 1895 og komu fjölmargir að verkinu. Varð garður þessi samtals 420 faðma langur. Litlar réttir voru byggðar hvor sínum megin garðsins, önnur utan við hann en hin sunnan við.

cc6e3034-498c-4764-80aa-bfc765878d82.story_eng: The name Draugavogur means 'ghost cove'. According to a local tale, an útburður haunted the place. In Icelandic folklore, an útburður is the ghost of an infant left outside to die.
cc6e3034-498c-4764-80aa-bfc765878d82.story_is: Sögn var um að þar væri útburður.

cc71b9be-ce03-0cd2-4823-8386e47b8828.story_eng: Hidden people (huldufólk) were said to live in Kishóll, a grassy hill about 100 metres north of the farm that juts south from the slopes above it. The hill is in fact a rock 7 to 10 metres high, now well covered in moss, lupins and birch scrub. In the middle of it is a hole that is hard to see through the vegetation. There are no structures on the hill itself, but close against its north-western side lies a collapsed potato store.
cc71b9be-ce03-0cd2-4823-8386e47b8828.story_is: Þar bjó huldufólk, segir í örnefnaskrá. Kishóll er gróinn hóll um 100 metra norðan við bæinn og gengur fram til suðurs úr hæðunum ofan bæjarins. Hóllinn er 7–10 metra hár klettur, vel gróinn mosa, lúpínu og birkikjarri. Á honum miðjum er hola sem sést lítið fyrir gróðri. Ekki sjást mannvirki á hólnum sjálfum, en þétt upp við hann norðvestanmegin er hrunin kartöflugeymsla.

cc85729a-d325-b9ab-186a-867b96b2bcab.story_eng: Along the river, small coves and rocky points alternate, some forming little inlets. The highest of these rocky points, with a ridge running from it up into Urðirnar, is called Nónklettur. Seen from Unaós it served as an eyktamark, a landmark that showed the time of day by the position of the sun, marking nón, mid-afternoon. At the farm Hrafnabjörg it was usually called Ferjuklettur (ferry rock), and the cove just beyond it Ferjubás (ferry cove), because the ferry crossing landed there on the eastern side.
cc85729a-d325-b9ab-186a-867b96b2bcab.story_is: Innan við Knararnes skiptast á með fljótinu básar og klettatangar, sem sumir mynda litlar víkur. Einn þessara klettatanga er hæstur og gengur þaðan hryggur nokkuð upp í Urðirnar. Þessi klettatangi heitir Nónklettur og var nón, eyktamark frá Unaósi. Á Hrafnabjörgum var hann oftast nefndur Ferjuklettur og básinn utan við hann Ferjubás, enda var þar landtaka að austanverðu á ferjustaðnum.

cc8a28ca-4202-0d20-c481-696d9b65512e.story_eng: The farmhouse of Láganúpur stood on this mound for centuries, until the household moved into a timber house a little further down, some time after 1934. The mound itself is probably made up largely of the remains of human habitation, built up since people first settled in the cove.
cc8a28ca-4202-0d20-c481-696d9b65512e.story_is: Á Bæjarhólnum stóð Láganúpsbærinn um aldir, eða þar til flutt var í timburhús nokkru neðar, eftir 1934. Hóllinn er líklega að mestu myndaður úr mannvistarleifum frá upphafi byggðar í víkinni.

cc9a2a01-b696-da8b-1b7c-bdf6b519a0fb.story_eng: Pollhóll is a fairly small gravel hill beside the river Svartá. Here the river swings east and runs straight into the hill, but Pollhóll withstands the onslaught and turns the river back to the west, after which it flows north-west for some distance. The motor road that ran south along the river crosses the western side of the hill.
cc9a2a01-b696-da8b-1b7c-bdf6b519a0fb.story_is: Pollhóll heitir frekar lítill melur við Svartá. Áin tekur á sig sveig til austurs og steytir á Pollhól, sem stendur af sér árásina og beinir ánni aftur til vesturs. Rennur áin þar til norðvesturs nokkurn spöl. Yfir hólinn vestanverðan liggur bílvegurinn sem var suður með ánni.

ccaa0ac0-8017-c07e-b849-e2add7efdde6.story_eng: Illakelda, roughly "the bad bog", is called by this name in old written sources. It could be crossed at only one place. To the west it ended in the home marsh west of Bakkárholt and at the edge of the home field at Kotströnd, southwest of the farm. This bog was not to be mown.
ccaa0ac0-8017-c07e-b849-e2add7efdde6.story_is: Illakelda heitir svo í fornum ritum. Hún var ófær nema á einum stað. Hún endaði vestur í heimamýri fyrir vestan Bakkárholt og við túnfótinn á Kotströnd, suðvestur af bænum. Þessa keldu mátti ekki slá.

ccb7d3b4-43c8-4e95-a3ae-093a38d5a3c9.story_eng: Nesbrú was an old built-up footpath, a walking causeway laid across the marshes from Óseyrarnes all the way up to the Kaldaðarnes farm cluster. It was very heavily used before the turn of the 20th century, and substantial remains of it can still be seen.
ccb7d3b4-43c8-4e95-a3ae-093a38d5a3c9.story_is: Frá Óseyrarnesi upp mýrarnar alla leið upp í Kaldaðarneshverfi var gömul hlaðin göngubrú sem hét Nesbrú. Var hún mjög mikið farin fyrir aldamótin. Enn eru miklar leifar þessarar göngubrúar.

cce5e9b1-d43b-37a6-2f01-ea2ee2efe477.story_eng: Bankinn, "the Bank", was a working building that housed, among other things, cold storage, stockfish processing, herring salting, fishermen's quarters (a verbúð) and a place for baiting fishing lines. It got its name because Guðmundur Björnsson had his office there and paid out wages from it.
cce5e9b1-d43b-37a6-2f01-ea2ee2efe477.story_is: Bankinn var atvinnuhúsnæði, þar var meðal annars kæligeymsla, skreiðarvinnsla, síldarsöltun, verbúð, beitningaraðstaða og fleira. Hann var kallaður Bankinn þar sem Guðmundur Björnsson hafði þar skrifstofuaðstöðu og greiddi þar út laun.

cce63a6c-9941-4071-a9ca-c39ca347fba0.story_eng: Two horses drowned in this pond long ago. It lies on Beinhöfði, and the ground around it is called Flosar, where hay was once cut. Heystæðisholt, a knoll whose name refers to a haystack site, is also there.
cce63a6c-9941-4071-a9ca-c39ca347fba0.story_is: Í Kaplatjörn fórust tveir hestar fyrir löngu síðan. Tjörnin er á Beinhöfða og kringum hana heita Flosar, þar var heyjað. Þar er einnig Heystæðisholt.

ccee499a-d014-d565-03cf-fdaa636b5344.story_eng: The name Timburás means "timber ridge". There were once extensive woods here, and in many places around the ridge and along the river (Fljótið) old charcoal pits are still easy to see. The last remnants of the woodland are said to have been burned in 1867.
ccee499a-d014-d565-03cf-fdaa636b5344.story_is: Þarna voru miklir skógar áður og víða þarna og meðfram Fljótinu eru kolagrafir áberandi. Sagt er að síðustu skógarleifunum hafi verið brennt árið 1867.

ccf65e43-6478-8ca6-9c1f-eca291251c08.story_eng: In front of and below this rock there was once a stekkur, a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes, set in a shallow fissure. Behind the rock a sheep fold was built early in the 20th century, and it was used until 1985. Háiklettur stands by Stekkjarvík, west of the point where the lava narrows the river Laxá and forms the channel called Sogið.
ccf65e43-6478-8ca6-9c1f-eca291251c08.story_is: Framan undir Háakletti var stekkur í grunnri gjá, en að baki honum var byggð fjárrétt snemma á tuttugustu öldinni og var hún notuð til 1985. Kletturinn stendur við Stekkjarvík, vestan Stekkjarnefs, þar sem hraunið þrengir að Laxá og myndar Sogið.

ccfcc304-0445-604e-217b-7b8c12faf4e3.story_eng: This crag in Blakkur, above Mávakambar (Gull Crests) and north of the Strengbergsgjá chasm, is often called Höfðinn í Mávakömbunum to tell it apart from Jónshöfði and the other headlands in Blakkur. People went down onto it to gather eggs in Mávakambar, and there were two ways to get there. One was to be lowered on a rope from the edge, which is flat on top. The descent was easy, with clean rock in the upper part, but in the lower part the rope hung free in the air. The other way was to go down into Sveltið, a spot in the edge a little further north, then down a rope pitch to Sveltisgangur, a long ledge running south that is narrow in places, past the chasm and onto the crag. Below the crag are long rope pitches, and men and eggs were often hauled up by rope.
ccfcc304-0445-604e-217b-7b8c12faf4e3.story_is: Höfðinn er ofan Mávakamba í Blakk, norðan Strengbergsgjár. Hann er oft nefndur „Höfðinn í Mávakömbunum“ til aðgreiningar frá Jónshöfða og fleiri höfðum í Blakknum. Niður á Höfðann var farið til eggja í Mávakömbunum og um tvær leiðir að velja. Annars vegar var sigið af brún, sem þarna er slétt að ofan. Sigið er létt og klettar hreinir ofan til, en neðri hluti sigsins er loft. Hin leiðin er að fara niður í Sveltið, sem er þarna í brún nokkru norðar, þaðan í lás niður í Sveltisgang, sem er langur gangur til suðurs og tæpur á köflum, fyrir gjána og á Höfðann. Langir lásar eru niður af Höfðanum og voru menn og egg oft tekin upp á vaðdrætti.

cd12807b-87c6-4663-96fb-c36996a56c96.story_eng: Flóagil is a ravine up on the heath, where a built-up stone bridge, essentially a stacked stone wall, was raised across the gully. The road Þingmannavegur crosses the ravine here, and the bridge dates from shortly after 1870. It is 20 metres long and just over 3 metres high at its highest point. The work was led by Sigurður Davíðsson, the farmer at Veturliðastaðir.
cd12807b-87c6-4663-96fb-c36996a56c96.story_is: Flóagil er uppi á heiði og yfir þetta gil var byggð hlaðin steinbrú (garður). Þar liggur Þingmannavegurinn yfir, laust eftir 1870. Brúin er 20 metra löng og rúmir 3 metrar á hæð þar sem hún er hæst. Fyrir þessu verki stóð Sigurður Davíðsson, bóndi á Veturliðastöðum.

cd2fd906-5cfc-166a-134a-e2507fe389c2.story_eng: Ferjulág, also called Ferjulaut, is a sloping hollow of heathland running down to the river Þjórsá, with a small boggy pool at the bottom. For a long time there was an official ferry crossing here, which explains the name: ferja means ferry. The hollow now lies in the middle of the home field at Egilsstaðir.
cd2fd906-5cfc-166a-134a-e2507fe389c2.story_is: Ferjulág eða Ferjulaut er hallandi móaslakki að Þjórsá með mýrarpolli neðst. Þar var lengi lögferja. Lautin er nú fyrir miðju Egilsstaðatúni.

cd42c6ff-aac0-3cc3-d3f9-b07787d83118.story_eng: In earlier times there was a sel here, a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked, belonging to the farm Hólar. It was called Fornasel, which means the old shieling, and the hills below Ytra-Selfjall took their name from it. The shieling stood "out in the Hæðir", the rounded rise above the shoulder at the mouth of Héðinsdalur.
cd42c6ff-aac0-3cc3-d3f9-b07787d83118.story_is: Niður undan Ytra-Selfjalli heita Fornaselshæðir. Þar var sel í fyrri tíð frá Hólum og kallað Fornasel. Selið er „fram í Hæðum“, en svo kallast bungan yfir öxlinni í mynni Héðinsdals.

cd435ed5-a9d8-79bf-917f-e616bf15a2f8.story_eng: Tóunafir is a stony ridge at the southern end of Tóunafarás, a ridge at the western edge of the moorland. The old road once ran along it. The ridge it belongs to was full of fox dens, which suits the name, as tóa is an old word for fox. The farm also had a beitarhús (a sheep house out in the grazing land) on the ridge.
cd435ed5-a9d8-79bf-917f-e616bf15a2f8.story_is: Tóunafir er grjóthryggur syðst í Tóunafarási, sem er vestast við Móana. Þar lá gamli vegurinn. Í þessum ási voru mikil gren og á ásnum voru beitarhús frá bænum.

cd47a359-f1d4-df52-43a3-5ec6127e44a9.story_eng: This wall ran right across the Tunga, the tongue of land between the rivers Hvítá and Baulós. It was built on the orders of Ófeigur hinn ríki (Ófeigur the Rich) of Fjall, who was allowed to keep the cattle he meant to slaughter in the autumn here during the summers. The wall must have been a great structure and stock-proof. Many of the old named places in this area can no longer be seen, or only barely, as the land has been levelled and some of it has gone, or is going, into the river.
cd47a359-f1d4-df52-43a3-5ec6127e44a9.story_is: Framan við Breiðudæl er Garðurinn. Nær hann þvert yfir Tunguna milli Hvítár og Baulóss. Lét Ófeigur hinn ríki í Fjalli gera hann og fékk að hafa þar á sumrum naut þau sem hann ætlaði til slátrunar að hausti. Hefur garður sá verið mikið mannvirki og gripheldur. Mikið af þeim stöðum sem hér hafa borið örnefni sjást nú ekki lengur eða illa. Landið er búið að slétta en sumt er komið eða á leið í ána.

cd6ad4e8-e37c-7322-672d-8d681986d577.story_eng: Hjallstólpi, also called Öskuhóllinn (the ash mound), is one of two hillocks below the present school building at Hólar. It is an old ash heap, where ashes from the household fires were dumped, and on top of it once stood the drying shed (hjallur) of the estate. The name means "drying-shed post". The hillock is no longer there.
cd6ad4e8-e37c-7322-672d-8d681986d577.story_is: Tveir hólar eru neðan við núverandi skólahús á Hólum. Annar þeirra heitir Hjallstólpi en hann var einnig kallaður Öskuhóllinn. Það er gamall öskuhóll, og uppi á honum stóð áður þurrkhjallur staðarins.

cd8d238d-fddc-4cf8-a3a5-a8e8da638793.story_eng: This band of rocks is where the boy Láki was hanged for theft in the 17th century. The name Lákaklettur means Láki's Rock.
cd8d238d-fddc-4cf8-a3a5-a8e8da638793.story_is: Þarna var drengurinn Láki hengdur á 17. öld fyrir þjófnað.

cd920343-aa09-8f79-45a1-3196059a7a0e.story_eng: Herpismór, also called Herplingsmór, is a large, grassy moor down on the lowland south of the river Hofsá, described as having exceptionally good grazing. In the travel book of Ólafur Olavius, Hof and Herpismór are listed among the abandoned farms of Hólahreppur.
cd920343-aa09-8f79-45a1-3196059a7a0e.story_is: Sunnan við Hofsá, niðri á láglendi, er stór mór, grasi vaxinn og afar jarðsæll, sem kallaður er Herplingsmór, en oftar Herpismór. Í Ferðabók Ólafs Olaviusar eru Hof og Herpismór meðal eyðibýla í Hólahreppi.

cdda7e6a-97c4-25ac-79ca-e67890de8e6b.story_eng: Hólakot is an ancient farmstead on Narfastaðafell, the hill above the farm Narfastaðir. According to research, it was built at least in part in the 10th to 12th centuries. Its purpose is uncertain, and no written records of it exist. The buildings are no longer standing.
cdda7e6a-97c4-25ac-79ca-e67890de8e6b.story_is: Fornt býli á Narfastaðafelli, byggt að einhverju leyti á 10.–12. öld samkvæmt rannsóknum. Óvíst er um hlutverk þess og engar heimildir eru til um það.

ce0c67f5-0d18-dbee-c0b2-3144349cd290.story_eng: Just north of Bæjarás flows the stream Bæjarlækur, and at its mouth lie the ruins of either a sel (a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked) or a farm. The ridge itself is a gravel ridge, partly grassed over, running south from Hrappsstaðasel along the river.
ce0c67f5-0d18-dbee-c0b2-3144349cd290.story_is: Norðan Bæjaráss er Bæjarlækur, og við ós hans eru rústirnar eftir selið eða bæinn. Ásinn er melalda, að nokkru gróin, sem liggur suður frá Hrappsstaðaseli meðfram ánni.

ce15360f-09c7-db8a-446d-cfc422fc48ae.story_eng: Clear traces of fortification walls or defensive ramparts can still be seen on Virkishóll, whose name means "fort hill". It is not known when they were built. In 1220 Bishop Guðmundur (Guðmundur the Good, a 13th-century bishop) came here and broke up stones for defence, but Sturlunga saga, which records the events of that age, makes no mention of a fort being built at the spot. The hill lies on the east side of Kirkjugarðslaut.
ce15360f-09c7-db8a-446d-cfc422fc48ae.story_is: Á Virkishóli má sjá greinileg merki virkisgarða eða varnargarða. Ekki er vitað hvenær þeir hafa verið gerðir. Árið 1220 var Guðmundur biskup hér á ferð og braut upp grjót til varnar, en ekki er nefnd virkisgerð þar í Sturlungu. Hóllinn er austanvert við Kirkjugarðslaut.

ce189a7e-475c-7ef9-1e40-a49478129aae.story_eng: These are the ruins of a farm at Hlíðarendinn. A farm stood here for three or four years around 1660, and it is said to have been abandoned because of the constant stream of travellers. That is quite possible, as right up until 1880 there was enormous traffic of travellers here, and everyone would naturally have stopped at the last farm before heading onto Kaldadalur, or the first one on coming down from it. The farm is gone; only ruins remain.
ce189a7e-475c-7ef9-1e40-a49478129aae.story_is: Bæjarrústir eru við Hlíðarendann. Hér var býli um 1660 í 3–4 ár og sagt er að það hafi farið í eyði vegna ágangs ferðamanna. Er það vel mögulegt, því allt fram til 1880 var geysilegur ferðamannastraumur hér og allir hafa auðvitað áð hjá síðasta bæ þegar farið var á Kaldadal eða þeim fyrsta þegar komið var af honum.

ce220c3a-8dda-646b-ba68-cafa9402e813.story_eng: Biskupstunga, "the bishop's tongue", is a tiny triangle of land south of the churchyard, between the stream and the farm lane, on the east side of the track leading up to the farm. It takes its name from a visit by the bishop: once, when he was on his tour of inspection, his horses were kept here.
ce220c3a-8dda-646b-ba68-cafa9402e813.story_is: Þar voru hestar biskups geymdir eitt sinn á yfirreið hans. Biskupstunga er örlítil þríhyrna sunnan kirkjugarðs, milli lækjar og heimreiðar, austan við brautina heim.

ce284a76-c737-17c4-1317-465daa3374f7.story_eng: Baklag is a sheer cliff rising straight from the sea, north of Fjallahöfn. Seal nets were once set here, and the farmer from Lón was allowed to lay his nets behind those of the farmer from Fjöll. The name, made of the plain words for 'back' and 'laying', fits this arrangement.
ce284a76-c737-17c4-1317-465daa3374f7.story_is: Baklag er standbjarg við sjó, norður af Fjallahöfn, milli Bríkartáar og Hafnarinnar. Þar voru selalagnir og fékk Lónsbóndinn að leggja þar bak við Fjallabóndann.

ce2b9bbc-c9fe-7cb9-e243-dd898d908dbd.story_eng: Torfvegur, meaning "turf road", is a nook and a path that runs up through a cleft out of the lava field, straight east onto Langasandur. The name dates from the time of Indriði Ólafsson at Garður and comes from the cutting of turf in Hellnaselsmýri and the carrying of that turf home to Garður.
ce2b9bbc-c9fe-7cb9-e243-dd898d908dbd.story_is: Torfvegur er kriki og stígur eftir klauf upp úr hrauninu, beint austur á Langasand. Nafnið er frá tíð Indriða Ólafssonar í Garði og stafar frá torfristu og flutningi torfsins úr Hellnaselsmýri heim í Garð.

ce43b0f6-de0b-4443-8420-20d7998b12d3.story_eng: The name refers to útburður, the old practice of carrying a newborn child out into the open and leaving it to die; such children were also thrown into rivers or lakes. The names Útburðarfell and Útburðartjörn are taken to show that people came to Skarðsdalur on such errands before the conversion to Christianity in the year 1000. When Christianity became law, the chieftain Þorgeir Ljósvetningagoði agreed to a compromise: the old laws on exposing children and on eating horsemeat would stand, though Christians had to baptise a child quickly before it was carried out. The practice is described as arising less from cruelty than from the needs of a very poor society that could not feed and clothe every child. Laws rooted in the old Norwegian Gulaþing law made certain deformities grounds for exposure. As the executioner was the lowest regarded of all men, chieftains had slaves or shepherds carry the child out. Among healthy children, it was mostly those of poor farmers and slaves who were exposed, girls more often than boys.
ce43b0f6-de0b-4443-8420-20d7998b12d3.story_is: Útburður er það kallað þegar nýfætt barn er borið út á víðavang og það skilið eftir til að deyja. Einnig var útburðum kastað í ár eða vötn í sama tilgangi. Örnefnin Útburðarfell og Útburðartjörn segja sína sögu. Þau staðfesta á sinn hátt að á Skarðsdal var fólk á ferð í þessum erindagjörðum fyrir kristnitöku árið 1000. Þegar kristni var lögtekin gerði Þorgeir Ljósvetningagoði þá málamiðlun að „um barnaútburð skyldu standa hin fornu lög og um hrossakjötsát.“ Kristnir menn urðu þó að skíra barnið í snatri áður en það var borið út. Harðneskja fyrri tíðar gagnvart óvelkomnum börnum kom ekki til af mannvonsku, miklu fremur komu þar til þarfir blásnauðs samfélags sem ekki gat fætt og klætt öll þau börn sem í heiminn komu. Um útburð giltu lög sem áttu uppruna í hinum fornu Gulaþingslögum og kváðu á um að tiltekinn vanskapnaður á börnum gerði þau útburðarskyld. Böðullinn var jafnan lægst metinn allra manna og því létu goðar og aðrir höfðingjar þræla eða smala bera út hið vanskapaða barn. Af heilbrigðum börnum voru það einkum börn fátækra bænda og þræla sem voru borin út, og þá frekar meybörn en sveinbörn.

ce4ec323-7901-35e6-ebde-199ce9302a64.story_eng: Dauðsmannshaugur, meaning dead man's mound, is a scree of huge boulders by the sea. According to a folk tale, there was once a sizeable beach here where fishermen stayed, until a great mass of rock broke away from the cliff and fell on them. The rockfall also sealed off a cave where seasonal fishermen were living. It was said that their cries could be heard until summer, since there was no way to get them out through the boulders.
ce4ec323-7901-35e6-ebde-199ce9302a64.story_is: Stórgrýtisurð við sjóinn. Þjóðsaga er til um að þar hafi áður verið allmikil fjara og veiðimenn haldið þar til uns mikil fylla hafi hrunið yfir þá úr bjarginu. Hrundi þá einnig fyrir helli sem vermenn héldu til í. Sagt var að ópin í þeim hafi heyrst fram á sumar, því ekki var unnt að ná þeim út í gegnum stórgrýtið.

ce64d543-c11d-7744-1ad7-b6e837d795af.story_eng: Önnustapi is a rocky stack named after a ship called Anna, which ran aground here after getting caught in the ice.
ce64d543-c11d-7744-1ad7-b6e837d795af.story_is: Önnustapi er klettastapi sem dregur nafn sitt af skipi sem hét Anna. Það strandaði þar eftir að hafa lent í ís.

ce9ad606-d2ea-f083-3a93-f4d9b0e95cb3.story_eng: On Dagmálaás stands a cairn called Dagmálavarða. Seen from the farm, it marks dagmál, the mid-morning hour (around 9 a.m.) in the old way of telling time by the sun's position over landmarks. The ridge is the higher northern part of a low ridge called Stekkarás, which rises sharply here and takes the name Dagmálaás.
ce9ad606-d2ea-f083-3a93-f4d9b0e95cb3.story_is: Á Dagmálaási er varða sem heitir Dagmálavarða, og eru dagmál á henni frá bænum. Norður af Stekkarnefi liggur lágur ás, Stekkarás, en norðar hækkar hann mikið og nefnist þá einu nafni Dagmálaás.

ce9ca417-4702-b8fb-fc76-f8a43c02d02a.story_eng: North of where the ravine stream flows into the river, wooded slopes run along the riverbank. They are called Fjárskjól, "sheep shelter". During a great, sudden north-easterly blizzard, sheep were driven by the storm from Einbúahús down to this spot, and the place has carried the name Fjárskjól ever since.
ce9ca417-4702-b8fb-fc76-f8a43c02d02a.story_is: Norðan við þann stað sem gilið rennur í ána eru skógarbrekkur með ánni sem heita Fjárskjól. Í miklu norðaustan byláhlaupi hrakti fé frá Einbúahúsi og þarna niður, og heitir þar síðan Fjárskjól.

cea31c93-5f8f-d51d-2c5d-53b9bb729988.story_eng: Lækjarflói is a fairly wide stretch of marshland east of Grænasundsmelur. Out in it, to the north-east of the gravel flat, lies a pit called Sigurðarpyttur. It is said that a man and a horse, saddle and all, fell into it, sank and were never seen again.
cea31c93-5f8f-d51d-2c5d-53b9bb729988.story_is: Austur af Grænasundsmel er allvíðáttumikill flói, Lækjarflói. Í honum, út og austur af Grænasundsmelnum, er pyttur sem kallast Sigurðarpyttur. Sagt er að maður og hestur með reiðtygjum hafi lent í honum, sokkið og aldrei sést meir.

cebcdbe4-34d9-8831-342a-b2d439692f13.story_eng: Stöðull was a milking place by the home-field gate, on the way from the farm west to Stekkatún. Valdimar, who lived there, remembered cows being milked at Stöðull in summer. Ewes were probably also milked here in the days when lambs were weaned from their mothers so the ewes could be milked, but that practice had ended before Valdimar's time.
cebcdbe4-34d9-8831-342a-b2d439692f13.story_is: Á leið frá bæ vestur í Stekkatún var Stöðull við túnhliðið. Valdimar man að kýr voru mjólkaðar þar á sumrin. Þar munu kvíaær hafa verið mjólkaðar meðan fært var frá, en því var hætt fyrir minni Valdimars.

cec52eaa-59af-7383-a534-b3baad29ba91.story_eng: Súrmjólkurbreiða means roughly "sour-milk stretch", and the name comes from a mishap. Once, when skin bags of sour milk were being carried down the narrow path to the ford, one of the bags struck the rock and split, and the sour milk ran into the river. The way down is hard to find, along a rock ledge from the east. The ford itself is rather bouldery and cannot be crossed when the river is high.
cec52eaa-59af-7383-a534-b3baad29ba91.story_is: Eitt sinn þegar súrmjólkurbelgir voru fluttir niður einstigið rakst annar belgurinn í og rifnaði, en súrmjólkin rann í ána. Vandratað er niður að vaðinu eftir klettasyllu austan frá. Það er fremur stórgrýtt og ekki fært sé vöxtur í ánni.

cedc43f4-1efb-4b53-b370-6e9fa0aed6a0.story_eng: Dauðsmannsþúfa means "dead man's mound". It is a large, grass-covered mound at the northern end of the high hills southwest of Ytri-Stekkjardalur. Nothing more is known about how it got its name. On its eastern side, however, there is a rectangular hollow in the mound, and it looks very much as if someone once dug into it there.
cedc43f4-1efb-4b53-b370-6e9fa0aed6a0.story_is: Á norðurenda háhæðanna suðvestan af Ytri-Stekkjardal er stór, gróin þúfa, Dauðsmannsþúfa, en ekki er vitað frekar um þá nafngift. Hins vegar er ferhyrningslaga kvos í þúfunni að austan og er þar líkast því að grafið hafi verið í hana.

cee0d9b7-6796-58f7-a536-c49fe39f6bde.story_eng: Fraghilla is a ledge in the cliffs, just a few metres above the ground. In earlier times Túbal Magnússon, the farmer at Múlakot, dried turnip seed on this ledge. A small stream, which has its source in Litla-Bólstaður, runs just west of it.
cee0d9b7-6796-58f7-a536-c49fe39f6bde.story_is: Í hömrunum, fáa metra frá jörðu, er hilla sem Fraghilla heitir. Þar þurrkaði Túbal Magnússon, bóndi í Múlakoti, gulrófnafræ áður fyrr. Vestan við hilluna rennur smálækur sem á upptök sín í Litla-Bólstað.

cefd0ab7-1269-e17e-2e3c-e9d63a233b21.story_eng: Hamrar (crags) is the usual name for a row of rock outcrops on the northern part of the ridge edge called Hálsbrún. The southernmost outcrop is called Messuborg. Beside it ran the paths that churchgoers took from Svartárdalur to mass, known as Messuvegur (the mass road). The northernmost outcrop, Ystaborg, marks the north-western corner of the Tunguháls land.
cefd0ab7-1269-e17e-2e3c-e9d63a233b21.story_is: Norðarlega í Hálsbrúninni eru klappir, venjulega nefndar Hamrar. Syðsta klöppin heitir Messuborg. Hjá henni lágu messufólksgötur úr Svartárdal, nefndar Messuvegur. Nyrst er Ystaborg, og þar er norðvesturhornmerki Tunguhálslands.

cf00ccd5-3a2d-9da8-1aec-d5a2d9912b40.story_eng: Hringur ("the Ring") is a hillock and an enchanted spot (álagablettur), a round patch of oddly shaped grass tussocks that do not all face the same way. It was said that misfortune would come to the household if anyone disturbed either the grass or the soil within the ring. Once, when a bridge was being built over the stream Myllulækur near the Ring, two farmhands were given strict orders not to take any material from inside it. They ignored the orders and took material for the bridge from within the Ring. Later that same summer the riding club Óðinn held a group ride around Svínavatn. At the end of the ride, at the farm track to Mosfell close to the Ring, a horse from Mosfell named Hringur broke its leg. No one present could understand it, as the horse was on a level road, but the break was so bad that the horse had to be put down on the spot. The horse's name had nothing to do with the enchanted spot; it was called Hringur because it had a white ring in one eye. The horse was very precious to its owners, both for its qualities and its beauty.
cf00ccd5-3a2d-9da8-1aec-d5a2d9912b40.story_is: Hringurinn er álagablettur með sérkennilega löguðum grasþúfum sem ekki snúa allar eins. Að sögn hvíldu þau álög á svæðinu að válegra atburða mætti vænta á heimilinu væri hróflað við annaðhvort grasi eða mold á þessu hringlaga svæði. Eitt sinn var unnið að brúargerð yfir Myllulækinn nálægt Hringnum og tveir vinnumenn voru fengnir til verksins með þeim fyrirmælum að efnistaka innan Hringsins væri stranglega bönnuð. Þeir höfðu fyrirmælin að engu og sóttu efni í brúna innan Hringsins. Seinna þetta sama sumar efndi hestamannafélagið Óðinn til útreiðarhópferðar kringum Svínavatn. Þegar komið var að heimreiðinni að Mosfelli í lok ferðar, í námunda við Hringinn, varð það slys að hestur frá Mosfelli sem hét Hringur fótbrotnaði. Öllum viðstöddum var þetta óskiljanlegt þar sem hesturinn var á sléttum vegi, en fótbrotið var svo slæmt að aflífa varð hestinn á staðnum. Nafn hestsins átti ekkert skylt við nafnið á álagablettinum heldur var það til komið vegna þess að hesturinn var með hvítan hring í öðru auga. Hesturinn Hringur var eigendum sínum afar dýrmætur, bæði vegna kosta sinna og fegurðar.

cf2afdd0-b1f8-ae49-fd38-0c1a12e89819.story_eng: Skelkutótt is the name of the ruins of old beitarhús (sheep houses out in the grazing land), west of the hill Tunguholt. The place was thought to be haunted.
cf2afdd0-b1f8-ae49-fd38-0c1a12e89819.story_is: Skelkutótt heita rústir beitarhúsa vestan við Tunguholt, en Tunguholt er niður af Timburkletti. Reimt þótti á þessum stað.

cf3bb887-d51e-4831-9022-39f61b0039e0.story_eng: Sauðaklettar (Sheep Rocks) are three rocks out in the river. An old tale says that sheep were taken into a boat here.
cf3bb887-d51e-4831-9022-39f61b0039e0.story_is: Þrír klettar úti í ánni. Gömul sögn hermir að þar hafi sauðfé verið tekið í bát.

cf6dd0cf-f506-302c-c8d6-a8287d10919d.story_eng: The letter Ó is carved into this stone. The story goes that some young travellers stopped in Hamralág and began a game with their weapons. During the game one of them was mortally wounded, a man whose name began with the letter Ó. He was carried up onto the gravel ridge, and there, before he died, he carved the Ó into the stone with his spear. He was then buried in a cairn just inside Hamralág, in the land of Kleppjárnsreykir, above the old road. Because of this event, Hamralág is sometimes called Spjótalág, which means spear hollow.
cf6dd0cf-f506-302c-c8d6-a8287d10919d.story_is: Ó er klappað í steininn. Sagan segir að ungir ferðamenn hefðu stoppað í Hamralág og tekið upp leik með vopn sín. Í leiknum særðist einn til ólífis og átti hann Ó fyrir upphafsstaf. Maðurinn var borinn upp á melinn og þar klappaði hann Ó-ið í steininn með spjóti sínu áður en hann dó. Maðurinn var svo dysjaður rétt innan við Hamralág, í Kleppjárnsreykjalandi, ofan við gamla veginn. Í tengslum við þennan atburð er Hamralág stundum nefnd Spjótalág.

cf6f7bf7-b490-46bf-9147-00b8a76574bf.story_eng: Sundpollur means "swimming pool". The name belongs to a hollow just south of and above the gravel ridge Sundpollsmelur, near the boundary between the farms Eyjólfsstaðir and Úlfsstaðir. Here Stefán Gíslason, a doctor who lived at Úlfsstaðir in the latter half of the 19th century, made a swimming pool and taught swimming for as long as he lived there. The pool is gone today, and the gravel ridge beside it, just below the road, has mostly disappeared through gravel extraction.
cf6f7bf7-b490-46bf-9147-00b8a76574bf.story_is: Sundpollur heitir lægð sunnan og ofan við Sundpollsmel, skammt frá landamerkjum Eyjólfsstaða og Úlfsstaða. Þar útbjó Stefán Gíslason læknir, sem bjó á Úlfsstöðum á síðari hluta 19. aldar, sundpoll og kenndi sund á meðan hann bjó á Úlfsstöðum. Melurinn var rétt fyrir neðan veg en er nú að mestu horfinn vegna efnistöku.

cf78dd4c-2d38-a31f-9144-86ad90bb6e00.story_eng: The old bridge here was built of stacked stone by the stonemason Steinþór Björnsson, probably in connection with the building of the house at Stóruvellir. It was swept away in a flood in 1942, and a new bridge was built in 1945 and later strengthened. Remains of the old stone bridge can still be seen.
cf78dd4c-2d38-a31f-9144-86ad90bb6e00.story_is: Steinþór Björnsson steinsmiður hlóð gömlu brúna, líklega í tengslum við byggingu Stóruvallahússins. Hún fór í hlaupi árið 1942 og ný brú var byggð 1945 og seinna styrkt. Enn má sjá leifar gömlu brúarinnar.

cf82b6af-beef-8fce-5f08-de466825d4e5.story_eng: The name Mannskaðafoss means roughly "waterfall of the loss of life", and a story explains it. Once, when hay was being made in Blikdalur valley, the hay was being carried home on a train of packhorses. Up on the edge above the waterfall, one of the ropes holding a load snapped. The man leading the packhorses went to fix it, but he slipped over the edge and fell down into the waterfall. The waterfall lies in the gorge above Ártún.
cf82b6af-beef-8fce-5f08-de466825d4e5.story_is: Þegar heyjað var í Blikdal var eitt sinn verið að flytja hey heim. Slitnaði þá sili á brúninni fyrir ofan fossinn. Sá sem var með lestina ætlaði að laga þetta en hrökk þá niður fyrir og í fossinn. Mannskaðafoss er í gljúfrunum ofan við Ártún, móti Berjamóa ofarlega.

cf90bd92-6353-1570-009e-3e0daebccafa.story_eng: This fertile stretch of flat land was once a hayfield named Lénharðarmóur, though in later times it has been called Flatir. It was considered good mowing land. The name is believed to come from an Englishman, Lénharður (Lienardt), who farmed at Kvíanes in the 17th century. A story was told to explain it: one summer Lénharður was out haymaking on the hillside with only his wife, who was expecting a child. There in the hayfield she went into labour. Lénharður took her in his arms and carried her home to the farm, close to two kilometres away, where she gave birth and all went well. This was thought a remarkable feat of strength, and the hayfield they had been working in was named after him. A small stream that often runs dry separates it from Merarsteinar, and the field is thought to lie below the road.
cf90bd92-6353-1570-009e-3e0daebccafa.story_is: Lítill lækur, sem oft þornar, skilur Merarsteina frá engjaplássi sem áður bar nafnið Lénharðarmóur en hefur á síðari tímum verið kallað Flatir. Þetta er gróðursælt flatlendi og þótti gott slægjuland. Lénharðarmóur munu hafa verið kenndar við Englendinginn Lénharð (Lienardt) sem var bóndi á Kvíanesi á 17. öld. Til nánari skýringar á nafninu var sögð þessi saga: Eitt sumar var Lénharður við heyskap úti á hlíð og var kona hans með honum en aðrir ekki. Hún var kona ekki einsömul og bar svo til að hún kenndi sín þarna í slægjunni. Lénharður tók hana þá á handlegg sér og bar hana til bæjar. Ól hún þar barnið og fór allt vel. Leiðin sem hann bar konuna er upp undir tveir kílómetrar. Þetta þótti afburða þrekvirki og var slægjan, sem þau voru að vinna í, kennd við hann og kölluð Lénharðarmóur. Ætla má að Lénharðarmóur séu hér neðan við veginn.

cfa0ae70-f3e2-8b35-1cec-4a190b6de39f.story_eng: Launfit is a flat stretch of dry grassland with small ponds, lying east and south of Högnholt. Hay was once cut here; in 1914, for example, 11 horse-loads of hay were carried from here up to Kópsvatn to pay off a hay debt. There is little view from this spot, and that is where the name comes from: laun means hiding or concealment, and fit is a grassy meadow.
cfa0ae70-f3e2-8b35-1cec-4a190b6de39f.story_is: Launfit nefnist slétt valllendi með smátjörnum austan og sunnan við Högnholt. Þar var heyjað fyrrum, til dæmis voru árið 1914 fluttir þaðan 11 kaplar upp að Kópsvatni til að greiða heyskuld. Þarna er lítið útsýni og af því er nafnið dregið.

cfc0db5d-6f04-da31-9769-eadc8ae66fc7.story_eng: The old bridge over Jökulkvísl was built in 1953 at a spot with a gorge below and very poor access. It was a wooden deck resting on flimsy piers, and it did not last long. The bridge was later moved to the place where it stands today, so it is no longer here. The newer bridge was made from part of the bridge over Jökulsá á Sólheimasandi, which sagged under the weight of snow in 1989–90.
cfc0db5d-6f04-da31-9769-eadc8ae66fc7.story_is: Gamla Jökulkvíslarbrúin var byggð 1953. Gljúfur er undir þar sem brúin var og aðgengi var mjög vont. Brúin var tréfleki á ræksnisstöplum og entist ekki lengi. Hún var síðar færð á þann stað sem hún er á í dag. Nýja brúin var hluti af brúnni á Jökulsá á Sólheimasandi en sú brú sligaðist undan snjó 1989–90.

cfd51888-b25e-4ae8-8422-9ecd8125aceb.story_eng: Old ruins once stood down in Nesmóar. Further out there may have been an old haystack site, and the ruins may have been the remains of a fráfærnastekkur or a beitarhús. A fráfærnastekkur was a fold used at weaning time, when lambs were separated from the ewes so the ewes could be milked. A beitarhús was a sheep house out in the grazing land. The ruins are gone. They were levelled in the spring of 2008, when a hayfield was made in Nesmóar.
cfd51888-b25e-4ae8-8422-9ecd8125aceb.story_is: Gamlar tóftir voru niðri í Nesmóum. Þar gæti hafa verið gamalt heystæði, utar, og leifar af fráfærnastekk eða beitarhúsi. Tóftirnar voru jafnaðar út vorið 2008, þegar tún var gert í Nesmóum.

d002144c-26ac-564a-fc29-ef16a6a937a0.story_eng: For a long time a ferry crossed from the farm Garður over Austurós, the eastern mouth of the Héraðsvötn river, to Lón on the other side. Also known as Garðsferja, it was a lögferja, a legal ferry: a crossing where, by the law of the land, a ferry boat had to be kept ready. The ferry was discontinued in 1895, after a bridge was built over the eastern branch of the river, Austur-Vötnin, below Vatnsleysa. The crossing no longer exists.
d002144c-26ac-564a-fc29-ef16a6a937a0.story_is: Frá Garði var löngum ferjað yfir Austurós Héraðsvatna á móti Lóni og þar var skipuð lögferja, þ.e. ferjustaður þar sem ferjubátur átti að vera til reiðu samkvæmt landslögum. Garðsferja var lögð niður 1895 eftir að brú kom á Austur-Vötnin suður og niður frá Vatnsleysu.

d00241e7-742c-46cd-bd13-66986bb4d01c.story_eng: The ridges north of Fljótshlíð and south of the mountain Þríhyrningur were called Þríhyrningshálsar. In past centuries people often travelled over these ridges, coming down to Hlíðarendi and other farms in Fljótshlíð.
d00241e7-742c-46cd-bd13-66986bb4d01c.story_is: Hálsarnir norður af Fljótshlíðinni og sunnan Þríhyrnings voru kallaðir Þríhyrningshálsar. Á fyrri öldum var mikið farið yfir þessa hálsa og komið niður að Hlíðarenda og öðrum bæjum í Fljótshlíð.

d004d4cf-ffc0-46b1-c2c3-8421a8d6bc74.story_eng: Efrihús was a beitarhús, a sheep house out in the grazing land, that was destroyed by an avalanche in 1951. Ásgeir frá Gottorp tells the story in his book Forystufé (Leader Sheep). The leader wether Hjarðarhagagráni usually pushed his way far inside the house when the sheep were brought in. This time, however, he refused and stayed by the door. When people reached the house after the avalanche, he was standing on top of the roof, which was still standing. In all, 50 to 60 sheep died in the disaster.
d004d4cf-ffc0-46b1-c2c3-8421a8d6bc74.story_is: Efrihús eru beitarhús sem fóru í snjóflóði 1951. Frásögn af því er í bók Ásgeirs frá Gottorp, Forystufé, en þar segir frá forystusauðnum Hjarðarhagagrána sem venjulega tróð sér innarlega í húsið þegar fé kom á hús. En í þetta sinn þráaðist hann við og stóð fram við dyr. Þegar komið var að eftir snjóflóðið stóð hann uppi á þekjunni sem enn stóð uppi. Alls drápust í slysi þessu 50 til 60 kindur.

d013edb2-f4b9-f1fe-d2f7-7d5cad8a56af.story_eng: Helguklöpp means Helga's rock slab. It is said that a woman named Helga died of exposure there, and the rock is named after her. It lies near the small stream Litlilækur, south of the long gravel ridge Langimelur, which runs from the mountain down to the river.
d013edb2-f4b9-f1fe-d2f7-7d5cad8a56af.story_is: Sagt er að þar hafi orðið úti kona að nafni Helga. Helguklöpp er sunnan Langamels, sem liggur frá fjalli að fljóti, skammt frá Litlalæk.

d0189046-3fb1-ff82-7a81-e2129c273a09.story_eng: Árni Oddsson is said to have rested his horse Högni in this hollow, which takes its name from the horse. Árni had come ashore in Vopnafjörður and was on his way to the Alþingi, the national assembly. He is said to have got Högni at the farm Hákonarstaðir, having already ridden one or two horses to exhaustion on the way from Vopnafjörður.
d0189046-3fb1-ff82-7a81-e2129c273a09.story_is: Þar mun Árni Oddsson hafa hvílt klárinn Högna eftir að hafa komið að landi á Vopnafirði, á leið sinni til þings. Hann mun hafa fengið klárinn Högna á Hákonarstöðum og þá verið búinn að uppgefa einn eða tvo hesta á leið sinni frá Vopnafirði.

d026d5cd-cb60-cfb8-3c59-fd7570e28a57.story_eng: Remains of the old farm at Hjaltadalur can still be made out here. The farm was swept away by an avalanche in 1737, and lives were lost.
d026d5cd-cb60-cfb8-3c59-fd7570e28a57.story_is: Þar má greina leifar af gamla bænum í Hjaltadal sem tók af í snjóflóði 1737 og varð af mannskaði.

d039cb4d-8332-1f04-d20e-4a8f6d30377d.story_eng: Finnsstaðatjörn lies on the lowland below the farm Finnsstaðir and was formerly called Fjúlatjörn. It is now only a shadow of what it once was and is better described as an area of ponds. In its northern part is Kerlingarauga ("old woman's eye"), and a story is told about it. Two brothers who lived at Finnsstaðir quarrelled over the fishing in the pond. Their mother, a frail old woman, then went down to the pond, chanted something potent and declared that there should never again be fish to catch there. In the southeast corner of the pond is Skessukelda, a bog hole said to be named after a ewe. The stream Gegnir flows south out of the pond all the way to the river Djúpá.
d039cb4d-8332-1f04-d20e-4a8f6d30377d.story_is: Finnsstaðatjörn er á láglendinu niður af bænum og hét áður Fjúlatjörn. Nú er hún ekki svipur hjá sjón og má fremur tala um tjarnarsvæði. Norðarlega í henni er Kerlingarauga og af því er sú saga að bræður sem bjuggu á Finnsstöðum deildu um veiði í tjörninni. Móðir þeirra, örvasa gamalmenni, fór þá að tjörninni, þuldi eitthvað mergjað og mælti svo um að þar skyldi ekki framar vera veiði. Í suðausturhorni tjarnarinnar er Skessukelda, kennd við rollu. Lækurinn Gegnir rennur suður úr tjörninni, alla leið til Djúpár.

d03baaf3-d2b1-47ff-b887-309f0f65fdb7.story_eng: Grátþúfur means 'weeping hummocks'. It is said that here the household servants of Helgi Ásbjarnarson wept for him after his death. Helgi is a figure from Fljótsdæla saga, and his burial mound, Helgahaugur, lay a little further west, nearer the stream. Grátþúfur lay beside Hrinuhali, also called Hrinutangi, a ridge that ran out from the north-west corner of the swimming pool building. The ground has since been levelled, and no one knows for certain where these places were. Their locations are based on a drawing in Benedikt Gíslason's Eiðasaga from 1958 and on the old place-name description.
d03baaf3-d2b1-47ff-b887-309f0f65fdb7.story_is: Hjá Grátþúfum grétu hjú Helga Ásbjarnarsonar hann dauðan. Vestar, nær læknum, var Helgahaugur, haugur Helga Ásbjarnarsonar, sbr. Fljótsdælu. Grátþúfur voru við Hrinuhala eða Hrinutanga, hrygg sem lá út frá norðvesturhorni sundlaugarhússins. Nú hefur svæðið verið sléttað og ekki er glöggt vitað hvar þessi örnefni voru, en við staðsetningu þeirra er farið eftir teikningu í Eiðasögu Benedikts Gíslasonar frá 1958, auk örnefnalýsingar.

d04a01f7-876e-8136-468e-0240e2af3972.story_eng: In the middle of Selmýri, 'shieling marsh' (a sel was a summer shieling where livestock were kept and milked), there are ruins. The marsh lies above the grassy hollows called Gontur. Above it rise the slopes known as Selbrekkur, which, seen from the farm, reach all the way up to the edge of the heights.
d04a01f7-876e-8136-468e-0240e2af3972.story_is: Í miðri Selmýri eru tóttir. Mýrin er ofan við Gontur, sem eru hvammar, og ofan við hana eru Selbrekkur sem ná upp á brún, séð frá bæ.

d04c0c43-8e05-e96a-dc77-540f43fcce4d.story_eng: Ofgóð was a well in a small hollow just east of Látalætishóll, a little hill close southeast of Hellahóll. It was used by the people of both Hellar and Látalæti, but it fell out of use because of a quarrel between them. Among other things, salted fish from one of the two farms had been put in the well to soak.
d04c0c43-8e05-e96a-dc77-540f43fcce4d.story_is: Í lítilli kvos austan við Látalætishól, sem er fast suðaustan í Hellahól, var brunnur sem hét Ofgóð. Hann var notaður frá Hellum og Látalæti en lagðist niður vegna ágreinings; meðal annars hafði saltfiskur frá öðrum hvorum bænum verið lagður í bleyti í brunninn.

d04e50a4-88ae-1c6d-9ed9-e65940a8e7c1.story_eng: Despite its name, which means 'green marsh', Grænamýri is not a marsh at all but sandy ground. It forms the lowest part of the home field at Kollsvík, below the farmhouse and south of the stream. There was once a farm here, also called Grænamýri.
d04e50a4-88ae-1c6d-9ed9-e65940a8e7c1.story_is: Grænamýri er ekki mýri heldur sendið land. Hún er neðsti hluti Kollsvíkurtúns, neðan íbúðarhúss og Húsatúns, sunnan Myllulækjar. Þarna var býli sem nefnt var Grænamýri.

d05b0768-f5af-4bbc-b481-79b06921d6d8.story_eng: In 1937 a burial cairn was found beside Bátagil. The National Museum's antiquarian at the time, Matthías Þórðarson, was notified and excavated it. The grave turned out to date from the pagan era, before Iceland's conversion to Christianity. It held the skeletons of three people and of a horse with its riding gear, along with weapons. Kuml is the Icelandic word for a pagan grave.
d05b0768-f5af-4bbc-b481-79b06921d6d8.story_is: Við Bátagil fannst dys árið 1937. Þáverandi þjóðminjaverði, Matthíasi Þórðarsyni, var gert viðvart og hann gróf í dysina. Hún reyndist úr heiðnum sið, og í henni fundust beinagrindur þriggja manna og hests með reiðtygjum, auk vopna.

d081a123-d67f-d711-8857-053e96f6c7b7.story_eng: In 1977, human bones were found at Litli-Skiphóll while gravel was being dug from the hill. How the bones came to be there, and what became of them afterwards, is not known. Much of the hill has been taken away for gravel. It lies just below the old road, beneath the homefield.
d081a123-d67f-d711-8857-053e96f6c7b7.story_is: Mannabein fundust árið 1977 við malartöku í Litla-Skiphól. Óvíst er um tilurð og frágang beinanna. Hóllinn hefur að miklu leyti verið tekinn í malarnám. Hann er rétt neðan við gamla veginn, neðan við tún.

d0939254-0106-86cb-f2d3-1dddcef20f8f.story_eng: Gunnarsgil (Gunnar's Ravine) is named after a man who died of exposure there.
d0939254-0106-86cb-f2d3-1dddcef20f8f.story_is: Kennt við mann sem varð þar úti.

d0b86f5d-6351-7426-c79d-d7f75a7ecacd.story_eng: Skjónuhvammur lies at the lowest end of Vöð, an old hay meadow along the Skógaá river, which forms the boundary with the farm Skógar here. Vöð is believed to take its name from fords in the river. The story told about how Skjónuhvammur got its name is that men at Skógarétt, the sheep fold, grew thirsty and had no brennivín, the Icelandic schnapps. A man was sent to Húsavík and told to be quick, but on the way back his horse collapsed and died from overexertion in Mósalaut.
d0b86f5d-6351-7426-c79d-d7f75a7ecacd.story_is: Sunnan við Bolagróf eru Vöð, en það er slægjuland sem lá neðan við Einarsstaðaengjar meðfram Skógaá, sem er hér á merkjum á móti Skógum. Mun nafnið draga nafn af vöðum í ánni. Neðst í Vöðunum er Skjónuhvammur. Tildrög nafns þessa eru þau að menn sem voru á Skógarétt gerðust þyrstir og vantaði brennivín. Var maður sendur til Húsavíkur og sagt að vera fljótur, en hesturinn sprakk í Mósalaut á leiðinni til baka.

d103945b-313f-568d-a962-43488aab4ee8.name_eng: Heystæði, ruins of a hay stack site
d103945b-313f-568d-a962-43488aab4ee8.story_eng: Heystæði, meaning hay-stack site, lies up on the edge of the slope south of Syðri-Vegargeiri. Hay was stacked here a number of times when leaves were gathered as fodder up on the heath and brought here on horseback. The writer recalls that the children were made to lead the horses carrying the bundles.
d103945b-313f-568d-a962-43488aab4ee8.story_is: Heystæði heitir uppi á brúninni sunnan við Syðri-Vegargeira. Þar var borið upp hey nokkrum sinnum þegar heyjað var lauf í heiðinni og flutt þarna að á hestum. Vorum við börnin látin teyma undir böggunum.

d12273c7-78e3-410d-840a-888f0043916d.story_eng: Reykjastekkur stands on a high knoll in heather moorland on the western side of Hrakholt, a fairly high ridge. The ruins here were once a beitarhús, a sheep house out in the grazing land, and were last used as a stekkur, a small fold where ewes and lambs were kept apart in early summer. Two ruined structures can still be seen, and they were probably built on top of an older one.
d12273c7-78e3-410d-840a-888f0043916d.story_is: Vestan í Hrakholti, allháum ási fyrir vestan Þormóðsmýri, eru gamlar beitarhúsarústir sem síðast voru notaðar sem stekkur, Reykjastekkur. Stekkurinn er í háum hól í lyngmóa. Tvær tóftir sjást í Reykjastekk, líklega byggðar á eldra mannvirki.

d12e6ab5-177e-df49-57f3-df4300f8e2f0.story_eng: Bekkur is a rocky ledge down on the shore, on the near side of Straumsker. At one point there is a hole in the ledge leading down into a fairly large cave, which opens to the sea below. The sea flows into the cave whenever it is not low tide. In heavy seas, especially from the west, the waves surging into the cave send great spouts of seawater up through the hole. Seen from the farm Láganúpur, these spouts sometimes reach halfway up the ridges, more than 20 metres high.
d12e6ab5-177e-df49-57f3-df4300f8e2f0.story_is: Bekkur er klettabekkur niðri í fjöru, heimanvið Straumsker. Í Bekkinn er á einum stað gat niður í allstóran helli sem opnast að neðanverðu til sjávar. Sjór gengur inn í þennan helli þegar ekki er háfjara. Í stórsjó, einkanlega af vestri, verða mikil sjávargos upp úr gatinu þegar öldur ganga í hellinn. Frá Láganúpi séð ná þessi gos stundum upp í miðja hryggi, eða yfir 20 metra hæð.

d14d970b-851a-81be-f72e-1dfe02df0261.story_eng: Ráðleysa was one of two small hillocks in the flat ground lying in line with the farm Framnes when seen from the farmyard at Fjall. Its twin was called Hosiló. The tops of both hillocks were later lowered, but traces of where they stood can still be made out. For some years Vigfús Ófeigsson, father of séra (the Reverend) Ófeigur of Fellsmúli, lived in a small hut built into the other hillock, Hosiló.
d14d970b-851a-81be-f72e-1dfe02df0261.story_is: Tveir smáhólar voru í flötunum í stefnu á Framnesbæinn þegar staðið er á hlaðinu í Fjalli. Hétu þeir Hosiló og Ráðleysa. Toppur þeirra var lækkaður en þó sér móta fyrir hvar þeir voru. Vigfús Ófeigsson, faðir séra Ófeigs í Fellsmúla, átti heima í nokkur ár í kofa í öðrum hólnum, þeim sem hét Hosiló.

d151e011-8cf3-d517-b58c-f2afb7631758.story_eng: Heljarvogur, whose name begins with Hel, an old word for death, was considered extremely dangerous in autumn and spring. When the man who described it was a small boy, two gemlingar (yearling sheep) fell through the same hole in the ice here. One was found a day later than the other: it had been carried in under the slush, but drifted up into the hole after the first one had been brought up. This is probably what gave the place its name. Other animals have gone in here as well, though some were saved. The pool lies just north of the stream Klapparlækur and reaches northwest into Spilda.
d151e011-8cf3-d517-b58c-f2afb7631758.story_is: Heljarvogur er rétt norður af Klapparlæk og gengur þar norðvestur í Spildu. Þar er snarhætta haust og vor. Þar fóru tveir gemlingar í eina og sömu vök þegar ég var smádrengur. Annar fannst degi síðar en hinn; hann hafði lent inn undir krapið en borist upp í vökina eftir að sá sem fyrr fannst var kominn upp. Þetta mun hafa ráðið nafngjöfinni. Fleira hefur farið þar en sumu verið bjargað.

d15e1fb1-28a9-1917-8f92-411de7a108dd.story_eng: Þverdalur ("cross valley") is a deep cleft that cuts right through the ridge Mjóavatnsháls. An old road, or set of tracks, known as Þverdalsvegur or Þverdalsgötur, runs through it and on over the ridge Stórásinn and down into Dýjahvammur. These tracks were the main route for travellers for as long as there was a ferry across the Lagarfljót river below the farm Rangá.
d15e1fb1-28a9-1917-8f92-411de7a108dd.story_is: Þverdalur er djúp dalskora sem sker Mjóavatnsháls í sundur. Um hann liggur gamall vegur eða götur, Þverdalsvegur eða Þverdalsgötur. Liggja þær áfram yfir Stórásinn, framan við Klofasteina, niður í Dýjahvamm. Þessar götur voru alfaraleið á meðan ferja var á Lagarfljóti undan Rangá.

d1759b3c-9945-4e76-9276-7845ef43f42d.story_eng: A hut known as Oddakofi once stood on this hillock, but it is now gone. A forlorn shepherd boy hanged himself there, and afterwards the place was said to be badly haunted. The hillock is one of many in the home field, west of the road up to the farm, by the field gate.
d1759b3c-9945-4e76-9276-7845ef43f42d.story_is: Oddakofi, sem var á hólnum, er nú horfinn. Umkomulaus smali hengdi sig þar, og síðan var þar reimt mjög, að sagt var. Í túni eru margir hólar, og er Oddskofahóll vestan við veginn heim, norður við túnhlið.

d1823d2b-50d9-3444-0884-fa9966dcd7f8.story_eng: Kvíamelur is the southernmost of the gravel ridges on the willow-covered slopes east of Bæjargróf, where the ridges alternate with wedges of grassland. Close by, in a small hollow, lies an old kvíaból, a site where ewes were penned for milking, which may explain the name, as kví means a milking pen.
d1823d2b-50d9-3444-0884-fa9966dcd7f8.story_is: Fyrir austan Bæjargrófina taka við víði vaxnar brekkur með melhryggjum og valllendisgeirum. Syðsti melhryggurinn heitir Kvíamelur og er gamalt kvíaból í hvammi þar skammt frá.

d1965dff-bd0f-a826-6416-4d7ff801136d.story_eng: Stekkjardalur takes its name from the remains of old lambing folds (stekkir) in its eastern part. These folds were used at weaning time, when lambs were separated from the ewes so the ewes could be milked. The valley lies southwest of the home field of Kárastaðasel, the old shieling of Kárastaðir, and runs northwest to southeast just south of Seldalur.
d1965dff-bd0f-a826-6416-4d7ff801136d.story_is: Í Stekkjardalnum austanverðum er brot af fráfærnastekkjum, og dregur hann nafn af því. Dalurinn er suðvestur frá Seltúninu við Kárastaðasel og liggur í norðvestur og suðaustur, næst sunnan við Seldalinn.

d1b785e4-3107-63c6-e7ba-34b0f9414f7e.story_eng: Grenjalág is a gap in the cliff belt along the edge of Breiðurinn, where the steep scree reaches all the way to the top and offers a way up onto the heights. People went this way when rounding up sheep and when they went to gather eggs on Breiðurinn. From below, the route first climbs a little to one side of where the gap lies above, then the path winds up the scree in slanting traverses. Although the route is now called Grenjalág, the name probably first belonged to a deep hollow below the slope, between it and Ytra-Breiðsholt. That hollow holds the fox dens that gave the route and the gap their name (greni means fox den, and lág means hollow), and the remains of a tófuhús, a fox house, can still be seen there.
d1b785e4-3107-63c6-e7ba-34b0f9414f7e.story_is: Um Grenjalág var farið til smalana og þegar farið var til eggja í Breiðnum. Leiðin liggur um skarð í klettabeltinu í brún Breiðsins, þar sem brött skriðan nær á brún, og er þar leið upp á Breið. Neðan frá er fyrst farið upp lítið eitt framar en skarðið er uppi og svo liggur gatan í sniðum upp skriðurnar. Þó að þessi leið nefnist nú Grenjalág á nafnið sennilega upprunalega við djúpa laut neðan hlíðarinnar, milli hennar og Ytra-Breiðsholts. Þar eru tófugrenin sem leiðin og skarðið eru kennd við, og þar má sjá leifar tófuhúss.

d1b8826f-878c-4f3c-a4bb-3a5413eb1878.story_eng: These low hillocks lie a short way in from the pond Randarhólstjörn, on a line between the farms Hóll and Sandur. On them are ancient remains of circular walls, which were known as Hringur (the Ring). There was also a stekkur here, a small fold where lambs were penned apart from the ewes, called Hringstekkur, and it gave the hillocks their name.
d1b8826f-878c-4f3c-a4bb-3a5413eb1878.story_is: Spölkorn innan við Randarhólstjörnina eru lágir hólar í stefnu milli bæjanna Hóls og Sands sem heita Hringstekkshólar. Þar eru forn garðlög, hringlaga, sem voru kölluð Hringur. Einnig var þar stekkur, nefndur Hringstekkur.

d1ca43b7-a982-c131-30dc-d5d34bb6cad9.story_eng: Stóratjörn, also called Fjárdrápstjörn (roughly "sheep-killing pond"), was once completely overgrown with sedge, except for its deep pool. At the start of winter, when the waters began to freeze, the ice over the sedge was thinner than elsewhere. The sheep were drawn to the sedge, which stayed green well into the winter, but the thin ice could not hold them. They fell through, "went under" as it was called, and then death was certain. The pond was drained in 1955.
d1ca43b7-a982-c131-30dc-d5d34bb6cad9.story_is: Tjörnin, sem einnig var kölluð Fjárdrápstjörn, var öll vaxin stör nema hylurinn. Í byrjun vetrar, er vötn tók að leggja, var ísinn í störinni þynnri en annars staðar. Fé sótti í störina, sem hélst græn fram á vetur, en þunnur ísinn hélt ekki kindunum. Þær fóru ofan í, sem kallað var, og var þeim þá dauðinn vís. Tjörnin var ræst fram árið 1955.

d1e645f6-e520-2fb0-217d-f8ade553a74c.story_eng: Stekkjarnes is a flat point of land by the sea. On it stands an old stekkur, a small pen used in the old days when lambs were kept apart from the ewes so the ewes could be milked. It remains as a reminder of that custom, and it gave the headland its name, which means "lamb-pen point".
d1e645f6-e520-2fb0-217d-f8ade553a74c.story_is: Stekkjarnes er tangi við sjóinn, í norðaustur frá Hvaltjörn. Nesið er slétt og þar er gamall stekkur til minningar um stekkjarsiðinn í gamla daga.

d1eec495-5116-c49f-6c51-32e8dcdd286c.story_eng: Búhólar are gravel hills with grass growing between them, lying at the very innermost end of the valley floor. It was said that they were the dwelling place of elves.
d1eec495-5116-c49f-6c51-32e8dcdd286c.story_is: Innst í botni dalsins eru Búhólar, melhólar með grasi á milli. Sagt var að þeir væru bústaður álfa.

d1ff36b1-1cb4-cfc3-b167-52d71d7845a5.story_eng: At the southern tip of Pollamýri, on the boundary, lies Draugsauga (Ghost's Eye), an extremely deep pit. Pollamýri, whose name means roughly 'pool bog', is a loosely defined part of the large stretch of marshland between the farms Geirbjarnarstaðir and Þóroddsstaðir, on Geirbjarnarstaðir land. It is said to lie south of the spot where the stream Hamralækur comes down onto the bog.
d1ff36b1-1cb4-cfc3-b167-52d71d7845a5.story_is: Syðst í Pollamýri er Draugsauga á merkjum, hyldjúpur pyttur. Pollamýri er nafn á óskilgreindum hluta Mýrarinnar, sem er mikið mýrlendi á milli Geirbjarnarstaða og Þóroddsstaða í landi Geirbjarnarstaða. Þessi hluti mýrarinnar er sagður sunnan Hamralækjarfitar, sem er þar sem Hamralækur kemur niður á mýrina.

d1ff5c63-7a7a-4c0e-95c4-0c1be4e724bc.story_eng: Einbúi, meaning 'the hermit' or 'one who lives alone', is a single solitary shrub. It is believed to have arrived with an avalanche around 1919, as avalanches often come down from the mountain Þverárfjall.
d1ff5c63-7a7a-4c0e-95c4-0c1be4e724bc.story_is: Stök hrísla. Mun hún hafa komið með snjóflóði í kringum 1919, en úr Þverárfjalli falla iðulega snjóflóð.

d212828f-3621-7f84-afaa-6d5a83d5bfdb.story_eng: Hádegisborg, also called Miðdegisborg, is an old eyktamark for the farm Nes: a landmark used to tell the time of day by the sun's position. Hádegi means midday. The rock stands southwest of the farm and rises above Álftatangi. It is shaped like a farmhouse, or like a trapezoid or the roof of a house, and it is believed that huldumenn (hidden people) live there. The rock is thought beautiful and well suited to be their home, and there are tales about "the inhabitants of the rock", though they are not recorded in the description. Another account describes it as a small rocky outcrop west of Nesvatn with a cairn on top. Seen from Nes, it looks like an old turf farmhouse with a chimney.
d212828f-3621-7f84-afaa-6d5a83d5bfdb.story_is: Hádegisborg er gamalt eyktamark frá Nesi. Hún er í suðvestur frá bænum, norðan við Kiðuklauf, ber yfir Álftatangann og minnir á trapisu eða þak á húsi. Borgin er eins og bær í laginu, og það er trú manna að huldumenn eigi þar bústað. Þykir borgin vera fögur og vel til þess valin, enda eru til sagnir um „íbúa borgarinnar“, þó að þær séu ekki tilgreindar hér. Hún er einnig nefnd Miðdegisborg og er lítil klöpp vestan við Nesvatnið. Það er varða á henni og heiman frá Nesi lítur hún út eins og maður sjái gamlan torfbæ með reykháfi.

d21d3ee3-7118-5344-b2c6-d7f0cfd518af.story_eng: Lýtingsstaðir once had a hálfkirkja (a minor church or chapel) and was the assembly site of the district, which took its name from the farm: Lýtingsstaðahreppur. The farm lies, roughly speaking, in the middle of the district. People spoke of Lýtingsstaðatorfa, a cluster of holdings that included at least Lýtingsstaðir, Neðrakot and Efrakot. Its former tenant farms, Árnes, Tunguhlíð and Teigakot, had long since become independent farms by around the year 2000, no longer owned by the main estate. In the summer of 1958 work began on a new farmhouse, and the farm site was moved about 550 metres south and downhill, close to the road, where transport and cultivation were easier. The house took several years to build, and the family did not move in until 1962.
d21d3ee3-7118-5344-b2c6-d7f0cfd518af.story_is: Á Lýtingsstöðum var hálfkirkja og þingstaður hreppsins og hreppurinn kenndur við þann stað. Talað var um Lýtingsstaðatorfu, en í henni voru að minnsta kosti Lýtingsstaðir, Neðrakot og Efrakot. Þessi býli eru, að segja má, í miðjum Lýtingsstaðahreppi. Um aldamótin 2000 voru allar fyrrum hjáleigurnar, Árnes, Tunguhlíð og Teigakot, löngu orðnar sjálfstæð býli og lausar úr eignatengslum við höfuðbólið. Sumarið 1958 var hafist handa við byggingu nýs íbúðarhúss og bæjarstæðið flutt suður og niður um 550 metra, niður undir veg þar sem auðveldara var með samgöngur og ræktun. Húsið var nokkur ár í byggingu og ekki flutt í það fyrr en 1962.

d21ded9b-139a-d31a-6cdc-938db02d618e.story_eng: This hill still clearly shows the remains of a fortification that the people of Skálholt built to defend themselves in 1548, when Bishop Jón Arason and his followers came to visit, intending to take the place by force of arms. The hill lies in the home field somewhat east of the present churchyard. It has been written that the fort was built inside the churchyard; if that is correct, the churchyard must have been made smaller not only on the north side but considerably on the east side as well. In everyday speech the hill no longer has a name, but it is believed to have once been called Virkishóll, which means fort hill, and the writer of the description felt that the name should of course be kept.
d21ded9b-139a-d31a-6cdc-938db02d618e.story_is: Þessi hóll sýnir enn glöggt minjar vígis þess sem Skálhyltingar gerðu sér til varnar árið 1548 þegar Jón biskup Arason og fylgdarmenn hans veittu þeim heimsókn og hugðust taka staðinn með vopnavaldi. Hóllinn er í túninu nokkuð austan við núverandi kirkjugarð. Sé það rétt sem Páll E. Ólason segir, að virkið sem hann er leifar af hafi verið gert í kirkjugarðinum, er auðsætt að garðurinn hefur ekki einungis verið minnkaður að norðan heldur einnig allverulega að austan. Virkishóll á sér nú í daglegu tali ekkert nafn en mun fyrrum hafa verið nefndur svo og ætti vitanlega að halda því nafni.

d231ec4c-7c84-4cfa-abe9-ed1cb6dd3d24.story_eng: Stekkur stood in a narrow rock gorge of columnar basalt, right beside the river. A stekkur was a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes in spring. Beyond it, a long ridge with basalt cliffs along both edges runs beside the river. This is Miðaftansás, which served as a time marker (eyktarmark) for the farm Jórvík, telling the time of day by the sun's position.
d231ec4c-7c84-4cfa-abe9-ed1cb6dd3d24.story_is: Utan við Djúpabotn er þröng klettagjá fast við fljótið, mynduð úr stuðlabergi. Þar er Stekkur. Meðfram fljótinu út frá Stekknum er alllangur ás með stuðlabergsklettum á báðum brúnum, Miðaftansás, eyktarmörk frá Jórvík.

d2519af4-9385-499b-b417-9909c84fefdf.story_eng: This plot proved hard to bring into cultivation. People from Hvanneyri set up an experiment here with different fertilisers and amounts to try to find out why. The name refers both to that experiment (tilraun) and to the struggles of cultivating the land (raunir, meaning trials or hardships). The uppermost part of the field is still infertile.
d2519af4-9385-499b-b417-9909c84fefdf.story_is: Illa gekk að koma rækt í stykkið. Hvanneyringar lögðu þar út tilraun með mismunandi áburð og skammta til þess að reyna að finna ástæðuna. Nafnið vísar til tilraunarinnar, sem og ræktunarraunanna. Enn er efsti hluti spildunnar ófrjósamur.

d260de3d-5b5b-b096-f3dc-9d9baea8f7b7.story_eng: A stekkur, a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes in spring, stood at the southern end of Hvammar, the area west of the river Rangá, by Stekkjarlág and Stekkjarmór, which are named after it. In the hollow Stekkjarlág is a pond called Sundpollur, where Marteinn Sigurðsson taught swimming for several springs after 1910.
d260de3d-5b5b-b096-f3dc-9d9baea8f7b7.story_is: Hvammar heitir svæði vestan Rangár. Syðst í þeim eru Stekkjarlág og Stekkjarmór, og þar var stekkur. Í Stekkjarlág er Sundpollur, þar sem Marteinn Sigurðsson kenndi sund nokkur vor eftir 1910.

d267aad1-b5f8-c056-c2e4-c34c2afff1a5.story_eng: On the firm, dry grassy knolls stretching from Mjósund to the river Valagilsá lie the ruins of a farm believed to have been the home of Glæsir. He lived here at the same time as Gaukur of Gauksstaðir, and Glæsir is said to have been "rather a loner." The name Glæsivellir, meaning Glæsir's fields, covers both the knolls and the ruins.
d267aad1-b5f8-c056-c2e4-c34c2afff1a5.story_is: Á harðvellisbölunum frá Mjósundum inn að Valagilsá eru tóftir af býli sem talið er að hafi verið bústaður Glæsis, sem þar bjó samtíða Gauki á Gauksstöðum. Glæsir er sagður hafa verið „einrænn frekar“. Balarnir og tóftirnar bera saman nafnið Glæsivellir.

d27370ac-5091-ae01-5c80-3549f518790f.story_eng: An elf tale is set in Stöplar, and it is recorded in Jón Árnason's collection of Icelandic folktales. Stöplar lie just east of the farm's home field and run across the land from south to north. They are gravel flats on top. Steep slopes grown with heather and dwarf birch climb up them to sharp edges at the top, in places with small crags.
d27370ac-5091-ae01-5c80-3549f518790f.story_is: Í Stöplunum gerðist álfasaga sem skráð er í Þjóðsögum Jóns Árnasonar. Austan túnsins taka við Stöplar og liggja þvert yfir landareignina frá suðri til norðurs. Þeir eru allir melar að ofan. Brattar brekkur, vaxnar lyngi og fjalldrapa, eru upp eftir þeim, en hvassar brúnir efst, sums staðar með smáklettum.

d28a105b-2c64-b52b-2a64-f73e981ca31b.story_eng: Late in summer, steam could often be seen rising from this hill, caused by heat in the ground. There was a hole in the hill, and it was therefore sometimes also called Gathóll (hole hill). Digrihóll, meaning the stout hill, is larger than the hill to its east.
d28a105b-2c64-b52b-2a64-f73e981ca31b.story_is: Síðla sumars mátti oft sjá gufu leggja upp úr Digrahól, er stafaði frá varma í jörðinni. Á hólnum var gat, enda var hann stundum nefndur Gathóll. Digrihóll er stærri en hóllinn austan við hann.

d2a1db0b-9917-585d-5875-54c296c604d7.story_eng: Dagmálapollur is a pool in the river, lying just east of and below Dagmálahóll, a low but broad gravel hill on the edge of the ravine. The hill served as an eyktamark, a landmark used to tell the time of day by the sun's position, as seen from the farm Stafn. It marked dagmál, the old mid-morning mealtime, which gave both the hill and the pool their names.
d2a1db0b-9917-585d-5875-54c296c604d7.story_is: Austan undir Dagmálahól í ánni er Dagmálapollur. Hóllinn er melhóll á gilbarminum neðan Dagmálamýrar, ekki hár en nokkur um sig, og var eyktamark frá Stafni.

d2ab63eb-3b8b-824a-9862-583e127d2fcb.story_eng: Búðalækur, "stream of the booths", takes its name from the fishing booths that once stood on both sides of it where it runs into the sea at Kollsvíkurver, an old fishing station. Verbúðir were the simple huts where fishermen lived during the fishing season. A salt house was also built beside the stream. Just before Búðalækur reaches the sea, the stream Syðrilækur joins it, and on the tongue of land between the two stood many fishing booths in two rows. For a time there was a dam or irrigation channel in Búðalækur, known as Gestarfljót.
d2ab63eb-3b8b-824a-9862-583e127d2fcb.story_is: Búðalækur rennur til sjávar í Kollsvíkurveri og dregur nafn af verbúðum sem við hann stóðu sitt hvorum megin. Við hann var byggt salthús. Rétt áður en Búðalækur fellur í sjó rennur Syðrilækur í hann. Í tungunni sem myndast milli þeirra voru margar verbúðir í tveimur röðum. Í Búðalæk var um tíma stífla eða áveita sem kölluð var Gestarfljót.

d2c170c4-0ef6-99d5-27d2-ad9283884136.story_eng: This cairn stands at the edge of the road, above a deep hollow called Draugalág (Ghost Hollow) on the slope up from the farm Jaðar. Road workers built two cairns here and named them Pétur and Þuríður, after the married couple at Reynihlíð in Mývatnssveit. Pétur was a road-work foreman for many years.
d2c170c4-0ef6-99d5-27d2-ad9283884136.story_is: Í brekku upp frá Jaðri er djúp lág sem heitir Draugalág. Ofan hennar er varða á vegarbrún. Vegagerðarmenn hlóðu tvær vörður og hétu þær Pétur og Þuríður eftir hjónunum í Reynihlíð í Mývatnssveit, en Pétur var lengi vegaverkstjóri.

d2e5062b-2392-0bdc-aa2a-55dd294beab9.story_eng: Stekkjardalur, 'fold valley', is a hollow tucked into the elbow between low hills on the land of Stóru-Laugar, south of and below Skeiðflöt. It takes its name from the stekkur that once stood here, a small fold where lambs were kept apart from the ewes so the ewes could be milked. Old, grassed-over fragments of the fold's ruins can still be seen. According to a later note, there are in fact two places called Stekkjardalur: one up on Hvítafell, which also has ruins, and the other north of Leyningsholt.
d2e5062b-2392-0bdc-aa2a-55dd294beab9.story_is: Lægð í olnboga milli holta, sunnan og neðan við Skeiðflöt í landi Stórulauga, heitir Stekkjardalur. Þar eru gömul tóftarbrot eftir stekk, gróin og forn. Stekkjardalir eru þó tveir. Annar er uppi í Hvítafelli og þar eru líka tóftarbrot. Hinn er norðan við Leyningsholtið.

d2e9130f-354d-3c44-12f1-7215e3817699.story_eng: Bóndhólsmýri is the marshy hollow lying west of the hills Bóndhóll and Hesthúshóll. West of the marsh, on a hillside sloping towards the south, an ancient and fairly large akurgerði (an enclosed field, of the kind once used for growing grain) could until recently be clearly seen. A somewhat smaller one lay in Leyningur, south of Miðaftanshóll. The enclosure walls were so intact that large ponds of meltwater formed at the lowest end of the enclosures each spring.
d2e9130f-354d-3c44-12f1-7215e3817699.story_is: Mýrardragið vestan við Bóndhól og Hesthúshól, sem er áfastur Bóndhól að norðan, heitir Bóndhólsmýri. Vestan mýrarinnar, á hólbarði sem hallar mót suðri, var til skamms tíma greinilegt fornt akurgerði, allstórt, og annað nokkru minna í Leyningnum sunnan við Miðaftanshól. Voru garðarnir svo heillegir að stórar leysingartjarnir mynduðust neðst í gerðunum á vorin.

d304d873-8dec-b2ea-c942-cd72e935a630.story_eng: This cove holds Kista (meaning chest), a kind of chasm with sheer rock walls that opens down to the sea. It is possible to climb down into it from above, and it has a sandy floor. Kista was the site of the last witch burning in Iceland, in the 17th century. People at the farm Stóra-Árvík did not usually name Kista on its own but called the cove and the chasm together Kistuvogur, and sometimes Galdravogur, which means sorcery cove.
d304d873-8dec-b2ea-c942-cd72e935a630.story_is: Í voginum er Kista, eins konar gjá með þverhníptum hamraveggjum, opin niður í sjó, og er hægt að komast niður í hana ofan frá. Sandbotn er í henni. Þarna var síðasta galdrabrenna á Íslandi á 17. öld. Frá Stóru-Árvík var venja að nefna ekki Kistu sérstaklega heldur voginn og Kistu einu nafni Kistuvog og stundum Galdravog.

d310e4ca-1885-ad3d-7303-55b0d03e2ec8.story_eng: Sveigsklettur is a tall rock standing in the middle of the river Jökulsá. The pool on its east side is called Sveigur. There was once a ferry crossing here, and there are stories of people who drowned at this spot on their way to the church at Hofteigur.
d310e4ca-1885-ad3d-7303-55b0d03e2ec8.story_is: Sveigsklettur er hár klettur í Jökulsá miðri. Hylurinn austan við klettinn heitir Sveigur. Þarna var áður ferjustaður og eru sagnir um að þarna hafi fólk farist á leið til Hofteigskirkju.

d3113452-7299-9e94-bf57-a05b3f9406a2.story_eng: Kirkjusteinar (Church Rocks) are distinctive stones that together form the shape of a roof ridge, and they are said to be an old elf church. They stand at the outer end of Brenniselsnes, a stretch of marshland below the ruins of Brennisel, an old shieling (sel, a summer station where livestock were kept and milked).
d3113452-7299-9e94-bf57-a05b3f9406a2.story_is: Kirkjusteinar eru sérkennilegir, mynda bust og eru gömul álfakirkja. Þeir eru yst í Brenniselsnesi, mýrlendi niður af tóftunum af Brenniseli, út og niður af Selinu.

d3217c51-76fb-7e4f-e090-ef11d990e7ba.story_eng: Konungshver, the King's Hot Spring, lies northwest of the hot spring Blesi. It is said to have come into being in 1874, when King Kristján 9. was travelling in the area.
d3217c51-76fb-7e4f-e090-ef11d990e7ba.story_is: Norðvestur frá Blesa er Konungshver. Hann hefur orðið til árið 1874, þegar Kristján 9. var á ferð.

d3292c47-787a-690f-7f7f-591cbf4ad288.story_eng: Helguhóll is a fairly large and rather unusual cone-shaped hill standing in the middle of a bog, close to where the river Stangá flows into Dunká. Helga Bárðardóttir, daughter of Bárður Snæfellsás, is said to be buried here.
